Ekegusii: Abanto bande abake mbaaberwe ase engencho y’amaabera; korende baria bare n’okobua mbaegwe egesusuro egetindi.

English: For the Sovereign Lord of all will not be impressed with anyone, neither will he show deference to greatness; because it is he who made both small and great, and cares about them all;
Ekegusii: Ase engencho Omonene o bonsi tamoirogeti monto onde bwensi, obonene bw’omonto tibokogera anyore ogwanchereria; nere omonyene obatongente bonsi, abanene n’abake, na nigo akorigereria okogania kwa bonsi atari gwanchereria.

English: but the scrutiny that comes upon the powerful is strict.
Ekegusii: Korende baria bare n’obonene mbaringorigwe mono.

English: Therefore, my words are to you, O princes, that you may learn wisdom and not fall away.
Ekegusii: Bono inwe abarwoti igwa amang’ana ane, bono eegerie koba n’obong’aini timocha komocha.

English: For those who have kept the things that are holy in holiness will be made holy. Those who have been taught them will find what to say in defense.
Ekegusii: Baria batenererete amang’ana y’obochenu mbancherwe koba abachenu. Boigo na baria begerigwe ayio mbanyore enchera yokwerwanerera engaki y’ekina.

English: Therefore set your desire on my words. Long for them, and you princes will be instructed.
Ekegusii: Bono twara erango ase amorokerio ane; kabe n’okogania ase aro erio abaorokereri mobe n’amasikani.

English: Wisdom is radiant and doesn’t fade away; and is easily seen by those who love her, and found by those who seek her.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bokoraba tibokorima. Baria banchete omong’aini nigo bakoborora bwango, boigo na baria bakoborigia nigo bakobonyora.

English: She anticipates those who desire her, making herself known.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bogotanga kweorokia ase baria babotagete.

English: He who rises up early to seek her won’t have difficulty, for he will find her sitting at his gates.
Ekegusii: Ekero okoboka mambia chuni korigia obong’aini aye togochandeka; nigo okobonyora bokoganyete gesieri kiaye.

English: For to think upon her is perfection of understanding, and he who watches for her will quickly be free from care;
Ekegusii: Gotegerera obong’aini buya n’okonyora chisemi chindonge. Koraborigie botuko na mobaso togochandeka.

English: because she herself goes around, seeking those who are worthy of her, and in their paths she appears to them graciously, and in every purpose she meets them.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini botambe nigo bokorigia baria baisaine; ekero bogocha nigo bokoerokia ase bare ase enchera y’obwanchani, nigo bokoba nabarabwo ase kera ebirengererio.

English: For her true beginning is desire for instruction; and desire for instruction is love.
Ekegusii: Omochakano bw’obong’aini nogotwara erango kwegerigwa; gotwara erango ase okwegera n’ogwancha obong’aini.

English: And love is observance of her laws. To give heed to her laws confirms immortality.
Ekegusii: Ogwancha obong’aini n’okobwata amachiiko aye; okobwata amachiiko aye n’koenekerigwa komenya kare na kare.

English: Immortality brings closeness to God.
Ekegusii: Okomenya obogima bwa kare na kare nigo gokorenta omonto ange na Nyasae.

English: So then desire for wisdom promotes to a kingdom.
Ekegusii: Ase igo erango y’okonyora obongaini nigo ekoraa omonto gochia ase oborwoti.

English: If therefore you delight in thrones and sceptres, you princes of peoples, honor wisdom, that you may reign forever.
Ekegusii: Bono inwe abarai b’abaanto, onye mogokerete ebinto biaino bi’erigori n’ekemanyererio ki’obonene igoro ase abanto, sika obong’aini erio momenye kare na kare.

English: But what wisdom is, and how she came into being, I will declare. I won’t hide mysteries from you; but I will explore from her first beginning, bring the knowledge of her into clear light, and I will not pass by the truth.
Ekegusii: Nimbateebie obongaini ninki na omochakano oye norori. Tinkobabisa kende gionsi, nimbateebie omogano oye bwonsi korwa omochakano oye, nakobateebia buya amang’ana aye ntari gotiga enkeene gionsi.

English: Indeed, I won’t travel with consuming envy, because envy will have no fellowship with wisdom.
Ekegusii: Endamwamu embe tekoba mogisangio one, ekiagera obongaini tibori kogenda amo n’endamwamu.

English: But a multitude of wise men is salvation to the world, and an understanding king is stability for his people.
Ekegusii: Obonge bw’abang’aini n’ogotoreka ase ense, omorwoti omong’aini nigo akoa abanto baye oborendi.

English: Therefore be instructed by my words, and you will profit.
Ekegusii: Ase igo bono mwegere korwa ase amang’ana ane nainwe monyore okonyora okuya.

English: I myself am also mortal, like everyone else, and am a descendant of one formed first and born of the earth.
Ekegusii: Inche Mwanyabaanto ogokwa buna abande, omoiborwa korwa ase omonto oria bw’eritang’ani oyio otongetwe korwa ase riroba. Nigo narosetigwe ’nkaba omobere ase enda ya mama ase engaki y’emetienyi kianda, magega yokoroisigwa goetera ase embego y’omonto na goetera ase omogooko bw’enywomo.

English: I molded into flesh in the time of ten months in my mother’s womb, being compacted in blood from the seed of man and pleasure of marriage.
Ekegusii: Ase emetienyi ekobwatia kianda, magega konaroisigwe korwa ase embego y’omonto ase omogooko bw’enywomo.

English: I also, when I was born, drew in the common air, and fell upon the kindred earth, uttering, like all, for my first voice, the same cry.
Ekegusii: Ekero naiboretwe ngachaka koeyana embeo eyio ere oo nkagwa inse ase riroba erio rimbwekaine, egento kw’eritang’ani nakorete n’okorera buna abande.

English: I was nursed with care in swaddling clothes.
Ekegusii: Inkaboigwa chianga chi’abana, ’nkarendwa ase enchera engiya.

English: For no king had a different beginning,
Ekegusii: Morwoti onde taiyo ochagete komenya ase enchera ende engao;

English: but all men have one entrance into life, and a common departure.
Ekegusii: ekiagera bonsi nigo bagocha ase ense goetera ase enchera eyemo na barwa ase ense goetera enchera eyemo.

English: For this cause I prayed, and understanding was given to me. I asked, and a spirit of wisdom came to me.
Ekegusii: Bono inche ngasaba nkaegwa obosemia; Ngasaba Nyasae ere akanga enkoro y’obong’aini.

English: I preferred her before sceptres and thrones. I considered riches nothing in comparison to her.
Ekegusii: Nigo naganetie obongaini kobua ebirogo na obonene, nkarora obonda koba egento bosa ekero bokorenganigwa na obongaini.

English: Neither did I liken to her any priceless gem, because all gold in her presence is a little sand, and silver will be considered as clay before her.
Ekegusii: Tinabwekanetie obongaini gento kende gionsi ki’erigori rinene, ekiagera etaabu yonsi ere ase ense nigo enga buna amaroba, ne chifeta mbosa ase obongaini.

English: I loved her more than health and beauty, and I chose to have her rather than light, because her bright shining is never laid to sleep.
Ekegusii: Nigo nanchete chisemi kobua ekieni na okoba buya, nigo nanchete obongaini obo kobua oborabu bw’erisase, ase engencho oborabu bwaye tibori korima nonya ngake.

English: All good things came to me with her, and innumerable riches are in her hands.
Ekegusii: Amaya onsi nigo angicherete nonya n’obongaini; ase obosio bwaye nigo nanyorete enibo etari kobareka.

English: And I rejoiced over them all because wisdom leads them; although I didn’t know that she was their mother.
Ekegusii: Nigo nagokerete aya onsi ekiagera andeterete obongaini; korende timanyeti buna obongaini nabwo obogima bwa ayio onsi.

English: As I learned without guile, I impart without grudging. I don’t hide her riches.
Ekegusii: Nigo negerete ntari nabwoba boigo nkaegeria ntari kwemurungania; timbiseti banto obotenenku bwaye.

English: For she is a treasure for men that doesn’t fail, and those who use it obtain friendship with God, commended by the gifts which they present through discipline.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini n’eniibo etari koera ase abanto; baria bakwenyorera obongaini nigo bakoba abasani ba Nyasae; ere nigo akoenekia onsi aria bakwegera korwa ase are.

English: But may God grant that I may speak his judgment, and to conceive thoughts worthy of what has been given me; because he is one who guides even wisdom and who corrects the wise.
Ekegusii: Nigo ngosaba Nyasae ankonye inkwane korengana buna aganetie, nebirengererio biane bibwekane naria negeire. Nyasae omonyene nere omoteneneri bw’obong’aini; ere nigo akobamochia baria bare abang’aini.

English: For both we and our words are in his hand, with all understanding and skill in various crafts.
Ekegusii: Intwe nigo tore ase amaboko aye amo namang’ana aito, chisemi chiaito boigo nonya noboroisia bwaito.

English: For he himself gave me an unerring knowledge of the things that are, to know the structure of the universe and the operation of the elements;
Ekegusii: Ere nere ongeire obongaini mono goetenia ebitongwa bionsi: Inee ense ninki na bionsi ebireo ninki biroseirie,

English: the beginning, end, and middle of times; the alternations of the solstices and the changes of seasons;
Ekegusii: Omochakano bwe chingaki, omoerio oye, na gati gati yaye, ogonchoreria gwechingaki n’ebiro,

English: the circuits of years and the positions of stars;
Ekegusii: okobwatana kw’emiaka nechingenangeni.

English: the natures of living creatures and the raging of wild beasts; the violence of winds and the thoughts of men; the diversities of plants and the virtues of roots.
Ekegusii: Onyegeirie igoro yebitongwa bire moyo biria, ching’iti chi’orosana, chinguru chi’omoika, okobua ne chinguru chia Mwanyabaanto, ebimeria ao ao boigo nemeri yebimeri n’eki egokorerwa.

English: All things that are either secret or manifest I learned,
Ekegusii: Negeire igoro y’amang’ana abisekanete boigo naria are maiso marore, ase engencho chisemi echio chire omworokia bw’ekeene chianyorokereirie.

English: for wisdom, that is the architect of all things, taught me. For there is in her a spirit that is quick to understand, holy, unique, manifold, subtle, freely moving, clear in utterance, unpolluted, distinct, invulnerable, loving what is good, keen, unhindered,
Ekegusii: Ase obongaini nore oo omoika bwechisemi n’obochenu; omoika bwoka okweorokia ase chinchera chinyinge, omwororo mono oyio okomenya ase obuya; ebirengererio ebiya, ebiororo na bitagosareka; ebio bigwancha amaya, boigo bitari gosinywa gokora kende;

English: beneficent, loving toward man, steadfast, sure, free from care, all-powerful, all-surveying, and penetrating through all spirits that are quick to understand, pure, most subtle.
Ekegusii: bire ebiororo na bianchete abanto; omoyo omoikeranu, oria okwegeneka na otari na bwoba bonde; ebio bibwate chinguru na okobua gwokorora onsi; oria ogweta ase kera oyobwate ebirengererio, bire ebikeranu na obongaini bwa igoro mono.

English: For wisdom is more mobile than any motion. Yes, she pervades and penetrates all things by reason of her purity.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bokogenda bwango kobua orogendo ronde rionsi; nigo bore obuya na nigo bogosoa ime ase kera egento.

English: For she is a breath of the power of God, and a pure emanation of the glory of the Almighty. Therefore nothing defiled can find entrance into her.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini n’Omoika bw’echinguru chia Nyasae, nokoenekia gwe chinguru na obonene bwa Nyasae bw’echinguru; ase igo kende gionsi getari gechenu tikegosoa nonya ngake.

English: For she is a reflection of everlasting light, an unspotted mirror of the working of God, and an image of his goodness.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini n’oborabu bwa Nyasae bwa kare na kare, ekerore ekerabu ki’ogokora kwa Nyasae na omobwekano bw’obuya bwaye.

English: Although she is one, she has power to do all things. Remaining in herself, she renews all things. From generation to generation passing into holy souls, she makes friends of God and prophets.
Ekegusii: Nonya obongaini bore obomo nabo bogokora kende gionsi, tibori goonchoka nonya bogokora kera egento ase oboyia. Ase ebigori bionsi nigo bogosoa ase emioyo y’abachenu na kobakora abasani ba Nyasae na ababani.

English: For God loves nothing as much as one who dwells with wisdom.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho Nyasae nigo anchete omonto ore n’obongaini.

English: For she is fairer than the sun, and above all the constellations of the stars. She is better than light.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nobuya goetenia omobaso na goetenia ebiombe biechingenangeni; nigo bore obuya goetenia oborabu bwa mobaso.

English: For daylight yields to night, but evil does not prevail against wisdom.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera magega yomobaso obotuko nigo bogosoa, korende obobe tibogoetania obongaini.

English: But she reaches from one end to the other with full strength, and orders all things well.
Ekegusii: Chinguru chi’obong’aini nigo chigosoa kera ase ense eye na kobeka kera egento ase omoroberio omuya.

English: I loved her and sought her from my youth. I sought to take her for my bride. I became enamoured by her beauty.
Ekegusii: Nigo nanchete obongaini nkaborigia korwa chingaki chi’obosae bwane; nigo nabwate okogania koira obongaini koba omwanchi one, nigo nangusegete mono n’obuya bwaye.

English: She glorifies her noble birth by living with God. The Sovereign Lord of all loves her.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bokoira ogotogia kwaye kw’eritang’ani ase okomenya na Nyasae, n’Omonene o bionsi nigo anchete obongaini.

English: For she is initiated into the knowledge of God, and she chooses his works.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bomanyete amang’ana yogokumia a Nyasae na nigo bogokora emeroberio yaye.

English: But if riches are a desired possession in life, what is richer than wisdom, which makes all things?
Ekegusii: Onye enibo n’egento giokaganerigwa ase obogima obo, obotenenku ninki korenganigwa n’obongaini bokomenta amang’ana onsi?

English: And if understanding is effective, who more than wisdom is an architect of the things that exist?
Ekegusii: Onye obomanyi n’egento giokaganerigwa koba nakio, kende tikeri kiya goetania obongaini obwo bokoroisia bionsi.

English: If a man loves righteousness, the fruits of wisdom’s labor are virtues, for she teaches soberness, understanding, righteousness, and courage. There is nothing in life more profitable for people than these.
Ekegusii: Inee, aye mbwanchete ekeene? Bono engeria y’emeremo yobongaini nokoba nembwa engiya, koba nobomanyi boke, ekeene noboremu. Ase obogima kende tikeri kiya goetania ebi.

English: And if anyone longs for wide experience, she knows the things of old, and infers the things to come. She understands subtleties of speeches and interpretations of dark sayings. She foresees signs and wonders, and the issues of seasons and times.
Ekegusii: Inee, aye notagete koba nobomanyi obonge? Obong’aini nigo bomanyete amang’ana a kare na boigo naria agochia gocha; nigo bomanyete keria abanto barengereretie na boigo nigo bomanyete koganyana abanto ase emechando yabo. Nigo bomanyete ebikone bia Nyasae na buna emegano yense egendereretekoba.

English: Therefore I determined to take her to live with me, knowing that she is one who would give me good counsel, and encourage me in cares and grief.
Ekegusii: Bono inche nigo nachorete komenya n’obongaini, ’namanyete buna mbong’e obosemia obuya na kombeka chinguru chingaki chi’obororo n’emechando.

English: Because of her, I will have glory among multitudes, and honor in the sight of elders, though I am young.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho y’obong’aini ninsikwe na abanto ekero bakuomerana, nonya n’abagaaka mbansike nonya kinde omosae.

English: I will be found keen when I give judgment. I will be admired in the presence of rulers.
Ekegusii: Nigo bararore buna okonacha kwane ase amang’ana nigo kore okwaboronge, nonya nabagaambi mbaansike.

English: When I am silent, they will wait for me. When I open my lips, they will heed what I say. If I continue speaking, they will put their hands on their mouths.
Ekegusii: Ekero ndabe gikirete ntari gokwana, nigo baranganye goika nkwane, na ekero ndakwane nigo barantegerere. Ninsa gokwana ase chingaki chintambe, nigo barantegerere buya.

English: Because of her, I will have immortality, and leave behind an eternal memory to those who come after me.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho y’obong’aini nigo ndaegwe ogotakwa, na baria barache magega yane mbanginyore botambe.

English: I will govern peoples. Nations will be subjected to me.
Ekegusii: Nigo ndame nokobua ase abanto b’ebisaku;

English: Dreaded monarchs will fear me when they hear of me. Among the people, I will show myself to be good, and courageous in war.
Ekegusii: baria bakoraa ase chinguru nigo baranyiroke ekero baraigwe igoro yane. Gati y’abanto baane nigo ndabe omobui na omonyanguru ase esegi.

English: When I come into my house, I will find rest with her. For conversation with her has no bitterness, and living with her has no pain, but gladness and joy.
Ekegusii: Ekero ngosoa nyomba nigo ngotimoka amo nobongaini, ekiagera bororo tibori ase okomenya naborobwo korende n’omogooko bwoka.

English: When I considered these things in myself, and thought in my heart how immortality is in kinship to wisdom,
Ekegusii: Ekero nkorengereria amang’ana aya ase omoyo one ime na ase ebirengererio biane, buna ogotakwa nigo gokonyorekana ase obongaini,

English: and in her friendship is good delight, and in the labors of her hands is wealth that doesn’t fail, and understanding is in her companionship, and great renown in having fellowship with her words, I went about seeking how to take her to myself.
Ekegusii: buna baria banchete obongaini nigo bakonyora omogooko botambe, na baria bagokora emeremo yaye nigo bakonyora enibo etari koera, na baria bagokwana naborobwo nigo bakoba abang’aini, na baria bakobwatia amang’ana aye nigo bakonyora amasikani; bono nigo natarire goeta nkorigia obongaini obo.

English: Now I was a clever child, and received a good soul.
Ekegusii: Ekero narenge omwana nigo narenge n’ebiegwa biria biokoiboreranigwa, nigo nabete n’egesio koba n’enkoro engiya, gose ase enchera ende nigo narenge omuya, ngasoa ase omobere omuya.

English: Or rather, being good, I came into an undefiled body.
Ekegusii: Korende nkamanya nga tikonyora obongaini onye tinkoegwa na Nyasae; na ekero namanya buna Nyasae nabo akong’a n’ekemanyererio kiobong’aini. Ase igo nigo nasabete Omonene n’omoyo one bwonsi nkamosorora ngoteeba:

English: “O God of my ancestors and Lord of mercy, who made all things by your word;
Ekegusii: Aye Nyasae bw’echisokoro chiaito, Omonene omonyamaabera! Ase ring’ana riao nigo gwatongete ebinto bionsi.

English: and by your wisdom you formed man, that he should have dominion over the creatures that were made by you,
Ekegusii: Ase obongaini bwao ogatonga omonto abitenenere bionsi biria gwatongete,

English: and rule the world in holiness and righteousness, and execute judgment in uprightness of soul,
Ekegusii: amenye ense ase omoroberio na obongaini, na gokorera ekeene ase omonyo omuya.

English: give me wisdom, her who sits by you on your thrones. Don’t reject me from among your servants,
Ekegusii: Nigo ngogosaba onge obongaini obwo bore ensemo yekerogo kiao ki’obonene; tobaisa konyanga inche gati y’abasomba bao.

English: because I am your servant and the son of your handmaid, a weak and short-lived man, with little power to understand judgment and laws.
Ekegusii: Inche n’omosomba oo, omwana bw’omosomba oo omosubati, omonto omoreu otari na kobua konde, tindi na nguru komanya igoro y’amachiiko ao gose okogambigwa.

English: For even if a man is perfect among the sons of men, if the wisdom that comes from you is not with him, he will count for nothing.
Ekegusii: Neisa koba omonto ore omoikeranu, onye tabwati obongaini bokorwa ase ore, oyio nigo are bosa.

English: You chose me to be king of your people, and a judge for your sons and daughters.
Ekegusii: Nigo gwanchorete koba obogambi bw’abaanto bao, oborwoti bw’abana bao abamura na abaiseke.

English: You gave a command to build a sanctuary on your holy mountain, and an altar in the city where you live, a copy of the holy tent which you prepared from the beginning.
Ekegusii: Nigo gwanchigete inyagache Hekalu ase egetunwa egechenu kiao, boigo n’egesasiimero ase omochie oyio gwachorete koba obomenyo bwao, omobwekano bwe’eema eria kwaroisetie kare.

English: Wisdom is with you and knows your works, and was present when you were making the world, and understands what is pleasing in your eyes, and what is right according to your commandments.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bore naye; na nigo bomanyete ogokora kwao; nigo bwarenge naye ekero gwatongete ense. Obong’aini nigo bomanyete aria agokogokia na aria are amaronge korengana n’amachiiko ao.

English: Send her from the holy heavens, and ask her to come from the throne of your glory, that being present with me she may work, and I may learn what pleases you well.
Ekegusii: Toma obongaini korwa agwo igoro ase achenu korwa ase ekerogo kiao ki’amaabera egechenu erio obongaini obwo bomenye amo nainche na gokora emeremo amo nainche erio inyare kwegera aria agokogokia.

English: For she knows all things and understands, and she will guide me prudently in my actions. She will guard me in her glory.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera obongaini mbomanyete amang’ana onsi, borobwo mbondae buya ase ogokora kwane; na omochenu bwaye mbondende.

English: So my works will be acceptible. I will judge your people righteously, and I will be worthy of my father’s throne.
Ekegusii: Ogokora kwane ngwacheranwe, erio ningambie abanto bao ase ekeene na ninganie koba ase ekerogo ki’obonene gia tata one.

English: For what man will know the counsel of God? Or who will conceive what the Lord wills?
Ekegusii: “Ningo oramanye ebirengererio bia Nyasae? Gose ningo oramanye emeroberio yaye?

English: For the thoughts of mortals are unstable, and our plans are prone to fail.
Ekegusii: Ebirengererio bia Mwanyabaanto tibisaini kende nonya nechisemi chiabo nigo chigosiria.

English: For a corruptible body weighs down the soul. The earthy tent burdens a mind that is full of cares.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho emebere eye yaito egokwa nigo ekongaina emioyo yaito. Omobere oroisirie korwa ase amaroba nigo ere egurube ase ebirengererio ebiikeranu.

English: We can hardly guess the things that are on earth, and we find the things that are close at hand with labor; but who has traced out the things that are in the heavens?
Ekegusii: Nigo togokagera bosa igo ase amang’ana y’ense; naria are ange naitwe titokoyanyora totagiramoreti. Ningo rende oranyare kwegera aria are igoro?

English: Who gained knowledge of your counsel, unless you gave wisdom, and sent your holy spirit from on high?
Ekegusii: Onde taiyo oranyare kwegera obosemia bwao aye Nyasae, onye aye tokomoa obongaini na gotoma Omoika Omochenu korwa agwo ase ore igoro.

English: It was thus that the ways of those who are on earth were corrected, and men were taught the things that are pleasing to you. They were saved through wisdom.”
Ekegusii: Nabo chinchera chi’abaanto ase ense chiabegetwe buya, bakabwata aria agokogokia erio bagatorigwa ase engencho y’obong’aini.”

English: Wisdom guarded to the end the first formed father of the world, who was created alone, and delivered him out of his own transgression,
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bwarendete oria otongetwe bw’eritang’ani, tata bw’ense, oria otongetwe ere bweka magega y’abande bonsi. Obong’aini bokabotoria korwa ase okomocha kwaye;

English: and gave him strength to rule over all things.
Ekegusii: obongaini bokamoa chinguru chi’okogambera ebitongwa bionsi.

English: But when an unrighteous man fell away from her in his anger, he perished himself in the rage with which he killed his brother.
Ekegusii: Korende omonto oyomo omomochi agaeatanana korwa ase obongaini ase engencho y’obororo bwaye, ere agasira ase engencho aitete momura omwabo ase engencho y’endamwamu yaye.

English: When for his cause the earth was drowning with a flood, wisdom again saved it, guiding the righteous man’s course by a paltry piece of wood.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho y’omonto oyio etoigo egacha ase ense, korende nainse ase engencho y’obong’aini agatoreka. Obong’aini bokaraa omonto oyomo omonyaboronge agetanga korwa ase etoigo.

English: Moreover, when nations consenting together in wickedness had been confounded, wisdom knew the righteous man, and preserved him blameless to God, and kept him strong when his heart yearned toward his child.
Ekegusii: Ekero chinse chiaigwananete ase ogokora amabe, obongaini bogakonya omonto oyomo oyio omoirogete Nyasae n’moyo oye bwonsi. Ase obongaini omonto oyio akabwata amachiiko a Nyasae nonya ngoika komorwa omwana oye oyio anchete mono.

English: While the ungodly were perishing, wisdom delivered a righteous man, when he fled from the fire that descended out of heaven on the five cities.
Ekegusii: Ekero abanyabibe bare gosirigwa, obongaini bogakonya omonto oyomo omonyaboronge ekero omorero oruete igoro na gosiria emechie etano korende ere agakonyeka.

English: To whose wickedness a smoking waste still witnesses, and plants bearing fair fruit that doesn’t ripen, a disbelieving soul has a memorial: a standing pillar of salt.
Ekegusii: Nonya ngoika reero iga oboene bw’ogosaria kwabo nigo gokororekana: ense eyio nigo ere erooro na nigo ekorwa erioki; emete y’aroro nigo ekwama amatunda korende takoba rinde, rigena ri’omonyo nao riteneine gotoinyoria igoro y’omonto otegenete.

English: For having passed wisdom by, not only were they disabled from recognising the things which are good, but they also left behind them for their life a monument of their folly, to the end that where they stumbled, they might fail even to be unseen;
Ekegusii: Abanto b’emechie eyio nigo bangete obongaini, tibari goatanana amaya na amabe. Goetania igo bebire oboriri bwabo erio okobugwa kwabo tikwebwa rinde.

English: but wisdom delivered those who waited on her out of troubles.
Ekegusii: Korende obongaini bogakonya baria baborigeti.

English: When a righteous man was a fugitive from a brother’s wrath, wisdom guided him in straight paths. She showed him God’s kingdom, and gave him knowledge of holy things. She prospered him in his toils, and multiplied the fruits of his labor.
Ekegusii: Omonto oyomo ekero are gotama korwa ase endamwamu ya momura omwabo, obongaini nigo bwamoraete buya. Nigo bwamworogeti oborwoti bwa Nyasae na komworokereria amang’ana amachenu. Obongaini bokamobuera ase emeremo yaye; na bokamoiborera amatunda y’emeremo yaye.

English: When in their covetousness men dealt harshly with him, she stood by him and made him rich.
Ekegusii: Ekero abachandi baye batagete koira enibo yaye ase obounereria, obongaini bokamokonya ere agatenenka.

English: She guarded him from enemies, and she kept him safe from those who lay in wait. Over his severe conflict, she watched as judge, that he might know that godliness is more powerful than every one.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini bokamorenda korwa ase ababisa baye na baria bamoboerete. Ase esegi yarenge endoro obongaini bokamoa obobui, erio akamanya nga obuya nigo bore n’echinguru kobua bionsi.

English: When a righteous man was sold, wisdom didn’t forsake him, but she delivered him from sin. She went down with him into a dungeon,
Ekegusii: Nainde ekero omonto oyomo omonyaboronge aonetigwe gochia ase obosomba, obongaini nigo bwamotangete korwa ase ebibe. Obong’aini nigo bwarenge nere ase echera,

English: and in bonds she didn’t depart from him, until she brought him the sceptre of a kingdom, and authority over those that dealt like a tyrant with him. She also showed those who had mockingly accused him to be false, and gave him eternal glory.
Ekegusii: ekero arenge echera, obongaini bokamokonya erio akaegwa okobua igoro ase omorwoti erio akamokora koba omonene ase abanene baye. Baria bamosoerete bakarorekana koba abanyaborimo, nere akanyora amasikani a kare na kare.

English: Wisdom delivered a holy people and a blameless seed from a nation of oppressors.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini bogatoria abanto abachenu batarenge na komocha abwo bairetwe ase ense engeni eyio yabakorete koba abasomba.

English: She entered into the soul of a servant of the Lord, and withstood terrible kings in wonders and signs.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini bogasoa ime y’omonto oyomo Omonene, na ase okobua akabarwania abarwoti abwo barenge kwobonyia.

English: She rendered to holy men a reward of their toils. She guided them along a marvelous way, and became to them a covering in the day-time, and a starry flame through the night.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini bokaa abanto ba Nyasae engeria y’emerebo yabo; obongaini bokabaraa ase enchera yogokumia bokoba ase bare egekengere ase omobaso na oborabu ase chingaki chia botuko.

English: She brought them over the Red sea, and led them through much water;
Ekegusii: Obong’aini bokabatambokia enyancha embariri, bokabaraa gati gati y’amache amange,

English: but she drowned their enemies, and she cast them up from the bottom of the deep.
Ekegusii: Korende bokabasiria ababisa babo ase amache bokarusia emebere yabo ase emerindo ya nyancha.

English: Therefore the righteous plundered the ungodly, and they sang praise to your holy name, O Lord, and extolled with one accord your hand that fought for them,
Ekegusii: Ase igo abanyaboronge bagachecheria abanyabibe bagatera na gotogia erieta riao richenu, ee aye Omonene bonsi bakagotogia ase engencho kwabarwanererete.

English: because wisdom opened the mouth of the mute, and made the tongues of babes to speak clearly.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini bokaigora emenwa yechisokoro chiaito bagakwana, boigo na gokora chimeme chi’abana abake gokwana buya.

English: Wisdom prospered their works in the hand of a holy prophet.
Ekegusii: Obongaini nigo bwabakonyete abanto abwo bare koraua n’omobani omochenu.

English: They traveled through a desert without inhabitant, and they pitched their tents in trackless regions.
Ekegusii: Bagaeta ase erooro ase abanto batamenyete bakaagacha chiema chiabo ase monto onde konya ataraeta.

English: They withstood enemies and repelled foes.
Ekegusii: Bakabua ababisa babo na kobabua baria barenge koamererania nabarabwo.

English: They thirsted, and they called upon you, and water was given to them out of the flinty rock, and healing of their thirst out of the hard stone.
Ekegusii: Ekero erang’o yabariete nigo bakoreerete, aye okobaa amache korwa ase egetare bakanywa erango yabo egasira.

English: For by what things their foes were punished, by these they in their need were benefited.
Ekegusii: Amaakwa aria kwaete ababisa babo agakonya abanto bao ase emechando.

English: When enemies were troubled with clotted blood instead of a river’s ever-flowing fountain,
Ekegusii: Ribaga ri’amache amaya agotirimboka buya amache agaonchoka akaba amanyinga.

English: to rebuke the decree for the slaying of babies, you gave them abundant water beyond all hope,
Ekegusii: Ase engencho ababisa baria baruete ogochika buna abana b’abaanto bao baitwe, aye okaa abanto bao amache amange.

English: having shown by the thirst which they had suffered how you punished the adversaries.
Ekegusii: Okaorokia goetera ase erango yabo chingaki chiria buna aye kwaete ababisa babo egesusuro.

English: For when they were tried, although chastened in mercy, they learned how the ungodly were tormented, being judged with wrath.
Ekegusii: Ekero batemetwe nonya bare koegwa egesusuro ase amaabera, bakerorera buna abanyabibe bachandetwe ekero kwabagambetie n’endamwamu.

English: For you tested these as a father admonishing them; but you searched out those as a stern king condemning them.
Ekegusii: Okabakuurera buna omoibori agokuurera abana baye. Korende akaenekia abanyabibe abwo buna omorwoti omotindi akogambia.

English: Yes and whether they were far off or near, they were equally distressed;
Ekegusii: Baria barenge are boigo nabarenge ange bonsi bagachandeka.

English: for a double grief seized them, and a groaning at the memory of things past.
Ekegusii: Bakaiyeria amariga ara kabere ekero bainyorete aria abanyorete.

English: For when they heard that through their own punishments the others benefited, they recognized the Lord.
Ekegusii: Ekero baigwete buna egesusuro kiao nigo giakonyete abanto bao, bagateeba buna aye Omonene naye gwakorete ayio onsi.

English: For him who long before was thrown out and exposed they stopped mocking. In the end of what happened, they marveled, having thirsted in another manner than the righteous.
Ekegusii: Nonya konya bachayire oyio agwo ritangani konya otugutirwe na gotigwa, magega yayio onsi nigo bamokumetie, ekero baigwete erango enene goetania abasaria.

English: But in return for the senseless imaginings of their unrighteousness, wherein they were led astray to worship irrational reptiles and wretched vermin, you sent upon them a multitude of irrational creatures to punish them,
Ekegusii: Ase engencho y’oboriri n’ebirengererio biabo ebibe ebio biabasiretie, bagasasiima ching’iti n’emegwekano yogosamimwa, aye okabaretera ebitongwa bitaisaini kende bibae egesusuro,

English: that they might learn that by what things a man sins, by these he is punished.
Ekegusii: mbamanye ng’a omonto nigo akoegwa egesusuro ase ebinto biria biria akorete nabio ebibe

English: For your all-powerful hand that created the world out of formless matter didn’t lack means to send upon them a multitude of bears, fierce lions,
Ekegusii: Ase okoboko kwao gwechinguru, ogatonga ense korwa ase kende getare, kwabeire botambe omonyanguru nabo kware kobaretera chingangau gose chindo chintindi,

English: or newly-created and unknown wild beasts, full of rage, either breathing out a blast of fiery breath, or belching out smoke, or flashing dreadful sparks from their eyes;
Ekegusii: gose ching’iti chintindi mono echio chitanya kobao, gose ching’iti echio chikoeyana omoika bw’omorero, gose chiria chikoeyana erioki ririto chiria chigosaria, gose chikorusia amariga y’okoondokia.

English: which had power not only to consume them by their violence, but to destroy them even by the terror of their sight.
Ekegusii: Ching’iti echi nigo chiare echi’okoondokia mono nonya tichiare goita omonto, nigo chiare kororekana chi’okondookia mono.

English: Yes and without these they might have fallen by a single breath, being pursued by Justice, and scattered abroad by the breath of your power; but you arranged all things by measure, number, and weight.
Ekegusii: Korende aya tarenge ay’engencho. Nabo kware kobarigia ase ekeene kiao nakobaita bakwe, korende aye gwachorire gokora kera egento ase ekerengo.

English: For to be greatly strong is yours at all times. Who could withstand the might of your arm?
Ekegusii: Aye nabo okoorokia chinguru chiao buna oragani, na onde taiyo oratenene mamincha yao.

English: Because the whole world before you is as a grain in a balance, and as a drop of dew that comes down upon the earth in the morning.
Ekegusii: Ase ore ense engima nigo enga buna enyeke eyemo ase eratiri; nigo enga buna entonyi yerimi ria mambia.

English: But you have mercy on all men, because you have power to do all things, and you overlook the sins of men to the end that they may repent.
Ekegusii: Korende aye n’omonyamaabera ase bonsi ekiagera aye n’omobui o bionsi; aye tori korigereria ebibe b’abaanto bao, nigo okobaa chingaki erio baangame.

English: For you love all things that are, and abhor none of the things which you made; For you never would have formed anything if you hated it.
Ekegusii: Aye nigo bwanchete ebinto bionsi bire ase ense, gose tibwangeti kende ase ebio gwatongete. Anga tigwatongete kende onye ndiria okiangete.

English: How would anything have endured unless you had willed it? Or that which was not called by you, how would it have been preserved?
Ekegusii: Gento kerabe moyo onye aye togwancha? Ngaki keragenderere kobao onye tikwagetongete?

English: But you spare all things, because they are yours, O Sovereign Lord, you who love the living.
Ekegusii: Gwancheire ebinto bionsi bibe oo aye Omonene.

English: For your incorruptible spirit is in all things.
Ekegusii: Omoika oo oyio otari gokwa nigo ore ase ebinto bionsi.

English: Therefore you convict little by little those who fall from the right way, and, putting them in remembrance by the things wherein they sin, you admonish them, that escaping from their wickedness they may believe in you, O Lord.
Ekegusii: Ase igo aye nigo okorongeyia baria bagokomochera ase enchera y’obwororo; nigo okobainyoria na kobakuurera igoro yaria bakomocheire, erio batige obobe bwabo na kogosemeria aye Omonene.

English: For truly the old inhabitants of your holy land,
Ekegusii: Boigo nonya mbaria bamenyete ase ense yao enchenu, nigo kwabagechete ase engencho bare gokora amang’ana yokogechia mono: nigo bare gokora oborogi n’ogosasiima gotare koronge;

English: hating them because they practiced detestable works of enchantments and unholy rites—
Ekegusii: aye nigo kwabagechete ase engencho bare gokora amang’ana y’okogechia mono:

English: merciless slaughters of children and sacrificial banquets of men’s flesh and of blood—
Ekegusii: nigo bare konyenya abana batari na amaabera, bakaria chinyama na manyinga y’abanto buna ekengwanso; barabwo bagasoa ase ogosasiima okobe kwa bobisi,

English: allies in an impious fellowship, and murderers of their own helpless babes, it was your counsel to destroy by the hands of our fathers;
Ekegusii: na goita abana abwo batare na nguru chi’ogwetanga korwa ase bare. Ase ogwancha kwao abanto abwo bagasirigwa n’abagaaka baito;

English: that the land which in your sight is most precious of all might receive a worthy colony of God’s servants.
Ekegusii: erio ense eyio aye bwanchete goetania chionsi ebe obomenyo bw’abaanto abwo babwenerete koba abasomba bao.

English: Nevertheless you even spared these as men, and you sent hornets as forerunners of your army, to cause them to perish little by little.
Ekegusii: Korende nonya naba aye nigo kwabarorerete amaabera ase engencho barabwo n’abanto bao. Nigo gwatomete chinchoke chigatangana omoganda bw’abarwani esegi erio chibasirie ngora ngora.

English: Not that you were unable to subdue the ungodly under the hand of the righteous in battle, or by terrible beasts or by a stern word to make away with them at once,
Ekegusii: Anga nabo gwancherete abanyaboronge basirie abanyabibe ase esegi; gose anga nabo kwabasiretie ase ogwanchera ching’iti chintindi chibaboere, gose goetera ase ring’ana riao erimo ritindi.

English: but judging them little by little you gave them a chance to repent, not being ignorant that their nature by birth was evil, their wickedness inborn, and that their manner of thought would never be changed.
Ekegusii: Korende aye okabagambia ng’ora ng’ora okabaa ribaga kwangama; nonya aye kwamanyete nga nigo bare gokora ebibe bobisi: nigo barenge ababurukanu korwa okoiborwa kwabo naende tibarenge goonchoreria embwa yabo.

English: For they were a cursed seed from the beginning. It wasn’t through fear of any that you left them unpunished for their sins.
Ekegusii: Barabwo nigo baragereirie korwa kare, gose tari ase engencho kwamoirogete monto onde bwensi erio tikwabaa egesusuro ase engencho y’ebibe biabo.

English: For who will say, “What have you done?” Or “Who will withstand your judgment?” Who will accuse you for the perishing of nations which you caused? Or who will come and stand before you as an avenger for unrighteous men?
Ekegusii: Ningo oranyare gotenena na koamereria ay’ogokora, gose nongo oranyare gotanga okogambigwa? Ningo oragosoere buna gwasiririe chinse echio gwatongete? Ningo oratenene bosio bwao koegerera abanto abwo ababe?

English: For there isn’t any God beside you that cares for all, that you might show that you didn’t judge unrighteously.
Ekegusii: Nyasae ende taiyo otatiga aye oria okorigereria okogania kw’abaanto bonsi, nase ngo obwenerete koorokia buna kwagambire bobe;

English: No king or prince will be able to confront you about those whom you have punished.
Ekegusii: gose morwoti onde tari gose omogambi oranyare kogosoera ekero kwaeire monto onde bwensi egesusuro.

English: But being righteous, you rule all things righteously, deeming it a thing alien from your power to condemn one who doesn’t deserve to be punished.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho aye n’omonyaboronge na nigo okogamba ebinto bionsi buya, tikwana kogambia monto onde bwensi ase chinguru.

English: For your strength is the source of righteousness, and your sovereignty over all makes you to forbear all.
Ekegusii: Okobua kwao n’ensoko y’oboronge bwao; nigo okororera abanto bonsi amaabera ekiagera aye Omonene o bonsi.

English: For when men don’t believe that you are perfect in power, you show your strength, and in dealing with those who think this, you confuse their boldness.
Ekegusii: Onye bwanyabaanto gakoba n’echitangutangu ase okobua kwao, bono aye nigo okoorokia chinguru chiao na kobaa egesusuro baria bamanyete okobua kwao korende tibagokora buna aye origeti.

English: But you, being sovereign in strength, judge in gentleness, and with great forbearance you govern us; for the power is yours whenever you desire it.
Ekegusii: Nonya kobwate okobua okonene, aye nigo okogambia ase obwororo; na nigo ogotogambera ase oboremereria obonene ekiagera aye nore n’okobua gwokogambia ngaki ende yonsi origetie.

English: But you taught your people by such works as these, how the righteous must be kind. You made your sons to have good hope, because you give repentance when men have sinned.
Ekegusii: Ase ogokora kwao kwaorokereirie abanto bao buna omonyaboronge naganeirie koba obwororo. Kwaeire abana bao ogosemeria okonene, ekiagera ekero abanto bamochire aye nigo okobaa okobua gw’okwangama.

English: For if on those who were enemies of your servants and deserving of death, you took vengeance with so great deliberation and indulgence, giving them times and opportunities when they might escape from their wickedness,
Ekegusii: Aye nigo kwarendete na nigo kwarenge omoremereria ase okoa ababisa b’abaanto bao egesusuro nonya baganeirie gokwa; nigo kwabaete ribaga rinene gotiga obobe bwabo.

English: with how great care you judged your sons, to whose fathers you gave oaths and covenants of good promises!
Ekegusii: Korende abanto bao aye omonyene okabaa egesusuro egetindi, nonya konya kwariereite chisokoro chiaito eira ase amang’ana amaya.

English: Therefore while you chasten us, you scourge our enemies ten thousand times more, to the intent that we may ponder your goodness when we judge, and when we are judged may look for mercy.
Ekegusii: Bono aye nigo ogotoa egesusuro, korende nigo ogosusura ababisa baito mara chiribu ikomi na goetania erio ekero toragambie toinyore obuya bwao na ekero tokogambigwa tosemerie kwaberwa.

English: Therefore also the unrighteous that lived in a life of folly, you tormented through their own abominations.
Ekegusii: Bono baria bamenyete chinchera chimbe, nigo kwabachandete korengana n’echinchera chiabo chi’okogechia.

English: For truly they went astray very far in the ways of error, Taking as gods those animals which even among their enemies were held in dishonor, deceived like foolish babes.
Ekegusii: Nigo basirerete are ase amamocho, bagasasiima ebingiti biria nonya n’ababisa babo bachayete; nigo bangainegete buna abana abariri.

English: Therefore, as to unreasoning children, you sent your judgment to mock them.
Ekegusii: Ase igo aye okabaa egesusuro ase engencho y’obobe bwabo, na egesusuro kiao gekabakora bakarorekana buna abanto abariri.

English: But those who would not be admonished by mild correction will experience the deserved judgment of God.
Ekegusii: Nigo kiarenge egesusuro ekiororo, korende baria batari koigwa ogokuurerwa kwa Nyasae nigo baganeirie konyora egesusuro ki’endamwamu ya Nyasae.

English: For through the sufferings they were indignant of, being punished in these creatures which they supposed to be gods, they saw and recognized as the true God him whom they previously refused to know. Therefore also the result of extreme condemnation came upon them.
Ekegusii: Ekero baetwe egesusuro n’echingiti chiria barogete chinyasae bakainyora buna Nyasae nere Nyasae bw’ekeene nere oria oria bangire komanya. Ase igo bakaegwa egesusuro egetindi.

English: For truly all men who had no perception of God were foolish by nature, and didn’t gain power to know him who exists from the good things that are seen. They didn’t recognize the architect from his works.
Ekegusii: Abanto bonsi baria batamanyeti Nyasae nigo bare abariri nonya korwa ime. Abanto abwo barorire ebinto ebiya bireo, korende basinyirwe komwancha Nyasae ore moyo. Ere nigo okorigereria ebitongwa biaye korende birobio tibimomanyeti ere oyio ore omoroisia obo.

English: But they thought that either fire, or wind, or swift air, or circling stars, or raging water, or luminaries of heaven were gods that rule the world.
Ekegusii: Barabwo nigo bakagete buna chinyasae echio chikogambera ense n’omorero, gose embeo, gose emerindo, gose ebitongwa bikoiruruka ase embeo.

English: If it was through delight in their beauty that they took them to be gods, let them know how much better their Sovereign Lord is than these, for the first author of beauty created them.
Ekegusii: Abanto nigo bagogetigwe n’obuya bw’ebinto ebio, bakabikagera koba chinyasae, korende anga nabo bamanyete buna ebinto ebio mbiabwate omonyene, oyio obietanetie bionsi. Oyio nere omochakano bw’obuya na nere omontongi o bionsi.

English: But if it was through astonishment at their power and influence, then let them understand from them how much more powerful he who formed them is.
Ekegusii: Bono ase engencho abanto bagokumeria chinguru chi’ebitongwa ebio, nebagwenerete kwegera korwa ase ebintongwa ebio buna oria obitongete nabwate chinguru mono.

English: For from the greatness of the beauty of created things, mankind forms the corresponding perception of their Maker.
Ekegusii: Buna obuya bw’ebitongwa bore obonene, bono Mwanyabaanto nagwenerete kweegeria igoro y’omotongi oye.

English: But yet for these men there is but small blame, for they too perhaps go astray while they are seeking God and desiring to find him.
Ekegusii: Kero kende banto aba tibari nakomocha. Naro eranyarekane buna nigo bakagerete buna Nyasae bare korigia korende tibamonyora.

English: For they diligently search while living among his works, and they trust their sight that the things that they look at are beautiful.
Ekegusii: Barobwo nigo baetananire n’ebitongwa bia Nyasae, bakabirigereria buya na omoerio oye bakabirora nga nigo bire ebiya na bakabiegena.

English: But again even they are not to be excused.
Ekegusii: Nonya nigo tibakonyara kwerwanerera buna tibari na komocha.

English: For if they had power to know so much, that they should be able to explore the world, how is it that they didn’t find the Sovereign Lord sooner?
Ekegusii: Korende onye bare n’okobua gw’okomanya ayio onsi, nonya n’okoringoria ense, ngaki rende batamanyete oria ore Omonene bw’ebinto ebi bionsi.

English: But they were miserable, and their hopes were in dead things, who called them gods which are works of men’s hands, gold and silver, skillfully made, and likenesses of animals, or a useless stone, the work of an ancient hand.
Ekegusii: Korende baria bataisaini kende, mbaria bagosemeria ebinto bikwete, baria bakoroka ebinto biria birosirie n’amaboko a Mwanyabaanto chinyasae: ebinto biria bie chitaabu biria biroisirie buya, emegwekano y’echingiti gose amagena atari nangencho.

English: Yes and some woodcutter might saw down a tree that is easily moved, skillfully strip away all its bark, and fashion it in attractive form, make a useful vessel to serve his life’s needs.
Ekegusii: Omogechi emete nigo akogecha emete eria ebwenerete, erio orusia amasabo aye, erio oroisia buya egento kebwenerete korwa ase omote oria.

English: Burning the scraps from his handiwork to cook his food, he eats his fill.
Ekegusii: Erio oira ebingese biria biatigara oroiseria endagera oria oigota.

English: Taking a discarded scrap which served no purpose, a crooked piece of wood and full of knots, he carves it with the diligence of his idleness, and shapes it by the skill of his idleness. He shapes it in the image of a man,
Ekegusii: Korende nabo akorusia ekengese ekemo keria getaisaini kende, ekio kebandegete naende kebochogete chingoro chinyinge, ere okeroisia buya chingaki atimogete goika kiabwenera buya kiaba omobwekano o Mwanyabaanto;

English: or makes it like some worthless animal, smearing it with something red, painting it red, and smearing over every stain in it.
Ekegusii: gose omobwekano o ngiti ende yonsi. Nigo akogiaka erangi embariri na gotuba buya chingoro chiria chionsi.

English: Having made a worthy chamber for it, he sets it in a wall, securing it with iron.
Ekegusii: Erio akaroisia ase gete agiya ase enyasi erio osunga omobwekano oria aroro,

English: He plans for it that it may not fall down, knowing that it is unable to help itself (for truly it is an image, and needs help).
Ekegusii: nigo agokora aya onsi ase engencho ere amanyete buna oyio n’omobwekano bosa otanyare gwetenenera korende nigo oganeirie gokonywa.

English: When he makes his prayer concerning goods and his marriage and children, he is not ashamed to speak to that which has no life.
Ekegusii: Korende ere tari koba n’obosoku ekero agochaka gosasiima omobwekano oyo otari na bomoyo ochaka koyoteebia igoro y’enywomo yaye boigo n’abana baye.

English: Yes, for health, he calls upon that which is weak. For life, he implores that which is dead. For aid, he supplicates that which has no experience. For a good journey, he asks that which can’t so much as move a step.
Ekegusii: Bono ere nigo agochaka gosaba igoro y’obogima obuya, obomoyo korwa ase omobwekano oyo otari moyo, nigo agosaba obokonyi korwa ase egento eke getabwati bomanyi, ogesaba orogendo oruya egento ekio getanyare kogenda nonya ngake!

English: And for profit in business and good success of his hands, he asks ability from that which has hands with no ability.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo agosaba okonyora okuya korwa ase emeremo yaye, korwa ase egento ekio amaboko aye atabwati nguru chinde!

English: Again, one preparing to sail, and about to journey over raging waves, calls upon a piece of wood more fragile than the vessel that carries him.
Ekegusii: Boigo nabo okonyora omonto otagete korina emeri ase emerindo emenge ogosaba obokonyi korwa ase egetugi ekio getari n’echinguru goetania emeri eria atagete korina!

English: For the hunger for profit planned it, and wisdom was the craftsman who built it.
Ekegusii: Omonto gete nigo aroisetie emeri eyio erio kwenyorera engeria, omoroisia akayeroisia ase obomanyi bwaye.

English: Your providence, O Father, guides it along, because even in the sea you gave a way, and in the waves a sure path,
Ekegusii: Korende aye Omonene oborendi bwao nabwo bokoraa emeri ayio. Ekiagera nonya nyancha aye nigo okoroisia enchera, nonya nase emerindo abanto nigo bagoeta buya;

English: showing that you can save out of every danger, that even a man without skill may put to sea.
Ekegusii: koorokia buna aye nabo ogotooria korwa ase kera ase, nonya n’omonto otabwati obomanyi obwo nabo agotara ase amaache.

English: It is your will that the works of your wisdom should not be ineffective. Therefore men also entrust their lives to a little piece of wood, and passing through the surge on a raft come safely to land.
Ekegusii: Nigo kwarigetie ebinto ebio aye gwatongete bibwenere Mwanyabaanto; abanto nigo bakorora buna nigo bare buya nonya nase ekengese ki’omote, nigo bagotamboka nyancha buya ase ekengese ki’omote na baika ngumbu ende buya.

English: For in the old time also, when proud giants were perishing, the hope of the world, taking refuge on a raft, your hand guided the seed of generations of the race of men.
Ekegusii: Aya naro akorekanete agwo ritangani, ekero amamonto gete amangainereria arenge gosira, omonto oria orenge ogosemeria gw’ense atamete gochia ase obwato inse y’oborai bwao agatigera ense oroiboro ri’ekegori ekeyia.

English: For blessed is wood through which comes righteousness;
Ekegusii: Ogosesenigwa kogacha ase obwato boria bwa Nuhu obwo bwaretete ogotoreka.

English: but the idol made with hands is accursed, itself and he that made it; because his was the working, and the corruptible thing was called a god.
Ekegusii: Korende okoragererigwa kwabeire ase emegwekano eyio eroisirie n’amaboko a Mwanyabaanto; boigo nonya noria oreisirie emegwekano eyio oragererigwe, oyio nigo aragererigwe ase engencho ere aroisirie omobwekano oyio otari na bomoyo bonde naende oyoroka e nyasae.

English: For both the ungodly and his ungodliness are alike hateful to God;
Ekegusii: Nyasae nigo agechete abanyabibe boigo nigo agechete ogokora kwabo.

English: for truly the deed will be punished together with him who committed it.
Ekegusii: Keria kiarosigwe boigo noria okeroisirie mbaegwe egesusuro.

English: Therefore also there will be a visitation among the idols of the nation, because, though formed of things which God created, they were made an abomination, stumbling blocks to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the foolish.
Ekegusii: Emegwekano y’ogosasomwa eyio baria batamomanyeti Nyasae baroisirie neegwe egesusuro, nonya keroisirie korwa ase ebinto ebio Nyasae atongete, yabeire okogechia okonene, na yabeire egetango ase emioyo y’abanto, na yabeire omoeto ase amagoro y’ abanto abariri.

English: For the devising of idols was the beginning of fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life.
Ekegusii: Obonyaka nigo bwachagete ekero emegwekano y’ogosasimwa yachagete koroisigwa. Yaochoganirie ebirengererio bia Mwanyabaanto korwa eroisigwa.

English: For they didn’t exist from the beginning, and they won’t exist forever.
Ekegusii: Mebwekano tiyarengeo korwa kare naende tekobao kare na kare.

English: For by the boastfulness of men they entered into the world, and therefore a speedy end was planned for them.
Ekegusii: Nigo yaretetwe ense goetera ase obwenenu bwa Mwanyabaanto, nakio gekogera omoerio oye obwango mono oroisigwe.

English: For a father worn with untimely grief, making an image of the child quickly taken away, now honored him as a god which was then a dead human being, and delivered to those that were under him mysteries and solemn rites.
Ekegusii: Omogaka oyomo agaichanigwa mono n’ogokwa kwa bwango mono kw’omwana oye, erio agwo akaroisia omobwekano bw’omwana oye oria okwete buna Mwanyabaanto onde bwensi agokwa akamoa amasikani buna Nyasae; erio akaa abanto abwo barenge inse yaye omoroberio bw’ogosasiima omobwekano oyio aroisetie.

English: Afterward the ungodly custom, in process of time grown strong, was kept as a law, and the engraved images received worship by the commandments of princes.
Ekegusii: Magega yaye, ebirengererio ebio ebibe bi’ogosasiima emegwekano bikaba n’echinguru goika bikaba buna ogochika, na emegwekano y’ogosasimwa ekaroisigwa abanto bagachiikwa koyesasiima.

English: And when men could not honor them in presence because they lived far off, imagining the likeness from afar, they made a visible image of the king whom they honored, that by their zeal they might flatter the absent as if present.
Ekegusii: Ekaba buna ekero abanto bamenyete are korwa ase omogambi obo oyio basigete mono, nigo bare korengereria buna ekieni kiaye kere erio baroisia omobwekano oye na koyosasiima nonya kare are nabarabwo goetera ase omobwekano nigo bakorengereria buna nao are ange nabarabwo.

English: But worship was raised to a yet higher pitch, even by those who didn’t know him, urged forward by the ambition of the architect;
Ekegusii: Abaroisia aba b’emegwekano nigo bare koroisia omobwekano omuya mono erio nonya mbaria batamomanyete bakogokigwa nere.

English: for he, wishing perhaps to please his ruler, used his art to force the likeness toward a greater beauty.
Ekegusii: Omoroisia kero kende nabo akogania kogokia abanene baye ase okoroisia omobwekano omuya mono goetania nonya n’omonene oye.

English: So the multitude, allured by reason of the grace of his handiwork, now consider an object of devotion him that a little before was honored as a man.
Ekegusii: Abanto nigo bakogokigwa n’obuya bw’emeremo eyio, erio barora emegwekano eyio koba egento kebwenerete gosasimwa oyio ase ekero egeke basigete buna Mwanyabaanto.

English: And this became an ambush, because men, in bondage either to calamity or to tyranny, invested stones and stocks with the Name that shouldn’t be shared.
Ekegusii: Bono eke nigo gekoba omoeto ogotega abanto, ekiagera ekero abanto bare ase emechando gose ekero omogambi ekogamba n’echinguru ere, nigo akoira ebinto ebio biroisirie korwa ase amagena gose emete obiaa amasikani ayio Nyasae bweka aganeirie koegwa!

English: Afterward it was not enough for them to go astray concerning the knowledge of God, but also, while they live in a great war of ignorance, they call a multitude of evils peace.
Ekegusii: Korende bono amang’ana akaba amabe mono. Bono tiyarenge bobe ase bare gotatwara obomanyi igoro ya Nyasae. Abanto nigo bamenyete ase obobe obonene n’echisegi ase oboriri goika bagakaga nga igo nario bare n’omorembe.

English: For either slaughtering children in solemn rites, or celebrating secret mysteries, or holding frenzied revels of strange customs,
Ekegusii: Bagaita abana baabo ase ebingwanso bia bobisi, bagakora ebinto bi’obobarimo n’amang’ana ande arenge mamincha y’obotongi.

English: no longer do they guard either life or purity of marriage, but one brings upon another either death by treachery, or anguish by adultery.
Ekegusii: Bakeba amagima abo nonya n’echinywomo chiabo tibachisigete. Omonto nigo arenge goita oyonde bosa igo gose omogechia mono ase okorara na mokaye.

English: And all things confusedly are filled with blood and murder, theft and deceit, corruption, faithlessness, tumult, perjury,
Ekegusii: Kera egento gekaba ekebe, abanto bagaitwa bosa igo, oboibi bogaichora, obongainereria, oborianania, obwegenwa bokabora, okoamererania, oborimo,

English: confusion about what is good, forgetfulness of favors, ingratitude for benefits, defiling of souls, confusion of sex, disorder in marriage, adultery and wantonness.
Ekegusii: okorianania baria batabwati komocha, abanto bagatiga goaka mbuya mono, emeburukano ase chinywomo, obonyaka n’obotomani.

English: For the worship of idols that may not be named is a beginning and cause and end of every evil.
Ekegusii: Gosasiima emegwekano eyio nonya n’amarieta abo atari gwatorwa, nakio omochakano, na engencho ya kera obobe.

English: For their worshipers either make merry to madness, or prophesy lies, or live unrighteously, or lightly commit perjury.
Ekegusii: Abanto bagosasiima emegwekano eyio nigo baborirwe obongaini, gose nigo bakobana oborimo, gose bamenya obogima obobe na gotiana oborimo batari korengereria.

English: For putting their trust in lifeless idols, when they have sworn a wicked oath, they expect not to suffer harm.
Ekegusii: Abanto nigo basemeretie emegwekano eyio etari moyo na gotiana ogotiana okobe barengereria buna tibagocha konyora egesusuro.

English: But on both counts, the just doom will pursue them, because they had evil thoughts of God by giving heed to idols, and swore unrighteously in deceit through contempt for holiness.
Ekegusii: Korende goika banyore egesusuro ase chinchera echi ibere: Ritangani nigo bakorete okomocha ekero batigete Nyasae bagachaaka gosasiima emegwekano, eriakabere tibakumeretie obochenu, nigo bare gokwana amang’ana y’oborimo erio kongaina abanto.

English: For it is not the power of things by which men swear, but it is the just penalty for those who sin that always visits the transgression of the unrighteous.
Ekegusii: Ekero abakori amabe bakomocha, nigo baranyore egesusuro tari korwa ase chinguru chi’ ebinto bagotiana, korende korwa ase egesusuro kebatungetie barabwo.

English: But you, our God, are gracious and true, patient, and in mercy ordering all things.
Ekegusii: Korende aye Nyasae oito, n’omoitongo na omonyakeene, aye n’omoremereria na nigo okogambera ebinto bionsi ase amaabera.

English: For even if we sin, we are yours, knowing your dominion; but we will not sin, knowing that we have been accounted yours.
Ekegusii: Nonya togokora ebibe ntomanyete chinguru chiao, intwe n’abanto bao. Titogokora ebibe ekiagera tomanyete buna itwe n’abanto bao.

English: For to be acquainted with you is perfect righteousness, and to know your dominion is the root of immortality.
Ekegusii: Gokomanya aye n’obochenu oboikeranu, komanya chinguru chiao n’omochakano bw’okomenya kare na kare.

English: For we weren’t led astray by any evil plan of men’s, nor yet by painters’ fruitless labor, a form stained with varied colors,
Ekegusii: Intwe titorasirigwa n’emeremo y’oboroisia ya Mwanyabaanto, gose ase gento kende gionsi egesinini ekio giakirwe chirangi ao ao n’omoroisia.

English: the sight of which leads fools into lust. Their desire is for the breathless form of a dead image.
Ekegusii: Ekio gekororekana buya na kongusa abanto abariri batwara okogania ase omobwekano oyio otabwati obomoyo.

English: Lovers of evil things, and worthy of such hopes, are those who make, desire, and worship them.
Ekegusii: Baria bakoroisia ebinto buna ebio, na baria bakorigia kobisasiima bonsi nigo bakoamererania gokora obobe.

English: For a potter, kneading soft earth, laboriously molds each article for our service. He fashions out of the same clay both the vessels that minister to clean uses, and those of a contrary sort, all in like manner. What shall be the use of each article of either sort, the potter is the judge.
Ekegusii: Omoroisia chinyongo nigo agotiringa esike buya erio oroisia ebinto biaye ase obongaini erio itwe twabikorera. Ebinto bionsi nigo akobiroisia korwa ase esike eria eria erio twarora mbiribi bibwenerete ase obokoreri na mbiribi bitabwenereti.

English: Also, laboring to an evil end, he molds a vain god out of the same clay, he who, having but a little before been made of earth, after a short space goes his way to the earth out of which he was taken, when he is required to give back the soul which was lent him.
Ekegusii: Naende ase emeremo ya bosa omoroisia oyo oroisia enyasae korwa ase esike eria eria are koroiseria ebinto binde, omoroisia oria nigo okorire korwa ase riroba buna ebinto biria akoroisia, ere nigo abwate omobere ogokwa, na ekero engaki yaikire yokoirania omoyo oye nigo akoirana gochia ase riroba aria ase aruete.

English: However he has anxious care, not because his powers must fail, nor because his span of life is short; But he compares himself with goldsmiths and silversmiths, and he imitates molders in brass, and considers it great that he molds counterfeit gods.
Ekegusii: Korende ere tari gokumia buna amakweri amobereire ange, gose obogima bwaye n’obwenge; ere nigo akoamererania n’eriroba, n’etaabu ebinto ebio bikorwa ase riroba ere nigo akoroisia emebwekano y’okwegia.

English: His heart is ashes. His hope is of less value than earth. His life is of less honor than clay,
Ekegusii: Enkoro yaye nigo ere ribu na ogosemeria kwaye nigo kore okoreu mono kobua ebuse. Obogima bwaye tibori bw’erigori kobua riroba;

English: because he was ignorant of him who molded him, and of him that inspired into him an active soul, and breathed into him a vital spirit.
Ekegusii: ekiagera ere tanya komanya Nyasae oria omotongete, Nyasae oria omoete obomoyo n’echinguru chi’ogokora ayio onsi.

English: But he accounted our life to be a game, and our lifetime a festival for profit; for, he says, one must get gain however one can, even if it is by evil.
Ekegusii: Omonto oyio nigo akorengereria obogima bwaito koba egento bosa igo, nigo bonga echiiro ase akonyora okonyora. Nigo agoteeba nga mbuya konyora chitaabu ase nchera ende yonsi neba neria etabwenereti.

English: For this man, beyond all others, knows that he sins, out of earthy matter making brittle vessels and engraved images.
Ekegusii: Omonto oyio oyio okoroisia emegwekano korwa ase riroba amo n’ebinto binde ebio bigwateka, nigo amanyete mono goetania abanto bande buna n’ebibe agokora.

English: But most foolish and more miserable than a baby, are the enemies of your people, who oppressed them;
Ekegusii: Korende abariri goetania bonsi na baria barachandeke goetania abana abake n’ababisa baria bachandete abanto bao.

English: because they even considered all the idols of the nations to be gods, which have neither the use of eyes for seeing, nor nostrils for drawing breath, nor ears to hear, nor fingers for handling, and their feet are helpless for walking.
Ekegusii: Barabwo nigo bakagete buna emegwekano y’abanto batamomanyeti Nyasae n’chinyasae, nonya ero tebwati maiso ekororera gose chimioro ekoeyanera, gose amato ekoigwera gose ebiara ekobwatera, n’amagoro abo takonyara gotara.

English: For a man made them, and one whose own spirit is borrowed molded them; for no one has power as a man to mold a god like himself.
Ekegusii: Mwanyabaanto nere omoroisia obo, omonto oyio obwate obomoyo botari obwaye nere oroisetie emegwekano eyio. Onde taiyo oranyare koroisia enyasae ere engiya goetania Mwanyabaanto.

English: But, being mortal, he makes a dead thing by the work of lawless hands; for he is better than the objects of his worship, since he indeed had life, but they never did.
Ekegusii: Kera omonto goika akwe korende kende gionsi ere akoroisia nigo gekwete korwa omochakano. Ere nigo are buya kobua egento ekio agosasiima. Ere ekeene nigo are moyo, korende keria agosasiima tikeri moyo naende tigekoba moyo riinde.

English: Yes, and they worship the creatures that are most hateful, for, being compared as to lack of sense, these are worse than all others;
Ekegusii: Abanto abwo nigo bagosasiima nonya n’echingiti chinde chi’ogokumia chindiri goetania ebitongwa binde.

English: Neither, as seen beside other creatures, are they beautiful, so that one should desire them, but they have escaped both the praise of God and his blessing.
Ekegusii: Ekero ogochirengania n’ebitongwa binde, chirochio tichiri kogokia nonya ngake. Chirochio tichianya konyora ogotogigwa korwa ase Nyasae.

English: For this cause, they were deservedly punished through creatures like those which they worship, and tormented through a multitude of vermin.
Ekegusii: Ase igo, abanto abwo bakanyora egesusuro korwa ase ebitongwa ebio ebio buna yaganeirie; bagachandwa korwa ase ekeombe ki’ebitongwa ebio.

English: Instead of this punishment, you, giving benefits to your people, prepared quails for food, a delicacy to satisfy the desire of their appetite,
Ekegusii: Korende aye Omonene ribaga ri’okoa abanto abwo egesusuro okabarorera amaabera. Aye okabanchera bakaria endagera y’ense engeni yarenge enyansu erio goisanekia okogania kwabo.

English: to the end that your enemies, desiring food, might for the hideousness of the creatures sent among them, loathe even the necessary appetite; but these, your people, having for a short time suffered lack, might even partake of delicacies.
Ekegusii: Nigo gwakorete igo erio abanto baria bare gosasiima emegwekano ekero baraigwe enchara basirie okogania gw’okoria endagera ase engencho y’ebitongwa biria bikogechia ebio baireretwe. Korende abanto bao nigo baigwete enchara ase ekero egeke erio magega yaye bakanyora endagera eria yare gwansa mono.

English: For it was necessary that inescapable lack should come upon those oppressors, but that to these it should only be showed how their enemies were tormented.
Ekegusii: Nigo yabwenerete abachandi baria b’abaanto bao bachandeke ase okoborwa ebinto biria baganeti ase obogima bwabo, korende abanto bao bakerorera buna ababisa babo bare gochandwa.

English: For even when terrible raging of wild beasts came upon your people, and they were perishing by the bites of crooked serpents, your wrath didn’t continue to the uttermost;
Ekegusii: Ekero ching’iti chiria chiare koondokia chiarenge n’esumo chiaborete abanto bao chibaite bakwe, aye tikwagendererete kogechigwa goika omoerio.

English: but for admonition were they troubled for a short time, having a token of salvation to put them in remembrance of the commandment of your law;
Ekegusii: Nigo bachandetwe ase ekero egeke erio kebe ekiorokererio ase bare. Erio aye okabaa ekemanyererio gi’okobagwenia, erio obainyorie okogania kw’amachiiko ao.

English: for he who turned toward it was not saved because of that which was seen, but because of you, the Savior of all.
Ekegusii: Onde bwensi ore korigereria ekemanyererio ekio kwabaete nigo are kogwena, eki kwamogwenia tari ekemanyererio keria korende naye omotoria obonsi.

English: Yes, and in this you persuaded our enemies that you are he who delivers out of every evil.
Ekegusii: Ase ogokora igo nigo kwaenekeretie ababisa baito buna aye naye ogotoria abanto korwa ase kebe kende gionsi.

English: For the bites of locusts and flies truly killed them. No healing for their life was found, because they were worthy to be punished by such things.
Ekegusii: Ababisa baito nigo bakwete ase okoromwa n’echingige n’echingi, na nchera ende yonsi y’okobatoria tiyarenge oo, ase engencho mbagwenerete koegwa egesusuro n’ebitongwa ebio.

English: But your children weren’t overcome by the very fangs of venomous dragons, for your mercy passed by where they were and healed them.
Ekegusii: Korende nonya n’echingiti chiria chiabwate esumo tichianyarete gosiria abanto bao, ekiagera aye nigo gwachete n’amaabera okabagwenia.

English: For they were bitten to put them in remembrance of your oracles, and were quickly saved, lest, falling into deep forgetfulness, they should become unable to respond to your kindness.
Ekegusii: Nigo barometwe n’echingiti erio bainyore amachiiko ao, korende bagatorigwa bwango erio tibakweba, na babe aboro ase okomanya obuya bwao.

English: For truly it was neither herb nor poultice that cured them, but your word, O Lord, which heals all people.
Ekegusii: Riogo rinde tiriyo riabagwenetie, korende goetera ase ring’ana riao rioka, aye Omonene abanto bao bakagwena.

English: For you have authority over life and death, and you lead down to the gates of Hades, and lead up again.
Ekegusii: Aye nobwate okobua igoro y’obogima n’ogokwa; aye nigo ogotirimbokia abanto goika ogokwa naende kwabairania.

English: But though a man kills by his wickedness, he can’t retrieve the spirit that has departed or release the imprisoned soul.
Ekegusii: Omonto omobe nabo agoita oyonde, korende ere takoirania oria okwa abe moyo, gose takonyara gotoria enkoro esibire ase ogokwa.

English: But it is not possible to escape your hand;
Ekegusii: Monto onde taiyo oranyare gotama korwa ase ore.

English: for ungodly men, refusing to know you, were scourged in the strength of your arm, pursued with strange rains and hails and relentless storms, and utterly consumed with fire.
Ekegusii: Abanyabibe baria nigo bangete gokomanya, okabasusura n’echinguru chi’okoboko kwao. Bakairwa n’emerindo emenene, n’embura y’amagena, n’echinkoba chitari gosira na gosirigwa n’omorero.

English: For, what was most marvelous, in the water which quenches all things, the fire burned hotter; for the world fights for the righteous.
Ekegusii: Ogokumia nkoria nga amache ayio akageire korimia omorero, tanyarete korimia, omorero oyio nigo bwogete ase chinguru mono ekiagera chinguru chi’ebitongwa chionsi nigo chikorwana erio gotoria abachenu.

English: For at one time the flame was restrained, that it might not burn up the creatures sent against the ungodly, but that these themselves as they looked might see that they were chased by the judgment of God.
Ekegusii: Ase chingaki gete, omorero oria ogasiria chinguru chiaye erio tosiria ebitongwa ebio biaretetwe erio koa abanyabibe egesusuro erio abanto abwo barore na komanya nga endamwamu yao nigo yababwatetie.

English: At another time even in the midst of water it burns more intensely than fire, that it may destroy the produce of an unrighteous land.
Ekegusii: Korende naende ase chingaki gete omorero oria ogoka mono okoba omotindi goetania omorero bw’amache, ogasiria ense eria abanyabibe abwo bamenyete.

English: Instead of these things, you gave your people angels’ food to eat, and you provided ready-to-eat bread for them from heaven without toil, having the virtue of every pleasant flavor, and agreeable to every taste.
Ekegusii: Korende amaakwa aya onsi tanyorete banto bao, aye nigo kwabaete endagera y’amalaika; nigo kwabaiyereretie emegati korwa igoro, emogati eyio nigo yare goisanekia kera oyomo.

English: For your nature showed your sweetness toward your children, while that bread, serving the desire of the eater, changed itself according to every man’s choice.
Ekegusii: Endagera yao nigo yaorogetie buna aye bwanchete abana bao. Endagera eyio nigo yaisanegetie enchara ya kera oyomo oyio oyeriete; endagera eyio nigo yaroisetigwe etaganetie onde ayeroisie naende.

English: But snow and ice endured fire, and didn’t melt, that people might know that fire was destroying the fruits of the enemies, burning in the hail and flashing in the rains;
Ekegusii: Endagera eyio nigo yanga buna amagena y’embura korende tiyare kobera esire; eke nigo kiagerete abanto bao komonya nga omorero oria na embura y’amagena ebio biasiretie ababisa babo ase chingaki echio;

English: and that this fire, again, in order that righteous people may be nourished, has even forgotten its own power.
Ekegusii: nigo obisete chinguru chiaye erio abanto bao banyore endagera.

English: For the creation, ministering to you, its maker, strains its force against the unrighteous for punishment and in kindness, slackens it on behalf of those who trust in you.
Ekegusii: Ense nigo yatongetwe inse y’erichiiko riao, na ebitongwa bionsi nigo bikogenda ase chinguru chiao na koa abanyabibe egesusuro; korende biabisa chinguru chiabo erio kobaisanekia baria bagosemeretie.

English: Therefore at that time also, converting itself into all forms, it ministered to your all-nourishing bounty, according to the desire of those who had need,
Ekegusii: Ase igo chingaki chiria ense nigo yaonchoreretie ase chingencho chinyinge erio kw’orokia buna ogoisanekia ase obwororo okogania kwa baria bonsi bakogosaba.

English: that your children, whom you loved, O Lord, might learn that it is not the growth of crops that nourishes a man, but that your word preserves those who trust you.
Ekegusii: Aya nigo akoregete erio abana bao abwo bwanchete aye Omonene bamanye buna aye tori gokirigwa ase ebimeri biria togosimeka, korende ring’ana riao nario rikorenda baria bagosemeretie.

English: For that which was not destroyed by fire, melted away when it was simply warmed by a faint sunbeam,
Ekegusii: Endagera eria etare gosarigwa n’omorero nigo yare kobera ekero omobaso ochakire kobara mambia.

English: that it might be known that we must rise before the sun to give you thanks, and must pray to you at the dawning of the light;
Ekegusii: Ekio nigo kogotoegeria buna ntobwenerete koboka mambia na gokoiraneria mbuya mono boigo na kogotogia ekero risare rikorimera.

English: for the hope of the unthankful will melt as the winter’s hoar frost, and will flow away as water that has no use.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera ogosemeria kw’omonto otari koiraneria mbuya mono nigo kogosira buna ritaturi, nigo kogosira buna amache atari n’engencho ende.

English: For your judgments are great, and hard to interpret; therefore undisciplined souls went astray.
Ekegusii: Aye Omonene emeroberio yao nigo ere ayaboronge; nakio gekogera baria batatageti korongeigwa basirire

English: For when lawless men had supposed that they held a holy nation in their power, they, prisoners of darkness, and bound in the fetters of a long night, kept close beneath their roofs, lay exiled from the eternal providence.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera ekero abanto ababe bakagete buna bairire ense yao ebe inse y’okobua kwabo, barabwo abanyene nigo basibetwe ase obotuko bware n’omosunte omonene, nigo batigarete ase chinyomba chiabo ase batare n’oborendi bwao bwa botambe.

English: For while they thought that they were unseen in their secret sins, they were divided from one another by a dark curtain of forgetfulness, stricken with terrible awe, and very troubled by apparitions.
Ekegusii: Nigo bakagete buna ebibe biabo nigo biare ebiabobisi bitakeire koorokigwa, nigo biatakeire kobiswa na gokunekwa n’egetambaa ekemwamu gi’okweba; korende bono barabwo bakanyorwa n’obwoba bw’okoondokia, bakoboa na gosebererekana ekero baroche riringori.

English: For neither did the dark recesses that held them guard them from fears, but terrifying sounds rang around them, and dismal phantoms appeared with unsmiling faces.
Ekegusii: Nonya n’echinyomba chiabo ase bamenyete tichiabatangete korwa ase obwoba. Nigo baetananetwe n’amariogi y’okondokia; ekababera chingaki chi’ogoichana na kogechigwa.

English: And no power of fire prevailed to give light, neither were the brightest flames of the stars strong enough to illuminate that gloomy night;
Ekegusii: Morero toiyo obwate chinguru chi’okobamorekera, gose engenangeni eria ekobara mono tiyare konyara komoreka omosunte oria bw’amakweri.

English: but only the glimmering of a self-kindled fire appeared to them, full of fear. In terror, they considered the things which they saw to be worse than that sight, on which they could not gaze.
Ekegusii: Bakaorokerwa n’omorero bw’ogokumia oyio bwogetigwe na Mwanyabaanto okabamorekera, na ase obwoba bwabo bakegena buna ayio barorire nigo are ay’okondokia mono kobua aria konya barorire.

English: The mockeries of their magic arts were powerless, now, and a shameful rebuke of their boasted understanding:
Ekegusii: Amang’ana aria konya bakorire ase oborogi bwabo akabugwa na obongaini bwabo bwonsi bogasokigwa.

English: For those who promised to drive away terrors and disorders from a sick soul, these were sick with a ludicrous fearfulness.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera baria bakagerete buna mbaserie obwoba korwa ase omorwaire, barabwo abanyene bakarwara ase obwoba bw’ogosekereria.

English: For even if no troubling thing frighted them, yet, scared with the creeping of vermin and hissing of serpents,
Ekegusii: Nonya nekero gento gi’okondokia getarenge oo, barabwo nigo barenge n’obwoba ase eriogi ri’echingiti n’ebitongwa biria biare kwagura.

English: they perished trembling in fear, refusing even to look at the air, which could not be escaped on any side.
Ekegusii: Bagasirigwa ase ogotengechigwa kw’obwoba, bakanga nonya nkorigereria igoro ase batare konyara gwetanga.

English: For wickedness, condemned by a witness within, is a coward thing, and, being pressed hard by conscience, always has added forecasts of the worst.
Ekegusii: Omochakano bw’obwoba n’okoiroka, na nigo bogweonchora bwoka obonyene. Onde bwensi okorire okomocha nigo akorora mono aria amabe goetania amaya.

English: For fear is nothing else but a surrender of the help which reason offers;
Ekegusii: Obwoba n’ogosiria ogosemeria okwo gokoretwa n’ebirengererio ebiya.

English: and from within, the expectation of being less prefers ignorance of the cause that brings the torment.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto agosiria ogosemeria kw’omoyo, nigo agosogwa n’obwoba obwo bokoretwa n’oboriri.

English: But they, all through the night which was powerless indeed, and which came upon them out of the recesses of powerless Hades, sleeping the same sleep,
Ekegusii: Obotuko bwonsi abanto abwo nigo bakorara batari gotimoka, nonya obotuko boria tibwabwate nguru chinde ase bare, ekiagera nigo bwaruete korwa ase ense y’abakuure agwo ase nguru chinde chitari.

English: now were haunted by monstrous apparitions, and now were paralyzed by their soul’s surrendering; for sudden and unexpected fear came upon them.
Ekegusii: Kero kende nigo baseretigwe n’emerengari y’okwoboyia bagatigara batari na nguru chinde ekiagera obwoba obonene bwabasoete.

English: So then whoever it might be, sinking down in his place, was kept captive, shut up in that prison which was not barred with iron;
Ekegusii: Ase igo monto onde bwensi orenge oo nigo asoetwe n’obwoba, akaba gasibire ase chinyororo chi’obwoba bwabo abanyene.
