English: for whether he was a farmer, or a shepherd, or a laborer whose toils were in the wilderness, he was overtaken, and endured that inescapable sentence; for they were all bound with one chain of darkness.
Ekegusii: Abaremi, abarisia n’abakori emeremo abwo bare gokora emeremo ase ebitunwa bonsi nigo basoetwe n’emechando eyio eyio batare konyara gwetanga, ekiagera bonsi nigo basibetwe chinyororo chiria chi’omosunte.

English: Whether there was a whistling wind, or a melodious sound of birds among the spreading branches, or a measured fall of water running violently,
Ekegusii: Kera ekero bare koigwa embeo ekogusa, gose eriogi ri’ororo ri’echinyoni chire ase chinsagia chi’emete, gose eriogi ri’amache agotirimboka bwango,

English: or a harsh crashing of rocks hurled down, or the swift course of animals bounding along unseen, or the voice of wild beasts harshly roaring, or an echo rebounding from the hollows of the mountains, all these things paralyzed them with terror.
Ekegusii: gose eriogi ri’ebitunwa bikogwa, gose eriogi ri’ebitongwa bikoiruruka na kominyoka, gose eriogi ri’echingiti chikwana ase obotindi, gose eriogi korwa ase ebitunwa, barabwo nigo bare gwaka inse ase obwoba.

English: For the whole world was illuminated with clear light, and was occupied with unhindered works,
Ekegusii: Ense yonsi nigo yamoregetwe n’omobaso na abanto nigo bagendererete gokora emeremo yabo ya kera rituko batari na bwoba bonde.

English: while over them alone was spread a heavy night, an image of the darkness that should afterward receive them; but to themselves, they were heavier than darkness.
Ekegusii: Mbarabwo boka batubetwe n’obotuko obwo bware obonene, omobwekano bw’mosunte oria bw’amakweri oria obaganyete; korende bakaba egurube endito ase barabwo abanyene goetania nonya n’omosunte oria.

English: But for your holy ones there was great light. Their enemies, hearing their voice but not seeing their form, counted it a happy thing that they too had suffered,
Ekegusii: Korende oborabu obonene bokabarabera abanto bao abachenu. Ababisa babo bakaigwa eriogi riabo korende tibanyarete kobarora; bakarora buna abanto bao bare n’egesio ekiagera barabwo tibachandegete.

English: yet for that they do not hurt them, though wronged by them before, they are thankful; and because they had been at variance with them, they begged for pardon.
Ekegusii: Ababisa abwo bakarora buya mono ekiagera abanto abwo bachandete agwo magega tibaakanete gesiomba, ase igo bakabasorora bagende.

English: Therefore you provided a burning pillar of fire, to be a guide for your people’s unknown journey, and a harmless sun for their glorious exile.
Ekegusii: Erio okaa abanto bao oborabu bware kobaraa ase oregendo ase enchera batamanyete, oborabu obwororo ase orogendo orochenu.

English: For the Egyptians well deserved to be deprived of light and imprisoned by darkness, they who had imprisoned your children, through whom the incorruptible light of the law was to be given to the race of men.
Ekegusii: Korende ababisa babo bakarinwa oborabu obwo, ekabagwenera gosibwa ase omosunte abwo konya basibire abanto bao, abwo goetera ase bare ense yonsi yarenge gocha koegwa oborabu bwa kare na kare bwa amachiiko ao.

English: After they had taken counsel to kill the babes of the holy ones, and when a single child had been abandoned and saved to convict them of their sin, you took away from them their multitude of children, and destroyed all their army together in a mighty flood.
Ekegusii: Ekero ababisa abwo baimogete goita abana abake b’abaanto bao, na omwana oria onde omoke otigetwe na gotorigwa, aye nigo kwabaete egesusuro ogoita abana babo abange, na okabasiria bonsi ase amache.

English: Our fathers were made aware of that night beforehand, that, having sure knowledge, they might be cheered by the oaths which they had trusted.
Ekegusii: Korende chisokoro chiaito konya chiamanyigwe igoro y’obotuko boria na ayare gocha gokoreka erio batware omoyo na kogokera chiira chiria baetwe.

English: Salvation of the righteous and destruction of the enemies was expected by your people.
Ekegusii: Abanto bao nigo bamanyete buna aye nigo kware gocha gotoria egesaku egechoore na gosiria ababisa babo.

English: For as you took vengeance on the adversaries, by the same means, calling us to yourself, you glorified us.
Ekegusii: Ase egekorwa ekio ekio gi’okoa ababisa baito egesusuro agatoa amasikani amanene ase ogotorangeria gocha asore.

English: For holy children of good men offered sacrifice in secret, and with one consent they agreed to the covenant of the divine law, that they would partake alike in the same good things and the same perils, the fathers already leading the sacred songs of praise.
Ekegusii: Ase obobisi abanto abwo abaya b’egesaku ekio egechore bakarwa ekengwanso na ase omoyo bw’okwerwa bakabwatia amachiiko a Nyasae abanto abachenu bakabwatana nabwo: Ase ogosesenigwa gose obobe bakaba ang’e bagateera bagotogia chisokoro chiabo.

English: But the discordant cry of the enemies echoed back, and a pitiful voice of lamentation for children was spread abroad.
Ekegusii: Korende eriogi ri’ababisa babo rikaigwekana kera ase bakorera abana babo abwo bakwete.

English: Both servant and master were punished with the same just doom, and the commoner suffering the same as king;
Ekegusii: Abasomba nigo banyorete egesusuro keria keria abanene babo banyorete; boigo n’abanto bande bonsi bakanyora ogosaria koria abarwoti banyorete.

English: Yes, they all together, under one form of death, had corpses without number. For the living were not sufficient even to bury them, Since at a single stroke, their most cherished offspring was consumed.
Ekegusii: Bonsi nigo bakwete ase enchera eria eria; emebere y’abakwete ekaba emenge mono na baria barenge moyo tibaisaine koyetindeka. Ase ogoakwa okomo abana baabo abwo banchente mono bagakwa.

English: For while they were disbelieving all things by reason of the enchantments, upon the destruction of the firstborn they confessed the people to be God’s children.
Ekegusii: Abanto abwo tibaigwerete ogokuurerwa nigo begenete oborogi bwabo. Korende ekero abana babo abatangi basiretigwe, bakamanya nga ekeene abanto abwo na ba Nyasae.

English: For while peaceful silence wrapped all things, and night in her own swiftness was half spent,
Ekegusii: Kera egento nigo kiare buya mono na konya bwabeire botuko gati,

English: your all-powerful word leaped from heaven, from the royal throne, a stern warrior, into the midst of the doomed land,
Ekegusii: ring’ana riao ri’echinguru chinene rigaika korwa igoro ase ekerogo kiao ki’amaabera, rire buna omonto omoremu bw’esegi, rigaikera ense eyio konya yanacheirwe ekiina gosirigwa,

English: bearing as a sharp sword your authentic commandment, and standing, it filled all things with death, and while it touched the sky it stood upon the earth.
Ekegusii: aimogeti omoro omwoge bwogoikerania ogochika kwao. Agatenena na amagoro aye nigo arenge inse na omontwe nigo oigete igoro ase amare, agaichoria ense yonsi n’ogokwa.

English: Then immediately apparitions in dreams terribly troubled them, and unexpected fears came upon them.
Ekegusii: Ase chingaki echio abanto abwo barenge ange n’ogokwa bagaichorwa n’echindoto chi’okoondokia.

English: And each, one thrown here half dead, another there, made known why he was dying;
Ekegusii: Bakarara inse kera aase barenge ang’e n’ogokwa na bakaorokia eki gekogera bakwe.

English: for the dreams, disturbing them, forewarned them of this, that they might not perish without knowing why they were afflicted.
Ekegusii: Chindoto chiabo chi’okoondokia chikabaorokia engencho y’ogokwa kwabo erio tibakwa batamanyeti engencho y’ogokwa kwabo.

English: The experience of death also touched the righteous, and a multitude were destroyed in the wilderness, but the wrath didn’t last long.
Ekegusii: Amakweri boigo agachera egesaku egechore, amarwaire amabe akabachera ekero barenge ase erooro, korende endamwamu yao ekaba eyegeka egeke.

English: For a blameless man hurried to be their champion, bringing the weapon of his own ministry, prayer, and the atoning sacrifice of incense. He withstood the indignation and set an end to the calamity, showing that he was your servant.
Ekegusii: Omonto oyomo oyio otarenge na komocha akabasabera. Ere akaba buna Omokuani obo akabasabera na akarua ekengwanso ki’ogosambwa erio akababwatania naye na akabaorokeria buna ere n’omosomba oo.

English: And he overcame the anger, not by strength of body, not by force of weapons, but by his word, he subdued the avenger by bringing to remembrance oaths and covenants made with the fathers.
Ekegusii: Ase enchera y’amasabo ere akabua obobe boria na kobainyoria chiira chiria kwarierete chisokoro chiaito.

English: For when the dead had already fallen in heaps one upon another, he intervened and stopped the wrath, and cut off its way to the living.
Ekegusii: Bono ekero emebere y’abakwete yaichorete inse, ere agasoa gati agakendia endamwamu yao erio tebanyora baria barenge moyo.

English: For the whole world was pictured on his long robe, and the glories of the fathers were upon the engraving of the four rows of precious stones, and your majesty was upon the diadem on his head.
Ekegusii: Nigo abegete eyanga entambe yachorire ekemanyererio gi’ense, na ase egekuba kiaye nigo abegete ekemanyererio gie’chisokoro chiaito ekio kiaroisirie n’amagena ane, na ase omotwe oye nigo abegete egobia eyio yarenge kw’orokia emiaka yabo.

English: The destroyer yielded to these, and they feared; for it was enough only to test the wrath.
Ekegusii: Omosaria oria oirogete aya, agasiria ogosemeria. Nigo kwabaorogeti endamwamu yao ake igo korende ekabaisana.

English: But indignation without mercy came upon the ungodly to the end; for God also foreknew their future,
Ekegusii: Endamwamu yao etari na moerio ekagenderera gochera abanyabibe goika omoerio. Aye nigo kwamanyete eki bare gochia gokora magega bataragekora.

English: how, having changed their minds to let your people go, and having sped them eagerly on their way, they would change their minds and pursue them.
Ekegusii: Nigo kwamanyete buna magega kwabancheire abanto bao bagende sobo, na nonya magega kwabayereirie ase orogendo rwabo, barabwo goika bare goonchoreria ebirengererio biabo bababwatie.

English: For while they were yet in the midst of their mourning, and lamenting at the graves of the dead, they made another foolish decision, and pursued as fugitives those whom they had begged to leave and driven out.
Ekegusii: Ekeene nonya konya tibaratiga korera ase engencho y’ogokwa kw’abaanto babo abwo bakwete, barabwo bagachora gokora ring’ana ri’oboriri mono; nigo babwatetie abwo konya babasoroire babatige bagende.

English: For the doom which they deserved was drawing them to this end, and it made them forget the things that had happened to them, that they might fill up the punishment which was yet lacking from their torments,
Ekegusii: Egesusuro keria baganeirie gekabaraa goikera agwo, goika bakeba ayio abanyorete; erio igoro ase emechando yabo bakamenta egesusuro ekio kiaborete.

English: and that your people might journey on by a marvelous road, but they themselves might find a strange death.
Ekegusii: Ekero abanto bao bagendererete ase orogendo rwabo ri’ogokumia ababisa abwo nigo baboeretwe n’amakweri y’okondokia.

English: For the whole creation, each part in its diverse kind, was made new again, complying with your commandments, that your servants might be kept unharmed.
Ekegusii: Ebitongwa bionsi nigo biakoretwe oboyia, korengana n’amachiiko ao, erio abanto bao tibachaywa.

English: Then the cloud that overshadowed the camp was seen, and dry land rising up out of what had been water, out of the Red sea an unhindered highway, and a grassy plain out of the violent surge,
Ekegusii: Igoro nigo yabakengete n’ekiiriri, na amaache agakama korwa roche erio bagatara ense enyomo, y’obonyansi bokaama gati y’emerindo y’enyancha, bakanyora enchera ase bagoeta.

English: by which they passed over with all their army, these who were covered with your hand, having seen strange marvels.
Ekegusii: Abanto bao bagatamboka bakoragwa n’okoboko kwao magega kobarorire ebikone ebio kwabakorerete.

English: For like horses they roamed at large, and they skipped about like lambs, praising you, O Lord, who was their deliverer.
Ekegusii: Bagaetaetanana buna chibarasi na gotuma tuma buna chimanwa ch’echingondi bakogotogia aye Omonene kwabatoretie.

English: For they still remembered the things that happened in the time of their sojourning, how instead of bearing cattle, the land brought forth lice, and instead of fish, the river spewed out a multitude of frogs.
Ekegusii: Chingaki echio bakainyora aria abanyorete ekoro barenge ase ense y’obosomba: ense eria egaichorwa n’echinda ribaga ri’echiombe, n’echindoche chigaichorwa n’ebioto ribaga ri’echinswe.

English: But afterwards, they also saw a new kind of birds, when, led on by desire, they asked for luxurious dainties;
Ekegusii: Omoerio bakarora chinyoni chingeni.

English: for, to comfort them, quails came up for them from the sea.
Ekegusii: Ekero baganetie endagera egwansa mono, bakaegwa chikware korwa roche echio bariete buna endagera.

English: Punishments came upon the sinners, not without the signs that were given beforehand by the violence of the thunder, for they justly suffered through their own wickednesses, for the hatred which they practiced toward guests was grievous indeed.
Ekegusii: Korende abanyabibe baria bakanyora egesusuro, magega ko bakuureretwe n’echinguru chi’echinkoba; nigo banyorete emechando eyio baganeirie ase engencho y’obobe bwabo. Nigo bangete abanto bao na bakabakorera bobe goetania ’nse ende yonsi.

English: For while the others didn’t receive the strangers when they came to them, the Egyptians made slaves of guests who were their benefactors.
Ekegusii: Abande nigo bangete kwarigania abageni ase chinka chiabo, korende abanto aba bagakora abageni aba koba abasomba babo; abageni abwo agwo magega barenge abaya ase bare.

English: And not only so, but while punishment of some sort will come upon the former, since they received as enemies those who were aliens;
Ekegusii: Ense ende yonsi etari kwarigania abageni nenyore egesususro,

English: because these first welcomed with feastings, and then afflicted with dreadful toils, those who had already shared with them in the same rights.
Ekegusii: korende abamisiri aba barabwo nigo baariganetie abanto bao agwo ritangani ase omogooko na bakabakorera buya buna abanyene ense aria, na magega yaye bakabaonchokera bagachaaka kobachanda.

English: And moreover they were stricken with loss of sight (even as were those others at the righteous man’s doors), when, being surrounded with yawning darkness, they each looked for the passage through his own door.
Ekegusii: Abanto aba nabarabwo bakanyora ogoakwa bakaba emeuko buna baria ba Sodomu ase egesieri ki’oria omochandi. Bagacherwa n’omosunte omonene, erio kera omonto agachaaka korigia enchera ase egesieri kiaye.

English: For as the notes of a lute vary the character of the rhythm, even so the elements, changing their order one with another, continuing always in its sound, as may clearly be conjectured from the sight of the things that have happened.
Ekegusii: Obokano nigo bobwate chiusi ao ao na kera eusi nigo ebwate eriogi riaye, na eriogi erimo nabo rikobekwa n’erinde erio eriogi rinde risoka. Igo nabo yabete engaki eria ekero ebitongwa biasoete ase omochogano rigereria buna biabete:

English: For creatures of the dry land were turned into creatures of the waters, and creatures that swim moved upon the land.
Ekegusii: ebitongwa bi’ense enyomo bigaochoka bikaba ebi’amache, na biria bi’amache bigata ase ense enyomo.

English: Fire kept the mastery of its own power in water, and water forgot its quenching nature.
Ekegusii: Omorero okagenderera gwoka nonya nase amache, amache nigo ebete emeremo yaye y’okorimia omorero.

English: On the contrary, flames didn’t consume flesh of perishable creatures that walked among them, neither did they melt the crystalline grains of ambrosial food that were melted easily.
Ekegusii: Nonya nigo omorero oria tonyarete gosiria ching’iti chiria chigosira echio chiarenge gotara gati gati y’omorero, gose tonyarete gosaria endagera eria ya igoro eyio yabwekaine amagena embura.

English: For in all things, O Lord, you magnified your people, and you glorified them and didn’t lightly regard them, standing by their side in every time and place.
Ekegusii: Aye Omonene nigo okorenda na gotogia abanto bao ase kera enchera, gose tigwatigete kobarenda as’engaki ende yonsi gose ande onsi.

English: All wisdom comes from the Lord, and is with him forever.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini bwonsi nigo bokorwa ase Omonene, nigo bore ase are kare na kare.

English: Who can count the sand of the seas, the drops of rain, and the days of eternity?
Ekegusii: Niing’o oranyare kobara omochanga o nyancha, gose chintonyi chi’embura? Niing’o oranyare kobara amatuko a kare na kare?

English: Who will search out the height of the sky, the breadth of the earth, the deep, and wisdom?
Ekegusii: Inee, mboare ki bore korwa ase ense gochia igoro? Inee, obogare bw’ense ng’aki bong’ana? Obotambe bw’Enyancha ng’aki bong’ana? Niing’o omanyete okomanya kw’obong’aini? Ningo orairanerie amaborio aya?

English: Wisdom has been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from everlasting.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini nigo bwatongetwe gento kende gionsi konya getaratongwa, na okomanya nao kwarenge korwa kare.

English: To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed? Who has known her shrewd counsels?
Ekegusii: Niing’o bw’orogetigwe oboroso bw’obong’aini? Niing’o oranyare chisemi chi’obong’aini?

English: There is one wise, greatly to be feared, sitting upon his throne: the Lord.
Ekegusii: Niing’o bworokererigwe oboroso bwe chisemi? Niing’o omanyete chimbachero chi’echisemi.

English: He created her. He saw and measured her. He poured her out upon all his works.
Ekegusii: Noyomo bweka obwate chisemi na nigo akairansete ase ekerogo kiaye kiobonene nere Omonene

English: She is with all flesh according to his gift. He gave her freely to those who love him.
Ekegusii: Nyasae omonyene nere omotongete obong’aini; ere nere omoroche na komorenga, naende omoikerania ase chigasi chiaye chionsi.

English: The fear of the Lord is glory, exultation, gladness, and a crown of rejoicing.
Ekegusii: Chisemi igo are gati-gati ya kera egetongwa; Nyasae nigo akomoitororera chisemi omonto oyo anchete.

English: The fear of the Lord will delight the heart, and will give gladness, joy, and length of days.
Ekegusii: Okomoiroka Nyasae nigo gokorenta ogwetogia n’amasikani, nigo gokorenta egutwa y’omogooko.

English: Whoever fears the Lord, it will go well with him at the last. He will be blessed in the day of his death.
Ekegusii: Komoiroka Nyasae n’okogokia omoyo, nigo gokorenta omogooko korwa enkoro, na komenta obogima komenya chingaki chintambe.

English: To fear the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. It was created together with the faithful in the womb.
Ekegusii: Oyomomanyete Nyasae, oyio kaa nasesenigwe, engaki yaye y’ogokwa omonto oyio nasesenigwe.

English: She laid an eternal foundation with men. She will be trusted among their offspring.
Ekegusii: Okomomanya Nyasae noro omochakano bwe chisemi, chisemi nigo atongetwe n’obwegenwa korwa ase enda yang’ina.

English: To fear the Lord is the fullness of wisdom. She inebriates men with her fruits.
Ekegusii: Chisemi bwebekeire oboroso bwa kare na kare gati y’abanto n’ororeria rogochia gocha ndokiine ase chisemi.

English: She will fill all her house with desirable things, and her storehouses with her produce.
Ekegusii: Okomomanya Nyasae obwo n’oboikeranu, Chisemi nigo akobaikerania abanto ase rigesa riaye.

English: The fear of the Lord is the crown of wisdom, making peace and perfect health to flourish.
Ekegusii: Chisemi nigo agoichoria chinyomba chiabo n’ebinto bionsi abanyene enyomba baganetie ase ebiage n’amarongo abo ase rigesa riaye.

English: He both saw and measured her. He rained down skill and knowledge of understanding, and exalted the honor of those who hold her fast.
Ekegusii: Okomwancha Nyasae nigo enga buna okobekerwa engobo y’echisemi, n’echisemi nigo akorenta omorembe amo n’obogima obuya bw’omobere.

English: To fear the Lord is the root of wisdom. Her branches are length of days.
Ekegusii: Nyasae nigo amoroche chisemi na komorenga, agatwa buna embura na kworokia ense n’obong’ani amo n’okomanya, na kobaa omogooko baria bagosanga amo nere.

English: Unjust wrath can never be justified, for his wrath tips the scale to his downfall.
Ekegusii: Okomomanya Nyasae n’oboroso bwe chisemi, n’echinsagia chiaye nigo chire n’obogima obotambe.

English: A man that is patient will resist for a season, and afterward gladness will spring up to him.
Ekegusii: Okobwatwa n’obororo tiyancheiri, ekiagera obororo nigo bokorenta ogosirigwa kw’omonto.

English: He will hide his words until the right moment, and the lips of many will tell of his understanding.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoremereria nigo akoganya egento goika engaki egwenerete, erio omoerio oye omonto oyio nigo omogooko okomochera buna ensoko.

English: A wise saying is in the treasures of wisdom; but godliness is an abomination to a sinner.
Ekegusii: Omonto oyio nigo agotanga amang’ana are gochia komonyora goika engaki egwenerete, erio nario abanto abange baratogie chisemi chiaye.

English: If you desire wisdom, keep the commandments and the Lord will give her to you freely;
Ekegusii: Ebigancha bi’echisemi biachoire emebayeno y’obong’aini, korende abanyabibe tibari na gento, otatiga ogochecheria gochia ase chinyasae.

English: for the fear of the Lord is wisdom and instruction. Faith and humility are his good pleasure.
Ekegusii: Onye gotagete chisemi, bwatia ebirage, na Nyasae nere n’akoe chisemi.

English: Don’t disobey the fear of the Lord. Don’t come to him with a double heart.
Ekegusii: Ase igo okomoiroka Nyasae n’echisemi nokworokereria, nigo akogokigwa n’obwegenwa amo n’obwororo.

English: Don’t be a hypocrite in men’s sight. Keep watch over your lips.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa komocha komoigwera Nyasae, gose kogenda asare n’omoyo bw’oborimo.

English: Don’t exalt yourself, lest you fall and bring dishonor upon your soul. The Lord will reveal your secrets and will cast you down in the midst of the congregation, because you didn’t come to the fear of the Lord and your heart was full of deceit.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koba omwerori bosio bw’abaanto, renda omonwa oo.

English: My son, if you come to serve the Lord, prepare your soul for temptation.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, onye gokomokorera Nyasae, kabe ang’e konyora amatemwa amakong’u kegima.

English: Set your heart aright, constantly endure, and don’t make haste in time of calamity.
Ekegusii: Kabe omwororo na obe n’omoyo oyomo; na tokumia ekero emechando egokonyora.

English: Cling to him, and don’t depart, that you may be increased at your latter end.
Ekegusii: Motunyane Nyasae tomotiga nonya ng’ake, erio nosesenigwe ase omoerio bw’obogima bwao.

English: Accept whatever is brought upon you, and be patient when you suffer humiliation.
Ekegusii: Yaanche onsi ay’arabe agokonyora; nonya are ayemechando n’ogochaaya yaremerererie.

English: For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of humiliation.
Ekegusii: Amagena y’Etaabu nigo agosambwa ase eriiko riomorero boigo nabo ere ase abanto baria bancheire na Nyasae

English: Put your trust in him, and he will help you. Make your ways straight, and set your hope on him.
Ekegusii: Mosemerie Omonene, nere nagokoonye, bwatia enchera endonge na komosemeria omonene bweka.

English: All you who fear the Lord, wait for his mercy. Don’t turn aside, lest you fall.
Ekegusii: Inwe baria momwegenete Omonene ganya amaabera aye, timoonchoka korwa asare erio morabaise kogwa.

English: All you who fear the Lord, put your trust in him, and your reward will not fail.
Ekegusii: Inwe baria mwensi abamomoirogete Omonene, mosemerie ere bweka erio ’na monyore eng’eria yaino.

English: All you who fear the Lord, hope for good things, and for eternal gladness and mercy.
Ekegusii: Inwe baria momoirogete Omonene, twara ogosemeria ase omogooko n’ogoesenigwa na amaabera akare na kare.

English: Look at the generations of old, and see: Who ever put his trust in the Lord, and was ashamed? Or who remained in his fear, and was forsaken? Or who called upon him, and he neglected him?
Ekegusii: Morengererie ebigori biaetire erio mweborie: Ning’o Omonene anagotiga oyio omosemeretie ere? Omonene onagotiga monto onde bwensi oyio ogendererete ase okomosika? Omonene onagotiga omonto onde bwensi oyio okomosaba?

English: For the Lord is full of compassion and mercy. He forgives sins and saves in time of affliction.
Ekegusii: Omenene Nyasae n’omwororo naende n’omonyamaabera, Nigo agotwabera ebibe biaito na gotorenda korwa ase emechando yaito.

English: Woe to fearful hearts, to faint hands, and to the sinner who goes two ways!
Ekegusii: Oragereriigwe omonto otateneini bokong’u oyore n’echitang’atang’u ase omoyo oye! Oragereriigwe omonyabibe n’otabwateti enchera y’omonene.

English: Woe to the faint heart! For it doesn’t believe. Therefore it won’t be defended.
Ekegusii: Baragereriigwe abanto baria bare n’obwoba ase emioyo yabo ime naboigo abanto batari n’okwegena! Abanto buna abwo tabakonyara korendeka.

English: Woe to you who have lost your patience! And what will you all do when the Lord visits you?
Ekegusii: Mwaragereriigwe inwe abanto aba mwasiririe ogosemeria kwaino ase Nyasae, korende ’naki morakore ekero Omonene Nyasae arabae egesusuro?

English: Those who fear the Lord will not disobey his words. Those who love him will keep his ways.
Ekegusii: Baria bamoiregete Nyasae tibari kwanga koigwera ebirage biaye; na baria bamwanchete nigo bakomenya buna ere aganetie bamenye.

English: Those who fear the Lord will seek his good pleasure. Those who love him will be filled with the law.
Ekegusii: Baria bamoirogete na bamwanchete Nyasae goika barigie komogokia na bakobwata ebirage biaye.

English: Those who fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and will humble their souls in his sight.
Ekegusii: Baria bamoirogete Nyasae nigo bare ang’e komokorera botaambe, barabwo abwo nigo bagwekeyia bosio bwaye na koboora iga:

English: We will fall into the hands of the Lord, and not into the hands of men; for as his majesty is, so also is his mercy.
Ekegusii: Tiga twebeke ase amaboko a Nyasae na tari ase amaboko a Mwanyabaanto. Ekiagera ase obonene bw’omonto oyio, nabo borabe buna amaabera aye.

English: Hear me, your father, O my children, and do what you hear, that you all may be safe.
Ekegusii: Abana baane, tegererera ogesemia gwa Iso. Kora buna ’nkobateebia, erio ’monyore obuya;

English: For the Lord honors the father over the children, and has confirmed the judgment of the mother over her sons.
Ekegusii: ekiagera Omonene Nyasae oeire abaiso okobua igoro y’Abana babo na goikerania okobua kw’abang’ina gochia ase abana babo.

English: He who honors his father will make atonement for sins.
Ekegusii: Oyokoigwera ise nigo akwenyorera amaabera korwa ase ebibe biaye;

English: He who gives glory to his mother is as one who lays up treasure.
Ekegusii: na onye gosigete nyoko ’mbwegachere obotenenku obonge.

English: Whoever honors his father will have joy in his own children. He will be heard in the day of his prayer.
Ekegusii: Oyosigete ise oyio nagokigwe n’Abana baye ere omonyene, n’ekero arasabe omwana kende gionsi omwana namotegerere.

English: He who gives glory to his father will have length of days. He who listens to the Lord will bring rest to his mother,
Ekegusii: Mwana onde bwensi osigete ise na komogokia ng’ina oyio namenye obogima obotambe.

English: and will serve under his parents, as to masters.
Ekegusii: Abana, igwera abaibori baino buna koreng’ana omosibwa akoigwera omonene oye.

English: Honor your father in deed and word, that a blessing may come upon you from him.
Ekegusii: Oigwere iso ase amang’ana na ase amakora, nario oranyore ogosesenigwa

English: For the blessing of the father establishes the houses of children, but the curse of the mother roots out the foundations.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera ogosesenia gwaiso nigo kogokong’ia ororeria rw’abana baye, korende okoragereria kwa nyoko nigo kogosiria oboroso bw’Ororeria rw’egesaku ekio.

English: Don’t glorify yourself in the dishonor of your father, for your father’s dishonor is no glory to you.
Ekegusii: Omwana one tobaisa gochaaya iso, ekiagera ogochaaya iso tigokorenta buya bonde bwonsi.

English: For the glory of a man is from the honor of his father, and a mother in dishonor is a reproach to her children.
Ekegusii: Ogosika kwao aye omonyene nigo gokorwa ase amasikani aria okorwa gochia ase iso.

English: My son, help your father in his old age, and don’t grieve him as long as he lives.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, orende iso ekero abeire omogotu, gose tomosiibia obororo.

English: If he fails in understanding, have patience with him. Don’t dishonor him in your full strength.
Ekegusii: Nonya nekero chisemi chi’amoereire, omoremererie; gose tomosiereria ase engencho ore n’echinguru n’obuya bw’omobere.

English: For the kindness to your father will not be forgotten. Instead of sins it will be added to build you up.
Ekegusii: Nyasae omobui takweba obuya boria gwakorerete iso, obuya obwo mbokorentere amaabera korwa ase ebibe biao.

English: In the day of your affliction it will be remembered for you, as fair weather upon ice, so your sins will also melt away.
Ekegusii: Ase rituko ri’emechando, ’ng’a riinyorwe ekero ebibe birabeere buna amagena y’embura buna akobeera ase amache amaberu.

English: He who forsakes his father is as a blasphemer. He who provokes his mother is cursed by the Lord.
Ekegusii: Oyokomotuguta ise oyio okorire chimuma as obosio bw’Omonene Nyasae; oyokorenta obororo ase ng’ina oyio onyorire okoragererigwa kwa Nyasae.

English: My son, go on with your business in humility; so you will be loved by an acceptable man.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, kabe omoitongo ase orogendo rwao ase amang’ana ande onsi, naye ’na bwanchwe na baria bonsi banchirwe n’omonene.

English: The greater you are, humble yourself the more, and you will find favor before the Lord.
Ekegusii: Buna ore omonene ang’ana naboigo bwekeyie ase enchera eyio eyio.

English: For the power of the Lord is great, and he is glorified by those who are lowly.
Ekegusii: Chinguru chia Omonene Nyasae nechinene kobua, korende nigo agotogigwa na baria bare n’ogwekeyia.

English: Don’t seek things that are too hard for you, and don’t search out things that are above your strength.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa korigia ebinto ebire ebikong’u ase ore, gose korigia ebinto bire aare n’okobua kwao.

English: Think about the things that have been commanded you, for you have no need of the things that are secret.
Ekegusii: Bwata mono ayio gwatebeetigwe gokora, toganeirie gwechandera amang’ana ayio abisekanete

English: Don’t be overly busy in tasks that are beyond you, for more things are shown to you than men can understand.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gwesoyia ase amang’ana akobweete chinguru, ekiagera ayio onsi okworokigwa ’ng’aete ase ebirengererio bia Mwanyabaanto.

English: For the conceit of many has led them astray. Evil opinion has caused their judgment to slip.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera abange basiriigwe ase ogwekora koba kemanyi ’ng’a mbamanyete mono kegima, korende ogwekaga kwabo gwasiririe ebirengererio biabo.

English: There is no light without eyes. There is no wisdom without knowledge.
Ekegusii: Onye tobwati amaiso tokonyara korora; tobaisa kweganeria obong’aini onye tobobwati.

English: A stubborn heart will do badly at the end. He who loves danger will perish in it.
Ekegusii: Omonto omwerori nigo agokoorera aabe; n’oyobwanchete amabe nigo agosirigwa.

English: A stubborn heart will be burdened with troubles. The sinner will heap sin upon sins.
Ekegusii: Omonto omwerori nigo akobugwa n’emechando; omokori amabe nigo agwetindeka ase ebibe kera engaki.

English: The calamity of the proud has no healing, for a weed of wickedness has taken root in him.
Ekegusii: Emechando y’omonto omwerori teri kogwenigwa, ekiagera obobe boria bwamerire emeri ime yaye.

English: The heart of the prudent will understand a proverb. A wise man desires the ear of a listener.
Ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini nigo akorengereria emebayeno omoyo oye ime; ng’a koba omonto ogotegerera obwo nabwo obong’aini

English: Water will quench a flaming fire; almsgiving will make atonement for sins.
Ekegusii: Buna amaache akorimia omorero omotindi mono, nabo n’ekengwanso ki’omotaka gekorenta okwaberwa kwe’ebibe bi’omotaka.

English: He who repays good turns is mindful of that which comes afterward. In the time of his falling he will find a support.
Ekegusii: Oyokororera oyomwabo amaabera nigo akorengereria aare, erio engaki y’emechando okoonywa.

English: My son, don’t deprive the poor of his living. Don’t make the needy eyes wait long.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, torina omotaka ribaga riokonyora enibo yaye, gose omotange omonto konyora okogania kwaye.

English: Don’t make a hungry soul sorrowful, or provoke a man in his distress.
Ekegusii: Tochanda omonto ekero are n’enchara, gose komogechia omonto ore n’emechando.

English: Don’t add more trouble to a heart that is provoked. Don’t put off giving to him who is in need.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa komentera omonto emechando kare n’eyende, gose konyoorwa korua ekeegwa kiao gochia ase omotaka onye okogosaba kende.

English: Don’t reject a suppliant in his affliction. Don’t turn your face away from a poor man.
Ekegusii: Tibwanga komokoonya omonto okogosaba egento ere kare n’okogania, gose komoa egento getaisainie okogania kwaye.

English: Don’t turn your eye away from one who asks. Give no occasion to a man to curse you.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kwebacha kororana n’omonto omotaka, ekiagera nigo oramoe ribaga riogokoragereria.

English: For if he curses you in the bitterness of his soul, he who made him will hear his supplication.
Ekegusii: Omonto omotaka aise gokoragereria ekiagera are n’obororo bw’okoremerwa, Omotongi oye nigo akoigwa esara yaye.

English: Endear yourself to the assembly. Bow your head to a great man.
Ekegusii: Yegokie eamate yao, erio egokigwe naye, tugama n’amasikani bosio bw’abanene bao.

English: Incline your ear to a poor man. Answer him with peaceful words in humility.
Ekegusii: Tegerera kegima, tobaisa gotegerera omonto omotaka, gose ekero akogokwania toitaba n’obwororo.

English: Deliver him who is wronged from the hand of him who wrongs him; Don’t be hesitant in giving judgment.
Ekegusii: Bogoria omonto ochandegete inse y’echinchera chia abachandi, gose tobaisa koba n’echitang’u-tang’u ekero okonacha ekiina.

English: Be as a father to the fatherless, and like a husband to their mother. So you will be as a son of the Most High, and he will love you more than your mother does.
Ekegusii: Kabe ise baanto ase chintakana buna omosacha, na ng’ina baanto ase bare buna omokungu; Naende nobe buna omwana bw’oyore igoro mono, nere nagwanche goetania nyoko.

English: Wisdom exalts her sons, and takes hold of those who seek her.
Ekegusii: Chisemi nigo chigotogia abana baye, na gokoonya baria bagochirigia.

English: He who loves her loves life. Those who seek her early will be filled with gladness.
Ekegusii: Oyo omwanchete chisemi, nigo anchete obogima. Baria bakomorigia chisemi nigo bakoboka maambia chuni erio bachia komorigia, erio baichorwa n’omogooko.

English: He who holds her fast will inherit glory. Where he enters, the Lord will bless.
Ekegusii: Oyokomobwatia chisemi nigo akonyora amasikani, na Nyasae omosesenia ande onsi ase agochia.

English: Those who serve her minister to the Holy One. The Lord loves those who love her.
Ekegusii: Baria bakomokorera chisemi, nigo bakomokorera Omonene; Nyasae nigo anchete abanto baria bamwanchete chisemi.

English: He who listens to her will judge the nations. He who heeds her will dwell securely.
Ekegusii: Oyokomoigwera chisemi, oyio nanachere chinse ekiina, n’oyokomotegerera chisemi namenye n’omorembe.

English: If he trusts her, he will inherit her, and his generations will possess her.
Ekegusii: Oyore omwegenwa nanyore chisemi, na baria bare abagisangio baye mbagendere koba nere.

English: For at the first she will walk with him in crooked ways, and will bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her judgments.
Ekegusii: Ritang’ani obong’aini nigo borakoire ase chinchera chinkong’u. Nigo borakwoboyie erio okagere buna tokonyara kogenderera. Amasikani boganetie nabo arabe ayemechando, korende nakobeke ase ogotemwa n’amaganio aye goika bwakwegenire buya.

English: Then she will return him again to the straight way, and will gladden him, and reveal to him her secrets.
Ekegusii: Nyuma yaye omochera ara rimo rioka na komogokia na komoteebia obobisi bwaye.

English: If he goes astray, she will forsake him, and hand him over to his fall.
Ekegusii: Korende omonto oyio karamoche, narwe bwoye nakomotiga ase obosiru bwaye omonyene.

English: Watch for the opportunity, and beware of evil. Don’t be ashamed of your soul.
Ekegusii: Erende korwa ase obobe ase chingaki chibwenerete erio bwetangere amabe, erio tibweretera obosoku aye omonyene.

English: For there is a shame that brings sin, and there is a shame that is glory and grace.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera obosoku mboreo bokoraa omonto gochia aase ebibe, korende obosoku mboreo bokorenta amasikani.

English: Don’t show partiality, discrediting your soul. Don’t revere any man to your falling.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koorokia ogwanchereria ase ogotanyora kwao gose ogwanchereria

English: Don’t refrain from speaking when it is for safety. Don’t hide your wisdom for the sake of seeming fair.
Ekegusii: Totiga gokwana ase chingaki chibwenerete, gose tobisa obong’aini bwao.

English: For wisdom will be known by speech, and instruction by the word of the tongue.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera obong’aini bwao nigo bokomanyekana goetera ase aria ogokwana, n’echisemi chiao goetera ase amang’ana aria ogokwana.

English: Don’t speak against the truth and be shamed for your ignorance.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koamereria ekeene, korende bwerende ase ogotamanya kwao.

English: Don’t be ashamed to confess your sins. Don’t fight the river’s current.
Ekegusii: Torora obosoku koangama ebibe biao, tobaisa gotema gotanga amache agoeta.

English: Don’t lay yourself down for a fool to tread upon. Don’t be partial to one who is mighty.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gwancha koragwa n’omonto omoriri, gose gokora ogwanchereria ase oria okoraa

English: Strive for the truth to death, and the Lord God will fight for you.
Ekegusii: Rwanerera ekeene nonya ngoika amakweri, ekiagera Omonene Nyasae nakorwanerere.

English: Don’t be hasty with your tongue, or slack and negligent in your deeds.
Ekegusii: Toba omwango ase ogokwana, gose omworo ase emeremo yao.

English: Don’t be like a lion in your house, or suspicious of your servants.
Ekegusii: Toba buna endo nyomba mwao, gose tonya gokagera abasomba bao.

English: Don’t let your hand be stretched out to receive, and closed when you should repay.
Ekegusii: Toba omonto oganetie kona koegwa rioka, gose toba omokongu ase okoa abande.

English: Don’t set your heart upon your goods. Don’t say, “They are sufficient for me.”
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kobeke okwegena kwao gwonsi ase enibo yao, naende toteeba ng’a: “Inche nimbwate enibo eisaine.”

English: Don’t follow your own mind and your strength to walk in the desires of your heart.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koraagwa n’ebirengerio biokogania okobe, gose ase okong’uswa n’echinguru echiao, ase okobwatia okogania okobe kwomoyo oo.

English: Don’t say, “Who will have dominion over me?” for the Lord will surely take vengeance on you.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteeba ng’a: “Ning’o oranyare kombua?” Ekiagera ase obomaene goika akoe egesusuro.

English: Don’t say, “I sinned, and what happened to me?” for the Lord is patient.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteeba ng’a: “Nakorire ekebe, korende bono, ninki rende kiaba ekebe?” Ekiagera Omonene tari kobwatwa n’obororo ase obwango.

English: Don’t be so confident of atonement that you add sin upon sins.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa konara konakwaberwa, gose komenta ekebe igoro ase ekebe.

English: Don’t say, “His compassion is great. He will be pacified for the multitude of my sins,” for mercy and wrath are with him, and his indignation will rest on sinners.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteeba ng’a: “Amabera a Nyasae n’amange, ere n’anyabere ebibe biane ebinge.” Inyora ng’a Nyasae nabwate amaabera nere nkobwatwa are obororo, n’obororo bwaye nigo b’ogosiria abanyabibe.

English: Don’t wait to turn to the Lord. Don’t put off from day to day; for suddenly the wrath of the Lord will come on you, and you will perish in the time of vengeance.
Ekegusii: Tonyorwa komoiranera Omonene Nyasae, totebana komoiranera rituko ase rituko; ekiagera endamuamu ya Nyasae nigo eragwokere mosiabano, n’engaki y’okonacha ekiina nigo orasirigwe.

English: Don’t set your heart upon unrighteous gains, for you will profit nothing in the day of calamity.
Ekegusii: Tibwegena enibo y’oborimo, ekiagera tekogokoonya kende gionsi.

English: Don’t winnow with every wind. Don’t walk in every path. This is what the sinner who has a double tongue does.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koirura engano yao ase kera ekarambauti gose kobwatia amang’ana onde bwensi, gose chingencho chi’omonyaborimo.

English: Be steadfast in your understanding. Let your speech be consistent.
Ekegusii: Bono tenena bokong’u ase okomanya kwao, n’amang’a ao tiga abwatane n’okomanya kwao.

English: Be swift to hear and answer with patience.
Ekegusii: Kabe omwango ase ogotegerera, n’omong’ora na korenda ng’a ninki okoiraneria.

English: If you have understanding, answer your neighbor; but if not, put your hand over your mouth.
Ekegusii: Onye komanyete ring’ana erio, moiranerie oyomino, ing’ana’ rinde rionsi erio otamanyeti kira kiri takoiraneria.

English: Glory and dishonor is in talk. A man’s tongue may be his downfall.
Ekegusii: Amasikani amo n’obosoku nigo bikorwa korwa ase amang’ana agokwanwa.

English: Don’t be called a whisperer. Don’t lie in wait with your tongue; for shame is on the thief, and an evil condemnation is on him who has a double tongue.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gwancha kwenyorera amasikani ase okwemurungania, tibwancha kobana amabe agochia kobanyora abanto baande. Ekiagera koreng’ana buna obosooku bokomonyora omoibi, naboigo okonacherwa ekiina koramonyore omonto omonyaborimo.

English: Don’t be ignorant in a great or small matter.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koba n’okomocha ase ’ng’ana rinde rionsi riike gose rinene, gose koba omobisa ekero otakeire koba omosani.

English: Don’t become an enemy instead of a friend; for an evil name will inherit shame and reproach. So it is with the sinner who has a double tongue.
Ekegusii: Chimbwa chimbe nigo chikoreta obosooku amo n’ogotogonyerwa, buna ayakomonyora omonto omorimo naende omonyabibe.

English: Don’t exalt yourself in the counsel of your soul, that your soul not be torn in pieces like a bull.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gwancha kogamberwa n’okogania kwao okobe, ekiagera okogania okwo nigo korataborane omoyo oo buna eeri

English: You will eat up your leaves, destroy your fruit, and leave yourself like a dry tree.
Ekegusii: eraimokerereri ebisago bi’emete yao na gotuguta amatunda ao onsi. Erio otigare buna omote bwomire.

English: A wicked soul will destroy him who has it, and will make him a laughing stock to his enemies.
Ekegusii: Okogania okobe nigo kogosiria omonto omonyene, erio yagera osekererwa n’ababisa baye.

English: Sweet words will multiply a man’s friends. A gracious tongue will multiply courtesies.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana y’obwororo nigo akomomentera omonto abasani, n’ogotwara amasikani nigo gokoreta oboamate obuya gati y’abanto.

English: Let those that are at peace with you be many, but your advisers one of a thousand.
Ekegusii: Kabe n’abasani abange mogokwanania nabwo, korende ase barabwo abwo oyokogosemia abe oyomo ase abanto abwo elifu.

English: If you want to gain a friend, get him in a time of testing, and don’t be in a hurry to trust him.
Ekegusii: Koganetie gotwara omosani, karamoitona ritang’ani, toayerera komwegena.

English: For there is a friend just for an occasion. He won’t continue in the day of your affliction.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera nareo orabe omosani ase engencho aganetie ogokoonya kwao, oyio otaabeo ekero aye ore n’emechando.

English: And there is a friend who turns into an enemy. He will discover strife to your reproach.
Ekegusii: Naende nareo omosani oraonchoke koba omobisa oo, na koreta okoamerererania okwo korarete eriomana gati yaiino.

English: And there is a friend who is a companion at the table, but he won’t continue in the day of your affliction.
Ekegusii: Naboigo, nareo omosani oyio ore omosani ekero kiendagera; korende ekero kiemechando takororekana nonya ng’ake erio agokoonye.

English: In your prosperity he will be as yourself, and will be bold over your servants.
Ekegusii: Omonto nareo oraikaranse naye ekero ebinto bionsi bire buya ase ore; erio bwebeka ekerengo buna aye na gochaka koa abakoreri bao amachiiko.

English: If you are brought low, he will be against you, and will hide himself from your face.
Ekegusii: Korende, ekero kwaereirwe n’enibo erio oonchoka, na gochaka kweongora korwa ase abanto.

English: Separate yourself from your enemies, and beware of your friends.
Ekegusii: Bera aare n’ababisa bao, erende n’abasani.

English: A faithful friend is a strong defense. He who has found him has found a treasure.
Ekegusii: Omosani omwegenwa nigo anga buna oboroso, oyonyorire omosani buna oyio onyorire ekeegwa kiobogima.

English: There is nothing that can be taken in exchange for a faithful friend. His excellency is beyond price.
Ekegusii: Omosani omwegenwa nigo are omonto bw’engencho mono kobua ebinto bionsi, n’onde taiyo oranyare korenga obuya bwaye.

English: A faithful friend is a life-saving medicine. Those who fear the Lord will find him.
Ekegusii: Omosani omuya nigo anga buna eriogo erio rikoreta chinguru ase omobere. Abanto bamoirogete omonene nabwo boka bakonyora omosani buna oyio.

English: He who fears the Lord directs his friendship properly; for as he is, so is his neighbor also.
Ekegusii: Oyomwenerete Nyasae, oyio nigo akonyora omosani bw’ekeene, ekiagera buna omonto are naende nabo akonyora omosani omobwekaine.

English: My son, gather instruction from your youth up. Even when you have gray hair you will find wisdom.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, korwa ase obwana bwao, chora okworokereria nonya n’ekero orabe omogotu n’ogenderere koba gokomonyora ere oyio ore chisemi.

English: Come to her as one who plows and sows and wait for her good fruit; for your toil will be little in her cultivation, and you will soon eat of her fruit.
Ekegusii: Kora omokia buna omoremi ase okomonyora chisemi, na konyora rigesa riao rigiya. Nekobetereretie ase chingaki chitari inke, korende ase engaki enke n’oragere korwa ase rigesa riao.

English: How exceedingly harsh she is to the unlearned! He who is without understanding will not remain in her.
Ekegusii: Abanto batabwati chimbwa chingiya nigo bakomorora chisemi koba omotindi, ase abanto abariri mbakonyara kobeera nere ase egeka egetaambe.

English: She will rest upon him as a mighty stone of trial. He won’t hesitate to cast her from him.
Ekegusii: Ase abande chisemi echinga buna omonto omorito buna rigena riokorengera, na barabwo tibagoteebana komotugutera aare.

English: For wisdom is according to her name. She isn’t manifest to many.
Ekegusii: Chisemi nabo are buna erieta riaye rire, ekiagera ere chisemi, tari konakwemanyekania ase abanto.

English: Give ear, my son, and accept my judgment. Don’t refuse my counsel.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, ’ntegerere kegima na obwatie ogosemia kwane. Tobaisa kwanga amang’ana yogosemia kwane.

English: Bring your feet into her fetters, and your neck into her chain.
Ekegusii: Esibe n’echinyororo chi’echisemi goetanana ’amagoro, tomocha gwesiba n’ebigoti biao boigo.

English: Put your shoulder under her and bear her. Don’t be grieved with her bonds.
Ekegusii: Bogoria omosigo oye, koreende torosa n’oborito bwaye.

English: Come to her with all your soul. Keep her ways with your whole power.
Ekegusii: Mochiere ere chisemi n’omoyo oo bwonsi, na kobwatia ebirage biaye n’echinguru chiao chionsi.

English: Search and seek, and she will be made known to you. When you get hold of her, don’t let her go.
Ekegusii: Moitone na komorigia chisemi, nere neorokie ogocha asore. Ko’ kwamonyorire chisemi tobaisa gotiga komotunyana.

English: For at the last you will find her rest; and she will be turned for you into gladness.
Ekegusii: Omoerio oye, ng’onyore omotimoko okorwa asare.

English: Her fetters will be to you for a covering of strength, and her chains for a robe of glory.
Ekegusii: Ebimanyererio bie ebinyuri nigo birabe enguba y’oboroso bw’oboikeranu bwao, na ebinyuri ebio mbibe buna richoki ase rigoti riaye.

English: For there is a golden ornament upon her, and her bands are a purple cord.
Ekegusii: Ekemanyererio ki’ebinyuri biaye nigo bire buna ogwechabera Kw’amameka ’amaabera. Ebinyuri ebio mbibe okoginga kwao ase engoba y’obogambi.

English: You shall put her on as a robe of glory, and shall put her on as a crown of rejoicing.
Ekegusii: N’obeeke chisemi nigo chinga buna egutwa y’obogambi.

English: My son, if you are willing, you will be instructed. If you will yield your soul, you will be prudent.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, onye kore n’okogania nosome. Onye gotagete koba omong’aini nabo okonyara onye gokwerwa ase okomanya.

English: If you love to hear, you will receive. If you incline your ear, you will be wise.
Ekegusii: Onye kwerwete gotegerera, nabo ogosoma na koba n’obong’aini.

English: Stand in the multitude of the elders. Attach yourself to whomever is wise.
Ekegusii: Bera ase abanto abanene bare; barenge buya orore gose omonto omong’aini nare ase egati yobo, erio obere nere.

English: Be willing to listen to every godly discourse. Don’t let the proverbs of understanding escape you.
Ekegusii: Obe ang’e gotegerera kera okworokereria na totiga obosemia bw’emebayeno bokominchorie.

English: If you see a man of understanding, get to him early. Let your foot wear out the steps of his doors.
Ekegusii: Korarore omonto omong’aini, mochiere bwango, morosie ase egesieri kiaye ase okomotaarera.

English: Let your mind dwell on the ordinances of the Lord and meditate continually on his commandments. He will establish your heart and your desire for wisdom will be given to you.
Ekegusii: Rengereria amachiiko y’Omonene enarie emeroberio yaye. Ere naikeranie ebirengererio biao naye nochinyore chisemi oganetie.

English: Do no evil, so no evil will overtake you.
Ekegusii: Otakoreti ayare amabe, mabe tagokonyora nonya ng’ake.

English: Depart from wrong, and it will turn away from you.
Ekegusii: Korebachere amabe, amabe natame korwa asore.

English: My son, don’t sow upon the furrows of unrighteousness, and you won’t reap them sevenfold.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, torema omogondo erio osimeke ayatari amaronge, ekiagera n’ogese ayio amabe ara gatano na kabere.

English: Don’t seek preeminence from the Lord, nor the seat of honor from the king.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koboria Omonene ase ogwesongororia, gose korigia ekerogo kiobonene bw’oboruoti.

English: Don’t justify yourself in the presence of the Lord, and don’t display your wisdom before the king.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gwekora omuya bosio bwa Nyasae, gose kworokia ng’a nore n’esemi bosio bw’abarwoti.

English: Don’t seek to be a judge, lest you not be able to take away iniquities, lest perhaps you fear the person of a mighty man, and lay a stumbling block in the way of your uprightness.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gwekora omonachi ebina erinde orabaise gosinywa kogikeria amabe; tobaisa gosirigwa na baria bakwenyara gose abare n’echinguru na bakobetereria ebinto buna bitari, erio osire orabaisa gosaria oboronge n’amasikani ao.

English: Don’t sin against the multitude of the city. Don’t disgrace yourself in the crowd.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kogechia abanto b’eamate y’abanto bande, egere orabaisa gwesareria amasikani ao gati y’abanto momenyete nabwo.

English: Don’t commit a sin twice, for even in one you will not be unpunished.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kwaberwa korwa ase ekebe ara kabere, ekiagera noegwe egesusuro nonya ase rimocho erimo rioka.

English: Don’t say, “He will look upon the multitude of my gifts. When I make an offering to the Most High God, he will accept it.”
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteeba ’ng’a: “Omonene nabwate ebigeni bie ekeng’wanso kiane, ko ’ndaruere Omonene Nyasae ekeng’wanso goika agianche.”

English: Don’t be faint-hearted in your prayer. Don’t neglect to give alms.
Ekegusii: Toba n’echitang’u-tang’u gose orose ekero ogosaba, na tibweba gokoonya abataka ase okobaa ebigeni.

English: Don’t laugh a man to scorn when he is in the bitterness of his soul, for there is one who humbles and exalts.
Ekegusii: Tomosekerera omonto ekero abwate obororo ase omoyo oye ime, ekiagera Omonene oria ogokeyia abanto korwa ase obonene bwabo nabo naende aramoimokererie igoro.

English: Don’t devise a lie against your brother, or do the same to a friend.
Ekegusii: Tiga koroberia igoro y’oborimo ogochia goteebia omoamate oo, gose orabaisa kweba okorere omosani oo boigo.

English: Refuse to utter a lie, for that habit results in no good.
Ekegusii: Tigana kegima n’ogoteeba oborimo, ekiagera oborimo tibwanya korenta gento kende gionsi kere ki’engencho asore.

English: Don’t babble in the assembly of elders. Don’t repeat your words in your prayer.
Ekegusii: Tiga gotabanana ase abagaaka baumeranire, gose obe omonto okonakoirorera ebinto ase ogosaba kwao.

English: Don’t hate hard labor or farm work, which the Most High has created.
Ekegusii: Tiga kogechigwa n’egasi enkong’u, gose egasi ya mogondo eyio yaroberetigwe na Nyasae omonyene.

English: Don’t number yourself among the multitude of sinners. Remember that wrath will not wait.
Ekegusii: Tiga kobwaterana n’ekeombe kiabakori amabe, naende inyora ng’a egesusuro ki’ebibe ebio tikegogoikeera.

English: Humble your soul greatly, for the punishment of the ungodly man is fire and the worm.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koba kogwekeiyia moono igo, ekiagera egesusuro kia abatamomanyeti Nyasae, omoerio oye n’omorero amo n’obogundo bw’amakweri.

English: Don’t exchange a friend for something, neither a true brother for the gold of Ophir.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa komorwa oyomino gooitwa erinde bwenyorere chitaabu, gose komorwa omosani oo bw’ekeene ase okwenyorera amagena ’amaabera ase ense eye.

English: Don’t deprive yourself of a wise and good wife, for her grace is worth more than gold.
Ekegusii: Nywoma kobwate obong’aini, naende omokungu omuya nigo are n’engencho mono kobua rigori ria ’etaabu.

English: Don’t abuse a servant who works faithfully, or a hireling who gives you his life.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa komokorera bobe omokori oo, na ore omwegenwa inse yao, gose omonto bw’ekonda oy’ogokoreire emeremo buya.

English: Let your soul love a wise servant. Don’t defraud him of liberty.
Ekegusii: Mwanche omokori emeremo oo.

English: Do you have cattle? Look after them. If they are profitable to you, let them stay by you.
Ekegusii: Inee, nore n’echiombe? Chirende bono! Onye chikoreta ebitoki, chirende.

English: Do you have children? Correct them, and make them obedient from their youth.
Ekegusii: Inee, nobwate abana bono? Borokererie bono amang’ana y’amasikani. Naende oborokererie oboigweri korwa ase obwana bwabo.

English: Do you have daughters? Take care of their bodies, and don’t be overly indulgent toward them.
Ekegusii: Inee, nore n’abana chinyaroka? Oborokereria igoro y’obochenu bw’emebere yabo, korende naende tobororobera moono igo.

English: Give your daughter in marriage, and you will have accomplished a great matter. Give her to a man of understanding.
Ekegusii: Oise komosokia omwana oo enyaroka anywomwe, igo gwaikeranirie emeremo yao emenene kegima.

English: Do you have a wife who pleases you? Don’t cast her out. But don’t trust yourself to one who is hateful.
Ekegusii: Inee, n’obwate bono omokungu as omoyo oo ime? Mwanche kegima? Tobaisa komoseria, korende onye tomwancheti, tobaisa komwegena rinde omokungu otari omwegenwa.

English: Honor your father with your whole heart, and don’t forget the birth pangs of your mother.
Ekegusii: Mosike iso n’omoyo oo bwonsi, naboigo, naende tibweba obororo bwa nyoko.

English: Remember that you were born of them. What will you repay them for the things that they have done for you?
Ekegusii: Oinyore ng’a abwo nabwo bakoiborete. Inee, nonyare kobaakana onsi aya bagokorerete?

English: Fear the Lord with all your soul; and revere his priests.
Ekegusii: Moiroke Nyasae Omobui n’omoyo oo bwonsi; na kae abakuani bao amasikani.

English: With all your strength love him who made you. Don’t forsake his ministers.
Ekegusii: Mwanche omotongi oo n’echinguru chiao chionsi; na tobaisa kobatuguta abakoreri baye.

English: Fear the Lord and honor the priest. Give him his portion, even as it is commanded you: the first fruits, the trespass offering, the gift of the shoulders, the sacrifice of sanctification, and the first fruits of holy things.
Ekegusii: Moiroke Omonene, na kobasika abakuani baye, Kae Nyasae ensemo yaye eyio emotungetie: rigesa riao ritang’ani.

English: Also stretch out your hand to the poor man, that your blessing may be complete.
Ekegusii: Kae abataka okogania kwabo ase obwororo, erio Nyasae akoe ogosesenia kwaye.

English: A gift has grace in the sight of every living man. Don’t withhold grace for a dead man.
Ekegusii: Obwororo bwao bobe ase abanto bonsi, gose tobarina obwororo bwao nonya n’abakuure.

English: Don’t avoid those who weep, and mourn with those who mourn.
Ekegusii: Tobaa omogongo baria bakwereirwe, korende obwatane nabarabwo ase ogwechanda kwabo.

English: Don’t be slow to visit a sick man, for by such things you will gain love.
Ekegusii: Totiga kobatarera abarwaire; ekiagera oise kobatarera aye mbwanchwe.

English: In all your words, remember eternity, and you will never sin.
Ekegusii: Ase ogokora kwao gwonsi bweinyorie ase ogokoorera naye togokora ebibe nonya ng’ake.

English: Don’t contend with a mighty man, lest perhaps you fall into his hands.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koamererania n’omonto ore nechinguru gokobua, ekiagera nigo orenyore ase obokong’u obonene mono.

English: Don’t strive with a rich man, lest perhaps he overpower you; for gold has destroyed many, and turned away the hearts of kings.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kw’omana na monto onde bwensi omoteneku, ekiagera obotenenku bwaye ’na bokobue ase ekegambero; ekiagera chitaabu nigo chikobua na gosiria emioyo y’abagambi.

English: Don’t argue with a loudmouthed man. Don’t heap wood upon his fire.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kwamererania n’omonto omwamereria; gose toigereria chinko gochia ase omorero oye.

English: Don’t make fun of a rude man, lest your ancestors be dishonored.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gokora echeche n’omonto omwenenu, ekiagera nigo arabaise gochecheria chisokoro chiaino.

English: Don’t reproach a man when he turns from sin. Remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gosiereria omonto bweitirie ebibe biaye. Inyora ’ng’a twensi nabanyabibe tore.

English: Don’t dishonor a man in his old age, for some of us are also growing old.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gosiereria omonto kagotire, ekiagera abange baino ng’a moche kogota boigo.

English: Don’t rejoice over anyone’s death. Remember that we all die.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kogokera amakweri omonto onde bwensi.

English: Don’t neglect the discourse of the wise. Be conversant with their proverbs; for from them you will learn discipline and how to serve great men.
Ekegusii: Toibaisa gochaya emeroberio y’abanto abang’aini, korende bwenarie korwa ase emereng’anio yabo, erio nario oranyare gokorera abanene.

English: Don’t miss the discourse of the aged, for they also learned from their parents, because from them you will learn understanding, and to give an answer in time of need.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gosiereria amang’ ana abagaaka bagokwana, ekiagera nabarabwo nigo borokereretigwe korwa ase chisokoro chiabo.

English: Don’t kindle the coals of a sinner, lest you be burned with the flame of his fire.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kogenka omwana bwomonyabibe, ekiagera “Chiarekondia chikori;”

English: Don’t rise up from the presence of an insolent man, lest he lie in wait as an ambush for your mouth.
Ekegusii: Toibasa gwancha koraagwa n’omotutukanu, erio arabaisa kogotega na gokobwaterania ase amang’ana aao aye omonyene.

English: Don’t lend to a man who is stronger than you; and if you lend, count it as a loss.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koa omonto onde bwesi egento singo okobuete chinguru; oise komoa singo, mbuya omanya ng’a ekio kiayiereire na togokenyora rinde.

English: Don’t be surety beyond your means. If you give surety, think as one who will have to pay.
Ekegusii: Toibasa kobeka egento kiao kiengencho ase ’ntenenera, onye gokoba omoteneneri, aye rirorio manya ng’a nore ang’e kogiakana aye omonyene.

English: Don’t go to law with a judge; for according to his honor they will give judgment for him.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gosoera omonyene richiko ase ekegambero, ekiagera ekiina nigo keranachwe ase ogwancherereria gochia asare.

English: Don’t travel with a reckless man, lest he be burdensome to you; for he will do as he pleases, and you will perish with his folly.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kogenda orogendo inchera n’omonto omoriri, ekiagera nigo arabaisa koba omosigo asore. Omonto oyio nigo agokora buna ebirengererio biaye amo n’okogania kwaye kore.

English: Don’t fight with a wrathful man. Don’t travel with him through the desert, for blood is as nothing in his sight. Where there is no help, he will overthrow you.
Ekegusii: Tiga kwomana n’omonto okobwantwa n’obororo ase obwango, gose togenda nere enchera ase abanto batari; ekiagera omonto buna oyio ogoitera amanyinga tikeri gento asare.

English: Don’t consult with a fool, for he will not be able to keep a secret.
Ekegusii: Torigia ogosemia korwa ase omonto omoriri, ekiagera takonyara kogacha obobisi.

English: Do no secret thing before a stranger, for you don’t know what it will cause.
Ekegusii: Torigia gokora kende gionsi kia bobisi ase omogeni, ekiagera tagokorera bobisi obwo kende.

English: Don’t open your heart to every man. Don’t let him return you a favor.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koigorera monto amang’ana obobisi bwonsi bore ase omoyo oo, gose gotiga onde bwensi akore ogwanchereria gocha asore.

English: Don’t be jealous over the wife of your bosom, and don’t teach her an evil lesson against yourself.
Ekegusii: Kore n’omosani oo, tobaisa koba n’endamwamu gochia ase omokungu oye ere anchete, ekiagera omosani oo nigo aragokorere bobe.

English: Don’t give your soul to a woman and let her trample down your strength.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa komotigera omokungu onde bwensi amasikani ao.

English: Don’t go to meet a woman who plays the prostitute, lest perhaps you fall into her snares.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kobwatana obosani n’omokuungu omotayayi ekiagera nigo orabwatwe ase emetego yaye.

English: Don’t associate with a woman who is a singer, lest perhaps you be caught by her tricks.
Ekegusii: Totwara oboamate n’omokuungu omoteeri, ekiagera nigo arabaisa kobwatwa ase n’obong’aini bwaye.

English: Don’t gaze at a virgin, lest perhaps you stumble and incur penalties for her.
Ekegusii: Totoonera omoiseke omwekungi, ekiagera aye nere nigo morasoe ase omotego erio ekobetererie omoakanere chiombe.

English: Don’t give your soul to prostitutes, that you not lose your inheritance.
Ekegusii: Tochwara omoyo oo gochia ase omokungu omotayayi, ekiagera nigo arasirie egesaku kiao gionsi.

English: Don’t look around in the streets of the city. Don’t wander in its deserted places.
Ekegusii: Tokona komagaga chichiro goeta gose konakoombogana ebinucha-nuchi ime aye bweka.

English: Turn your eye away from a beautiful woman, and don’t gaze at another’s beauty. Many have been led astray by the beauty of a woman; and with this, passion is kindled like a fire.
Ekegusii: Totoonera omokungu omuya, tomotogoreria amaiso omokungu otari oyoo. Abasacha abange baagoranirwe korwa ase emeroberio yabo okoba abakuunga abanyakieni, ekiagera ring’ana eri nigo rikobeka ase okogania konga buna okw’omwana.

English: Don’t dine at all with a woman who has a husband, or revel with her at wine, lest perhaps your soul turn away to her, and with your spirit you slide into destruction.
Ekegusii: Toikaransa rinde n’omokuungu bw’omogisangi oo; ekiagera nigo omoyo oo oramwanche erio tonyaara gwetooria korwa ase emerindo emebe eragoite.

English: Don’t forsake an old friend; for a new one is not comparable to him. A new friend is like new wine: if it becomes old, you will drink it with gladness.
Ekegusii: Totuguta omosani oo bw’emiaka emenge, ekiagera noba n’omosani omoyia takonyara buna ere. Omosani omoyia nigo abuekaine n’edivai enyia, korende edivai enkoro nigo ekonyweka n’omogooko.

English: Don’t envy the success of a sinner; for you don’t know what his end will be.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koreera omonto otari omooronge endamwamu ekero are n’obuya, ekiagera tokomanya ng’a obuya obwo ’mechando ki boramoretere.

English: Don’t delight in the delights of the ungodly. Remember they will not go unpunished to the grave.
Ekegusii: Togokera emechando y’abanto batamomanyeti Nyasae. Inyora ng’a tibakwebachera egesusuro kiabo ase ense eye.

English: Keep yourself far from the man who has power to kill, and you will not be troubled by the fear of death. If you come to him, commit no fault, lest he take away your life. Know surely that you go about in the midst of snares, and walk upon the battlements of a city.
Ekegusii: Bera aare n’omonto oragokorere bobe na kogoita okwe; ekiagera tokomokagera ng’a nagoite. Korende, onye ekobetereria omobeere ang’e riorio bwerende kegima. Naende erenda kiagera nigo ogotaara ase emetego botaambe, ekiagera nigo otegire.

English: As well as you can, aim to know your neighbors, and take counsel with the wise.
Ekegusii: Manya abaamate boa kegima koreng’ana buna chisemi chiao ching’ana, gose rigia ogosemia korwa ase abanto bare n’echisemi.

English: Let your conversation be with men of understanding. Let all your discourse be in the law of the Most High.
Ekegusii: Gokogamba, gamba n’abanto bare n’echisemi, n’enkwana yaino ebe igoro y’amachiko a Nyasae.

English: Let righteous people be companions at your table. Let your glorying be in the fear of the Lord.
Ekegusii: Abanto abororo babe abasani bao mokoragera nabwo, ogwetogia kwao kobe ase okomomanya Nyasae.

English: A work is commended because of the skill of the artisan; so he who rules the people will be considered wise for his speech.
Ekegusii: Emeremo emiya y’omonto nigo ekomorentera ogosika. Omonto okogambera abanto goika abe omoikeranu ase ama’angana aye.

English: A loudmouthed man is dangerous in his city. He who is reckless in his speech will be hated.
Ekegusii: Omonto omweturungi nigo akoreta obwoba ase omochie oye; gose omonto otari omweriiti ase amang’a nigo akogechwa.

English: A wise judge will instruct his people. The government of a man of understanding will be well ordered.
Ekegusii: Omogambi ore n’echisemi nigo agosomia abanto baria akogambera n’obogambi bw’omonto ore n’echisemi nigo bore n’omoroberio omuya.

English: As is the judge of his people, so are his officials. As the city’s ruler is, so are all those who dwell in it.
Ekegusii: Buna omogambi bw’abaanto are naboigo n’abanto baye bare. Nonya mbaria bakombwatisia ase obogambi bwaye; buna omogambi are n’abamenyete aroro bare igo.

English: An undisciplined king will destroy his people. A city will be established through the understanding of the powerful.
Ekegusii: Omogambi otari n’echisemi nigo are emechando ase abanto baye; obogambi nigo bogokiina na gotenena bokong’u ekero abagambi baye bare abang’aini.

English: The government of the earth is in the Lord’s hand. In due time, he will raise up over it the right person at the right time.
Ekegusii: Obogambi bw’ense nigo bore ase amaboko a Nyasae nere nigo akomobeka omogambi oisaine ase engaki yaye.

English: A man’s prosperity is in the Lord’s hand. He will lay his honor upon the person of the scribe.
Ekegusii: Oboikeranu bwa Mwanyabaanto nigo bore ase amaboko a Nyasae. Omonene nigo akomoa omoriki amasikani.

English: Don’t be angry with your neighbor for every wrong. Do nothing by works of violence.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kogechigwa n’omwamate oo. Gose tokora kende ekero gwatokeirwe n’oboro.

English: Pride is hateful before the Lord and men. Arrogance is abhorrent in the judgment of both.
Ekegusii: Obwerori nigo bokogechia Nyasae, na mwanyanto boigo; amang’ana y’okwamereria n’echinguru chitari chia boronge ekio n’egento giokogechia ase bonsi babere.

English: Sovereignty is transferred from nation to nation because of injustice, violence, and greed for money.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho y’aya atari aboronge, nakwo ogoteeba, obwerori na gwancha enibo, obogambi bw’ense eyemo ’na boirwe n’ense ende.

English: Why are dirt and ashes proud? Because in life, my body decays.
Ekegusii: Inee, omonto oyio ere ore ebuse n’eribu, ninki igo arerorere?

English: A long disease mocks the physician. The king of today will die tomorrow.
Ekegusii: Oborwaire bw’engaki entaambe nigo bokomwoboyia omogwenia reero, na mambia omogambi, erio abwo bakwa bonsi baba ebitondo.

English: For when a man is dead, he will inherit maggots, vermin, and worms.
Ekegusii: Aria akobanyora ekero bakuure bonsi abwo nigo bare egento ekemo: amakonde, ching’iti chintindi chintindi, amo n’ebigwankwa.

English: It is the beginning of pride when a man departs from the Lord. His heart has departed from him who made him.
Ekegusii: Omochakano bw’obwerori n’okomotiga Omonene na goonchora omoyo oye aare korwa ase Omonene n’omotongi.

English: For the beginning of pride is sin. He who keeps it will pour out abomination. For this cause the Lord brought upon them strange calamities and utterly overthrew them.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera omochakano bw’obwerori n’ekebe, na monto onde bwensi orabwatane nakio, oyio nigo araichorwe n’obobe.

English: The Lord cast down the thrones of rulers and set the lowly in their place.
Ekegusii: Nyasae obaikirie abanene korwa ase ebirogo biabo bi’obonene, n’eribaga riabo obaikaransirie abaitongo.

English: The Lord plucked up the roots of nations and planted the lowly in their place.
Ekegusii: Nyasae obasebareranirie aberori korwa ase oboroso bwabo; nase ribaga riabo oikaransirie abaitongo.

English: The Lord overthrew the lands of nations and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
Ekegusii: Omonene Nyasae ong’usire ebisaku bionsi bi’ense, na kobisiria goika omoerio bw’ense.

English: He took some of them away and destroyed them, and made their memory to cease from the earth.
Ekegusii: Ebisaku binde obirusirieo na kobisiria, erio obotinyirie ebimanyerio biabo bionsi korwa ase ense.

English: Pride has not been created for men, nor wrathful anger for the offspring of women.
Ekegusii: Obwerori tibwatongetwe okoba abanto, gose okoba Mwanyabaanto.

English: Whose offspring has honor? Human offspring who fear the Lord. Whose offspring has no honor? Human offspring who break the commandments.
Ekegusii: Mbitongire ki ebio igo bisaine amasikani? ’Mwanyabaanto? Mbitongire ki bisanerete ogosikwa? ’Mwanyabaanto? Mbaria bamomanyete Nyasae. Mbitongire ki bisanerete ogosikwa? ’Mwanyabaanto. Mbitongire ki bisanerete amasikani? Mbarabi bakobuna amachiiko?

English: In the midst of kindred he who rules them has honor. Those who fear the Lord have honor in his eyes.
Ekegusii: Gati abamura bamwabo omomura omonene nere ogwenerete gosikwa. Baria bamoirogete Nyasae mbagwenerete amasikani bosio bwaye.

English: The rich man, the honorable, and the poor all glory in the fear of the Lord.
Ekegusii: Abatenenku, nigo bagosikwa bosio bw’abataka, korende abataka tiga bamwetogerie Nyasae.

English: It is not right to dishonor a poor man who has understanding. It is not fitting to glorify a man who is a sinner.
Ekegusii: Tari buya gosiereria omonto ore omotaka korende nabwate obong’aini, nonya nabo teri buya kogokera omonyabibe.

English: The prince, the judge, and the mighty man will be honored. There is not one of them greater than he who fears the Lord.
Ekegusii: Omogambi, na omonachi ebina oyio obwate ekerogo oyio nigo agosikwa, korende oyo omoirogete Nyasae n’omonene kegima kobua bonsi abwo.

English: Free men will minister to a wise servant. A man who has knowledge will not complain.
Ekegusii: Omorikwa emeremo ore n’echisemi nakorerwe emeremo n’abanto bare n’obosibore; n’oyore n’obong’aiani takomwemurunganeria.

English: Don’t flaunt your wisdom in doing your work. Don’t boast in the time of your distress.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gwekora kemanyi ekero ogokora emeremo yao, gose gwetogia ekero obwate obokong’u.

English: Better is he who labors and abounds in all things, than he who boasts and lacks bread.
Ekegusii: Nigo are buya oyore n’omokia ase emeremo, oyio nigo abwate kera eki aganetie, kobua omonto okona goetaanana erio ochaka kweng’ereria ase abande ng’a tari n’endagera.

English: My son, glorify your soul in humility, and ascribe to yourself honor according to your worthiness.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, etogerie ogwekeyia, na bwerore aye bweka koba ng’a toisaini.

English: Who will justify him who sins against his own soul? Who will honor him who dishonors his own life?
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto agwekora omotaka, bweka kobwaye, ning’o otamorore koba omonto omoriri? Omonto buna oyio ning’o oramosike, ekiagera bwesiererie ere omonyene?

English: A poor man is honored for his knowledge. A rich man is honored for his riches.
Ekegusii: Ekero ore omonto omotaka torigosikwa ase obong’aini bwao; n’omotenenku ase obotenenku bwao.

English: But he who is honored in poverty, how much more in riches? He who is dishonored in riches, how much more in poverty?
Ekegusii: Onye omonto osikire nonya n’ekero are omotaka, oyio nabo agokwa mono kegima ekero abeire omokama.

English: The wisdom of the lowly will lift up his head, and make him sit in the midst of great men.
Ekegusii: Eisa koba Ng’a oyore n’omogooko noria bweka ore n’echisemi, rirorio oyio nare n’engencho yogwetogia, naende erio nabo araikaranse n’abanto b’engencho, na korengerigwa koba omonto ogwenerete ase abande.

English: Don’t commend a man for his good looks. Don’t abhor a man for his outward appearance.
Ekegusii: Totogia momura kieni ’motogi nkoro, gose tosiereria omonto ase ekieni kiaye gioka.

English: The bee is little among flying creatures, but what it produces is the best of confections.
Ekegusii: Enchoke n’eyemo ase ebitongire biria ebike bikoiruruka, korende eke gekonyorekana korwa ase emeremo yabo n’egiansu mono kegima.

English: Don’t boast about the clothes you wear, and don’t exalt yourself in the day of honor; for the Lord’s works are wonderful, and his works are hidden among men.
Ekegusii: Tibwetogia ekiagera obegete eanga amaritati, kogunkwara ekero kwairwe amasikani. Oise kogunkwara, Nyasae ngokora are ebikone bi’ogokumia.

English: Many kings have sat down upon the ground, but one who was never thought of has worn a crown.
Ekegusii: Abagaambi abange bakoreire emeremo yabo ase aabe, baikaransete, erio chigutwa chiabo chi’obogambi chibeekire n’abanto batana komanyekana.

English: Many mighty men have been greatly disgraced. Men of renown have been delivered into other men’s hands.
Ekegusii: Abanto baria abanene-abanene baagoranirwe kegima, abanene abange babekirwe chinchera gati-gati y’abanto bande.

English: Don’t blame before you investigate. Understand first, and then rebuke.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kogosia omonto otaramoitona, rengereria ritang’ani, erio omanye komomochia.

English: Don’t answer before you have heard. Don’t interrupt while someone else is speaking.
Ekegusii: Kwarategerera ritang’ani erio kwamanya koiraneria, gose tong’aina onde ekero ogokwana.

English: Don’t argue about a matter that doesn’t concern you. Don’t sit with sinners when they judge.
Ekegusii: Tiga gwesoia ase abande n’amang’ana atakorengeti; tiga gwesoia ase eriomana ri’abanyabibe.

English: My son, don’t be busy about many matters; for if you meddle much, you will not be unpunished. If you pursue, you will not overtake, and you will not escape by fleeing.
Ekegusii: Omwana one, tiga gwechandera amang’ana amaange bosa; riika riaigo, ementere emeremo erio onyare kwebachera emetego yokomochigwa bosa. Notaka kobwatia amang’ana amaange tokoyaikeria, gose tokonyara koyabogerera ase ogotama gwoka.

English: There is one who toils, labors, and hurries, and is even more behind.
Ekegusii: Abanto bande nigo bagokora emeremo ase omokia omonene kegima, korende omoerio oye banyora ng’a nigo bakonakoirana magega kera engaki.

English: There is one who is sluggish, and needs help, lacking in strength, and who abounds in poverty, but the Lord’s eyes looked upon him for good, and he raised him up from his low condition,
Ekegusii: N’abande mbareo batari gokora emeremo yabo ase omokia, abwo baganetie ogokoonya, mbari nagento na nigo baikaranseire n’obotaka. Korende, abwo Omonene Nyasae nigo akobarigereria n’amaabera na kobaimokereria igoro;

English: and lifted up his head so that many marveled at him.
Ekegusii: nigo akobatura na kobaa chinguru erio babe n’enibo. Nonya n’abanto nigo bagochia kobarora goika babakumia kegima.

English: Good things and bad, life and death, poverty and riches, are from the Lord.
Ekegusii: Amaya n’amabe, obogima n’amakweri, obotaka amo n’obokama ebio bionsi nigo bikorwa ase Nyasae.

English: The Lord’s gift remains with the godly. His good pleasure will prosper forever.
Ekegusii: Chisemi, okoigwa okomanya ekerage, obwanchani n’ogokora okuya, ebio bionsi nigo bikorwa ase Nyasae.

English: One grows rich by his diligence and self-denial, and this is the portion of his reward:
Ekegusii: Obobe nomosunte nigo biamenyete nabanyabibe korwa omochakano, na baria bakogokera ebibe nigo baragende nabirobio goika obogotu bwabo.

English: when he says, “I have found rest, and now I will eat of my goods!” he doesn’t know how much time will pass until he leaves them to others and dies.
Ekegusii: Ebigeni bikorwa ase Nyasae igo bire ebiegwa bia kare na kare ase baria bamoirogete. Obuya bwa Nyasae nigo borabeo na kobaraa goika kare na kare.

English: Be steadfast in your covenant and be doing it, and grow old in your work.
Ekegusii: Abanto abange nigo bakoba abakama kobua mono goetera ase ogokora emeremo ase omokia amo n’echinguru, korende eng’eria yabo nero eye;

English: Don’t marvel at the works of a sinner, but trust the Lord and stay in your labor; for it is an easy thing in the sight of the Lord to swiftly and suddenly make a poor man rich.
Ekegusii: nonya bagoteeba ng’a: “Bono ninyare gotimoka na kogokera eng’eria nanyorire,” tibamanyeti ng’a nengaki eng’a ki erabeo; ekiagera nigo barakwe batigere abanto bande enibo yabo.

English: The Lord’s blessing is in the reward of the godly. He makes his blessing flourish in an hour that comes swiftly.
Ekegusii: Aye bwata emeremo yao erio ogote kore ase emeremo yao.

English: Don’t say, “What use is there of me? What further good things can be mine?”
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kororera omonyabibe endamwamu ase biria anyoorire ase enchera etari endonge. Korende moiroke Nyasae na gokora emeremo yao. Ekiagera ase Nyasae amang’ana ayio onsi nigo are amororo kegima ase okomotenenkia omotaka rimo rioka.

English: Don’t say, “I have enough. What harm could happen to me now?”
Ekegusii: Abanto abaya nigo bakonyoora ogosesenigwa korwa ase Nyasae. Omonene nigo akogosesenia rimo rioka.

English: In the day of good things, bad things are forgotten. In the day of bad things, a man will not remember things that are good.
