English: I was exalted like a palm tree on the sea shore, like rose bushes in Jericho, and like a fair olive tree in the plain. I was exalted like a plane tree.
Ekegusii: Ngatambea buna emekendo ya Engedi, buna amaua yobwanchani a Yeriko, buna emesabibu ekogokia erandete ase omogondo, buna emete ye chindeege emerete rooche mbarabare.

English: Like cinnamon and aspalathus, I have given a scent to perfumes. Like choice myrrh, I spread abroad a pleasant fragrance, like galbanum, onycha, stacte, and as the smell of frankincense in the tabernacle.
Ekegusii: Inche ngatioka buya buna ogwansa kwa udi na ubani egotongiwa ase Hekalu.

English: Like the terebinth, I stretched out my branches. My branches are glorious and graceful.
Ekegusii: Buna omoaluni nkarambora chinsagia chiane nokwegokia amo nobwari.

English: Like the vine, I put forth grace. My flowers are the fruit of glory and riches.
Ekegusii: Ingaseboka buna omosabibu na ogosiicha kwane gokarenta okwama kwa amatunda amange.

English: “Come to me, all you who desire me, and be filled with my fruits.
Ekegusii: Inchwo asende mwensi abwo morang’ete morie na koigota amatunda aane.

English: For my memory is sweeter than honey, and my inheritance than the honeycomb.
Ekegusii: Inwe inamoinyore buna obwansu bwane boire obuya buna obooke, ee obosanonoku buna oboke korwa ase amachoe.

English: Those who eat me will be hungry for more. Those who drink me will be thirsty for more.
Ekegusii: Indie na inwe morang’e kegima; inywe inche nainwe ina mondang’e mono.

English: He who obeys me will not be ashamed. Those who work with me will not sin.”
Ekegusii: Oyoranyigwere inche ere tagosookigwa nonya ng’ake, ere oyore nainche tagosoa ase ebibe.

English: All these things are the book of the covenant of the Most High God, the law which Moses commanded us for an inheritance for the assemblies of Jacob.
Ekegusii: Aya onsi namachiiko y’Omonene Nyasae ore igoro, ayio Musa atochiigete koyatunyana. Eyio nereo ensemo abanto b’egesaku kia Yakobo baetwe.

English: It is he who makes wisdom abundant, as Pishon, and as Tigris in the days of first fruits.
Ekegusii: Ogochika nigo gokobanyitororeria abanto obong’aini buna orooche rwa Eyufurate, boigo buna orooche rwa Tigiri ase chingaki chintang’ani chi’okwama amatunda.

English: He makes understanding full as the Euphrates, and as the Jordan in the days of harvest,
Ekegusii: Ogochika nigo gokobaichoria chisemi buna orooche rwa Eyufurate, ee buna orooche rwa Yorodani ase chingaki chi’erigesa.

English: who makes instruction shine forth as the light, as Gihon in the days of vintage.
Ekegusii: Nigo rigokora amorokererio yamesa buna risase, buna Gihoni ase chingaki chi’ogotora amasabibu.

English: The first man didn’t know her perfectly. In like manner, the last has not explored her.
Ekegusii: Omonto bw’eritang’ani tanyaarete komanya obong’aini boronge, boigo omonto bw’omoerio takonyaara komomanya.

English: For her thoughts are filled from the sea, and her counsels from the great deep.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera ebirengererio biaye nebinge buna amaache y’enyaancha nogotebereria kwaye nigo kobwate obotambe kobua endiba ya amaache are inse yense.

English: I came out as a canal stream from a river, and as an irrigation ditch into a garden.
Ekegusii: Inche nigo nesogetie buna emberesi ya amaache agosiarerwa mogondo.

English: I said, “I will water my garden, and will drench my garden bed.” Behold, my stream became a river, and my river became a sea.
Ekegusii: Ingateeba, “Inche ninyaare konyonsia amatunda y’omogondo one na goichoria emetaro yaye.” Rora omomberesi one okaba orooche, na orooche rwane rokaba enyancha.

English: I will yet bring instruction to light as the morning, and will make these things clear from far away.
Ekegusii: Bono ninyaare komesia amorokererio aane buna ogotonga kw’erioba, ninyamesie arabe goika aare.

English: I will continue to pour out teaching like prophecy, and leave it to all generations.
Ekegusii: Naende ninyaare gotononkeria amorokererio aane buna obobani erio mbotigere ebiare bigochia goocha.

English: See that I have not labored for myself only, but for all those who diligently seek wisdom.
Ekegusii: Komoranche inwe inyora buna inche tinakorete emeremo eyio yonsi ase ogwekorera inche omonyene; korende buna inyare gokoonya onde bwensi origetie kworokererigwa obong’aini.

English: I enjoy three things, and they are beautiful before the Lord and men: the agreement of kindred, the friendship of neighbors, and a woman and her husband who walk together in agreement.
Ekegusii: Enkoro yane nigo egokerete amang’ana atato; amang’ana ayio are amaya ase obosio bw’Omonene na Mwanyabaanto: ekero abanto bare abamwabo baigwanaine, abanto basinyaine bare noboamate obuya, na omokungu n’omosaacha oye bamenyete n’omogooko.

English: But my soul hates three sorts of people, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man who is arrogant, a rich man who is a liar, and an old fool who is an adulterer.
Ekegusii: Enkoro yane nigo egechete abanto be chingencho isato, abanto abwo bagechirie nobogima bwabo; abasabereri abetakoori, omonda omonyaborimo, na omogaka omonyaka otari na semi.

English: If you gathered nothing in your youth, how could you find anything in your old age?
Ekegusii: Onye tikwanyaarete korogota gento kende kiogosemia ekero kwarenge omosae, inaki oranyaare konyoora egento ase obogotu bwao?

English: How beautiful a thing is judgment in the gray-haired, and for elders to know good counsel!
Ekegusii: Nering’ana rigiya ase omogaka ore ne chimbuche igoro ase omotwe oye goetia ayare amaya nere oria ore n’emiaka emenge komanya buna agoteebereria.

English: How beautiful is the wisdom of old men, and understanding and counsel to men who are in honor!
Ekegusii: Obong’aini ase abagaaka, amorokererio agwenerete, na boigo amorokererio korwa ase abasike nering’ana rigiya kegima.

English: Much experience is the crown of the aged. Their glory is the fear of the Lord.
Ekegusii: Abanto abagotu nigo babegete egutwa yobomanyi, nogwetogia kwabo nase okomoiroka Omonene.

English: There are nine things that I have thought of, and in my heart counted happy, and the tenth I will utter with my tongue: a man who has joy with his children, and a man who lives and sees the fall of his enemies.
Ekegusii: Inche nimbateebie amang’ana kianda ayio angogetie ase omoyo one, ee nerinde ria ikomi boigo nimbariteebie: omonto ogogete ase engencho ya abana baye, omonto oyio okomenya goika orora ababisa baye bagochandeka na gosira,

English: Happy is he who dwells with a wife of understanding, he who has not slipped with his tongue, and he who has not served a man who is unworthy of him.
Ekegusii: omosacha ore negesio giokomenya nomokuungu ore nechiseemi, ere oria otari koremia chiombe amo nechitigere ase omogondo oye, ere oria otana korentererwa noromeme rwaye, omonto otari gokorera omonto otaisaini,

English: Happy is he who has found prudence, and he who speaks in the ears of those who listen.
Ekegusii: omonto ore negesio giokonyoora omosani omwegenwa, boigo omonto oria abanto bakogooka komotegerera.

English: How great is he who has found wisdom! Yet there is none greater than one who fears the Lord.
Ekegusii: Inaki ere engencho enene omonto konyoora obong’aini! Korende tai aroro omonto omonene buna oria omoirogete Omonene!

English: The fear of the Lord surpasses all things. To whom shall he who holds it be likened?
Ekegusii: Omonto omoirogete Omonene tabwati ekerengo. Okomoiroka Omonene nigo kobuete amang’ana onsi.

English: Any wound but a wound of the heart! Any wickedness but the wickedness of a woman!
Ekegusii: Tiriri riote ribe buna riote rienkoro! Tiboiyo obobe buna obobe bw’omokuungu!

English: Any calamity but a calamity from those who hate me! Any vengeance but the vengeance of enemies!
Ekegusii: Tikori ogoakwa okonene buna okw’omonto ore n’obororo. Tikori ogoakana egesiomba okobe buna koria kogokorwa n’omobisa.

English: There is no venom worse than a snake’s venom. There is no wrath worse than an enemy’s wrath.
Ekegusii: Tibori obosongo obobe buna obw’eng’iti na tikeri ekeririanda ekebe buna ekeririanda kiomobisa.

English: I would rather dwell with a lion and a dragon than keep house with a wicked woman.
Ekegusii: Nigo ere aororo komenya n’endo amo n’eng’iti kobua komenya n’omokuungu omobe.

English: The wickedness of a woman changes her appearance, and darkens her countenance like that of a bear.
Ekegusii: Obobe bw’omokuungu nigo b’ogosaria ekieni kiaye, obosio bwaye bwaba buna obw’etokoro.

English: Her husband will sit among his neighbors, and when he hears it, he sighs bitterly.
Ekegusii: Omosacha oye ekero akoria endagera bw’omoamate takomocha goita egekoe nobororo.

English: All malice is small compared to the malice of a woman. Let the portion of a sinner fall on her.
Ekegusii: Tibori obobe obonene buna obw’omokuungu bw’omonto; oyio nanyorwe n’obokong’u bwa abanyene ebibe.

English: As walking up a sandy hill is to the feet of the aged, so is a wife full of words to a quiet man.
Ekegusii: Omosacha omwororo komenya nomokuungu omonyariogi nabo egwekaine emechaando omogaka omogotu akonyoora ase okoriina egetunwa kere n’omosere bw’amaroba.

English: Don’t be ensnared by a woman’s beauty. Don’t desire a woman for her beauty.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kobwatwa nobonyakieni bwo omokungu gose gosanera obotenenku bw’omokuungu.

English: There is anger, impudence, and great reproach if a woman supports her husband.
Ekegusii: Ekero omosacha akoraagerigwa n’omokuungu oye, nigo akomenya ase obosooku, obororo na ogochaaya.

English: A wicked woman is abasement of heart, sadness of countenance, and a wounded heart. A woman who won’t make her husband happy is like hands that hang down, and weak knees.
Ekegusii: Enkoro echaandegete, koborwa omosasoko boigo gokwa omoyo nigo bikorentwa n’omokuungu omobe. Omokungu otari komogokia omosacha oye ere nigo akorenta okobuneka chinengo amo nokogoya kw’amaboko ase omosacha oye.

English: The beginning of sin came from a woman. Because of her, we all die.
Ekegusii: Ebibe nigo biarentetwe nomokuungu na ase engencho yaye goika intwe twensi tokwe.

English: Don’t give water an outlet, and don’t give a wicked woman freedom of speech.
Ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana ogotanga ekerama kegotwa tikegoiterera amaache, boigo tobaisa komwanchera omokungu omobe gokwana buna ere anchete.

English: If she doesn’t go as you direct, cut her away from your flesh.
Ekegusii: Onye ere tagokora buna okomoteebia, moserie arue asore.

English: Happy is the husband of a good wife. The number of his days will be doubled.
Ekegusii: Omosacha ore nomokuungu omuya nare negesio; ere namenye emiaka ara kabere ase engencho yaye.

English: A faithful wife gives joy to her husband. He will fulfill his years in peace.
Ekegusii: Omokungu omwegenwa nigo are omogooko ase omosacha oye; omosacha oyio nigo aramenye nomorembe emiaka yaye yonsi.

English: A good wife is a great gift. She will be given to those who fear the Lord.
Ekegusii: Omokungu omuya nekemo kiebiegwa ebiya biogosesenia bakoegwa baria bamoirogete Omonene.

English: Whether a man is rich or poor, a good heart makes a cheerful face at all times.
Ekegusii: Omonto buna oyio abe omotaka gose omonda, ase obogima bwaye bwonsi nigo akomenya nomorembe ase omoyo oye; na ase ebiro bionsi nigo are nobosio bosasogete.

English: Of three things my heart was afraid, and concerning the fourth kind I made supplication: The slander of a city, the assembly of a mob, and a false accusation. All these are more grievous than death.
Ekegusii: Enkoro yane nigo eirogete amang’ana atato, ne ria kane nigo rikongosa; chinkuma chimbe ime yomochie, omosangererekano bwa abanto ababe, na ogosoera kw’oborimo. Aya onsi nigo are amabe kobua amakweri.

English: A grief of heart and sorrow is a woman who is jealous of another woman. Her tongue-lashing makes it known to all.
Ekegusii: Korende nigo ere ring’ana riogoichania ekero omokungu oyomo agotwara ribero ase oyonde na gotwara oromeme rogosiarokera kera omonto.

English: A wicked woman is like a chafing yoke. He who takes hold of her is like one who grasps a scorpion.
Ekegusii: Omokungu omobe nabo anga richoki rigosionora rigoti, goteema komogambera nabo enga kobogoria riagaga rire nobosongo.

English: A drunken woman causes great wrath. She will not cover her own shame.
Ekegusii: Omokungu omotindu nigo akorenta obororo ekiagera ere tari konyara gokengera chinsoni chiaye.

English: The fornication of a woman is in the lifting up of her eyes; it will be known by her eyelids.
Ekegusii: Omokungu omotayayi nigo akororekana ase amaiso aye naende nigo akomanyekana ase ebioge biaye.

English: Keep strict watch on a headstrong daughter, lest she find liberty for herself, and use it.
Ekegusii: Kabe omotindi ase omoiseke oo okorigia gotwara obosibore bwaye omonyene, otakoreti boigo, nigo aresarie ase akabaga agake.

English: Watch out for an impudent eye, and don’t be surprised if it sins against you.
Ekegusii: Erende na amaiso aye atari n’obosooku naende tibwegosa ekero arakorentere obosooku.

English: She will open her mouth like a thirsty traveller, and drink from every water that is near. She will sit down at every post, and open her quiver to any arrow.
Ekegusii: Ere naigore ebinama biaye ande onsi ase kera omonto omotagete buna omoeti ore nerang’o agwasamerera ase okonywa amaache ande onsi agoeta.

English: The grace of a wife will delight her husband. Her knowledge will strengthen his bones.
Ekegusii: Omokungu omuya nigo akomogookia omosacha oye na obomanyi bwaye bwamokora omosacha oye koba chinguru.

English: A silent woman is a gift of the Lord. There is nothing worth so much as a well-instructed soul.
Ekegusii: Omokungu omokiriru nekeegwa korwa ase Omonene na tiriyo rigori riranyaare koreng’anigwa nere.

English: A modest woman is grace upon grace. There are no scales that can weigh the value of a self-controlled soul.
Ekegusii: Omokungu ore nekerengo nigo akomenta koba omonyakieni, kerengo kierigori tikeiyo keranyaare korengerwa omokungu oyio.

English: As the sun when it arises in the highest places of the Lord, so is the beauty of a good wife in her well-organized home.
Ekegusii: Ekieni kiomokuungu omuya nobochenu bw’enyomba yaye nigo binga ogosaseria kwe risase igoro ase erioba ri’Omonene.

English: As the lamp that shines upon the holy lampstand, so is the beauty of the face on a well-proportioned body.
Ekegusii: Naende buna etaya egwoka igoro ase ekebekerero gi’echitaaya ase hekalu.

English: As the golden pillars are upon a base of silver, so are beautiful feet with the breasts of one who is steadfast.
Ekegusii: Buna emetobwa yetaabu, igoro ase ebikaransero biaye bw’echifeta, nabo ere emerondo yaye emeronge igoro ase amagoro aye.

English: For two things my heart is grieved, and for the third anger comes upon me: a warrior who suffers for poverty, men of understanding who are counted as garbage, and one who turns back from righteousness to sin— the Lord will prepare him for the sword!
Ekegusii: Nareo amang’ana abere akong’ichania ase enkoro yane, nering’ana ria gatato rikombeyia: omosigari otari na besa, abanto abang’aini bachaayire, nomonto ogotiga oboronge ochaaka gokora amabe. Omonene nigo aramoe egesusuro n’omoro.

English: It is difficult for a merchant to keep himself from wrong doing, and for a retailer to be acquitted of sin.
Ekegusii: Nakong’u mono ase omoonchoreria gocharoka amamocho, na omoonia kwebacha korwa ase ebibe.

English: Many have sinned for profit. He who seeks to multiply wealth will turn his eye away.
Ekegusii: Abanto abange bakorire ebibe ase okorigia ebitoki; oyotagete koba omotenenku nemogwenerete arende amaiso aye.

English: As a nail will stick fast between the joinings of stones, so sin will thrust itself in between buying and selling.
Ekegusii: Buna ere akong’u korusia egesigisa gekong’onteire ase egati ya amagena ase enyomba, boigo nakong’u korusia obong’ainereria korwa ase okogora n’okoonia.

English: Unless a person holds on diligently to the fear of the Lord, his house will be overthrown quickly.
Ekegusii: Monto onde bwensi otatunyaneti okomoiroka Omonene, enyomba yaye nesirigwe keri keri.

English: In the shaking of a sieve, the refuse remains, so does the filth of man in his thoughts.
Ekegusii: Buna egechunchugo gekorusia eogoto, naboigo amang’ana akorwa ase omonwa bw’omonto agocheng’enenia amamocho aye.

English: The furnace tests the potter’s vessels; so the test of a person is in his thoughts.
Ekegusii: Buna eriko rikorenga emeremo yomokori chinyongo, naboigo chinkwana chikomorenga omonto.

English: The fruit of a tree discloses its cultivation, so is the utterance of the thought of a person’s heart.
Ekegusii: Buna okwama kw’amatunda gokoorokia buna omote orendire, naboigo amang’ana akorwa ase omonto akomororekania.

English: Praise no man before you hear his thoughts, for this is how people are tested.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa komotogia omonto otaragamba nere ekiagera omonto nigo akorengwa na amang’ana aria agokwana.

English: If you follow righteousness, you will obtain it, and put it on like a long robe of glory.
Ekegusii: Ekero oraganie koba omuya nabo ogoikerania koba omuya, naboigo kweboyia obuya buna rituko riomochengo.

English: Birds will return to their own kind, so truth will return to those who practice it.
Ekegusii: Kera enyoni nigo egotunyana chinyoni chi’omogwekano oye, naboigo nekeene kegotunyana baria bakogeikerania.

English: The lion lies in wait for prey. So does sin for those who do evil.
Ekegusii: Buna endo ekoboera ching’iti chiria egotwara, naboigo ebibe bikoboera abakori amabe.

English: The discourse of a godly man is always wise, but the fool changes like the moon.
Ekegusii: Chinkwana chi’abaanto bamoirogete Omonene nigo chire nobong’aini botambe, korende abariri nigo bakoonchoka buna omotienyi.

English: Limit your time among people void of understanding, but persevere among the thoughtful.
Ekegusii: Ekero orenyore ase egati ya abanto abariri aye karue aroro,; korende obere ase egati yabaanto abang’aini.

English: The talk of fools is offensive. Their laughter is wantonly sinful.
Ekegusii: Chinkwana chi’abaanto abariri nokogechia, ogoseka kwabo noboriania bw’ebibe.

English: Their talk with much swearing makes hair stand upright. Their strife makes others plug their ears.
Ekegusii: Ogokwana kwabo nigo kogokora bwegose kegima na okoamererania kwabo nigo gokomokora omonto goticha amato.

English: The strife of the proud leads to bloodshed. Their abuse of each other is a grievous thing to hear.
Ekegusii: Eriomana riabaanto abetogia nigo rikorenta ogoitana, nokorama kwabo nigo kore obosooku kogotegerera.

English: He who reveals secrets destroys trust, and will not find a close friend.
Ekegusii: Omonto okorwa obobisi nigo ere agosiria obwegenwa bwonsi, na ase obogima bwaye bwonsi takonyoora omosaani omoganetie.

English: Love a friend, and keep faith with him; but if you reveal his secrets, you shall not follow him;
Ekegusii: Ancha omosaani na obe omwegenwa ase are, korende onye kogosokia obobisi bwaye, tobaisa gotaara nere naende.

English: for as a man has destroyed his enemy, so you have destroyed the friendship of your neighbor.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera buna omonto agosiria omobisa, naye boigo gwasaririe obosaani nomoamate oo.

English: As a bird which you have released out of your hand, so you have let your neighbor go, and you will not catch him again.
Ekegusii: Buna ere enyoni etairane gocha koboko kwao ekero yaminchoirie, naboigo tokomonyoora omosaani oo naende.

English: Don’t pursue him, for he has gone far away, and has escaped like a gazelle out of the snare.
Ekegusii: Tomotunyana ekiagera ere ochiire are mono, ere ominyokire buna egesia kiaminchoirie korwa ase omotego.

English: For a wound may be bound up, and after abuse there may be reconciliation; but he who reveals secrets is without hope.
Ekegusii: Riote nabo riragwenigwe, na okoramwa kwaberwe; korende, oria osokirie obobisi tabaisa gosemeria kende gionsi.

English: One who winks the eye contrives evil things; and those who know him will keep their distance.
Ekegusii: Omonto okogosumera amaiso nigo arigetie gokora amabe, naende onde taiyo oranyaare komoremereria.

English: When you are present, he will speak sweetly, and will admire your words; but afterward he will twist his speech and set a trap in your words.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto oyio are ase ore aye, nigo agokwana amang’ana amansu naende nigo akogookera aria aye okomoteebia. Korende ere nigo araonchore chinkwana chiaye na kogotega ase amang’ana ao.

English: I have hated many things, but nothing like him. The Lord will hate him.
Ekegusii: Ase obogima bwane bwonsi ningeechete amang’ana amange korende inche tingecheti ing’ana rinde rionsi buna ingeechete omonto onga buna oyio, Omonene boigo nigo amogeechete.

English: One who casts a stone straight up casts it on his own head. A deceitful blow opens wounds.
Ekegusii: Omonto okoruta rigena gochia igoro nigo akoriruta igoro ase omotwe oye omonyene. Oyoogoaka chinkundi nigo akweremaria ere omonyene.

English: He who digs a pit will fall into it. He who sets a snare will be caught in it.
Ekegusii: Oyokorema engoro nigo akogwa ime ere omonyene, naboigo oria ogotega omotego nigo ere akobwatwa nomotego oria.

English: He who does evil things, they will roll back upon him, and he will not know where they came from.
Ekegusii: Omonto ogokorera abande bobe, ere nanyorwe nobobe naboigo takomanya ase obobe obwo bokomoruera.

English: Mockery and reproach are from the arrogant. Vengeance lies in wait for them like a lion.
Ekegusii: Omonto omwerori nigo akorama na gochaaya, korende egesusuro nigo kemoganyete buna endo.

English: Those who rejoice at the fall of the godly will be caught in a snare. Anguish will consume them before they die.
Ekegusii: Baria bakogookera okogwa kwa baria bamoirogete Omonene, barabwo ina babwatwe nomotego naende ina banyoore obosareru obonene barabwo batarakwa.

English: Wrath and anger, these also are abominations. A sinner will possess them.
Ekegusii: Ekeririanda n’okoberoroka nigo bire ebinto ebibe, korende abakori amabe nigo babibogoretie ebio bionsi.

English: He who takes vengeance will find vengeance from the Lord, and he will surely make his sins firm.
Ekegusii: Ere oyogoakana egesiomba nere naakanwe n’Omonene, n’Omonene naenekie buna omonto oyio nare nebibe.

English: Forgive your neighbor the hurt that he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.
Ekegusii: Mwabere omogisangio oo ase amamocho agokoreire, naye ekero ogosaba inabwaberwe amamocho ao.

English: Does anyone harbor anger against another and expect healing from the Lord?
Ekegusii: Onye omonto okomenya nekeririanda ase oyomwabo, inaki ere araganie Omonene amwabere amororere amaabera?

English: Upon a man like himself he has no mercy, and does he make supplication for his own sins?
Ekegusii: Onye omonto takororera oyomwabo amaabera, inee, omonto oyio nanyare gosaba Nyasae erio nere anyare komwabera ebibe biaye?

English: He himself, being flesh, nourishes wrath. Who will make atonement for his sins?
Ekegusii: Onye oyio ore egetongire bosa, okogacha obobe ase obororo rirorio oyio takonyora amaabera korwa ase Omonene.

English: Remember your last end, and stop enmity. Remember corruption and death, and be true to the commandments.
Ekegusii: Inyora iga! Omoerio bw’obogima bwao erio otige obobisa bwao.

English: Remember the commandments, and don’t be angry with your neighbor. Remember the covenant of the Highest, and overlook ignorance.
Ekegusii: Ebache korwa ase amang’ana okonakwamererania. Ekiagera okwo nigo korarete obobisa bw’amakweri, inyora ebirage.

English: Abstain from strife, and you will diminish your sins, for a passionate man will kindle strife.
Ekegusii: Ebachere korwa ase eriomana, erio nario otakore ekebe. Ekiagera omonto ore n’obororo nigo akereta eriomana.

English: A man who is a sinner will trouble friends and sow discord among those who are at peace.
Ekegusii: Omonyabibe nigo agosaria obosani gati y’abanto na kobeekera obobisa ase bare

English: As is the fuel of the fire, so it will burn; and as the stoutness of the strife is, so it will burn. As is the strength of the man, so will be his wrath; and as is his wealth, so he will exalt his anger.
Ekegusii: Koreng’a buna obwate chinko ching’ana na buna okoigereria ang’ana nabo n’omorero okoba ong’ana, nobigo koreng’ana buna okoamaereania kogendererete ang’ana n’eriomana narirorio riraabe ring’ana. Koreng’ana buna omonto are omonene ang’ana, naboigo nere aranyare koba n’obororo obonge. Koreng’ana buna omonto akona koba omotenenku, buna akogenrera koba n’obororo obonene.

English: A contention begun in haste kindles a fire; and hasty fighting sheds blood.
Ekegusii: Okona kwomana nonya mbosa igo nigo kogoseta amang’ana amake koba amaneene go gwaitera n’onya n’amanyinga.

English: If you blow on a spark, it will burn; and if you spit upon it, it will be quenched. Both of these come out of your mouth.
Ekegusii: Onye kogouterera riakara ’omorero nigo rigwoka mono kegima, korende oise koritwera amate nabo rikorima. Ayio onsi

English: Curse the whisperer and double-tongued, for he has destroyed many who were at peace.
Ekegusii: Oragererigwe omonto ore omogenki naende omorimo, ekiagera osiririe abanto abange abwo bamenyete are okwegena.

English: A slanderer has shaken many, and dispersed them from nation to nation. It has pulled down strong cities and overthrown the houses of great men.
Ekegusii: Obogima bw’abange bwasarekire naende baserigwe korwa ase chinka chiabo ase engencho y’abanto bagosoanana n’emeroberio yabo. Ogosoanana buna okwo kwagerire emechie emenene n’echinka chi’abanto bamasikani gosarigwa.

English: A slanderer has cast out brave women and deprived them of their labors.
Ekegusii: Abagenki bagerire abakungu abaya goserigwa n’abasaacha baabo, na kobaura amatunda y’ebigeri biabo.

English: He who listens to it will not find rest, nor will he live quietly.
Ekegusii: Onde bwensi ogotegerera omonto omogenki, oyio takoba n’omorembe rinde, gose takomenya n’omorembe.

English: The stroke of a whip makes a mark in the flesh, but the stroke of a tongue will break bones.
Ekegusii: Ogoakwa kw’omocharichi nigo kogotiga emekirimbi, ko bono, ogoakwa kw’oromeme nigo gokobuna-buna amauga.

English: Many have fallen by the edge of the sword, yet not so many as those who have fallen because of the tongue.
Ekegusii: Abanto abange bakuure okoba omoro, ko bono, abange bakuure ase oromeme.

English: Happy is he who is sheltered from it, who has not passed through its wrath, who has not drawn its yoke, and has not been bound with its bands.
Ekegusii: Mbuya ase omonto kogingwa korwa ase oromeme, n’omonto otaragamberwa n’obororo bwaye. Omonto orabogoria richoki rie’chuma ase ebigoti biaye gose, ogosibwa n’echinyororo ase amagoro aye.

English: For its yoke is a yoke of iron, and its bands are bands of brass.
Ekegusii: Nare n’egesio omonto ogingire korwa ase omorero oyio. Omonto oyio otari koorokia obororo Bwaye.

English: Its death is an evil death, and Hades is better than it.
Ekegusii: Amakweri akoretwa n’emeroberio emebe n’amakweri amabe, mbuya nokwa kobua gokorerwa emeroberio emebe.

English: It will not have rule over godly men. They will not be burned in its flame.
Ekegusii: Korende, obogenki tibokonyara kogambera abanto bamoirogete Nyasae, abwo tibagosambwa n’omorero oye.

English: Those who forsake the Lord will fall into it. It will burn among them, and won’t be quenched. It will be sent against them like a lion. It will destroy them like a leopard.
Ekegusii: Baria bakogenda mamincha y’Omonene nigo baragwe ase omotego bw’omorero oyio; nigo barabe ’nse y’obogaambi bwaye. Obogenki nigo borabe ime yabo korende omorero oyio tokorimeka. Obogambi obwo ng’a bobatogonyere bun’Endo na bobataborane buna egwachi.

English: As you hedge your possession about with thorns, and secure your silver and your gold,
Ekegusii: Enekia ng’a kwabekire orwaki roetanane enibo yao, enekia ng’a gwasiekeire chitaabu chiao.

English: so make a balance and a weight for your words, and make a door and a bar for your mouth.
Ekegusii: Enekia ng’akwagiteire enibo yao n’amagwa.

English: Take heed lest you slip with it, lest you fall before one who lies in wait.
Ekegusii: Renda tobaisa kogochwa oromeme, onye taibo nigo oragochwe bosio bw’abaanto n’amang’ana ao ayeye omonye.

English: He who shows mercy will lend to his neighbor. He who strengthens him with his hand keeps the commandments.
Ekegusii: Omonto ore n’amaabera nigo akoa oyomwabo singo; gokoonya omwamate oo okwo nakwo oikerania ebirage.

English: Lend to your neighbor in time of his need. Repay your neighbor on time.
Ekegusii: Kae omoamate oo singo ekero are n’okogania kwogokoonywa, n’ekero ogosaba singo, iraneria omonyene ase obwango.

English: Confirm your word, and keep faith with him; and at all seasons you will find what you need.
Ekegusii: Onye kogoikerania emeremo ekorengete, rirorio nabo okonyara gosaba singo, n’oyio ogosaba singo ase okogania kwao ng’a goikeranigwe kera engaki.

English: Many have considered a loan to be a windfall, and have given trouble to those who helped them.
Ekegusii: Abanto bande nigo bakagete ng’a ogosaba egento singo n’ekeegwa, na koretera obosooku baria babarierete eira.

English: Until he has received, he will kiss a man’s hands. For his neighbor’s money he will speak submissively. Then when payment is due, he will prolong the time, return excuses, and complain about the season.
Ekegusii: Omonto nanyunyunte okoboko kw’omonto onde goiko omoire singo, erio ochaka komonyerera abande igoro y’obotenenku bw’omoamate oye. Korende ase engaki y’ogoakana esira nario erio orache komanya. Oyio nigo arakane ase okwemurungania okonge mono na kwerora ng’a taetwa chingaki chisaine.

English: If he prevails, the creditor will hardly receive half; and he will count it as a windfall. If not, he has deprived him of his money, and he has gotten him for an enemy without cause. He will pay him with cursing and railing. Instead of honor, he will pay him disgrace.
Ekegusii: Naende naisa komwaakana, nigo aranya komoa ’nkenke, ekiagera omosabi singo tari oyo bogwaakana. Onye tari konyara gwaakana omonyene singo, oyio rirorio omoibeire, naende obeire rirorio omobisare bw’oria omoete singo. Gose amoakane ase okoraama na koragereria; ribaga riokomosika nigo akomoakana ase okomochecheria.

English: Many on account of fraud have turned away. They are afraid of being defrauded for nothing.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho eyio abange tibarigetie gokabesa, nigo baoboete koriananigwa.

English: However be patient with a man in poor estate. Don’t keep him waiting for your alms.
Ekegusii: Nonya nabo, kabe omoremereria ase omonto omotaka, gose tomotiga aganye ogokoonya kwao ase egeka egetaambe.

English: Help a poor man for the commandment’s sake. According to his need don’t send him empty away.
Ekegusii: Koonya omonto omotaka keria agaanetie ekiagera erio nario richiiko, tomotiga agende amaboko amasa.

English: Lose your money for a brother and a friend. Don’t let it rust under a stone and be lost.
Ekegusii: Korera chifeta chiao emeremo na ase ogokoonya omwana omino gose omosani oo, gose tobaisa gotiga ebesa yao eboosere abwo ase oyebisete.

English: Allocate your treasure according to the commandments of the Most High and it will profit you more than gold.
Ekegusii: Kora emeremo ase obotenenku bwao koreng’ana n’ogochika kwa Nyasae erio naye n’onyore eng’eria ase obogima bwao kobua chitaabu.

English: Store up almsgiving in your store-chambers and it will deliver you out of all affliction.
Ekegusii: Ichoria ekegancha kiao ase okoa abataka, eyio nero eng’eria eragotoorie ase chingaki chigwenerete.

English: It will fight for you against your enemy better than a mighty shield and a ponderous spear.
Ekegusii: Eng’eria eyio n’ekorwanerere bosio bw’omobisa oo, buya kobua enguba yo’gokumia amo n’eritimo ririto.

English: A good man will be surety for his neighbor. He who has lost shame will fail him.
Ekegusii: Omonto omuya nabo arabe ’ntenenera ase omwamate oye. Korende omonto otari na bosoku nabo akomotiga gochia abuo igo

English: Don’t forget the kindness of your guarantor, for he has given his life for you.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kueba obuya bw’onto okobereire ’ntenenera, ekiagera oyio obekire obogima bwaye akong’u okoba aye.

English: A sinner will waste the property of his guarantor.
Ekegusii: Korende ase omonto omokori amabe, nigo agosaria obotenenku bw’oria omoberete ’ntenenera, omonto atari korora ng’a n’egento kiengecho goaka ng’a mbuya mono, oyio nigo agotiga oria omokoonyete.

English: He who is thankless will fail him who delivered him.
Ekegusii: Okobeka egento ’ntenenera gwaitire abanto abatenenku abange, na kwabanyegeirie buna omwaga omorito.

English: Being surety has undone many who were prospering and shaken them as a wave of the sea. It has driven mighty men from their homes. They wandered among foreign nations.
Ekegusii: Kobeka egento ’ntenenera kwabekire abanto abange b’engencho komenya buna abatami, abanto abwo nigo bakona koombogana ase chingongo chiande.

English: A sinner who falls into suretiship and undertakes contracts for work will fall into lawsuits.
Ekegusii: Omonyabibe ogwancha koba omoteneneri o singo n’erorere amang’ana amakong’u, naarigie eng’eria ko bono tanyenyora, nigo arenyore ase obokong’u n’erichiko.

English: Help your neighbor according to your power, and be careful not to fall yourself.
Ekegusii: Mokonye omwamate oo buna oranyare, korende bwerende kegima erio tobaisa kogochwa na kogwa ase amakweri.

English: The essentials of life are water, bread, a garment, and a house for privacy.
Ekegusii: Okogania okonene kw’obogima na amache, chiaanga amo n’enyomba ase oranyare kwebisa.

English: Better is the life of a poor man under a shelter of logs than sumptuous fare in another man’s house.
Ekegusii: Mbuya koba omotaka kore n’enyomba yao omonyene, kobua koba n’endagera buna ey’abanda nyomba mwabande.

English: With little or with much, be well satisfied.
Ekegusii: Isaneka n’egeke ekio ore nakio, erio nario abanto batanyagokwemurunganeria ng’a nigo bwanche ebinto biabo na koria ebigeri biabande.

English: It is a miserable life to go from house to house. Where you are a guest, you dare not open your mouth.
Ekegusii: Nigo ere egento kiobosoku koombogana korwa enyomba gochia eyende, aande onsi ase ore omogeni tokoigora monwa oo.

English: You will entertain, serve drinks, and have no thanks. In addition to this, you will hear bitter words.
Ekegusii: Nigo okoarigania omogeni kwaboa ekenyugwa, na onde tari okogoakera ng’a mbuya mono. Korende abanto nigo bagokwana amang’ana yokogechia buna

English: “Come here, you sojourner, set a table, and if you have anything in your hand, feed me with it.”
Ekegusii: “Aye omorwa isiko! Inchwo gocha igi gaaiga oariganie emesa! Na onye kore na gento ng’aa ndie.

English: “Leave, you sojourner, for an honored guest is here. My brother has come to be my guest. I need my house.”
Ekegusii: Kore omogeni genda bwoo erio omotigerere omonto bw’engencho. Momura omonto ngochare bwone aiga ninde nokogania kw’eribaga ase enyomba yane.”

English: These things are grievous to a man of understanding: The scolding about lodging and the insults of creditors.
Ekegusii: Ekero okorinwa oboraro na koramwa igoro y’oboraro, ayio tari koremerereka ase omonto ore n’obong’aini.

English: He who loves his son will continue to lay stripes upon him, that he may have joy from him in the end.
Ekegusii: Omoibori bwanchete omwano oye nigo akomogambera n’ekeranya engaki ase engaki, erio anyare komwetogeria ekero akinire.

English: He who chastises his son will have profit from him, and will brag about him among his acquaintances.
Ekegusii: Oyo okogaambera momura oye ekio n’egento kiengencho kegima, oyio ng’anyore eng’eria yaye korwa ase are. Onyio ng’anyera gwetogeria omwana oye maiso marore.

English: He who teaches his son will provoke his enemy to jealousy. Before friends, he will rejoice in him.
Ekegusii: Omonto okworokereria omwana oye nigo akogera ababisa baye bamoigwera endamwamu, na kogwetogeria omwana oye bosio bw’abasani baye.

English: His father dies, and is as though he had not died; for he has left one behind him like himself.
Ekegusii: Ekero omoibori oyio are moyo nigo akwegokeria omwana oye, nonya n’ekero ise akuure nigo arabe buna oyotakweti; ekiagera otigire omomura omobwekaine.

English: In his life, he saw his son and rejoiced. When he died, it was without regret.
Ekegusii: Ekero ise arenge moyo, nigo agokirie nere, n’ekero ise akuure tari koba n’ogokumia.

English: He left behind him an avenger against his enemies, and one to repay kindness to his friends.
Ekegusii: Otigire omonto orenge gocha goakana ababisa baye egesiomba magega, nere oyio oraakane abasani baye amaya.

English: He who makes too much of his son will bind up his wounds. His heart will be troubled at every cry.
Ekegusii: Omonto okworokia omwana oye amabe, nigo arabe n’emeremo y’okoboerera amaote, na ase kera ekere ase omoyo oye nigo kerakogose bose.

English: An unbroken horse becomes stubborn. An unrestrained son becomes headstrong.
Ekegusii: Ebarasi yorokererigwe bobe nigo ekoba eng’enenenu, n’omwana otarokoreirie chingencho chingiya nigo araonchoke koba omoenenenu.

English: Pamper your child, and he will make you afraid. Play with him, and he will grieve you.
Ekegusii: Onakwebereria omwana oo, nere nakoirianyekie, konagokora echeche amo nere nagere oirianyeke.

English: Don’t laugh with him, lest you have sorrow with him, and you gnash your teeth in the end.
Ekegusii: Onye tibwancheti omonto takonagosekaseka nakoragera nere; omoerio oye nigo n’agochande goika oche korianania amoino.

English: Give him no liberty in his youth, and don’t ignore his follies.
Ekegusii: Totiga omonto akore buna aganetie ekero are omwana, naende gose totiga komogororora ekero akorire bobe.

English: Bow down his neck in his youth, and beat him on the sides while he is a child, lest he become stubborn, and be disobedient to you, and there be sorrow to your soul.
Ekegusii: Aaka omwana ebiranya kare omoke, onye taibo, nigo araenene erio atige gokoigwera, arabaisa kogochanda omoyo.

English: Chastise your son, and give him work, lest his shameless behavior be an offense to you.
Ekegusii: Orokereria omwana oo chimbu chingiya erio abe omoremereria, erio tobaisa konyora obosooku korwa ase oboriri bwaye.

English: Better is a poor man who is healthy and fit, than a rich man who is afflicted in his body.
Ekegusii: Mbuya koba omotaka, korende kore n’obuya bw’omobere n’echinguru, kobua koba omotenenku korende ochandegete n’amarwaire ase omobere oye.

English: Health and fitness are better than all gold, and a strong body better than wealth without measure.
Ekegusii: Obuya bw’omobere n’echinguru n’ebiya kobua amagena ’amaabera; omobere ore n’echinguru n’omuya kobua obotenenku obonge.

English: There is no wealth better than health of body. There is no gladness above the joy of the heart.
Ekegusii: Botenenku tibori bore obuya kobua obuya bw’omobere, na mogooko tori ore omuya kobua omogooko.

English: Death is better than a bitter life, and eternal rest than a continual sickness.
Ekegusii: Amakweri n’amaya kobua obogima bw’emechando, naende gokwa na gotimoka kobua oborwaire botari kogwena.

English: Good things poured out upon a mouth that is closed are like food offerings laid upon a grave.
Ekegusii: Koa omonto endagera otari konyara koragera, nigo enga buna okobekerera endagera eyio igoro ase embeera.

English: What does an offering profit an idol? For it can’t eat or smell. So is he who is punished by the Lord,
Ekegusii: Inee! Ekengwanso ninki kegwenerete gochia ase emegwekano eyio etanyare koria gose kogetiokerera? Nabo bono ere igo ase omonto ochandire na Nyasae.

English: seeing with his eyes and groaning, like a eunuch embracing a virgin and groaning.
Ekegusii: Omonto oyio nigo akorora n’amaiso aye ere omonyene na goita ebikoe, buna omosacha riteba riabwatire omoiseke omwekuungi rigoita egokoe.

English: Don’t give your soul to sorrow. Don’t afflict yourself deliberately.
Ekegusii: Tagwetugutana aye omonyene gochia ase amagombo, gose kwea obororo aye omonyene n’ogwancha.

English: Gladness of heart is the life of a man. Cheerfulness of a man lengthens his days.
Ekegusii: Omogooko nigo okoa obomoyo emiaka emenge; omogooko noro okoa obogima amatuko amange.

English: Love your own soul, and comfort your heart. Remove sorrow far from you, for sorrow has destroyed many, and there is no profit in it.
Ekegusii: Egokie ase okoba omotoereru bw’omoyo; beka amagombo aare naye. Ekiagera amagombo aitire abanto abange, gose tari nang’eria ende ase obogima bw’omonto onde bwensi.

English: Envy and wrath shorten life. Anxiety brings old age before its time.
Ekegusii: Endamuamu amo n’obororo nigo bikweng’eyia obogima, ogosegasega nigo bikogera omonto ogota bwango.

English: Those who are cheerful and merry will benefit from their food.
Ekegusii: Omonto obwate omoyo omuya naende omworo, nigo akogokera endagera eria akoria.

English: Wakefulness that comes from riches consumes the flesh, and anxiety about it takes away sleep.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto akorengereria mono igoro yokoborwa chitaabu nigo akorea; ogwechandera ring’ana erio nigo gokomorina chitoro.

English: Wakeful anxiety will crave slumber. In a severe disease, sleep will be broken.
Ekegusii: Ogwechandera ebiasara nigo kogokorina chitoro kegima buna oborwaire bonde bwonsi obonene bogokora.

English: A rich man toils in gathering money together. When he rests, he is filled with his good things.
Ekegusii: Omonto omotenenku nigo agokora omokia korigia obonda; ekero abonyorire oikaransa kobwechegeria.

English: A poor man toils in lack of substance. When he rests, he becomes needy.
Ekegusii: Omonto omotaka boigo nigo agokora emeremo n’ebigeri korende ebitoki biaye biagenderera gokea, ekero ere agotimoka, onyora tabwati kende agwetogeria.

English: He who loves gold won’t be justified. He who follows destruction will himself have his fill of it.
Ekegusii: Onde bwensi bwanchete chitaabu takobarwa koba omooronge ekiagera okorigia kwaye chitaabu nigo gokomokora omomochi.

English: Many have been given over to ruin for the sake of gold. Their destruction meets them face to face.
Ekegusii: Abange basariigwe nechitaabu na ogoitwa kwabo nigo gokabachera obosio ase obosio.

English: It is a stumbling block to those who sacrifice to it. Every fool will be taken by it.
Ekegusii: Obotenenku nigo bore omotego ase baria bakoirwa na borobwo, nigo bore omotego ase akogwa kera omonto omoriri.

English: Blessed is the rich person who is found blameless, and who doesn’t go after gold.
Ekegusii: Nasesenirie omonto ore omotenenku otari komochigwa, omonto oria otari kominyokia obotenenku.

English: Who is he, that we may call him blessed? For he has done wonderful things among his people.
Ekegusii: Onde nare omanyete omonto bw’engeencho buna eyio inwe tomotogie? Ee ekiagera ere okorire egekone monto onde atana gokora.

English: Who has been tried by it, and found perfect? Then let him boast. Who has had the power to transgress, and has not transgressed? And to do evil, and has not done it?
Ekegusii: ’Monto ki otemirwe n’obotenenku na kobua atari na komocha? Omonto buna oyio karabeo, ere nare noboronge bw’ogwetogia! Gose ning’o onyorire ribaga riogokora ebibe ere tabikora?

English: His prosperity will be made sure. The congregation will proclaim his alms.
Ekegusii: Obotenenku bw’omonto onga buna oyio inabomenye na emeganda nemanye oboitongo bwaye.

English: Do you sit at a great table? Don’t be greedy there. Don’t say, “There is a lot of food on it!”
Ekegusii: Ekero oraariganigwe ase omoyega omonene, aye tobaisa koba nokogania okonene kw’endagera gose goita egekoe oteebe, “Endagera eye tekari enyinge!”

English: Remember that a greedy eye is a wicked thing. What has been created more greedy than an eye? Therefore it sheds tears from every face.
Ekegusii: Inyora buna eriso riobonyandambe neribe. Inee, egento nkere egetoonu buna eriiso? Nakio gekogera amaiso akorwa amariga chingaki chionsi.

English: Don’t stretch your hand wherever it looks. Don’t thrust yourself with it into the dish.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa korambora okoboko kwao kobogoria egento oyomino aganetie, gose komoaka ekegokoro oyomino erio omoure endaagera.

English: Consider your neighbor’s feelings by your own. Be discreet in every point.
Ekegusii: Manya okogania kw’oyomino na omwereng’anie ere boigo obabogorerie abamino ase kera enchera.

English: Eat like a human being those things which are set before you. Don’t eat greedily, lest you be hated.
Ekegusii: Karie kera egento okoegwa buna omonto ore na amasikani gose tobaisa gotakuna-takuna obaise kwangwa.

English: Be first to stop for manners’ sake. Don’t be insatiable, lest you offend.
Ekegusii: Nering’ana rigiya ase ore aye koba omotang’ani koigota, toba rinyandambe obaise kogechia abanto.

English: And if you sit among many, Don’t reach out your hand before them.
Ekegusii: Ekero orabe gwaikaransire aye amo na abanto baane, tobaisa koba oyo bw’eritang’ani kobogoria endagera.

English: How sufficient to a well-mannered man is a very little. He doesn’t breathe heavily in his bed.
Ekegusii: Endagera enke nigo ere enyinge ase omonto obwate amasikani, ere tagwechaanda ekero akoirana gochia bwoye.

English: Healthy sleep comes from moderate eating. He rises early, and his wits are with him. The pain of wakefulness, colic, and griping are with an insatiable man.
Ekegusii: Omonto okoragera nekerengo nigo akonyoora chitoro chingiya, ere nabooke bwango na kweigwa ore buya. Korende rinyandambe takonyoora chitoro, ere nigo akoonchoka omoyo naende na koromwa enda.

English: And if you have been forced to eat, rise up in the middle of it, and you shall have rest.
Ekegusii: Keraabe yakobetereirie koria endagera eetanetie ekerengo, sooka oroke erio aye noigwe buya.

English: Hear me, my son, and don’t despise me, and in the end you will appreciate my words. In all your works be skillful, and no disease will come to you.
Ekegusii: Ntegerere omwana one, aye tobaisa gonsiereria naye omoerio noyamanye buya aya nkogoteebia. Aye obe nomokia ase emeremo yao yonsi eyio oraabe kogokora, naye tokonyorwa na borwaire bonde bwonsi.

English: People bless him who is liberal with his food. The testimony of his excellence will be believed.
Ekegusii: Abanto nigo bagotogia oria ore omwasioku ase okobaa endaagera, ne chinkwana chiabo igoro y’obuya bwaye nigo chire echi’ekeene.

English: The city will murmur at him who is a stingy with his food. The testimony of his stinginess will be accurate.
Ekegusii: Omonto omwegimeria ase ebiakoria nigo arararigwe ase ekenyoro ekegima, n’echinkwana igoro yobong’iti bwaye nigo chire e chikeene.

English: Don’t show yourself valiant in wine, for wine has destroyed many.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kwerorekania buna nigo ore egeata giokonywa amarwa, ekiagera edivai yaitire abange.

English: The furnace tests the temper of steel by dipping; so does wine test hearts in the quarreling of the proud.
Ekegusii: Chinchera chi’omonto omoenenu nigo chikororekana ese chinkwana chiaye ekero atindire, buna boigo obokong’u bwechuuma bokororekana ekero yasambirwe ere embariri kegima na gosoigwa ime ase amaache.

English: Wine is as good as life to men, if you drink it in moderation. What life is there to a man who is without wine? It has been created to make men glad.
Ekegusii: Edivai nigo enga obogima oboyia ekero omonto akoyenywa ase ekerengo. Obogima ninki edivai etaiyo? Aro nigo aroisirie agokie abanto.

English: Wine drunk in season and in moderation is joy of heart and gladness of soul:
Ekegusii: Okonywa Edivai ase ekerengo nechingaki chiaye nigo bikorenta omogooko ase omoyo nemosasoko ase enkoro.

English: Wine drunk excessively is bitterness of soul, with provocation and conflict.
Ekegusii: Korende okonywa edivai goetania ekerengo nigo gokorenta ogwatigwa omotwe, obororo na amachaaya.

English: Drunkenness increases the rage of a fool to his hurt. It diminishes strength and adds wounds.
Ekegusii: Ogotinda nigo gokomenta ekeririanda kiomonto omoriri nogweita omonyene; nigo gokomoreyia na komomenta amaote.

English: Don’t rebuke your neighbor at a banquet of wine. Don’t despise him in his mirth. Don’t speak a word of reproach to him. Don’t distress him by making demands of him.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa komotogonyera omoamate oo ase edivai, gose komochaaya ekero akwegokia ase omoyega. Tobaisa komoteebia ring’ana riokomokuurera, gose komochaanda ase okogania aakane edeni.

English: Have they made you ruler of a feast? Don’t be lifted up. Be among them as one of them. Take care of them first, and then sit down.
Ekegusii: Ekero aye orakorwe koba omoteneneri bw’omoyega, tobaisa koresania omotwe, aye bwekore koba buna abande ase omoyega; obagenie ritang’ani erio aye oikaranse.

English: And when you have done all your duties, take your place, that you may be gladdened on their account, and receive a wreath for your good service.
Ekegusii: Ekero gwakorire emeremo yao, ikaransa aase ao, ogoke na abande na koegwa esiko yao ase emeremo yao emiya.

English: Speak, you who are older, for it’s your right, but with sound knowledge; and don’t interrupt the music.
Ekegusii: Onye aye kore omonene ase emiaka, kwana; korende okwane nobong’aini tobaisa gosaria omoino.

English: Don’t pour out talk where there is a performance of music. Don’t display your wisdom at the wrong time.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gotambeyia chinkwana onye ebinyugwa bikoruugwa. Tobaisa kwerora namasomo ao ekero ebiro biaye bitaraika.

English: As a ruby signet in a setting of gold, so is a music concert at a wine banquet.
Ekegusii: Chingero ase omoyega bw’okonywa Edivai nabo chigwekaine ekemanyererio gietaabu igoro ase amagena yerigori rinene.

English: As an emerald signet in a work of gold, so is musical melody with pleasant wine.
Ekegusii: Chingero chingiya amo n’edivai nabo chigwekaine ogochaberwa okuya gwechiruru igoro ase etaabu.

English: Speak, young man, if you are obliged to, but no more than twice, and only if asked.
Ekegusii: Onye aye kore omosae, okwane ekero rioka ebetereretie; korende tari goetania ara kabere na rioka ekero oraborigwe gokora boigo.

English: Sum up your speech, many things in few words. Be as one who knows and yet holds his tongue.
Ekegusii: Okwane maiso marore, okwane amake ase ayaare amange; tiga erorekane buna nigo omanyete amange korende aye totageti kona gokwana.

English: When among great men, don’t behave as their equal. When another is speaking, don’t babble.
Ekegusii: Ekero orabe ase egati ya abanene tibwereng’ania na barabwo, tobaisa gokwana amang’ana ataisaini aria onarete.

English: Lightning speeds before thunder. Approval goes before one who is modest.
Ekegusii: Buna okomesa kogotang’anera okogukura, naboigo esiko egotang’anera omonto bwesigete.

English: Rise up in good time, and don’t be last. Go home quickly and don’t loiter
Ekegusii: Soka korwa ase omoyega ase chingaki chigwenerete, tobaisa koba oyo bw’omoerio; ogende inka bwango na tobaisa kona koganya-ganya.

English: Amuse yourself there and do what is in your heart. Don’t sin by proud speech.
Ekegusii: Aye bwegokie na gokora keria oganetie, korende tobaisa komocha ase amang’ana y’obwerori.

English: For these things bless your Maker, who gives you to drink freely of his good things.
Ekegusii: Tibweba komotogia Omonene ere oria ogotongete na kogoichoria nebiegwa biaye ebiya.

English: He who fears the Lord will receive discipline. Those who seek him early will find favor.
Ekegusii: Ere oria omoirogete Omonene nigo agwancherana okomochigwa nere, na ere oria ogotang’ana komorigia nanyoore ogosesenigwa kwaye.

English: He who seeks the law shall be filled with it, but the hypocrite will stumble at it.
Ekegusii: Oria okobwatia amachiiko, nigo agoisaneka koyanyoora, korende omong’ainereria goika anyore egetango.

English: Those who fear the Lord will find true judgment, and will kindle righteous acts like a light.
Ekegusii: Baria bamoirogete Omonene inabamanye gokora aya aboronge, na amakora abo namese buna risase.

English: A sinful man shuns reproof, and will find a judgment according to his will.
Ekegusii: Abanyene ebibe tibancheti komochigwa; nigo bakonyora ogotaamera kwogokora aria barabwo batagete.

English: A sensible person won’t neglect a thought. An insolent and proud man won’t crouch in fear, even after he has done a thing by himself without counsel.
Ekegusii: Omonto obwate chisemi tari gosiereria ebirengererio bi’omonto onde, korende omonto omoenenu na omweimokia ere taoboeti gento.

English: Do nothing without counsel, but when you have acted, don’t regret it.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gokora gento kende gionsi isiko yebirengererio, erio aye tobetererigwa kweitia nyuma ekero gwakorire egento.

English: Don’t go in a way of conflict. Don’t stumble in stony places.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gokora enchera ere nebitango ebinge, aye obaise gochia kogochwa igoro ase amagena.

English: Don’t be overconfident on a smooth road.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa kwegena mono enchera erambogete,

English: Beware of your own children.
Ekegusii: korende aye bwerende mono ase oboeto bwao.

English: In every work guard your own soul, for this is the keeping of the commandments.
Ekegusii: Bwerende ase kera ok’ogokora, ekiagera eye nero engencho y’okobwata amachiiko.

English: He who believes the law gives heed to the commandment. He who trusts in the Lord will suffer no loss.
Ekegusii: Ere oria osemeretie amachiiko nigo akoigwera amachiiko, na oria omosemeretie Omonene takonyora chingoma.

English: No evil will happen to him who fears the Lord, but in trials once and again he will deliver him.
Ekegusii: Obobe tibori boramonyore omonto omoirogete Omonene, ase chingaki chiamatemwa Omonene nigo akoiranerera komokoonya boire boire.

English: A wise man will not hate the law, but he who is a hypocrite about it is like a boat in a storm.
Ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini takogeecha amachiiko korende omong’ainereria ase richiiko nigo anga obwato bokorutwa-rutwa ase enyancha yemerindo.

English: A man of understanding will put his trust in the law. And the law is faithful to him, as when one asks a divine oracle.
Ekegusii: Omonto omong’aini ere nabe omwegenwa ase richiiko, ase are ere richiiko nabo rigwekaine nokonacha kw’Omonene.

English: Prepare your speech, and so you will be heard. Bind up instruction, and make your answer.
Ekegusii: Roberia keria origetie gochia gokwana naye notegererwe; roberia amo aria aye omanyete erio onyare koiraneria.

English: The heart of a fool is like a cartwheel. His thoughts are like a rolling axle.
Ekegusii: Enkoro y’omonto omoriri nabo enga buna rigari riomogongoteni na ebirengererio biaye buna oborundarundia.

English: A stallion horse is like a mocking friend. He neighs under every one who sits upon him.
Ekegusii: Omosaani omokoora nabo anga ebaarasi eria egoaka eriogi ase kera omoriini.

English: Why does one day excel another, when all the light of every day in the year is from the sun?
Ekegusii: Ninki gekogera kera rituko rikororekana koba riao ko onsi nigo akonyoora omobaso obo korwa ase risase erimo?

English: They were distinguished by the Lord’s knowledge, and he varied seasons and feasts.
Ekegusii: Omonene nere oetetie gwatanana, na kobeeka ebiro ao ao bi’omwaka na amatuko amanene boigo.

English: Some of them he exalted and hallowed, and some of them he has made ordinary days.
Ekegusii: Akaroisia amatuko ande koba amachenu na ayande koba amatuko bosa igo.

English: And all men are from the ground. Adam was created from dust.
Ekegusii: Mwanyabaanto bonsi nigo barwete ase riroba na Adamu nigo atongetwe korwa ime y’orotu.

English: In the abundance of his knowledge the Lord distinguished them, and made their ways different.
Ekegusii: Korende Omonene ase obong’aini bwaye oboikeranu, akabaatanana na koa kera oyomo emeremo ere emeao korwa ase eyoyonde.

English: Some of them he blessed and exalted, and some of them he made holy and brought near to himself. Some of them he cursed and brought low, and overthrew them from their place.
Ekegusii: Ase egati yabo agakiinia abande na kobaa obonene, abande akabakora koba abachenu na kobabeeka ang’e ase are ere. Korende boigo akabaragereria abande na kobakeyia, akabarusia korwa ase abo.

English: As the clay of the potter in his hand, all his ways are according to his good pleasure, so men are in the hand of him who made them, to give to them according to his judgment.
Ekegusii: Nabo enga riroba rire ase amaboko yomoroisia chinyongo ere oyio okoribomba buna ere omonyene anchete, naboigo ere ase Mwanyabaanto ime ase amaboko aye ere oria obatongete; ere bweka nigo agokora buna omonyene agoetia.

English: Good is the opposite of evil, and life is the opposite of death; so the sinner is the opposite of the godly.
Ekegusii: Obuya nigo bore mamincha y’obobe, na obomoyo nigo bore mamincha y’ogokwa, nabo ere boigo omonyabibe nigo are mamincha y’omonto omosigete Omonene.

English: Look upon all the works of the Most High like this, they come in pairs, one against another.
Ekegusii: Yerigererie emeremo yonsi y’Omonene, nigo ere ebere, kera oyomo mamincha yo oyonde.

English: I was the last on watch, like one who gleans after the grape gatherers.
Ekegusii: Inche nabeire oyo bw’omoerio koyarigereria ayio, buna omonto okorogota amasabibu ekero abagesi bachiire.

English: By the Lord’s blessing I arrived before them, and filled my winepress like one who gathers grapes.
Ekegusii: Korende Omonene onsesenirie mono, inkababua bonsi; buna omogesi bwa amasabibu naichoirie ekebaari kiane giokoigatera.

English: Consider that I labored not for myself alone, but for all those who seek instruction.
Ekegusii: Inyora tinekorerete emeremo eye ase ogweisanekia inche omonyene korende nase bonsi baria barigetie kweorokereria.

English: Hear me, you great men of the people, and listen with your ears, you rulers of the congregation.
Ekegusii: Ntegerere inwe abanene abwo more ase egati ya abanto; inwe abanene b’ebiombe, ntegerere inche.

English: To son and wife, to brother and friend, don’t give power over yourself while you live, and don’t give your goods to another, lest you regret it and must ask for them.
Ekegusii: Ebiro bionsi omenyete, tobaisa komotigera omokungu omwana, gose momura omino, gose omosani akogambere; tobaisa komoa omonto onde obonda bwao, obaisa korwa ekerengererio na kogania oiranerigwe.

English: While you still live and breath is in you, don’t give yourself over to anybody.
Ekegusii: Ekero ore moyo, aye gokoeyaana, tobaisa gwanchera monto onde bwensi abogorie ribaga riao.

English: For it is better that your children should ask from you than that you should look to the hand of your children.
Ekegusii: Nigo ere buya abana bao bagosemerie aye kobua aye kobasemeria barabwo.

English: Excel in all your works. Don’t bring a stain on your honor.
Ekegusii: Kora kera egento kebe ekiya kegima, tobaisa kobeka ekemoa ase esiko yao.

English: In the day that you end the days of your life, in the time of death, distribute your inheritance.
Ekegusii: Omoerio bw’obogima bwao, ase ensa yao yomoerio, gaba obonda bwao.

English: Fodder, a stick, and burdens are for a donkey. Bread, discipline, and work are for a servant.
Ekegusii: Obonyansi, egurube ne ekeranya ase ebunda, endagera, amasikani nemeremo ase omokori emeremo.

English: Set your slave to work, and you will find rest. Leave his hands idle, and he will seek liberty.
Ekegusii: Kae omokori emeremo oo emeremo naye notimoke, motige bosa atari na meremo erio ere arigie obosibore.

English: Yoke and whip will bow the neck. For an evil slave there are racks and tortures.
Ekegusii: Beka etugo ende yonsi ase oboigweri goetera ase egesibo na amakorogoto, na omotomwa omobe ase okomochaanda.

English: Send him to labor, that he not be idle, for idleness teaches much mischief.
Ekegusii: Moe emeremo erio ere tabaisa koba omworo, ekiagera obworo nigo bokomoa omonto obobe obonge.

English: Set him to work, as is fit for him. If he doesn’t obey, make his fetters heavy.
Ekegusii: Moe emeremo buna ekogwenerete aye, onye tagokoigwera mosibe ebinyuri.

English: Don’t be excessive toward any. Do nothing unjust.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa komokorera monto onde bwensi goetania ekerengo naboigo tobaisa gokora kende gionsi otari nobong’aini.

English: If you have a slave, treat him like yourself, because you have bought him with blood.
Ekegusii: Onye kore nomokori emeremo tiga abe buna aye, ekiagera aye kwamogorete ase rigori nebigeri biao.

English: Vain and false hopes are for a man void of understanding. Dreams give wings to fools.
Ekegusii: Omonto omoriri nigo agotwara ogosemeria kwa bosa na okwoborimo; chindoto nigo chikomoa omonto omoriri chimbaba oiruruka.

English: As one who grasps at a shadow and follows after the wind, so is he who sets his mind on dreams.
Ekegusii: Omonto okwegena chindoto nabo anga omonto okomonyokia omorengari gose embeo erio ayebwate.

English: The vision of dreams is a reflection, the likeness of a face near a face.
Ekegusii: Okorota nabo konga ekerore, ekieni okorigereria ase obosio bwao.

English: From an unclean thing what can be cleansed? From that which is false what can be true?
Ekegusii: Ngento ki keranyaare gochenwa neubi? Inee, ekeene nkenyorekane ase oborimo?

English: Divinations, and soothsayings, and dreams, are vain. The heart has fantasies like a woman in labor.
Ekegusii: Koruta chinche, obomera n’echindoto noboriri; chiseemi nigo chikoba n’ebirengererio binga ebio omokungu okoibora.

English: If they are not sent in a visitation from the Most High, don’t give your heart to them.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa gochirengereria chindoto ase engencho ende yonsi otatiga rioka ekero chikorwa ase Omonene.

English: For dreams have led many astray. They have failed by putting their hope in them.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera chindoto chiabang’ainire abanto abange, na baria bachiegenete banyorire ogosookigwa.

English: Without lying the law will be fulfilled. Wisdom is complete in a faithful mouth.
Ekegusii: Amachiiko nigo are amaikeranu atabwati okongaineka okwo, n’obong’aini nigo bore oboikeranu ase omonto omwegenwa:

English: A well-instructed man knows many things. He who has much experience will declare understanding.
Ekegusii: Omonto otarire mono nigo amanyete amange, na omonto otwarire okwenaria amange nigo amanyete keria agokwana.

English: He who has no experience knows few things. But he who has traveled increases cleverness.
Ekegusii: Omonto otana koumerana na amakong’u ande onsi tamanyeti amange,

English: I have seen many things in my travels. My understanding is more than my words.
Ekegusii: korende ere oria otaarire mono bwenyoreire obomanyi.

English: I was often in danger even to death. I was preserved because of these experiences.
Ekegusii: Ase ogotaara kwane neroreire amange; nigo imanyete kobua buna indanyaare gokwana.

English: The spirit of those who fear the Lord will live, for their hope is in him who saves them.
Ekegusii: Ase ebiro ebinge nabeire ase obokong’u bw’ogokwa, korende naetire ase engencho yobomanyi obo.

English: Whoever fears the Lord won’t be afraid, and won’t be a coward, for he is his hope.
Ekegusii: Baria bamoirogete Omonene ina babe moyo,

English: Blessed is the soul of him who fears the Lord. To whom does he give heed? Who is his support?
Ekegusii: ekiagera ogosemeria kwabo nigo kore ase ere oria okobatooria.

English: The eyes of the Lord are on those who love him, a mighty protection and strong support, a cover from the hot blast, a shade from the noonday sun, a guard from stumbling, and a help from falling.
Ekegusii: Oria omoirogete Omonene takoba n’obwoba, takoiroka ekiagera Omonene nere ogosemeria kwaye.

English: He raises up the soul, and enlightens the eyes. He gives health, life, and blessing.
Ekegusii: Nasesenirie ere oria omoirogete Omonene!

English: He who sacrifices a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is made in mockery. The mockeries of wicked men are not acceptable.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera ere nigo amorigereretie ere oria asemeretie.

English: The Most High has no pleasure in the offerings of the ungodly, Neither is he pacified for sins by the multitude of sacrifices.
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo akobarigereria ase obuya baria bamwanchete. Ere nenguba embibo na ogosemeria kwabo ogokong’u; ere negekengero kiabo korwa ase omwaga omotindi, nekiriri kiabo ase omobaso ogwoka; ere nigo akobarenda tibanyara korichaniwa, obakoonya tibabaisa kogwa.

English: Like one who kills a son before his father’s eyes is he who brings a sacrifice from the goods of the poor.
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo agoichoria emioyo omogooko, na koyabeka amaiso oborabu. Ere nigo akobaa abanto obomenyo obuya, obomoyo na ogosesenigwa

English: The bread of the needy is the life of the poor. He who deprives him of it is a man of blood.
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto akorua ebiegwa korwa ase okonyora kwobong’ainereria, ekeng’wanso kiaye nigo gekoba nekemoa. Okorua kwa abanto batari abaigweri tigwancheiri.

English: Like one who murders his neighbor is he who takes away his living. Like a shedder of blood is he who deprives a hireling of his hire.
Ekegusii: Omonene tari gwancha chisadaka chi’abaanto batamoirogeti, gose obonge bw’okorwa tigokorenta okobwatanigwa.

English: When one builds, and another pulls down, what profit do they have but toil?
Ekegusii: Ere oria okorua esadaka yegento keria akobaura abataka nigo egwekaine omonto okomoita omwana ase obosio bwa ise.

English: When one prays, and another curses, whose voice will the Lord listen to?
Ekegusii: Endagera y’omotaka nero obogima bwaye; onde bwensi okomoibera omotaka endagera oyio nomoiti.

English: He who washes himself after touching a dead body, and touches it again, what does he gain by his washing?
Ekegusii: Komoura omoamate endagera okwo nokomoita; na komorina omokori emeremo ogoakanwa kwaye okwo nokomoita.

English: Even so a man fasting for his sins, and going again, and doing the same, who will listen to his prayer? What profit does he have in his humiliation?
Ekegusii: Omonto oyomo araagaacha noyonde atagore, inee natware okonyoora konde goetania goitera ebigeri?

English: He who keeps the law multiplies offerings. He who heeds the commandments sacrifices a peace offering.
Ekegusii: Ere oria obwatete amachiiko orure okorua okonene.

English: He who returns a kindness offers fine flour. He who gives alms sacrifices a thank offering.
Ekegusii: Ere oyokobwatia amachiiko orure esadaka yomorembe.

English: To depart from wickedness pleases the Lord. To depart from unrighteousness is an atoning sacrifice.
Ekegusii: Oria okoiraneria buna mbuya mono orure esadaka yechinyeke chinchenu;

English: See that you don’t appear in the presence of the Lord empty.
Ekegusii: nere oria ogokoonya abataka orure esadaka yokoiraneria buna mbuya mono.

English: For all these things are done because of the commandment.
Ekegusii: Ogotiga obobe nigo gokogookia Omonene, na gotiga amabe nokwerentera okobwatana.

English: The offering of the righteous enriches the altar. The sweet fragrance of it is before the Most High.
Ekegusii: Ekengwanso ki’omonto omonyaboronge nigo kegochena egesasiimero, n’erimisu rigiya nigo rigotira gochia ase oyore igoro mono.

English: The sacrifice of a righteous man is acceptable. It won’t be forgotten.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera ebinto ebi bionsi nigo biganirie kobwatekana nogochika;

English: Glorify the Lord with generosity. Don’t reduce the first fruits of your hands.
Ekegusii: esadaka yomonto omoigweri nigo egoaka egesasiimero amaguta na ogotioka kwaye okuya kwariina goika ase obosio Omonene.

English: In every gift show a cheerful countenance, And dedicate your tithe with gladness.
Ekegusii: Esadaka yomonto omoigweri nigo egwancherwa; nero tekwebwa kare na kare.

English: Give to the Most High according as he has given. As your hand has found, give generously.
Ekegusii: Moimokererie Omonene igoro ase omoyo omorabu, gose tobaisa koba omong’iti ase ogotongora kwe rigesa riao.

English: For the Lord repays, and he will repay you sevenfold.
Ekegusii: Orwe ebiegwa biao bionsi ase omoyo omorabu, ochirwe chisadaka chiao chionsi ase omogooko.

English: Don’t plan to bribe him with gifts, for he will not receive them. Don’t set your mind on an unrighteous sacrifice, For the Lord is the judge, and with him is no respect of persons.
Ekegusii: Moe Omonene buna ere akoeire, orwe koreng’ana buna aye obwate.

English: He won’t accept any person against a poor man. He will listen to the prayer of him who is wronged.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera Omonene nere oakanete nere nagoakane ara gatano na kabere (7)

English: He will in no way despise the supplication of the fatherless or the widow, when she pours out her tale.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa goteema komoa riaki ekiagera ere takoira;

English: Don’t the tears of the widow run down her cheek? Isn’t her cry against him who has caused them to fall?
Ekegusii: gose tobaisa gosemeria chisadaka kwanyorire ase obong’ainereria. Ekiagera Omonene n’omonachi ebiina gose ere tabwati ogwanchereria.

English: He who serves God according to his good pleasure will be accepted. His supplication will reach to the clouds.
Ekegusii: Omonene takoorokia ogwanchereria ase abataka; ekero oria omocheire agosaba nigo akomoigwa.

English: The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds. until it comes near, he will not be comforted. He won’t depart until the Most High visits and he judges righteously and executes judgment.
Ekegusii: Ere tari gosiereria amasabo yechintakana, gose amasabo yomoboraka ekero akomotebia omogano oye.

English: And the Lord will not be slack, neither will he be patient toward them, until he has crushed the loins of the unmerciful. He will repay vengeance to the heathen until he has taken away the multitude of the arrogant and broken in pieces the sceptres of the unrighteous,
Ekegusii: Amariga yomoboraka nigo agoiteka ase chimboto chiaye,

English: until he has rendered to every man according to his deeds, and repaid the works of men according to their plans, until he has judged the cause of his people, and he will make them rejoice in his mercy.
Ekegusii: ase okomosoera ere oria omorenteire emechaando yaye.

English: Mercy is as welcome in the time of his affliction, as clouds of rain in the time of drought.
Ekegusii: Ere oria okomokorera Omonene ase okomogookia nigo agwancherwa nere, ogosaba kwaye inagoike igoro.

English: Have mercy upon us, O Lord the God of all, and look at us with favor;
Ekegusii: Otokwere mabera aye Omonene Nyasae o bonsi.

English: and send your fear upon all the nations.
Ekegusii: Bikore ebisaku bionsi bikoiroke.

English: Lift up your hand against the foreign nations and let them see your mighty power.
Ekegusii: Imokia okoboko kwao mamincha yebisaku binde, obikore birore okobua kw’obonene bwao.

English: As you showed your holiness in us before them, so be magnified in them before us.
Ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana gwatotomete intwe koorokia obochenu bwao ase bare barabwo; boigo bono toorokie okobua kwao goetera ase bare barabwo.

English: Let them know you, as we also have known you, that there is no God but only you, O God.
Ekegusii: Barabwo boigo inabamanye buna intwe tomanyete, buna taiyo naende Omonene Nyasae onde goetania aye Omonene.

English: Show new signs, and work various wonders. Glorify your hand and your right arm.
Ekegusii: Naende bono kora ebikone amo nebimanyererio binde;

English: Raise up indignation and pour out wrath. Take away the adversary and destroy the enemy.
Ekegusii: gokore okoboko kwao kobe igokore n’ogotogigwa kegima.

English: Hasten the time and remember your oath. Let them declare your mighty works.
Ekegusii: Orokia obororo bwao,, itera ekeririanda kiao;

English: Let him who escapes be devoured by raging fire. May those who harm your people find destruction.
Ekegusii: basirie abaengereria, na kobatinyia ababisa.

English: Crush the heads of the rulers of the enemies who say, “There is no one but ourselves.”
Ekegusii: Ayereria rituko erio naende oinyore ogotiana kwao; obakore abanto bateebe igoro yamakora ao yogokumia.

English: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and take them for your inheritance, as from the beginning.
Ekegusii: Tiga onde bwensi oyio oraminchorie asambwe nekeririanda kiao ekenene, na baria bakobachaanda abanto bao banyoore ogoitwa.

English: O Lord, have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Israel, whom you likened to a firstborn.
Ekegusii: Basenyente abanene ba ababisa bao abwo bagoteeba; “Onde taiyo naende otatiga intwe abanyene!”

English: Have compassion upon the city of your sanctuary, Jerusalem, the place of your rest.
Ekegusii: Bisangererie ebisaku bionsi bia Yakobo,

English: Fill Zion. Exalt your oracles and fill your people with your glory.
Ekegusii: Oichorie Hekalu yao ere ase egetunwa gia Sayoni obonene na amateera y’okogotogia.

English: Give testimony to those who were your creatures in the beginning, and fulfill the prophecies that have been spoken in your name.
Ekegusii: Eorokie ase abanto bao, abwo gwatongete korwa omochakano; oikeranie obobani bwao obwo gwatorete ase erieta riao.

English: Reward those who wait for you, and men will put their trust in your prophets.
Ekegusii: Obae ebiegwa biao kwaroberetie korwa omochakano na tiga ababani bao baegwe amasikani.

English: Listen, O Lord, to the prayer of your servants, according to the blessing of Aaron concerning your people; and all those who are on the earth will know that you are the Lord, the eternal God.
Ekegusii: Obarorere amaabera abanto abwo bakorangerigwa ase erieta riao; Abaisraeli abwo kwarogete omwana oo omoisia omotangi.

English: The belly will eat any food, but one food is better than another.
Ekegusii: Oyokwere maabera omochie oyio ase Hekalu yao ere, Yerusalemu omochie oo bw’ogotimokera.

English: The mouth tastes meats taken in hunting, so does an understanding heart detect false speech.
Ekegusii: Oyoichorie omochie o Sayoni omochengo bwamakora ao y’ogokumia, erio Hekalu yao eichore obonene bwao.

English: A contrary heart will cause heaviness. A man of experience will pay him back.
Ekegusii: Obaikeranerie abanto bao abwo gwatongete ritang’ani na goikerania obobani obwo gwakwanete ase erieta riao.

English: A woman will receive any man, but one daughter is better than another.
Ekegusii: Obae ebiegwa baria bakoganyete, erio ababani bao barorekane buna barabwo nabegeenwa bare.

English: The beauty of a woman cheers the countenance. A man desires nothing more.
Ekegusii: Aye Omonene, otegerere ogosaba kwa abakoreri bao, koreng’ana n’ogosesenia kwa Aroni igoro ase abanto bao. Erio Mwanyabaanto bonsi ase ense bamanye aye naye Omonene, bwe chingaki chionsi.

English: If kindness and humility are on her tongue, her husband is not like other sons of men.
Ekegusii: Endagera ende yonsi nabo eranyaare koriegwa, korende nereo endagera ere engiya kobwa eyende.

English: He who gets a wife gets his richest treasure, a help meet for him and a pillar of support.
Ekegusii: Buna oromeme rokoigwa obuya bwogwansa gwechindaagera, naboigo nomonto ore nechiseemi akonyaara gwatanana amang’ana yoborimo.

English: Where no hedge is, the property will be plundered. He who has no wife will mourn as he wanders.
Ekegusii: Oria obwate obongo bw’ebirengererio ebibe nigo akorenta omoichano korende ere oria onarete obogima goika amoakane buna egwenerete.

English: For who would trust a nimble robber who skips from city to city? Even so, who would trust a man who has no nest, and lodges wherever he finds himself at nightfall?
Ekegusii: Omokungu nabo aranyare konywuomwa nonde bwensi, korende nareo omoiseke oyomo omuya kobua oyonde.

English: Every friend will say, “I also am his friend”; but there is a friend which is only a friend in name.
Ekegusii: Kera omonto nabo aranyare goteeba, “Inche ninche omosaani oo.” Korende abasani bande nigo bare abasani ase erieta.

English: Isn’t there a grief in it even to death when a companion and friend is turned into an enemy?
Ekegusii: Inee, teri amaakwa y’amakweri ekero momura omino gose omosaani akoba omobisa?

English: O wicked imagination, why were you formed to cover the dry land with deceit?
Ekegusii: Aye okoroberia obobe, ninki kiagerete ogatongwa goika oyeichorie ense noborimo?

English: There is a companion who rejoices in the gladness of a friend, but in time of affliction will be against him.
Ekegusii: Abande ase abanto bamwabo nigo bakogokera omogooko bw’obosaani, korende ase chingaki chi’obokong’u bamotiga.

English: There is a companion who for the belly’s sake labors with his friend, yet in the face of battle will carry his buckler.
Ekegusii: Abande nigo bakomokoonya omosaani ase engencho y’endagera korende ekero esegi ekoba, beegerera boka abanyene.

English: Don’t forget a friend in your soul. Don’t be unmindful of him in your riches.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa komweba omosani oo bw’ekeene; na ekero orabe omonda tomotinyia korwa ase enkoro yao.

English: Every counselor extols counsel, but some give counsel in their own interest.
Ekegusii: Kera omoseemia narue oboseemia korende abande nigo bakorua oboseemia ase okwenyorera ayabo.

English: Let your soul beware of a counselor, and know in advance what is his interest (for he will take counsel for himself), lest he cast the lot against you,
Ekegusii: Orende buya igoro yomoseemia, otuke kegima riria origetie ase oboseemia, ekiagera nabo erabe ere nigo erengereretie omonyene. Nabo erabe oroisirie omoroberio asore.

English: and say to you, “Your way is good.” Then he will stand near you, to see what will happen to you.
Ekegusii: Nabo ere arabaisa kogoteebia: “Bionsi mbuya bire”, erio atenene egeka korora riria rigokonyoora.

English: Don’t take counsel with one who looks askance at you. Hide your counsel from those who are jealous of you.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa korigia oboseemia korwa ase omonto ore nechitang’utang’u nere, na tobaisa komoseemia omonto okomogorerete.

English: Don’t consult with a woman about her rival, with a coward about war, with a merchant about business, with a buyer about selling, with an envious man about thankfulness, with an unmerciful man about kindliness, with a sluggard about any kind of work, with a hireling in your house about finishing his work, or with an idle servant about much business. Pay no attention to these in any matter of counsel.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa korigia oboseemia ase omokungu korwa ase omobisa oye, torigia oboseemia korwa ase omonto omwoba igoro y’eseegi, gose omoonchoreria ase oboonchoreria, gose omogori ase oboonia bw’ebinto, gose omonto omong’iti igoro y’oboitongo, gose omonto omotindi igoro yobwororo, gose omonto omworo igoro yemeremo, gose omosomba omworo igoro yemeremo emekong’u. Aye tobaisa kobakumeria abanto bengeencho eyio, ase ring’ana riokonyoora oboseemia.

English: But rather be continually with a godly man, whom you know to be a keeper of the commandments, who in his soul is as your own soul, and who will grieve with you, if you fail.
Ekegusii: Korende aye ase kera engaki obe noboamate nomonto omoirogete Omonene, oyio aye omanyete buna nkoigwera are amachiiko, oyio mokoigwana nere, oyio oragoichanere aye ekero okobugwa.

English: Make the counsel of your heart stand, for there is no one more faithful to you than it.
Ekegusii: Semeria mono oboseemia bw’enkoro yao; ekiagera monto taiyo omwegenwa kobua enkoro yao.

English: For a man’s soul is sometimes inclined to inform him better than seven watchmen who sit on high on a watch-tower.
Ekegusii: Ase ebiro ebinge enkoro yomonto nigo ekomoa omonyene oboseemia obuya goika ara gatano na kabere kobua abarendi bensinyo bakorenda ase okoererania.

English: Above all this ask the Most High that he may direct your way in truth.
Ekegusii: Ase onsi, omosabe Omonene erio ayerae enchera yao ase ekeene.

English: Let reason be the beginning of every work. Let counsel go before every action.
