English: For all this the people didn’t repent. They didn’t depart from their sins, until they were carried away as a plunder from their land, and were scattered through all the earth. The people were left very few in number, but with a ruler from the house of David.
Ekegusii: Nonya nyuma ayio onsi gakorekanire, abanto tibaonchogete. Tibatigete ebibe biabo goika bagooswa aare korwa aase chinka chiabo. Bagasiarerwa ense yonsi. Abanto batigarete nabake mono, barabwo bakagaamberwa nororeria rwa Daudi.

English: Some of them did that which was right, but some multiplied sins.
Ekegusii: Abande ase egati yabo bagakora aria amogogetie Omonene, korende abande bakamenta gokora ebibe.

English: Hezekiah fortified his city, and brought water into its midst. He tunneled through rock with iron, and built cisterns for water.
Ekegusii: Hezekia akaywoagaachera omochie oye orwaki, na goetia amaache goika imeo nechimberesi. Akarema emetaro n’echichuma ase arenge egetare egekong’u, na koagacha amatibo y’amaache.

English: In his days Sennacherib invaded, and sent Rabshakeh, and departed. He lifted up his hand against Zion, and boasted great things in his arrogance.
Ekegusii: Ase amatuko aye, Senakeribu akamogwera, akamotoma omonene bw’abarwani baye, akagwera omochie o Sayoni na gwetogia noboenenu obonene.

English: Then their hearts and their hands were shaken, and they were in pain, as women in labor.
Ekegusii: Chinkoro chia Abaisraeli chikabarwania na amaboko abo akaiguswa, bakaba nobokong’u buna obwo omokungu okobina.

English: But they called upon the Lord who is merciful, spreading out their hands to him. The Holy One quickly heard them out of Heaven, and delivered them by the hand of Isaiah.
Ekegusii: Korende barabwo bakamorangeri’Omonene bw’amaabera, bakamoimokeria amaboko igoro. Nere oyio Omochenu akabaigwa kegima korwa igoro, akabatoria nokoboko gwa Isaya.

English: He struck the camp of the Assyrians, and his angel utterly destroyed them.
Ekegusii: Omonene agaaka egetuori kia Abaashuri na omomalaika oye akabatugutera are.

English: For Hezekiah did that which was pleasing to the Lord, and was strong in the ways of his ancestor David, which Isaiah the prophet commanded, who was great and faithful in his vision.
Ekegusii: Ezekia agakora amaya na kobwatia chimbaratero chia Daudi sokoro yaye, buna ere amochiigete omobani Isaya, ere oyio bwegenetwe kegima ase amaroro aye.

English: In his days the sun went backward. He prolonged the life of the king.
Ekegusii: Ase ebiro biaye ere Isaya, risase rikairana magega, akayatambeyia amatuko yomorwoti.

English: He saw by an excellent spirit what would come to pass in the future; and he comforted those who mourned in Zion.
Ekegusii: Ase chinguru chi’omoika ere akayarora amang’ana yomoerio, akabaremia baria abarenge kweumia ase omochie o Sayoni.

English: He showed the things that would happen through the end of time, and the hidden things before they came.
Ekegusii: Akabamaanorera amang’ana arenge gochia gokoreka ase omoerio, akabateebia amang’ana y’obobisi aro atarachia gokoreka.

English: The memory of Josiah is like the composition of incense prepared by the work of the perfumer. It will be sweet as honey in every mouth, and like music at a banquet of wine.
Ekegusii: Komoinyora Yosia nigo enga buna omwochogano omuya bw’ekoroso, eyio n’omonto oria ore n’okomanya okonene kegima, ekoroso eyio nigo egwansa kegima buna oboke ase kera omonto, na nigo enga buna ogoteera kw’obokano ase omoyega bw’edivai engiya kegima.

English: He did what was right in the reforming of the people, and took away the abominations of iniquity.
Ekegusii: Yosia nigo araetwe buya buna akoraa abanto erio akarusia obobisa bwonsi obwo bwarenge bwabo bw’obobe.

English: He set his heart right toward the Lord. In lawless days, he made godliness prevail.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo arenge amwegenwa kegima ase Nyasae! Ekero abanto barenge ababe kegima, erio nere agating’ia obokoreri obuya.

English: Except David, Hezekiah, and Josiah, all were wicked, because they abandoned the law of the Most High. The kings of Judah came to an end.
Ekegusii: Gotatiga Daudi, Hezekia amo na Yosia, abagaambi abange ba Yuda nigo bakorete ebibe ebinge mono kegima, ekiagera nigo batigete richiiko ri’Omonene, goika omoerio.

English: They gave their power to others, and their glory to a foreign nation.
Ekegusii: Chinguru chiabo nigo bachitigerete abanto bande, n’amasikani abo bakayatigera abarwa isiko;

English: They set the chosen city of the sanctuary on fire and made her streets desolate, as it was written by the hand of Jeremiah.
Ekegusii: abwo basaambete omochie obo n’amaache arwete ase Hekalu, erio bakayotiga omochie oria amo n’echinchera chiaye bosa buna koreng’ana Yeremia abaanete.

English: For they mistreated him; yet he was sanctified in the womb to be a prophet, to root out, to afflict, to destroy and likewise to build and to plant.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera abanto abwo nigo bachandete Yeremia, Ng’a nonya orenge omochore n’omwakua amaguta o Nyasae koba omobanikonya ataraiborwa, erio asimore, asarie, na gosiria, naende nonya nabo aagache na gosimeka.

English: Ezekiel saw the vision of glory, which God showed him on the chariot of the cherubim.
Ekegusii: Ezekieri nere oroche oborori bw’obosiani, obwo Nyasae amworogetie ase egari y’ebitongwa bia igoro bikoiruruka.

English: For truly he remembered the enemies in rainstorm, and to do good to those who directed their ways aright.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera Nyasae nigo abainyorete ababisa baye ase emerindo, korende akabakorera amaya baria bonsi bamenyete obogima obuya.

English: Also of the twelve prophets, may their bones flourish again out of their place. He comforted the people of Jacob, and delivered them by confident hope.
Ekegusii: Amauga y’ababani baria ikomi na babere tiga ating’e aaria chimbera ime; ekiagera nigo bababegete omoyo abanto ba Yakobo, erio bakabatooria ase okobaa ogosemeria ogoikeranu.

English: How shall we magnify Zerubbabel? He was like a signet ring on the right hand.
Ekegusii: Nang’a ng’aki toramotogie Serubabeli?

English: So was Jesus the son of Josedek, who in their days built the house, and exalted a people holy to the Lord, prepared for everlasting glory.
Ekegusii: Ase enchera buna eyio eyio, na Yoshua omwana o Yozadoki. Ase engaki eyio yabo, bakaagacha enyomba ya Nyasae enchenu eyio yarenge y’obosiani bwaye bwa kare na kare.

English: Also of Nehemiah the memory is great. He raised up for us fallen walls, set up the gates and bars, and rebuilt our houses.
Ekegusii: Ekeinyorio kia Neemia n’egia kare na kare. Ere nigo atwaagacherete naende chindwaki echio konya chiatagotagoirwe na kogwa, agachitenenera naende erio chigachia nkuma, chionsi chikaagachwa oboyia chinyomba echio konya chiatagoirwe.

English: No man was created upon the earth like Enoch, for he was taken up from the earth.
Ekegusii: Ase ense eye yonsi, onde taiyo nonya n’oyomo otongetwe buna Enoku arenge, ekiagera ere nigo airetwe korwa ase ense eye.

English: Nor was there a man born like Joseph, a leader of his kindred, a supporter of the people. Even his bones were cared for.
Ekegusii: Naende ase ense eye onde tari oiboretwe buna Yosebu arenge; n’amauga aye nigo agachire goika bono.

English: Shem and Seth were honored among men, but above every living thing in the creation was Adam.
Ekegusii: Semu, Seti na Enoku nigo barenge abanto basikire kegima, n’abanto abwo, Korende Adamu nigo asikire mono kegima goetania ebitongwa bionsi bire moyo ase ense aye.

English: It was Simon, the son of Onias, the high priest, who in his life repaired the house, and in his days strengthened the temple.
Ekegusii: Ere oyio orenge omonene ase abamura bamwabo na ogwetogeria kwa abanto baye, nere Simioni Omokuani omonene mosinto bwo Onia. Ase obogima bwaye akayeagaacha Hekalu boyia naboigo koyeagaachera orwaki.

English: The foundation was built by him to the height of the double walls, the lofty retaining walls of the temple enclosure.
Ekegusii: Akabeeka chinyasi ibere chi’orobago rwe Hekalu.

English: In his days, a water cistern was dug, the brazen vessel like the sea in circumference.
Ekegusii: Ase engaki yaye nario egesima kia amaache kiaremetwe, amaache amange ang’a buna enyaancha akagiterwa.

English: He planned to save his people from ruin, and fortified the city against siege.
Ekegusii: Ere akarengereria buna aranyare kobakoonya abanto tibasira, akayokong’ia omochie na koyogitera korwa ase obosagaani.

English: How glorious he was when the people gathered around him as he came out of the house of the veil!
Ekegusii: Rora, ere nigo asigetwe mono na goetananwa na abanto, kera ekero arenge korwa ase agwo aachenu.

English: He was like the morning star among clouds, like the full moon,
Ekegusii: Ere nigo arenge buna eng’enang’eni ya mambia ere ase amare, nigo arenge buna omotienyi orabete.

English: like the sun shining on the temple of the Most High, like the rainbow shining in clouds of glory,
Ekegusii: Nigo arenge buna okoraba kwomobaso igoro ase Hekalu y’Omonene, buna omokubinyongo orabete korwa ime yamare.

English: like roses in the days of first fruits, like lilies by a water spring, like the shoot of the frankincense tree in summer time,
Ekegusii: Nigo arenge buna ogosiicha kw’eritang’ani kwa amaua yobwanchani, buna ebisiicha biamatoke a rooche, buna ogoseboka kw’emecharake igoro ase egetunwa kia Lebanoni ase chingaki chiegurugura.

English: like fire and incense in the censer, like a vessel of beaten gold adorned with all kinds of precious stones,
Ekegusii: Buna ekoroso ime ase egesagusero kiaye, buna ekebekerero gi’etaabu esibirie kegima, gechabeire na kera amagena amaya akomeka meka.

English: like an olive tree loaded with fruit, and like a cypress growing high among the clouds.
Ekegusii: Nigo arenge buna Omozeituni bwamire amatunda, buna ekerobo egetambe gekinete goika ase amare.

English: When he put on his glorious robe, and clothed himself in perfect splendor, ascending to the holy altar, he made the court of the sanctuary glorious.
Ekegusii: Ere ekero arenge kobeeka chianga chiaye chiesiko, ekero arenge kogenda ase egesasiimero egechenu, ekero abegete chianga chiaye boikeranu, nigo arenge gokora ekeoreri gie Hekalu komenta koba nobonene kobua.

English: When he received the portions out of the priests’ hands, as he stood by the hearth of the altar, with his kindred like a garland around him, he was like a young cedar in Lebanon surrounded by the trunks of palm trees.
Ekegusii: Ekero abakuani barenge komoa ebitari biaye bi’ekeng’wanso, ekero ere ateneine ange negesasiimero, oetananire na abamwabo buna egutwa, ere nigo arenge buna omocharake omorere igoro ase egetunwa kia Lebanoni. Abamwabo nigo barenge komoonchokana buna emekendo nechinsagia chiaye.

English: All the sons of Aaron in their glory, held the Lord’s offering in their hands before all the congregation of Israel.
Ekegusii: Ababiare bonsi ba Aroni, ekero babeekire chianga chiabo chi’obonene, ekero babogoretie ebing’wanso biokomorwera Omonene ase amaboko abo, ekero barabwo batenenire ase obosio bw’omosangererekano bwonsi bw’Abaisraeli.

English: Finishing the service at the altars, that he might arrange the offering of the Most High, the Almighty,
Ekegusii: Ekero akorire emeremo yobokoreri ase egesasiimero, koroberia ebing’wanso bi’Omonene, Omobui,

English: he stretched out his hand to the cup of libation, and poured out the cup of the grape. He poured it out at the foot of the altar, a sweet smelling fragrance to the Most High, the King of all.
Ekegusii: akarambora okoboko kwaye na kobogoria egekombe, agaitera edivai inse ase oboroso bw’egesasiimero, eyio ere ekeng’wanso giokonyuugwa gekomogokia Omonene Omorwoti bwa abanto bonsi.

English: Then the sons of Aaron shouted. They sounded the trumpets of beaten work. They made a great fanfare to be heard, for a reminder before the Most High.
Ekegusii: Erio ababiare ba Aroni, bagaaka eriogi, na kobugia egetuureri, ebituureri biabo biroisirie korwa ase efeta, bakoraria okobao kw’Omonene.

English: Then all the people together hurried, and fell down to the ground on their faces to worship their Lord, the Almighty, God Most High.
Ekegusii: Erio abanto bonsi ase obomo bakaayerera, bagekumba na komosasiima Omonene obo, Omonene Nyasae, Omobui Omonene kobua.

English: The singers also praised him with their voices. There was a sweet melody in the whole house.
Ekegusii: Abateeri boigo bakamotogia ase amariogi abo, ase chingeero chingiya na amariogi areng’anaine buya.

English: And the people implored the Lord Most High, in prayer before him who is merciful, until the worship of the Lord was finished, and so they accomplished his service.
Ekegusii: Erio abanto bakamogaramera Omonene kegima, bakamosaba ere omonyene amaabera goika omoroberio bw’okomosasiima Omonene okaera. Naboigo banyaarete gokora okomosasiima ere.

English: Then he went down, and lifted up his hands over the whole congregation of the children of Israel, to give blessing to the Lord with his lips, and to glory in his name.
Ekegusii: Sioni akarua aroro, akaimokereria amaboko aye igoro ase omosangererekano bwonsi bwa Abaisraeli, erio koraria ogosesenigwa kw’Omonene korwa ase omonwa oye omonyene, na korimokereria erieta riaye igoro.

English: He bowed himself down in worship the second time, to declare the blessing from the Most High.
Ekegusii: Barabwo bagatung’ama naende eria kabere, konyora ogosesenigwa korwa ase Omonene ere oria ore igoro ase bionsi.

English: Now bless the God of all, who everywhere does great things, who exalts our days from the womb, and deals with us according to his mercy.
Ekegusii: Bono tiga tomotogie Nyasae o bonsi, ere oria ogokora amanene kera aase; ere oyio okorenda obogima bwaito gochaakera okoiborwa na gotokorera koreng’ana n’amaabera aye.

English: May he grant us joyfulness of heart, and that peace may be in our days in Israel for the days of eternity,
Ekegusii: Aye otoe omogooko bwe chinkoro chiaito, na gotorentera omorembe ase amatuko yobomenyo bwaito ase Israeli buna yarenge chingaki chia kare.

English: to entrust his mercy with us, and let him deliver us in his time!
Ekegusii: Amabera aye amenye ase tore; ere atotorie ase amatuko aito.

English: With two nations my soul is vexed, and the third is no nation:
Ekegusii: Mbireo ebisaku bibere inche ngechete, boigo egesaku kiagatato tigeisaini korokwa egesaku.

English: Those who sit on the mountain of Samaria, the Philistines, and the foolish people who live in Shechem.
Ekegusii: Abamenyi b’egetunwa gia Edomu naboigo Abafilisiti, na abanto baria abariri bamenyete Shekemu.

English: I have written in this book the instruction of understanding and knowledge, I Jesus, the son of Sirach Eleazar, of Jerusalem, who out of his heart poured forth wisdom.
Ekegusii: Inche nariikire ime ase egetabu eke amorokererio y’obong’aini na obomanyi. Ninche Yoshua mosinto o Sira omwana bw’Eliezeri korwa Yerusalemu, inche ase enkoro yane nigo ing’ichire obong’aini.

English: Blessed is he who will exercise these things. He who lays them up in his heart will become wise.
Ekegusii: Nasesenirie omonto okoyarengereria amang’ana ayio; nere oria orayabeeke ase enkoro yaye nabe nobong’aini.

English: For if he does them, he will be strong in all things, for the light of the Lord is his guide.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera ere oyorayakore nakong’igwe ase engaki etakoera, ekiagera okomoiroka Omonene nakwo obogima.

English: I will give thanks to you, O Lord, O King, and will praise you, O God my Savior. I give thanks to your name,
Ekegusii: Aye Omonene Nyasae, nagwakeire buya na kogotogia, omotooria one. Naribakire eriata riao.

English: for you have been my protector and helper, and delivered my body out of destruction, and out of the snare of a slanderous tongue, from lips that fabricate lies. You were my helper before those who stood by,
Ekegusii: Ekiagera aye kwabeire omorendi n’omokoonyi one. Gwatooririe omobere one korwa ase amakweri, na korwa ase emeeto y’abanto abanyaborimo ababe. Korwa bosio bw’ababisa baane abwo barenge gochia gonsiria ogantooria erio okaba obotamero bwane.

English: and delivered me, according to the abundance of your mercy and of your name, from the gnashings of teeth ready to devour, out of the hand of those seeking my life, out of the many afflictions I endured,
Ekegusii: Ase engencho y’obonene bw’amaabera ao ogankoonya, korwa ase chinchera chia ababisa baane abwo batagete gonsiria ogantooria, na korwa ase baria barenge korigia obogima bwane, na korwa ase emechando eria naremereretie, aye ogantooria,

English: from the choking of a fire on every side, and out of the midst of fire that I hadn’t kindled,
Ekegusii: na korwa ase omorero ore gwoka korwa chinsemo chionsi, oyio inche omonyene ntautete,

English: out of the depth of the belly of Hades, from an unclean tongue, and from lying words—
Ekegusii: na korwa emerindo y’amakweri, na korwa ase baria bakoraama bobe na goteeba amang’ana ’oborimo, na korwa ase abagenki b’echimeme chikorasa n’obosongo bw’amabe ogantooria.

English: the slander of an unrighteous tongue to the king. My soul drew near to death. My life was near to Hades.
Ekegusii: Konya naikigwe bosio ase obosio n’amakweri, n’obogima bwane konya bwaikire aang’e n’ogokwa.

English: They surrounded me on every side. There was no one to help me. I was looking for human help, and there was none.
Ekegusii: Ababisa baane konya bandomeirie korwa chinsemo chionsi n’erio tinarenge na monto ogonkoonywa. Ngasemeria ’nyore ogokoonya kwa Mwanyabaanto. Korende monto onde taankoonya.

English: Then I remembered your mercy, O Lord, and your working which has been from everlasting, how you deliver those who wait for you, and save them out of the hand of their enemies.
Ekegusii: Korende, nonya nabo, ’nkainyora amaabera ao aye Omonene, nonya n’emeremo yao korwa kare na kare, ng’a aye nigo ogotooria baria bakomotamera, erio kwabarusia gati-gati y’echinchera chi’ababisa baabo.

English: I lifted up my prayer from the earth, and prayed for deliverance from death.
Ekegusii: Nainche nkareta ogosaba kwane ase ore, erio ngasaba ng’a ontoorie korwa ase amakweri.

English: I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, that he would not forsake me in the days of affliction, in the time when there was no help against the proud.
Ekegusii: Nkamoreera Omonene ngoteeba: “Aye Nyasae, naye Tata! Koranche, tontiga ase engaki y’emechando yane, ekero ’ntari na gokoonya konde gwonsi, tontuguta ekero ’ntari kwenyara bosio bw’ababisa baane.

English: I will praise your name continually. I will sing praise with thanksgiving. My prayer was heard.
Ekegusii: Nintogie erieta riao goika kare na kare, ningotererie ogoteera kw’ogogwakera buya” Ogosaba kwane ng’a koigweke ase ore;

English: You saved me from destruction and delivered me from the evil time. Therefore I will give thanks and praise to you, and bless the name of the Lord.
Ekegusii: ekiagera ’ngwtoretie korwa ase obwoba bw’amakweri, erio okaang’a obosibore ekero naare ase aabe. Ase igo, ningwakere mbuya mono na kogotogia na gotogia erieta riao.

English: When I was yet young, before I went abroad, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer.
Ekegusii: Ekero naarenge omwana omoke, ekero konya ntaramanya kogenda, ase esara yane nigo nasabete maiso marore ng’a ’nyore chisemi.

English: Before the temple I asked for her. I will seek her out even to the end.
Ekegusii: Ekero ’nteneine isiko y’Hekalu naamorigetie, na nimorigie amatuko onsi goika omoerio.

English: From the first flower to the ripening grape my heart delighted in her. My foot walked in uprightness. From my youth I followed her steps.
Ekegusii: Korwa okoiborwa kwane goika obogotu nche naamogokerete kegima ase omoyo one ime. Amagoro aane akabwatia enchera enyorooro; korwa obwana bwane akabwatia enchera yaye.

English: I inclined my ear a little, and received her, and found for myself much instruction.
Ekegusii: Nigo nategete ogoto kwane ngategerera kegima erio ’nkamwaarigania chisemi, erio nainche ’nkenyoorera ogosemia okonene kegima.

English: I profited in her. I will give glory to him who gives me wisdom.
Ekegusii: Erio ’nkagenderera komenya n’echisemi, n’oria onyororkererie obong’aini nimotogie kegima.

English: For I determined to practice her. I was zealous for that which is good. I will never be put to shame.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera inche nanachire ekiina ng’a nimenye koreng’ana n’echisemi, na niimbe n’erang’o enene ase ogokora ayare amaya, gose tinkoba na bosooku nonya ’ng’ake.

English: My soul has wrestled with her. In my conduct I was exact. I spread out my hands to the sky above, and bewailed my ignorances of her.
Ekegusii: Inche n’erwete mono kegima ase okwenyorera chisemi, na nkaba omong’aini kegima ase orogendo rwane. Erio ’nkarambora amaboko aane gochia igoro erio ngasaba, nkemurungania ng’a tinamanyete chisemi.

English: I directed my soul to her. In purity I found her. I got myself a heart joined with her from the beginning. Therefore I won’t be forsaken.
Ekegusii: Nkaroria obogima bwane gochia ase chisemi, erio nainche ’nkanyora chisemi. Korwa ase chisemi nkanyoora obong’aini korwa omochakano, na bono namanyire ng’a ninyoore ogokoonya korwa ase are. N’ere chisemi tagontiga nche bweka ntari n’okomanya kwaye.

English: My belly also was troubled to seek her. Therefore I have gained a good possession.
Ekegusii: Nabeire n’eng’eria enene ekiagera nigo nasugetigwe n’okogania gw’okonyora chisemi, ekio nakio kiagerire nanyoorire obotenenku bwaye obonene.

English: The Lord gave me a tongue for my reward. I will praise him with it.
Ekegusii: Omonene nigo ang’eete oromeme rwane buna ekeegwa, nainche nindokorere emeremo ase okomotogia ere omonyene.

English: Draw near to me, all you who are uneducated, and live in the house of instruction.
Ekegusii: Nchwo ase ’nde baria mwensi motamati gento, mosoe na goikaransa ase esukuru yane ime erio mosome chisemi.

English: Why therefore are you all lacking in these things, and your souls are very thirsty?
Ekegusii: Ninki mokwemurunganeria ng’a timomanyeti amang’ana aye, na nase ki emioyo yaino etari n’erang’o n’echisemi?

English: I opened my mouth and spoke, “Get her for yourselves without money.”
Ekegusii: Nkaigora omonwa one ngateeba: “Enyoorere chisemi chia bosa, motari goakana gento kende gionsi.”

English: Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction. She is near to find.
Ekegusii: Kanya ebigoti biaino ’nse y’erikorogoto erio motige emioyo yaino enyoore chisemi; chisemi nigo chikokonyooreka ang’e kegima nase ore.

English: See with your eyes how I labored just a little and found for myself much rest.
Ekegusii: Rigereria morore ng’a nakorire emeremo emeke, korende nche nenyooreire omorembe omonene.

English: Get instruction with a great sum of silver, and gain much gold by her.
Ekegusii: Nonya rigori riaye rire rinene buna chitaabu, inwe ng’a mwenyorere eng’eria y’chifeta.

English: May your soul rejoice in his mercy, and may you all not be put to shame in praising him.
Ekegusii: Tiga emioyo yaino egokere amaabera a Nyasae, gose tari timwenyoorera obosooku, na mono ekero mokomotogia Omonene Nyasae.

English: Work your work before the time comes, and in his time he will give you your reward.
Ekegusii: Kora emeremo yaino bwaango engaki eria moire etaraika, Erio nario Omonene arabae eng’eria yaino ase engaki eria aganetie.

English: These are the words of the book which Baruch the son of Nerias, the son of Maaseas, the son of Sedekias, the son of Asadias, the son of Helkias, wrote in Babylon,
Ekegusii: Egetabu eke nigo kiarigetwe na Baruku mosito o Neria, mochokoro o Maseria, bw’ororeria rwa Zedekia, Hasadia, na Hilikia. Nigo kiariikeretwe aria Babiloni;

English: in the fifth year, in the seventh day of the month, at the time when the Chaldeans took Jerusalem and burned it with fire.
Ekegusii: ase rituko riagatano na kabere omwaka o gatano korwa Ababeli baboerete Yerusalemu na koyosaria ase okoyosamba.

English: Baruch read the words of this book in the hearing of Jechonias the son of Joakim king of Judah, and in the hearing of all the people who came to hear the book,
Ekegusii: Baruku agasoma amang’ana aya ayio ariigete ase obosio bw’omorwoti Yehoakini mosito o Yehoakimu omorwoti o Yuda, na gochia ase abanto bonsi abwo bamenyete aria Babiloni mbarabare ase oroche rwa Sudi. Kera oyomo agacha koigwa amang’ana aya kagosomwa-abanene, abana b’oborwoti, abagaaka, na abanto bonsi bo bokwenyara ao ao.

English: and in the hearing of the mighty men, and of the kings’ sons, and in the hearing of the elders, and in the hearing of all the people, from the least to the greatest, even of all those who lived at Babylon by the river Sud.
Ekegusii: Ekero baigwete amang’ana aya bonsi bakarera, bakeng’ata na gosaba Omonene.

English: Then they wept, fasted, and prayed before the Lord.
Ekegusii: Erio bonsi bakarwa chitaabu chinyinge buna bare konyara,

English: They also made a collection of money according to every man’s ability;
Ekegusii: erio chigatomwa gochia Yerusalemu gochia ase Yehoakimu Omokuani omonene mosinto o Hilkia mochokoro o Shallum, na gochia ase abakuani bande na gochia ase abanto bonsi abwo barenge nere aria Yerusalemu.

English: and they sent it to Jerusalem to Joakim the high priest, the son of Helkias, the son of Salom, and to the priests and to all the people who were found with him at Jerusalem,
Ekegusii: Ase rituko ria ikomi ase omotienyi o Siwani, Baruku akaira ebibekeroro ebichenu ebio biairetwe korwa ase Hekalu erio akaberania gochia Yuda. Ebibekerero ebio bie echifeta nigo biarosetigwe na n’omorwoti Sedekia mosinto o Yosia omorwoti o Yuda.

English: at the same time when he took the vessels of the house of the Lord, that had been carried out of the temple, to return them into the land of Judah, the tenth day of Sivan—silver vessels which Sedekias the son of Josias king of Judah had made,
Ekegusii: Nyuma y’omoruoti Nebukadinesaro koira omorwoti Yekonia o Yerusalemu ase obosomba aria Babiloni, amo na abarai bande abanene, abanto bande abwo babwate obomanyi ase emeremo y’oborosia, boigo n’abanto bande.

English: after Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon had carried away Jechonias, the princes, the captives, the mighty men, and the people of the land from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon.
Ekegusii: Abanto bakariika riruube ribwate amang’ana aya: Chibesa echi twabatomeire mogore etugo y’okoruegwa Ekeng’wanso kw’ogosambwa na keria giokorusia ebibe boigo na ubani, boigo mwegorere endagera y’okorugwa ekeng’wanso. Mobirwe ase egesasiimero ki’Omonene Nyasae,

English: And they said: Behold, we have sent you money; therefore buy with the money burnt offerings, sin offerings, and incense, and prepare an oblation, and offer upon the altar of the Lord our God;
Ekegusii: mosabere omorwoti Nebukadinesaro o Babiloni n’omwana oye Belshaza bamenye obogima obotambe buna koreng’ana igoro ere.

English: and pray for the life of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon, and for the life of Baltasar his son, that their days may be as the days of heaven above the earth.
Ekegusii: Erio Omonene natoremie na gotoraa. Nebukadinesaro na momura oye Belshaza batorende, naintwe tobe abaigweri ase bare buna koreng’ana toramenye, erio barabwo bagokigwe naintwe.

English: The Lord will give us strength and light to our eyes. We will live under the shadow of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon and under the shadow of Baltasar his son, and we shall serve them many days, and find favor in their sight.
Ekegusii: Nigo tokobaboria motosabere Omonene Nyasae, ekiagera twakorire ebibe ase obosio bwaye, nere ogechiigwe ase tore.

English: Pray for us also to the Lord our God, for we have sinned against the Lord our God. To this day the wrath of the Lord and his indignation is not turned from us.
Ekegusii: Gaki soma egetabu eke twabatomeire naende mweitie ebibe biaino inwe abanyene ase Hekalu ase rituko ri’eritang’ani ri’omoyega bw’ebigutu boigo namatuko ande amachenu y’omosangererekano.

English: You shall read this book which we have sent to you, to make confession in the house of the Lord upon the day of the feast and on the days of the solemn assembly.
Ekegusii: Aya naro moratebe ekero mogweitia ebibe: Omonene Nyasae oito nomonyaboronge, korende intwe goika bono nigo totubire n’obosoku. Intwe twensi abanto ba Yuda boigo naba Yerusalemu,

English: You shall say: To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us confusion of face, as at this day—to the men of Judah, to the inhabitants of Jerusalem,
Ekegusii: Abarwoti baito, abanene baito, abakuani baito, ababani baito, n’echisokoro chiaito bonsi babekirwe ase obosoku,

English: to our kings, to our princes, to our priests, to our prophets, and to our fathers,
Ekegusii: ekiagera intwe twakorire ebibe ase obosio bw’Omonene Nyasae oito,

English: because we have sinned before the Lord.
Ekegusii: na togatiga komoigwera intwe titwamoigwerete gose komenya koreng’ana n’amachiiko aye.

English: We have disobeyed him and have not listened to the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in the commandments of the Lord that he has set before us.
Ekegusii: Korwa chingaki chiria Omonene arusetie chisokoro chiaito aria Misiri goika rero iga, intwe twagendereire gotaba abegenwa ase are, na twabeire aboro komoigwera.

English: Since the day that the Lord brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt to this present day, we have been disobedient to the Lord our God, and we have been negligent in not listening to his voice.
Ekegusii: Korwa agwo kare ekero Omonene araete chisokoro chiaito korwa aria Misiri, erio atoe ense entenenku na entobu, ere agatoragereria goetera ase omosomba oye Musa. Na goika rero iga intwe nigo togendererete gochandeka ase okoragererigwa okwo.

English: Therefore the plagues have clung to us, along with the curse which the Lord declared through Moses his servant in the day that he brought our fathers out of the land of Egypt to give us a land that flows with milk and honey, as at this day.
Ekegusii: Intwe tokanga koigwera ring’ana ri’Omonene Nyasae oito erio akwanete gocha ase tore goetera ase ababani. Korende intwe ntwensi togakora buna yatogwenerete na tokagenda chinchera chiaito chi’obobe. Togaonchokera chinyasae chinde na gokora ebinto Omonene agechete.

English: Therefore the Lord has made good his word which he pronounced against us, and against our judges who judged Israel, and against our kings, and against our princes, and against the men of Israel and Judah,
Ekegusii: Ase igo bono Omonene okorire ring’ana riria akwanete igoro ase tore, na igoro ase abagambi baito, abarwoti baito, abanene baito, boigo n’abanto na ba Israeli na Yuda.

English: to bring upon us great plagues such as never happened before under the whole heaven, as it came to pass in Jerusalem, according to the things that are written in the law of Moses,
Ekegusii: Ande taiyo ense eng’ima ring’ana riana koba buna eri riabeire Yerusalemu, Omonene nigo akorete aria arigetwe ase amachiiko a Musa.

English: that we should each eat the flesh of our own son, and each eat the flesh of our own daughter.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana nigo abete amakong’u mono goikera omonto are koria abana baye.

English: Moreover he has given them to be in subjection to all the kingdoms that are around us, to be a reproach and a desolation among all the people around us, where the Lord has scattered them.
Ekegusii: Omonene agatoserebania, agatobeka ase amaboko y’echinse chinde echio chiatoetanaine, barabwo bagatorigereria na gotochaya mono.

English: Thus they were cast down and not exalted, because we sinned against the Lord our God in not listening to his voice.
Ekegusii: Nigo twakorete ebibe mamincha y’Omonene Nyasae oito na tokanga komoigwera. Ase igo ense yaito ekabugwa ribaga yarenge ense yobobui.

English: To the Lord our God belongs righteousness, but to us and to our fathers confusion of face, as at this day.
Ekegusii: Omonene Nyasae oito botambe nigo are omonyaboronge, korende intwe amo n’echisokoro chiaito nigo toichire n’obosaria bw’ebirengererio bwaito

English: All these plagues have come upon us which the Lord has pronounced against us.
Ekegusii: Nonya Omonene otoete egesusuro buna ateebete;

English: Yet have we not entreated the favor of the Lord by everyone turning from the thoughts of his wicked heart.
Ekegusii: intwe titwairanete gochia asare na gosaba buna totige ebirengererio biaito ebibe.

English: Therefore the Lord has kept watch over the plagues. The Lord has brought them upon us, for the Lord is righteous in all his works which he has commanded us.
Ekegusii: Titwamoigwerete gose komenya koreng’ana n’amachiiko aye amachenu, goikera Omonene agatorentera egesusuro ekio atogacherete.

English: Yet we have not listened to his voice, to walk in the commandments of the Lord that he has set before us.
Ekegusii: Bono aye Omonene Nyasae o Israeli aye kwarusetie abanto bao ase ense ya Misiri goetera ase okoboko kwao gw’echinguru, goetera ase ebikone, na ase chinguru chinene. Okaorokia chinguru chiao na koeagachera erieta goika rero iga.

English: And now, O Lord, you God of Israel who have brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand, with signs, with wonders, with great power, and with a high arm, and have gotten yourself a name, as at this day:
Ekegusii: Aye Omonene Nyasae oito intwe twakorire ebibe; twabeire aba totari abegenwa; twabeire totari koigwera amachiiko ao onsi.

English: O Lord our God, we have sinned. We have been ungodly. We have done wrong in all your ordinances.
Ekegusii: Korende nigo tokogosaba togenderera kogechigwa naitwe. Aa gati yebisaku ase gwatoserebanetie, intwe twatigirwe ababoraka.

English: Let your wrath turn from us, for we are but a few left among the heathen where you have scattered us.
Ekegusii: Igwa aye Omonene ogosaba gwaito kw’ogosorora; totorie ase engencho y’amasikani ao aye omonyene. Tiga baria batoirete ase omosomba batwanche.

English: Hear our prayer, O Lord, and our petition, and deliver us for your own sake. Give us favor in the sight of those who have led us away captive,
Ekegusii: Erio ense yonsi emanye buna aye Omonene naye Nyasae oito na buna aye gwachorire ense ya Israeli koba abanto bao.

English: that all the earth may know that you are the Lord our God, because Israel and his posterity is called by your name.
Ekegusii: Aye Omonene, Torigererie aa inse korwa agwo igoro orore ogwechanda gwaito. Igwa ogosaba gwaito.

English: O Lord, look down from your holy house and consider us. Incline your ear, O Lord, and hear.
Ekegusii: Igora amaiso ao otorigererie. Abakuure batabwati obomoyo naende ase emebere yabo tibakogotogia gose gokwana igoro y’obuya bwao.

English: Open your eyes, and see; for the dead that are in Hades, whose breath is taken from their bodies, will give to the Lord neither glory nor righteousness;
Ekegusii: Korende abare moyo nabwo boka baragotogie na goitaberana n’ekeene kiao, nonya bachandegete mono, aboro, abare nenchara na emeuko.

English: but the soul who is greatly vexed, who goes stooping and feeble, and the eyes that fail, and the hungry soul, will declare your glory and righteousness, O Lord.
Ekegusii: Aye Omonene Nyasae, nigo togosaba otororere amabera, tari ase engencho ya gento kende kiya giakoretwe n’echisokoro chiaito.

English: For we do not present our supplication before you, O Lord our God, for the righteousness of our fathers and of our kings.
Ekegusii: Nigo gwaonchorete endamwamu yao n’obororo bwao gocha ase tore, buna koreng’ana gwatebete ekero abasomba bao ababani bakwanete ring’ana riao ase tore bagateeba,

English: For you have sent your wrath and your indignation upon us, as you have spoken by your servants the prophets, saying,
Ekegusii: kumba emegongo yaino mokorere omorwoti o Babiloni, nainwe momenye ase ense eria naete chisokoro chiaino.

English: “The Lord says, ‘Bow your shoulders to serve the king of Babylon, and remain in the land that I gave to your fathers.
Ekegusii: Korende komorange koigwera ogochika kwane gwokomokorera,

English: But if you won’t hear the voice of the Lord to serve the king of Babylon,
Ekegusii: nindete omoerio amariogi onsi y’omogoko nemeyega ase emechie ya Yuda na Yerusalemu. Nonya namariogi y’emeyega y’echinyangi takoigwekana naende. Ense yonsi netigwe bosa etamenyiri;

English: I will cause to cease out of the cities of Judah and from the region near Jerusalem the voice of mirth, the voice of gladness, voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride. The whole land will be desolate without inhabitant.’”
Ekegusii: Korende intwe titwaigwerete ogochika kwao gwokomokorera omorwoti o Babiloni, erio aye ogaikerania emeroberio yao eyio gwakorete ekero gwakwanete goetera ase abasomba bao ababani, ekero gwatebete buna amauga y’abarwoti baito n’echisokoro chiaito nairwe korwa ase chimbera chiabo na gosiarerwa.

English: But we wouldn’t listen to your voice, to serve the king of Babylon. Therefore you have made good your words that you spoke by your servants the prophets, that the bones of our kings and the bones of our fathers would be taken out of their places.
Ekegusii: Na ase ekeene bono amauga ayio atugutirwe ase riberera riamobaso na ase obokendu bwa botuko. Barabwo nigo bakwete ase emechando y’enchara, esegi, n’amarwaire.

English: Behold, they are cast out to the heat by day and to the frost by night. They died in great miseries by famine, by sword, and by pestilence.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho y’ebibe bi’abanto ba Israeli na Yuda, gwatigire Hekalu yao yabeire ritombe goika buna ere rero iga.

English: You have made the house that is called by your name as it is today because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
Ekegusii: Korende aye Omonene kwabeire omoremereria ase tore na gwatworokirie amabera amange,

English: Yet, O Lord our God, you have dealt with us after all your kindness and according to all your great mercy,
Ekegusii: Buna kwariete eira goetera ase omosomba oo Musa ekero kwamochiigete ariike amachiiko ao ase obosio bw’Abaisraeli.

English: as you spoke by your servant Moses in the day when you commanded him to write your law in the presence of the children of Israel, saying,
Ekegusii: Onye timokonyigwera’ aye ogateeba goika motigare abake mono ase abanto b’ebisaku agwo ase ndabaserebanie gochia.

English: “If you won’t hear my voice, surely this very great multitude will be turned into a small number among the nations where I will scatter them.
Ekegusii: Nimanyete buna timokonyigwera, ekiagera inwe nabanyabigoti bikong’u. Korende ekero morairwe ase obosomba ase ense ende, imoiranere ibirengererio biaino.

English: For I know that they will not hear me, because they are a stiff-necked people; but in the land of their captivity they will take it to heart,
Ekegusii: Erio momanye ng’a inche ninche Omonene Nyasae, erio nimbae enkoro yokogania komanya n’ebirengererio bi’okomanya.

English: and will know that I am the Lord their God. I will give them a heart and ears to hear.
Ekegusii: Aria ase ense y’obosomba montogie na kong’inyora.

English: Then they will praise me in the land of their captivity, and think about my name,
Ekegusii: Motige koba abanyabigoti bikong’u n’abanyabibe, ekiagera moinyore eki kiaberete chisokoro chiano ekero bangete koigwera Omonene.

English: and will return from their stiff neck and from their wicked deeds; for they will remember the way of their fathers who sinned before the Lord.
Ekegusii: Erio nimbairanie gochia ase ense eria nariete eira koa chisokoro chiaino, Aburaamu, Isaka, Yakobo, erio ebe eyaino naende. Nimbakore mobe abange timogokea naende.

English: I will bring them again into the land which I promised to their fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, and they will rule over it. I will increase them, and they won’t be diminished.
Ekegusii: Ninkore okobwatana gwa kare na kare nainwe; Nimbe Nyasae oino nainwe mobe abanto bane. Tinkobarusia naende inwe abanto ba Israeli korwa ase ense eyio nabaete.

English: O Lord Almighty, you God of Israel, the soul in anguish and the troubled spirit cries to you.
Ekegusii: “Aye Omonene Omobui, Nyasae o Israeli, nigo togokorera intwe korwa ase omoyo ochandegete.

English: Hear, O Lord, and have mercy; for you are a merciful God. Yes, have mercy upon us, because we have sinned before you.
Ekegusii: Toigwe aye Omonene, otororere amabera, ekiagera intwe twakorire ebibe ase ore.

English: For you are enthroned forever, and we keep perishing.
Ekegusii: Aye noo ore kare na kare korende intwe nigo togosira kare na kare.

English: O Lord Almighty, you God of Israel, hear now the prayer of the dead Israelites, and of the children of those who were sinners before you, who didn’t listen to the voice of you their God; because of this, these plagues cling to us.
Ekegusii: Aye Omonene Omonguru, Nyasae bw’Abaisraeli, igwa ogosaba gwaito. Intwe titori abaya kobua abakuure. Chisokoro chiaito chigakora ebibe ase ore aye Omonene Nyasae obo. Bakanga gokoigwera ase igo intwe nigo tochandegete ase engencho y’ebibe biabo.

English: Don’t remember the iniquities of our fathers, but remember your power and your name at this time.
Ekegusii: Toinyora amabe ayio chisokoro chiaito chiakorete agwo kare; ase chingaki chinga buna echi rengereria igoro y’obobui bwao n’erieta riao,

English: For you are the Lord our God, and we will praise you, O Lord.
Ekegusii: ekiagera aye naye Omonene Nyasae oito, naye intwe toratogie.

English: For this cause, you have put your fear in our hearts, to the intent that we should call upon your name. We will praise you in our captivity, for we have called to mind all the iniquity of our fathers who sinned before you.
Ekegusii: Gwatokorire twakoirokire, erio intwe togosabe aye. Aiga ase obosomba ntogotogie ekiagera intwe twatigire ebibe bi’echisokoro chiaito.

English: Behold, we are yet this day in our captivity where you have scattered us, for a reproach and a curse, and to be subject to penalty according to all the iniquities of our fathers who departed from the Lord our God.
Ekegusii: Gwatosiareire intwe ase chinse chinde, kwabakorire batochayire na gotoragereria. Nigo ogotoa egesusuro ase engencho y’ebibe bi’echisokoro chiaito ekero bakorete ebibe mamincha yao aye Omonene Nyasae.”

English: Hear, O Israel, the commandments of life! Give ear to understand wisdom!
Ekegusii: Tegerera ogochika kw’obogima, aye Israeli! Tega ogoto oigwe obong’aini.

English: How is it, O Israel, that you are in your enemies’ land, that you have become old in a strange country, that you are defiled with the dead,
Ekegusii: Inaki yabete aye Israeli okenyora ase ense y’obosomba? Na kobekwa ogotacheneka buna oria okwete?

English: that you are counted with those who are in Hades?
Ekegusii: Inaki yabete aye okabarwa koba oyomo bwa baria bakuure?

English: You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom.
Ekegusii: Nase engencho aye gwatigire ensoko y’omogima!

English: If you had walked in the way of God, you would have dwelled in peace forever.
Ekegusii: Onye nkwagendete ase chinchera chia Nyasae, ang’a nigo kwamenyete n’omorembe goika kare na kare.

English: Learn where there is wisdom, where there is strength, and where there is understanding, that you may also know where there is length of days and life, where there is the light of the eyes and peace.
Ekegusii: Eegerie korwa ase chisemi, obomanyi n’echinguru bikonyorekana. Erio aye omanye ase oranyore obogima obuya obotambe, oborabu bokorae boigo n’omorembe.

English: Who has found out her place? Who has come into her treasuries?
Ekegusii: Onde taiyo ona konyora ase obong’aini bomenyete gose onde taiyo ona gosoa ase ekiage kiaye,

English: Where are the princes of the heathen, and those who ruled the beasts that are on the earth,
Ekegusii: Ngai bare abanene b’echinse, baria bakoraa ching’iti ase chinguru? Ngai bare baria bakogosoria n’echinyoni chia igoro baria bakwegachera chifeta n’echitaabu echio abanto baganetie naende tibari goisaneka gochirigia?

English: those who had their pastime with the fowls of the air, and those who hoarded up silver and gold, in which people trust, and of their getting there is no end?
Ekegusii: Ng’ai bare baria baroberetie na gwechanda korigia enibo abwo emeremo yabo etatigete kemanyererio kende?

English: For those who diligently sought silver, and were so anxious, and whose works are past finding out,
Ekegusii: Bonsi abwo basirire basoire ase ense y’abakuure. Abande bachire bairire ribaga riabo.

English: they have vanished and gone down to Hades, and others have come up in their place.
Ekegusii: Ekegori ekeyia kiaiboirwe na komenya ase ense, korende nonya nkerokio tikiamanyete enchera y’echisemi. Tikiamanyete enchera y’obong’aini gose koboikera.

English: Younger men have seen the light and lived upon the earth, but they haven’t known the way of knowledge,
Ekegusii: Nonya n’abana babo nigo basireretigwe n’obong’aini.

English: nor understood its paths. Their children haven’t embraced it. They are far off from their way.
Ekegusii: Bong’aini tibwanyorekanete gati y’abakanani, boigo nonya na ba Edomu tibaboroche.

English: It has not been heard of in Canaan, neither has it been seen in Teman.
Ekegusii: Nonya bakorigia chisemi, enchera yobong’aini teranyorekana ase egati y’abaonchoreria ba Merani na Tamani gose ase baria bagokwana igoro y’emegano, tibaregera kende gionsi igoro y’obong’aini, tibamanyeti kende gionsi igoro y’echinchera chi’obong’aini.

English: The sons also of Agar who seek understanding, which are in the land, the merchants of Merran and Teman, and the authors of fables, and the searchers out of understanding—none of these have known the way of wisdom or remembered her paths.
Ekegusii: Aye Israeli ngaki ore omonene enyomba ya Nyasae! Inaki ore omonene aye ense y’Omonene!

English: O Israel, how great is the house of God! How large is the place of his possession!
Ekegusii: Nigo ere enene mono tebwati moerio; nigo ere engare etanyare korengeka.

English: It is great and has no end. It is high and unmeasurable.
Ekegusii: Amamonto a kare noo aiboretwe aa; abanto abanyanguru na abamanyi ase esegi.

English: Giants were born that were famous of old, great of stature, and expert in war.
Ekegusii: Korende Nyasae tabachorete babe abanto baye gose tabaorogeti chinchera chi’echisemi.

English: God didn’t choose these, nor did he give the way of knowledge to them,
Ekegusii: Ase igo bagasira ase engencho batarenge n’obong’aini; bagasira ase engencho y’oboriri bwabo abanyene.

English: so they perished, because they had no wisdom. They perished through their own foolishness.
Ekegusii: Ning’o orinete gochia igoro erio korigia obong’aini, akaboreta korwa igoro ase amare?

English: Who has gone up into heaven, taken her, and brought her down from the clouds?
Ekegusii: Ning’o onya gotara ase amache ime erio korigia obong’aini, gose kobogora ase rigori ri’echitaabu.

English: Who has gone over the sea, found her, and will bring her for choice gold?
Ekegusii: Monto onde taiyo omanyete enchera y’okogenda ase bore, gose omanyete enchera ekogenda ase bore.

English: There is no one who knows her way, nor any who comprehend her path.
Ekegusii: Oyo bweka omanyete obong’aini Nyasae, na ere nigo amanyete ebinto bionsi. Goetera ase okomanya kwaye ere akabonyora. Agakora ense korwa kare erio akayeichoria ebintongwa bionsi.

English: But he that knows all things knows her, he found her out with his understanding. He who prepared the earth for all time has filled it with four-footed beasts.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo agotoma oborabu na borobwo bwamoigwera; akaborangeria naborobwo bokamoigwera.

English: It is he who sends forth the light, and it goes. He called it, and it obeyed him with fear.
Ekegusii: Ching’enang’eni nigo chikobara ase abo ase omogoko, ere nigo agochirangeria na chirochio chiaitaba, “Noo tore aa”. Nigo chikobara ase omogoko gochia ase oria ochitongete.

English: The stars shone in their watches, and were glad. When he called them, they said, “Here we are.” They shone with gladness to him who made them.
Ekegusii: Oyo nere Nyasae oito, onde taiyo orareng’anigwe nere.

English: This is our God. No other can be compared to him.
Ekegusii: Nyasae nere omanyete enchera ekogenda ase okomanya na akaa abasomba baye Abaisraeli abwo anchete obong’aini

English: He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant and to Israel who is loved by him.
Ekegusii: Korwa chingaki echio kogenderera, obong’aini bokarorekana ase ense na bokamenya na mwanyabaanto.

English: This is the book of God’s commandments and the law that endures forever. All those who hold it fast will live, but those who leave it will die.
Ekegusii: Obong’aini n’egetabu ki’amachiiko a Nyasae, borobwo n’erichiiko riria riramenye kare na kare. Baria bonsi bakobwaterera obong’aini mbamenye, korende baria barabotige mbakue.

English: Turn, O Jacob, and take hold of it. Walk toward the shining of its light.
Ekegusii: Onchokera obong’aini inwe abanto ba Israeli na mobobwate. Tara gochia ase chinchera chi’okobara kwaye.

English: Don’t give your glory to another, nor the things that are to your advantage to a foreign nation.
Ekegusii: Tobaisa koa monto onde bwensi obomanyi.

English: O Israel, we are happy; for the things that are pleasing to God are made known to us.
Ekegusii: Mogoko ki ase intwe Abaisraeli; ekiagera twaikire komanyigwa aria akomogokia Nyasae okoremia kw’Abaisraeli.

English: Be of good cheer, my people, the memorial of Israel.
Ekegusii: Ee omoyo inwe abanto bane; abwo mokorenda erieta ria Israeli.

English: You were not sold to the nations for destruction, but because you moved God to wrath, you were delivered to your adversaries.
Ekegusii: Inwe timwaonetigwe ase abanto b’ebisaku erio mosire, korende nigo mwabegetwe ase amaboko ababisa baino ase engencho mwamogechetie Nyasae.

English: For you provoked him who made you by sacrificing to demons and not to God.
Ekegusii: Ekero mwaruete ebingwanso ase ebirecha ribaga ria Nyasae nigo mwabeetie oria obatongete.

English: You forgot the everlasting God who brought you up. You also grieved Jerusalem, who nursed you.
Ekegusii: Mokeeba Nyasae o kare na kare oyio obarerete, mokareta amagombo ase omochie o Yerusalemu oyio obarendete.

English: For she saw the wrath that came upon you from God, and said, “Listen, you who dwell near Zion; for God has brought upon me great mourning.
Ekegusii: Omochie o Yerusalemu okarora endamwamu eyio yabacherete korwa ase Nyasae: Ogateeba gochia ase emechie eria yayoetananete Rora obororo obwo Nyasae andeteire.

English: For I have seen the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting has brought upon them.
Ekegusii: Narorire abana bane bakoirwa obosomba, eyio Nyasae okare na kare abarenteire.

English: For with joy I nourished them, but sent them away with weeping and mourning.
Ekegusii: Inche nigo nabarerete ase omogoko, korende bono nabatigire bagendire n’amariga y’obororo.

English: Let no man rejoice over me, a widow and forsaken by many. For the sins of my children, I am left desolate, because they turned away from the law of God
Ekegusii: Monto onde tagokera ogochandeka kwane bono ase engencho inde omoboraka, na abana bane abange bakure. Nigo natigetwe buna omochie otamenyiri ase engencho bangete koigwera amachiiko a Nyasae.

English: and had no regard for his statutes. They didn’t walk in the ways of God’s commandments or tread in the paths of discipline in his righteousness.
Ekegusii: Tibabwate masikani ase ebirage bia Nyasae nakomenya koreng’ana nokogania kwa Nyasae. Bakanga koraagwa n’oboronge bwa Nyasae.

English: Let those who dwell near Zion come and remember the captivity of my sons and daughters, which the Everlasting has brought upon them.
Ekegusii: Inwe abaamate ba Siyoni inchuo morore buna Nyasae o kare na kare atomire abana bane gochia obosomba.

English: For he has brought a nation upon them from afar, a shameless nation with a strange language, who didn’t respect old men or pity children.
Ekegusii: Akabarentera ense korwa are, ense etabwati masikani eyio egokwana ase omonwa omogeni na etabwati masikani ase abagaka gose amabera ase abana.

English: They have carried away the dear beloved sons of the widow, and left her who was alone desolate of her daughters.”
Ekegusii: Abanto abwo bakaira abana abamura na abaiseke abanchwa bane erio inche ngatigara omoboraka, nigo inde inche bweka.

English: But I—how can I help you?
Ekegusii: Abana bane abwo bare ase obosomba, kende tikeiyo ndakore erio mbakonye.

English: For he who brought these calamities upon you will deliver you from the hand of your enemies.
Ekegusii: Oria bweka obarenterete egesusuro eke nere orabatorie korwa ase ababisa baino.

English: Go your way, O my children. Go your way, for I am left desolate.
Ekegusii: Genda inwe abana bane; menya obogima bwaino! Bono natigaire inche bweka.

English: I have put off the garment of peace, and put on the sackcloth of my petition. I will cry to the Everlasting as long as I live.
Ekegusii: Naaboirie omwambaro oria nkobeka ase engaki y’omorembe, neboirie buna omonto okorera. Nindere gochia ase Nyasae o kare na kare chingaki chiane chionsi erio ange obokonyi.

English: Take courage, my children. Cry to God, and he will deliver you from the power and hand of the enemies.
Ekegusii: Eremie inwe abana bane, na rera gochia ase Nyasae erio abae obokonyi. Ere nabakonye korwa ase ogochandwa, na korwa ase chinguru chi’ababisa baino.

English: For I have trusted in the Everlasting, that he will save you; and joy has come to me from the Holy One, because of the mercy that will soon come to you from your Everlasting Savior.
Ekegusii: Ninde n’ogosemeria buna Nyasae o kare na kare nabasibore bwango iga. Omochenu, omotoria oino o kare na kare nandetere omogoko ekero arabarorere amabera.

English: For I sent you out with mourning and weeping, but God will give you to me again with joy and gladness forever.
Ekegusii: Nigo narerete na kweumia ekero mwairetwe, korende Nyasae nabairanie gocha naende erio andetere omogoko.

English: For as now those who dwell near Zion have seen your captivity, so they will shortly see your salvation from our God which will come upon you with great glory and brightness of the Everlasting.
Ekegusii: Buna korengana chinse echio chibaetanaine chiabaroche buna mokoirwa obosomba, chirochio naende nchirore Nyasae o kare na kare ogocha ase obonene bwaye kobatoria.

English: My children, suffer patiently the wrath that has come upon you from God, for your enemy has persecuted you; but shortly you will see his destruction and will tread upon their necks.
Ekegusii: Abana bane remereria egesusuro kia Nyasae. Ababisa baino babachandire, korende bwango iga nkobarora more bagosirigwa ase engencho mwaroreirwe amabera.

English: My delicate ones have traveled rough roads. They were taken away like a flock carried off by enemies.
Ekegusii: Abana baane nigo nababegete ase obwanchani, korende mogachora kogenda ase chinchera chimbe erio mokaimokigwa buna ching’ondi chiabwatirwe na koirwa n’ababisa.

English: Take courage, my children, and cry to God; for you will be remembered by him who has brought this upon you.
Ekegusii: “Remereria abana bane, na morere ase Nyasae monyore obokonyi. Ere nigo abaete egesusuro korende tarabeba.

English: For as it was your decision to go astray from God, return and seek him ten times more.
Ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana mweruete kogenda mamincha ya Nyasae, bono inwe irana gochia ase are momokorere ara ikomi.

English: For he who brought these calamities upon you will bring you everlasting joy again with your salvation.
Ekegusii: Ere oria obareterete emechando eye nabatorie nakobaretera omochengo o kare na kare.”

English: Take courage, O Jerusalem, for he who called you by name will comfort you.
Ekegusii: Eremie aye Yerusalemu. Nyasae oria okoete erieta riao, nakoretere oboremu.

English: Miserable are those who afflicted you and rejoiced at your fall.
Ekegusii: Obobe n’obwabo baria bakorenterete emechando erio bakagosekerera ekero kwaguete.

English: Miserable are the cities which your children served. Miserable is she who received your sons.
Ekegusii: Emechando nechere emechie eria yairete abana bao buna abasomba. Emechando nechere Babiloni omochie oria omerete abana bao.

English: For as she rejoiced at your fall and was glad of your ruin, so she will be grieved at her own desolation.
Ekegusii: Buna koreng’ana omochie oria ogogete na gochengera okogwa kwao, nabo igo bono norere ekero oro omonyene oratigwe.

English: And I will take away her pride in her great multitude and her boasting will be turned into mourning.
Ekegusii: Ning’onchore ogwetogia kwaye kobe okorera na nindusie obonge bw’abanto baye abwo agwetogeria.

English: For fire will come upon her from the Everlasting for many days; and she will be inhabited by demons for a long time.
Ekegusii: Inche Nyasae o kare na kare nintome omorero igoro ase are, oyio orasambe ase amatuko amange. Amatombe aye nabe obomenyo bw’ebirecha ase amatuko amange.

English: O Jerusalem, look around you toward the east, and behold the joy that comes to you from God.
Ekegusii: Rigeria gochia ensemo ya moocha morore omogoko Nyasae abarenteire.

English: Behold, your sons come, whom you sent away. They come gathered together from the east to the west at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the glory of God.
Ekegusii: Rora abana baino bairanire gocha inka, abana abwo bairetwe korwa ase more. Basangererigwe bonsi amo korwa moocha na bosongo ase ogochika kwa Nyasae Omochenu. Na bono nkoirana bare gocha inka bare n’omogoko ase obonene bwa Nyasae.

English: Take off the garment of your mourning and affliction, O Jerusalem, and put on forever the beauty of the glory from God.
Ekegusii: Aye Yerusalemu eaborie chianga chiria kwabegete ase engaki y’emechando n’okweumia, eboyie botambe obuya n’obonene bwa Nyasae.

English: Put on the robe of the righteousness from God. Set on your head a diadem of the glory of the Everlasting.
Ekegusii: Eboyie oboronge bwa Nyasae. Beka egutwa y’oboronge bwa Nyasae o kare na kare ase omotwe oo.

English: For God will show your splendor everywhere under heaven.
Ekegusii: Nyasae naorokie obonene bwao gochia ase chinse chionsi.

English: For your name will be called by God forever “Righteous Peace, Godly Glory”.
Ekegusii: Ere nakoe erieta eri kare na kare “Omorembe oo nigo okorwa korwa ase obochenu bwao, na obonene bwao nigo bogocha goetera ase okwerwa ase Nyasae.”

English: Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand upon the height. Look around you toward the east and see your children gathered from the going down of the sun to its rising at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing that God has remembered them.
Ekegusii: Imoka aye Yerusalemu, tenena ase ebitunwa igoro; rigereria ase Nyasae Omochenu agosangereria abana baino korwa moocha na bosongo. Nigo bagogete buna Nyasae obainyoire.

English: For they went from you on foot, being led away by their enemies, but God brings them in to you carried on high with glory, on a royal throne.
Ekegusii: Yerusalemu, abana bao nigo bairetwe korwa ase ore n’ababisa babo; bakagotiga bakagenda n’amagoro, korende Nyasae nkobairania are gocha ase ore n’obonene.

English: For God has appointed that every high mountain and the everlasting hills should be made low, and the valleys filled up to make the ground level, that Israel may go safely in the glory of God.
Ekegusii: Nyasae orure ogochika ng’a kera egetunwa ekenene na biria bia kare na kare bikeigwe; ochikire buna amabwago atichwe n’ense earanigwe, erio abanto ba Israeli bairane gocha inka ase obonene bwa Nyasae.

English: Moreover the woods and every sweet smelling tree have shaded Israel by the commandment of God.
Ekegusii: Ase ogochika kwa Nyasae chinsana n’emete eyio okorwa ogotioka okuya nee abanto ba Israeli ekiriri.

English: For God will lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory with the mercy and righteousness that come from him.
Ekegusii: Nyasae narae Abaisraeli ase omogoko gocha inka; bakoragwa n’amabera aye boigo n’obonene bwaye baetananire n’oborabu bw’obonene bwaye.

English: A copy of a letter that Jeremy sent to those who were to be led captives into Babylon by the king of the Babylonians, to give them the message that God commanded him.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho y’ebibe mwakorire ase Nyasae, bono omorwoti Nebukadinesaro nkobaira are obosomba aria Babiloni.

English: Because of the sins which you have committed before God, you will be led away captives to Babylon by Nabuchodonosor king of the Babylonians.
Ekegusii: Nyuma komwaikire oo, mobere oo ase emiaka emenge, mobee oo ase ebigori bitano na bibere. Korende nyuma yayio Nyasae nabairanie gocha inka seino ase omorembe.

English: So when you come to Babylon, you will remain there many years, and for a long season, even for seven generations. After that, I will bring you out peacefully from there.
Ekegusii: Agwo Babiloni ase omosomba inwe ina mwerorere chinyasae chirosirie korwa ase emete, chifeta boigo n’echitaabu-chinyasae echio abanto bakoimokia ase amareko abo erio kwoboyia abanto abwo batamomanyeti Nyasae.

English: But now you will see in Babylon gods of silver, gold, and wood carried on shoulders, which cause the nations to fear.
Ekegusii: Mwerende inwe timobaisa kwegia abanto abwo b’ebisaku. Chinyasae echio tichiboboyia ekero morarore abanto bagochisasiima ase okorobekana kwabo.

English: Beware therefore that you in no way become like these foreigners. Don’t let fear take hold of you because of them when you see the multitude before them and behind them, worshiping them.
Ekegusii: Korende inwe eteebie ase emioyo yaino: “Naye bweka Omonene, naye intwe toganeirie gosasiima!”

English: But say in your hearts, “O Lord, we must worship you.”
Ekegusii: Omomalaika o Nyasae nabe nainwe; ere nabarende.

English: For my angel is with you, and I myself care for your souls.
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echio nigo chibwate emenwa, korende nigo chibachire n’abaroisia, ekeene nigo chichabeire chitaabu, korende tichiri chinyasae chi’ekeene ekiagera tichigokwana.

English: For their tongue is polished by the workman, and they themselves are overlaid with gold and with silver; yet they are only fake, and can’t speak.
Ekegusii: Abanto abwo nigo bakoroisia chigutwa chi’echitaabu erio babekera chinyasae echio ase emetwe yabo, buna korengana bakobekera omoiseke bwanchete gwechabera.

English: And taking gold, as if it were for a virgin who loves to be happy, they make crowns for the heads of their gods.
Ekegusii: Chingaki chinde abakuani nigo bakoiba chitaabu korwa ase chinyasae echio, bakorera emeremo yabo abanyene;

English: Sometimes also the priests take gold and silver from their gods, and spend it on themselves.
Ekegusii: naende baa chitaabu n’echifeta chinde abatayayi b’ekalu. Abanto nigo bakoira chinyasae echi chi’emete, chifeta, boigo n’echitaabu bachibekera chianga orakagere buna n’abanto.

English: They will even give some of it to the common prostitutes. They dress them like men with garments, even the gods of silver, gods of gold, and gods of wood.
Ekegusii: Korende nonya chinyasae echio chiboirie chianga buna abarwoti, korende chirochio tichikonyara gwetanga koriegwa n’amage.

English: Yet these gods can’t save themselves from rust and moths, even though they are covered with purple garments.
Ekegusii: Ekero ebuse ekorwa ase hekalu egochigwera ase obosio bwabo, omonto goika achitinyie.

English: They wipe their faces because of the dust of the temple, which is thick upon them.
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echio nigo chibwate chinyimbo chi’oborwoti ase amaboko abo, korende tichibwati nguru chinde chiokoa onde bwensi orachikorere bobe egesusuro.

English: And he who can’t put to death one who offends against him holds a sceptre, as though he were judge of a country.
Ekegusii: Chingaki chinde nigo chikoimokia omoyio obirende n’egesire koboko kwabo, korende chirochio tichikonyara gwetanga korwa gosarigwa ase esegi gose korwa koirwa n’abaibi.

English: He has also a dagger in his right hand, and an axe, but can’t deliver himself from war and robbers.
Ekegusii: Ebio bionsi nigo bigotoorokia buna chirochio tichiri chinyasae ase igo timochisasiima.

English: By this they are known not to be gods. Therefore don’t fear them.
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echio chikaransete ase chikaru chiabo nigo chire bosa buna enyongo yategete. Amaiso abo nigo aichire ebuse eyio abanto bagwetinyia amagoro ekero bagosoa hekalu ime.

English: For like a vessel that a man uses is worth nothing when it is broken, even so it is with their gods. When they are set up in the temples, their eyes are full of dust through the feet of those who come in.
Ekegusii: Abakuani nigo bagosieka ebiita boigo n’echinyasi n’echichuma erio gotanga abaibi. Chinyasae echio nigo chisiekeire buna omosibwa ore ange gochia goitwa ase okomochera omorwoti.

English: As the courts are secured on every side upon him who offends the king, as being committed to suffer death, even so the priests secure their temples with doors, with locks, and bars, lest they be carried off by robbers.
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echio nigo chigotongerigwa chitaaya chinyinge goetania nonya buna abakuani abwo baganetie korende chirochio tichikorora kende.

English: They light candles for them, yes, more than for themselves, even though they can’t see one.
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echio nigo chikoriegwa korwa ime n’amage, buna emetobwa y’emete y’ekalu, n’echianga chiabo nigo chigosarigwa korende chirochio tichikomanya.

English: They are like one of the beams of the temple. Men say their hearts are eaten out when things creeping out of the earth devour both them and their clothing. They don’t feel it
Ekegusii: Amasio abo abaire amamwamu kobwatekana n’erioki rikorwa ase hekalu.

English: when their faces are blackened through the smoke that comes out of the temple.
Ekegusii: Ebitabaramato, n’ebiongo boigo n’echinyoni chinde nigo chikoiruruka igoro y’echinyasae echio, nonya n’ebimoni nigo bigochinkaransera.

English: Bats, swallows, and birds land on their bodies and heads. So do the cats.
Ekegusii: Ayio onsi nigo agotworokia buna chirochio tichiri chinyasae timochisasiima.

English: By this you may know that they are no gods. Therefore don’t fear them.
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echio nigo chichabeire chitaabu erio gochikora chirorekane buya, korende tichikororekana buya otatiga omonto eyeigosire ekero chiare kobachwa chirochio tichiaigwete kende.

English: Notwithstanding the gold with which they are covered to make them beautiful, unless someone wipes off the tarnish, they won’t shine; for they didn’t even feel it when they were molten.
Ekegusii: Tari mang’ana igori ring’ana ng’aki chirabekerwe; chirochio tichiri koeyana.

English: Things in which there is no breath are bought at any cost.
Ekegusii: Nigo chikobogorigwa n’abanto ase amareko ase engencho tichikonyara gotara ase amagoro abo ayio nigo akworokia abanto maiso marore buna chirochio tichibwati kobua konde.

English: Having no feet, they are carried upon shoulders. By this, they declare to men that they are worth nothing.
Ekegusii: Nonya nabwo bagochikorera nigo bagochirorera obosoku ekero chikogwa inse, ekiagera nigo akobetererigwa gochimokia naende.

English: Those who serve them are also ashamed, for if they fall to the ground at any time, they can’t rise up again by themselves. If they are bowed down, they can’t make themselves straight; but the offerings are set before them, as if they were dead men.
Ekegusii: Abakuani nigo bakoonia biria bikorugwa ebingwanso ase chinyasae echio baira chitaabu. N’abakungu b’abakuani nigo bakogacha biria bikorugwa ebingwanso ase okobibeka omonyo tibisareka ribaga bagosanga n’abataka na baria batari kwenyara.

English: And the things that are sacrificed to them, their priests sell and spend. In like manner, their wives also lay up part of it in salt; but to the poor and to the impotent they give none of it.
Ekegusii: Nonya n’abakungu baria bare ase chingaki chiabo na baria bagonkirie nigo bagwancherwa gokuna ebingwanso. Ayio onsi nigo agotworokia buna chinyasae echio tichiri echi’ekeene-timochisasiima.

English: The menstruous woman and the woman in childbed touch their sacrifices, knowing therefore by these things that they are no gods. Don’t fear them.
Ekegusii: Inaki chirarokwe chinyasae, ekero abakungu bagwancherwa korwa ebingwanso ase ebinto ebio biroisirie korwa ase emete, chifeta n’echitaabu?

English: For how can they be called gods? Because women set food before the gods of silver, gold, and wood.
Ekegusii: Nonya n’abakuani nigo bagoinsaransa ase chikalu chingaki chi’okorera beboyetie chianga chitandogete n’emetwe egingeire etatubiri.

English: And in their temples the priests sit on seats, having their clothes torn and their heads and beards shaven, and nothing on their heads.
Ekegusii: Abakuani abwo nigo bakorera ase chinyasae chiabo orakage buna na chirochio nao chiare ase ebirero.

English: They roar and cry before their gods, as men do at the feast when one is dead.
Ekegusii: Nigo bakorusia chianga chi’echinyasae chiabo baa abakungu babo boigo n’abana babo.

English: The priests also take off garments from them and clothe their wives and children with them.
Ekegusii: Gokorera chinyasae echio amabe gose amaya tari mang’ana; ekiagera ero enyene tekonyara goakana egesiomba. Tichikonyara kobeka omorwoti gose komorusia,

English: Whether it is evil or good what one does to them, they are not able to repay it. They can’t set up a king or put him down.
Ekegusii: tichigokora omonto omonda gose chimoe chitaabu. Onye omonto orire eira ase chire korende tayeikerania, tichikomokora aakane.

English: In like manner, they can neither give riches nor money. Though a man make a vow to them and doesn’t keep it, they will never exact it.
Ekegusii: Tichigotoria omonto korwa amakweri gose gokonya omonto otari na nguru korwa ase oria ore n’echinguru.

English: They can save no man from death. They can’t deliver the weak from the mighty.
Ekegusii: Tichikonyara gokora omouko arore naende, gose chitorie omonto korwa ase emechando.

English: They can’t restore a blind man to his sight, or deliver anyone who is in distress.
Ekegusii: Tichikororera ababoraka gose chintakana amabera.

English: They can show no mercy to the widow, or do good to the fatherless.
Ekegusii: Ebinto ebi bibachire korwa ase emete na gochaberwa chifeta n’echitaabu tibiri na nguru chinde, nigo binga buna rigena riarusigwe korwa ase egetunwa; na baria bakobisasiima mbabekwe ase obosoku.

English: They are like the stones that are cut out of the mountain, these gods of wood that are overlaid with gold and with silver. Those who minister to them will be confounded.
Ekegusii: Inaki eranyarekane omonto akagere buna birobwo n’echinyasae gose abiroke chinyasae?

English: How could a man then think or say that they are gods, when even the Chaldeans themselves dishonor them?
Ekegusii: Ekero omonto are rimama nigo bakomoimokia bamoira ase hekalu baboria Bel amoe chinguru chi’ogokwana, orakage buna Bel naigwete kende.

English: If they shall see one mute who can’t speak, they bring him and ask him to call upon Bel, as though he were able to understand.
Ekegusii: Nonya nekero abanto bamanyete buna chinyasae chiabo tichikobakonya, barabwo nigo bagendererete koba abariri ase ogochisasiima.

English: Yet they can’t perceive this themselves, and forsake them; for they have no understanding.
Ekegusii: Tari ayio oka, abakungu nigo bagwesiba chinkini na goisaransa ase chinchera bagosamba ubani na gokora obotayayi bwabo. Oyomo obo ekero airirwe n’omosacha na korara nere, nigo akoirana na gosekerera oria onde otigara buna ere tari kieni nakio gekogera atairwa.

English: The women also with cords around them sit in the ways, burning bran for incense; but if any of them, drawn by someone who passes by, lies with him, she reproaches her fellow, that she was not thought as worthy as herself and her cord wasn’t broken.
Ekegusii: Kera egento igoro y’echinyasae echio n’oborimo; ngaki rende eranyarekane korengereria gose gochiroka chinyasae?

English: Whatever is done among them is false. How could a man then think or say that they are gods?
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echio nigo chiroisirie n’ababachi be chibao na baria b’echichuma, ase igo chirochio tichikoba kende gionsi otatiga keria ababachi batagete kebe.

English: They are fashioned by carpenters and goldsmiths. They can be nothing else than what the workmen make them to be.
Ekegusii: Nonya nabaroisia babo tibari komenya ngaki ’ntambe! Inaki rende eranyarekane barabwo korosia chinyasae?

English: And they themselves who fashioned them can never continue long. How then should the things that are fashioned by them?
Ekegusii: Abanto abwo nigo bagotiga oborimo n’obosoku ase oroiboro rwabo.

English: For they have left lies and reproaches to those who come after.
Ekegusii: Ekero chiseegi gose emechando yachire, abakuani nigo bakoroberia ase bakwebisa n’echinyasae chiabo.

English: For when there comes any war or plague upon them, the priests consult with themselves, where they may be hidden with them.
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echio tichibwati nguru ase esegi gose emechando. Inki gekogera abanto batari komanya buna emegwekano eye teri chinyasae?

English: How then can’t men understand that they are no gods, which can’t save themselves from war or from plague?
Ekegusii: Emegwekano eye teri kende, eye n’emete ebachire egachaberwa chifeta n’echitaabu; rituko erimo nemanyekane buna ekeene echi tichiri chinyasae.

English: For seeing they are only wood and overlaid with gold and silver, it will be known hereafter that they are false.
Ekegusii: Chinse chionsi n’abarwoti mbache komanya buna emegwekano tari kende otatiga emeremo ya mwanyabaanto. Ero tebwati chinguru chi’echinyasae;

English: It will be manifest to all nations and kings that they are no gods, but the works of men’s hands, and that there is no work of God in them.
Ekegusii: n’onde bwensi naganeirie komanya buna emegwekano eye teri nyasae.

English: Who then may not know that they are not gods?
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echi tichigokora onde bwensi koba omorwoti gose tichikoreta mbura.

English: For they can’t set up a king in a land or give rain to men.
Ekegusii: Tichikonyara konacha kina igoro y’amang’ana abo gose gokonya omonto oyio okoriananigwa; chirochio tichigokora kende; nigo chinga ebigonkoru bikoiruruka ase embeo.

English: They can’t judge their own cause, or redress a wrong, being unable; for they are like crows between heaven and earth.
Ekegusii: Ekero hekalu yabwatirwe omorero, abakuani nigo bagotama erio gwetoria, batiga chinyasae echio chichongire korwa ase emete na gochaberwa chifeta n’echitaabu chikoyia buna obonyansi.

English: For even when fire falls upon the house of gods of wood overlaid with gold or with silver, their priests will flee away, and escape, but they themselves will be burned apart like beams.
Ekegusii: Tichikorwania barwoti gose kogenda esegi ase ababisa. Inaki omonto aregene buna echio n’echinyasae?

English: Moreover they can’t withstand any king or enemies. How could a man then admit or think that they are gods?
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echi chi’emete echabeire chifeta n’echitaabu, tichikonyara gwetanga korwa ase abaibi gose abauri,

English: Those gods of wood overlaid with silver or with gold aren’t able to escape from thieves or robbers.
Ekegusii: abwo bakoira chifeta n’echitaabu boigo n’echianga chi’echinyasae erio bagenda nabirobio bionsi. Chinyasae tichigokora kende erio gokania abaibi nabauri.

English: The gold, silver, and garments with which they are clothed—those who are strong will take from them, and go away with them. They won’t be able to help themselves.
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echio nigo chire bosa tichikoreng’anigwa omorwoti ore n’echinguru gose ekengese ki’enyongo ekio kebwenerete omonyene. Chinyasae echio chi’oborimo tichikorenganigwa nonya n’omorangwa bw’enyomba oyio ogosikwa orenda ebinto nyoma. Nonya n’esiro eyemo ase enyomba y’omorwoti nigo ere buya goetania chinyasae echio chi’oborimo.

English: Therefore it is better to be a king who shows his manhood, or else a vessel in a house profitable for whatever the owner needs, than such false gods—or even a door in a house, to keep the things safe that are in it, than such false gods; or better to be a pillar of wood in a palace than such false gods.
Ekegusii: Nyasae akarwa omobaso, omotienyi boigo n’eching’enang’eni birwe oborabu nabirobio bikamoigwera.

English: For sun, moon, and stars, being bright and sent to do their jobs, are obedient.
Ekegusii: Boigo chinkoba nembeo. Enkoba nabo ekororekana are na agare, n’embeo nabo ekogusa ande onsi.

English: Likewise also the lightning when it flashes is beautiful to see. In the same way, the wind also blows in every country.
Ekegusii: Ekero Nyasae agochika amare arande igoro ase ense yonsi aro nigo akomoigwera.

English: And when God commands the clouds to go over the whole world, they do as they are told.
Ekegusii: Ekero Nyasae agotoma omorero korwa igoro osambe ebitunwa n’echinsana, oro nigo ogokora keria otebigwa. Emegwekano tegokora binto ebi ero tegokora nonya eki kegocherera.

English: And the fire sent from above to consume mountains and woods does as it is commanded; but these are to be compared to them neither in show nor power.
Ekegusii: Inaki rende ero erarokwe chinyasae onye tekonyara gotokonya gose gotomochera ase nchera ende yonsi?

English: Therefore a man shouldn’t think or say that they are gods, seeing they aren’t able to judge causes or to do good to men.
Ekegusii: Imomanyete buna ero teri nyasae timoyesasiima.

English: Knowing therefore that they are no gods, don’t fear them.
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echi tichibwati nguru igoro ase abarwoti; tichikonyara koragereria gose gosesenia.

English: For they can neither curse nor bless kings.
Ekegusii: Tichikonyara gokorera chinse kemanyererio kende gionsi igoro ase amare; tichikonyara kobara buna risase gose omotienyi.

English: They can’t show signs in the heavens among the nations, or shine as the sun, or give light as the moon.
Ekegusii: Nonya n’eching’iti chi’orosana nigo chire buya goetania emegwekano eye; chirochio nabo chigotama korwa ase amakueri erio gwetoria.

English: The beasts are better than they; for they can get under a covert, and help themselves.
Ekegusii: Ase igo nabo emanyekanete buna chirochio tichiri chinyasae timochisasiima.

English: In no way then is it manifest to us that they are gods. Therefore don’t fear them.
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echio chiabo chiroisirie korwa ase emete na gochaberwa chifeta n’echitaabu, nigo chinga omoeto biogosereria chinyoni ase omogondo tichikonyara korenda monto onde bwensi.

English: For as a scarecrow in a garden of cucumbers that keeps nothing, so are their gods of wood overlaid with gold and silver.
Ekegusii: Chinyasae echio nigo chinga buna orosana rwa magwa ase omogondo, ribaga rogotanga chinyoni tichicha ase omogondo, rororwo nigo rokoa chinyoni ase chigoikaransa. Chinyasae echio nigo chinga omobere otugutire ase omosunte.

English: Likewise also their gods of wood overlaid with gold and with silver are like a white thorn in an orchard that every bird sits upon. They are also like a dead body that is thrown out into the dark.
Ekegusii: Chianga chiaye chia monyinga echio chibekeire nigo chikogota, ase igo twamanyire buna chirochio tichiri chinyasae. Omoerio nigo chikoriegwa n’amage na onde taiyo oratware kende agochikorera.

English: You will know them to be no gods by the bright purple that rots upon them. They themselves will be consumed afterwards, and will be a reproach in the country.
Ekegusii: Omonto omochenu otabwati emegwekano nigo are buya goetania abande; ere tamanyeti nyasae ende, na onde taiyo oramochaye.

English: After Alexander the Macedonian, the son of Philip, who came out of the land of Chittim, and struck Darius king of the Persians and Medes, it came to pass, after he had struck him, that he reigned in his place, in former time, over Greece.
