English: They have hired Arabians to help them, and are encamped beyond the brook, ready to come against you to battle.” So Judas went to meet them.
Ekegusii: Timotheo boigo konye ogorire abarwani esegi ba Abaarabu abwo boigo bebegete ang’e ase ekeng’umbu kiengegu ende yorooche erio bamogwere Yuda. Yuda agasooka kogenda korwana na barabwo.

English: Timotheus said to the captains of his army when Judas and his army drew near to the brook of water, “If he crosses over to us first, we won’t be able to withstand him, for he will certainly defeat us;
Ekegusii: Ekero Yuda na abarwani esegi baye baikire ang’e norooche, Timotheo akabateebia abanene baye, “Onye ere kagototang’anera kwamboka orooche, titokonyaara komoiraneria ekero agotogwera ere nigo aratobue.

English: but if he is afraid, and encamps beyond the river, we will cross over to him, and defeat him.”
Ekegusii: Korende ere aise kwoboa na gotenena ekeng’umbu, intwe nigo tokwamboka na komogwera na komobua.”

English: Now when Judas came near to the water brook, he caused the scribes of the people to remain by the brook, and commanded them, saying, “Allow no man to encamp, but let all come to the battle.”
Ekegusii: Ekero Yuda aigete ase engegu, akabateebia abanene baye: timobaisa gotiga onde atenene; tiga abanto bonsi basoe ase esegi!

English: Then he crossed over against them first, and all the people after him; and all the Gentiles were defeated before his face, and threw away their weapons, and fled to the temple at Carnaim.
Ekegusii: Erio ere akaba omonto bw’eritang’ani kwamboka orooche. Abanto baye bonsi bakamobwatia. Ababisa bagaitwa bobe erio bagatuguta ebirwanero biabo inse na gotama gochia Hekalu yarenge ase omochie o Karinaumu.

English: They took the city and burned the temple with fire, together with all who were in it. Carnaim was subdued. They couldn’t stand any longer before the face of Judas.
Ekegusii: Ekaba Yuda na abanto baye bakayoira omochie oyio, bakeyesamba omorero hekalu eyio na kobasamberania bonsi abwo barenge ime. Karinaimu okairwa na abanto baye tibanyaara naende komotanga Yuda.

English: Judas gathered together all Israel, those who were in the land of Gilead, from the least to the greatest, with their wives, their children, and their stuff, an exceedingly great army, that they might come into the land of Judah.
Ekegusii: Ere Yuda akabasangereria Abayahudi bonsi barenge Gileadi, korwa abana abake goika abagaaka abagotu, abakungu na abana amo ne chinibo chiabo chionsi; gekaba ekeombe ekenene gekoirana gochia Yudea.

English: They came as far as Ephron, and this same city was large and very strong. It was on the road where they were going. They couldn’t turn away from it on the right hand or on the left, but needed to pass through the middle of it.
Ekegusii: Bakagenda goika Efuroni. Oyio nomochie orenge omonene naende omokong’u kegima oagaachire enchera ensemo. Tibanyaarete koyoetanana gochia borio gose komosi; ekababetereria goetera gati gati yomochie.

English: The people of the city shut them out and blocked the gates with stones.
Ekegusii: Korende abamenyi ba Efuroni bakabasiekera Abayahudi isiko na gosieka ebiita bi’omochie na amagena.

English: Judas sent to them with words of peace, saying, “We will pass through your land to go into our own land, and no one will harm you. We will only pass by on our feet.” But they wouldn’t open to him.
Ekegusii: Yuda akabatomera amang’ana agoteeba iga: “Totige intwe toete gati yomochie oino erio toirane gochia seito. Onde taiyo orabamochere inwe. Nigo toraete na kogeenda seito.” Korende barabwo bakaanga koigora ebiita.

English: Then Judas commanded proclamation to be made in the army, that each man should encamp in the place where he was.
Ekegusii: Erio Yuda akabateebia bonsi abwo babwatanetie naabarwani esegi baye batenene ase bare.

English: So the men of the army encamped, and fought against the city all that day and all that night, and the city was delivered into his hands.
Ekegusii: Erio akabateebia abasikari baye kwearigania ase esegi ase omochie o Efuroni. Ekaba esegi omobaso boira na obotuko bokia goika omochie okairwa na Abayahudi.

English: He destroyed all the males with the edge of the sword, razed the city, took its plunder, and passed through the city over those who were slain.
Ekegusii: Yuda akabaita abasacha bonsi ba Efuroni ase omoro agataagora omochie na gosakora. Barabwo ere amo na abarwani esegi baye bagaeta gati gati ya amaomo abo bagotacha ebitindo igoro.

English: They went over the Jordan into the great plain near Bethshan.
Ekegusii: Bakaamboka orooche rwa Yorodani na goika ase ense omweya bosio bwa Beth-sheani.

English: And Judas gathered together those who lagged behind and encouraged the people all the way through, until he came into the land of Judah.
Ekegusii: Agwo ase enchera Yuda akaba okobabogoria baria konye barosire na kobaa omoyo abanto baye goika ekero baigete Yudea.

English: They went up to mount Zion with gladness and joy, and offered whole burnt offerings, because not so much as one of them was slain until they returned in peace.
Ekegusii: Ase omochengo na okoiraneria buya, bakariina egetunwa gia Sayoni, erio bakarua ebing’wanso biogosaamba ekiagera barabwo bairanete buya batasireti nonya noyomo ase egati yaabo.

English: In the days when Judas and Jonathan were in the land of Gilead, and Simon his brother in Galilee before Ptolemais,
Ekegusii: Ekero Yuda na Yonathani barenge Gileadi na ekero Simioni momura omwabo ayogwerete omochie o Tolemai agwo Galili,

English: Joseph the son of Zacharias, and Azarias, rulers of the army, heard of their exploits and of the war, and what things they had done.
Ekegusii: Yosefu na Asaria abanene be esegi abwo batigarete Yudea, bakaigwa amang’ana igoro yoboremu na obobui bwabo.

English: They said, “Let’s also get us a name, and let’s go fight against the Gentiles who are around us.”
Ekegusii: Bagateebania: “Tiga naintwe tochaake esegi nebisaku ebi bitoetanaine erio naintwe twenyoorere esiko.”

English: So they gave orders to the men of the army that was with them, and went toward Jamnia.
Ekegusii: Erio bakarua ogochika ase abanto baabo, na barabwo bakayogwera omochie o Yamunia

English: Gorgias and his men came out of the city to meet them in battle.
Ekegusii: Gorgia na abanto baye bagasooka erio bakarwana amo na Abayahudi abwo.

English: Joseph and Azarias were put to flight, and were pursued to the borders of Judea. About two thousand men of Israel fell on that day.
Ekegusii: Abanto ba Gorgia bakababua Asaria na Yosefu na kobamonyokia goika chinsinyo chio omochie o Yudea. Ase rituko erio, bagaita Abaisraeli batari inse yabaanto 2,000.

English: There was a great overthrow among the people, because they didn’t listen to Judas and his kindred, thinking to do some exploit.
Ekegusii: Ogosiria okwo nigo kwabanyoorete ase engencho Yosefu na Asaria barigetie benyorere esiko bakanga kobaigwera Yuda na abamura bamwabo.

English: But they were not of the family of those men by whose hand deliverance was given to Israel.
Ekegusii: Goetania ayio, barabwo tibarenge abeamate ya Makabi abwo konye Omonene achoorete korenta obosibore ase Abaisraeli.

English: The man Judas and his kindred were glorified exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and of all the Gentiles, wherever their name was heard of.
Ekegusii: Yuda Makabi amo na abamura bamwabo nigo basikire mono na Abaisraeli na abanto bonsi be ebisaku binde. Ekero abanto baigwete chinkuma chiabo,

English: Men gathered together to them, acclaiming them.
Ekegusii: nigo barenge kobekana amo ase ebiombe ase okobairaneria mbuya mono.

English: Judas and his kindred went out and fought against the children of Esau in the land toward the south. He struck Hebron and its villages, pulled down its strongholds, and burned its towers all around.
Ekegusii: Erio Yuda, amo na abamura bamwabo bakageenda Irianyi gochia korwania basinto b’Esau. Akagwera Heburoni amo nemechie yabaetanaine, agatagora chinsinyo chiaye na gosamba chinyasi chiaye chionsi.

English: He marched to go into the land of the Philistines, and he went through Samaria.
Ekegusii: Erio akaba oikire ase ense ya Abafilisiti agaetera Marisa.

English: In that day certain priests, desiring to do exploits there, were slain in battle, when they went out to battle unadvisedly.
Ekegusii: Ase rituko erio abakuani batari bake bagaitwa ase esegi ase engencho yogwetakera esiiko y’oboremu ebio biagerete bagaturia esegi.

English: But Judas turned toward Azotus, to the land of the Philistines, pulled down their altars, burned the carved images of their gods with fire, took the plunder of their cities, and returned into the land of Judah.
Ekegusii: Yuda akaonchoka na kogenda Ashidodi ime ya Filisiti. Agwo agataagora ebisasimero biabo, agasaamba emegwekano y’echinyasae chiabo omorero, erio ere akairana gochia ase omochie o Yudea.

English: King Antiochus was traveling through the upper countries; and he heard that in Elymais in Persia there was a city renowned for riches, for silver and gold,
Ekegusii: Ekero Omorwoti Antioko o kane arenge goeta Mesopotamia ime yechingongo chi’ebitunwa akaigwa amang’ana yomochie bwe Elimaisi ase ense ya Abaperisi oyio okumete kegima ase obonda bwaye bw’echifeta ne etaabu.

English: and that the temple which was in it was exceedingly rich, and that in it were golden shields, breastplates, and weapons which Alexander, son of Philip, the Macedonian king, who reigned first among the Greeks, left behind there.
Ekegusii: Hekalu yaye nigo yabwate obotenenku obonene, eichire chinguba chi’etaabu, abietubo biegekuba na ebirwanero biatigetwe aroro na Alekisanda omwana bw’omorwoti mosinto o Filipo omorwoti o Makedonia oyio orenge omoteneneri bw’eritang’ani bwa Abagiriki.

English: So he came and tried to take the city and to pillage it; and he was not able, because his plan was known to them of the city,
Ekegusii: Antioko agaika Elimaisi, agateema gosakora na koyoira omochie oyio korende tanyaara egekogera konye abamenyi b’omochie oyio bamanyire omoroberio oye,

English: and they rose up against him in battle. He fled and returned to Babylon with great disappointment.
Ekegusii: barabwo bagasangereria abarwani esegi baabo na koamererania nere. Ekaba Antioko akairana gochia Babuloni ore n’obororo.

English: Then someone came into Persia bringing him news that the armies which went against the land of Judah had been put to flight,
Ekegusii: Agwo Perisi, omorwoti Antioko akarenterwa amang’ana buna abarwani esegi abwo atomete Yudea babaiurwe;

English: and that Lysias went first with a strong army and was put to shame before them, and that they had grown strong because of weapons, power, and a supply of plunder which they took from the armies that they had cut off,
Ekegusii: boigo buna Lisia na abarwani esegi baye baria barenge abanyanguru nigo babetereretigwe gotama Abayahudi; buna Abayahudi bakong’ire mono kobwatekana nogosangereria ebirwanero ebio babeire bagosakora korwa ase abarwani esegi b’ababisa baabo

English: and that they had pulled down the abomination which he had built upon the altar that was in Jerusalem, and that they had surrounded the sanctuary with high walls, as before, and also Bethsura, his city.
Ekegusii: buna barabwo batagoire egesasiimero kia enyasae y’oborimo eyio Antioko aagachete agwo igoro y’egesasiimero kia Abayahudi agwo Yerusalemu; boigo buna barabwo baetananirie enyasi entambe ase Hekalu buna yarenge omochakano konye ere Antioko ataracha, buna barabwo bairire na koyorenda omochie o Beth-zuri oyio oreenge oyomo bw’emechie y’omorwoti Antioko.

English: It came to pass, when the king heard these words, he was astonished and moved exceedingly. He laid himself down on his bed, and fell sick for grief, because it had not turned out for him as he had planned.
Ekegusii: Ekero omorwoti aigwete amang’ana ayio, agaichana na konyegerigwa akagwa borere akarwara ase engencho amang’ana abeete mamincha nogosemeria kwaye.

English: He was there many days, because great grief continually gripped him, and he realized that he would die.
Ekegusii: Ere akaba ore omorwaire ase ebiro ebitambe ase engencho ya amang’ana ayio; akarambereria na akarora omosunte bw’obwoba, erio akamanya ng’a ngokwa are.

English: He called for all his friends, and said to them, “Sleep departs from my eyes, and my heart fails because of worry.
Ekegusii: Erio akabarangeria abasani baye bonsi akabateebia: Tindi na toro na enkoro yane yaichoirwe n’obwoba nokoiroka.

English: I said in my heart, ‘To what suffering I have come! How great a flood it is that I’m in, now! For I was gracious and loved in my power.’
Ekegusii: Ritang’ani nigo neboretie ninki kiagerete emechaando eye ekanyoora inche agwo ase oborwoti bwane inche nabeire omuya na bwanchire na abanto bonsi!

English: But now I remember the evils which I did at Jerusalem, and that I took all the vessels of silver and gold that were in it, and sent out to destroy the inhabitants of Judah without a cause.
Ekegusii: Erio inche nkainyora obobe nakorete Yerusalemu ase okobogoria ebibeekerero bietaabu n’efeta korwa ase Hekalu erio inche inkarigia kobasiria bosa abamenyi ba Yudea.

English: I perceive that it is because of this that these evils have come upon me. Behold, I am perishing through great grief in a strange land.”
Ekegusii: Namanyire buna eke nakio kiagerire obokong’u abo bwanchicheire nainche bono nigo inde ang’e gokwa ase ense eye y’abanyene.

English: Then he called for Philip, one of his friends, and set him over all his kingdom.
Ekegusii: Erio akamorangeria Filipo, oyomobwa abaseemia baye omonene akamoa bionsi ebio ere abwate.

English: He gave him his crown, his robe, and his signet ring, so that he could guide Antiochus his son, and nourish him up that he might be king.
Ekegusii: Akamoa egutwa yaye, eyanga yaye nebonyi yaye yomouri. Akamochiika amorere na komosomia omwana oye Antioko o gatano goika ere obeire omorwoti.

English: Then King Antiochus died there in the one hundred forty-ninth year.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti Antioko agakwa ase omwaka o 149.

English: When Lysias learned that the king was dead, he set up Antiochus his son to reign, whom he had nourished up being young, and he called his name Eupator.
Ekegusii: Ekero Lisia aigwete buna omorwoti okuure, Akamobeka omosae Antioko ase oborwoti ribaga ria ise na komoa erieta Eupatori. Lisia konye omorerire Antioko o gatano kowa obwana bwaye.

English: Those who were in the citadel kept hemming Israel in around the sanctuary, and always sought to harm them and to strengthen the Gentiles.
Ekegusii: Ase ebiro ebio ababisa nigo barenge ase chinsinyo barenge kona kobatianera Abaisraeli ang’e nenseemo ye Hekalu. Barabwo nigo barenge kona goteema kera ekero kobaremaria Abayahudi na kobikong’ia ebisaku binde.

English: Judas planned to destroy them, and called all the people together to besiege them.
Ekegusii: Erio Yuda akaroberia kobasiria kegima. Akabasangereria abanto baye bonsi erio babanarie ababisa.

English: They were gathered together, and besieged them in the one hundred fiftieth year, and he made mounds to shoot from, and engines of war.
Ekegusii: Abanto bagasangererekana na goetanana orwaki orwo ase omwaka o 150, na bakaagacha emerobiri na ebibekerero binde biokoruta ebirwanero.

English: Some of those who were hemmed in came out, and some of the ungodly men of Israel were joined to them.
Ekegusii: Ekaba ase egati ya ababisa baria banaaretigwe bagatama, na egati yabo Abayahudi ababe abwo bababwatesetie.

English: They went to the king, and said, “How long will you not execute judgment, and avenge our kindred?
Ekegusii: Erio bakageenda ase omorwoti, bagateeba, “Aye ninki oganyete otarachia goakana egesiomba ase amabe ayio bakoreirwe abaaminto?

English: We were willing to serve your father and to live by his words, and to follow his commandments.
Ekegusii: Intwe nigo tweruete komokorera iso, kobwata amachiiko aye na koigwera amorokererio aye.

English: Because of this, the children of our people besieged the citadel and were alienated from us; but as many of us as they could catch, they killed, and plundered our inheritances.
Ekegusii: Intwe inki twanyoorete? Bono abanto baminto babeire ababisa baito. Ase ekeene bamoitire kera oyomo oito oyio bakorora na boigo gotoibera chinibo chiaito.

English: Not against us only did they stretch out their hand, but also against all their borders.
Ekegusii: Korende nintwe tweka batarakorera bobe; babagwereire abababebekaine bonsi.

English: Behold, they are encamped this day against the citadel at Jerusalem to take it. They have fortified the sanctuary and Bethsura.
Ekegusii: Bono baetananire orwaki rwa Yerusalemu nigo batagete koyoira.

English: If you don’t quickly prevent them, they will do greater things than these, and you won’t be able to control them.
Ekegusii: Aye otakoreti bwango ase okobatanga rirorio barabwo inabakore amange naye tokonyara kobatanga.”

English: When the king heard this, he was angry, and gathered together all his friends, the rulers of his army, and those who were over the cavalry.
Ekegusii: Ekero omorwoti aigwete ayio, ere akabea mono. Akabasangereria abateneneri ba abarwani be esegi bonsi, abanene ba abarwani baye be esegi na baria batenenerete abarwani be chibaarasi.

English: Bands of hired soldiers came to him from other kingdoms and from islands of the sea.
Ekegusii: Boigo akabagora abasikai b’eng’eria korwa chinse chinde na korwa ase ebisinga bia Abagiriki.

English: The number of his forces was one hundred thousand infantry, and twenty thousand cavalry, and thirty-two elephants trained for war.
Ekegusii: Abarwani baye be esegi bagotaara na amagoro bakaba 10,000, abechibaarasi 20,000 ne chinchogu chi’eseegi 32.

English: They went through Idumaea, and encamped against Bethsura, and fought against it many days, and made engines of war. The Jews came out and burned them with fire, and fought valiantly.
Ekegusii: Barabwo bagaetera Idumea erio bagende koyonaria omochie o Beth-zuri agwo ase aseegi yairete amatuko amange. Abarwani be esegi bo omorwoti bakaagacha chitinga chi’okoruta ebioge korende abanto abwo barenge omochie ime bakerwanerera noboremu bagasooka isiko na gosaamba etinga eyio yababisa yarenge kobaruta ebioge.

English: Judas marched away from the citadel and encamped at Bethzacharias, near the king’s camp.
Ekegusii: Erio Yuda akabarusia abarwani baye be esegi korwa ase orwaki rwa Yerusalemu, akabeeka ekambi aria Beth-zaria, koumerana ne ekambi y’abarwani be esegi b’omorwoti.

English: The king rose early in the morning, and marched his army at full speed along the road to Bethzacharias. His forces made themselves ready to battle and sounded their trumpets.
Ekegusii: Mambia chuni ase rituko riare kobwatia omorwoti akabogoria abarwani baye b’esegi ase obwango na kobabeeka ase enchera yokogeenda Beth-zakaria. Ebiombe bia abarwani be esegi baye bikebaanga na kwearigania ase esegi; bakabugia egetuureri.

English: They offered the elephants the juice of grapes and mulberries, that they might prepare them for the battle.
Ekegusii: Bagachinyoinsia chinchogu chiabo amaache yeemesabibu ne chibiribiri erio gochiseegeta ase esegi.

English: They distributed the animals among the phalanxes. They set by each elephant a thousand men armed with coats of mail and helmets of brass on their heads. Five hundred chosen cavalry were appointed for each elephant.
Ekegusii: Chinchogu echio chikagaba ebiombe bia abasikari bagochiera amagoro: ase kera enchogu eyemo, abasikari ba amagoro 1,000 babeegete ebigogwa chiechuma ase emetwe yaabo na abarwani be chibaarasi 500, bagotunyana chinchogu echio korwa magega.

English: These were ready beforehand, wherever the elephant was. Wherever the elephant went, they went with it. They didn’t leave it.
Ekegusii: Abwo bakaba bakobwatia chinchogu echio gochia kera ase chiarenge kogeenda batari gochitiga nonya ng’ake.

English: Strong, covered wooden towers were upon them, one upon each elephant, fastened upon it with secure harnesses. Upon each were four valiant men who fought upon them, beside his Indian driver.
Ekegusii: Agwo ase omogongo bwenchogu nigo baagachete enyomba enkong’u yabwate abanto baane bare ne ebioge nyuma y’Omoindi oyio orenge kogendia enchogu eyio.

English: The rest of the cavalry he set on this side and that side on the two flanks of the army, striking terror into the enemy, and protected by the phalanxes.
Ekegusii: Lisia akabaroberia baria bariinete chibarasi ase amakere ya abarwani be esegi baye ase okorio na bomosi, agwo ase barenge konyaara gokengerwa na abasikari baria bagochiera amagoro erio barabwo bagendererete koumokera ababisa.

English: Now when the sun shone upon the shields of gold and brass, the mountains lit up, and blazed like flaming torches.
Ekegusii: Risase rigachimesia chinguba chiabo chi’etaabu ne chichuma, ebitunwa bikairaneria obomekameku boria buna ebieri bi’omorero.

English: A part of the king’s army was spread upon the high hills and some on the low ground, and they went on firmly and in order.
Ekegusii: Ensemo ya abarwani be esegi b’omorwoti ekaimokererigwa buna ebigoro ebitambe na ebinde bireng’anaine erio abasikari bagasuka motwe ase ogwesigoria na obokanyeku.

English: All who heard the noise of their multitude, the marching of the multitude, and the rattling of the weapons trembled; for the army was exceedingly great and strong.
Ekegusii: Bonsi bakegosa ekero baigwete amatitiria ya amagoro abo na ogoakana kwebirwanero biabo. Ase ekeene abarwani be esegi baabo nigo barenge abange naende bare nechinguru kegima.

English: Judas and his army drew near for battle, and six hundred men of the king’s army fell.
Ekegusii: Korende Yuda na abarwani be esegi baye bagasoa ase esegi na goita abarwani be esegi b’omorwoti 600.

English: Eleazar, who was called Avaran, saw one of the animals armed with royal breastplates, and it was taller than all the animals, and the king seemed to be on it.
Ekegusii: Eliezari oyio okorokwa Avarani akarora buna enchogu eyemo nigo yarenge enene kobua echinde na buna nigo yaboyirie emiambaro yomorwoti. Erio akarengereria buna omorwoti omonyene nao ariinete enchogu eyio.

English: He gave his life to deliver his people, and to get himself an everlasting name.
Ekegusii: Ere akerua obogima bwaye ere omonyene kobatooria abanto baye erio ere boigo enyoorere esiiko etaere.

English: He ran upon him courageously into the midst of the phalanx, and killed on the right hand and on the left, and they parted away from him on this side and on that.
Ekegusii: Ase oboremu akayechiera enchogu eria ase egati ya abarwani be esegi bagochiera amagoro. Ere agasuka motwe bwango ogoita abanto okorio no okobee nonya na abasikari b’omorwoti bakamwebachera kera ensemo.

English: He crept under the elephant, and stabbed it from beneath, and killed it. The elephant fell to the earth upon him, and he died there.
Ekegusii: Akanyenyeka inse yamagoro yenchogu eria na koyebeta ritimo ase enda yaye. Enchogu eria agakwa, ekamogwera Eliezari na komoita.

English: They saw the strength of the kingdom and the fierce attack of the army, and turned away from them.
Ekegusii: Ekero Abayahudi barooche chinguru chia abarwani be esegi b’omorwoti na okorwana kwabo, bakairana magega.

English: But the soldiers of the king’s army went up to Jerusalem to meet them, and the king encamped toward Judea and toward mount Zion.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti na abarwani be esegi baye bagasuka motwe erinde babagwere Abayahudi agwo ase omochie o Yerusalemu. Bakabeeka ekambi Yudea na ase egetunwa gia Sayoni.

English: He made peace with the people of Bethsura. He came out of the city because they had no food there to endure the siege, because it was a Sabbath to the land.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti akaroisia omorembe na abanto ba Beth-zuri, erio abanto abwo bakarua ase omochie oyio egekogera barabwo tibaarenge nendaagera ebaisaine ase omwaka oyio bw’ogotimoka ekero abanto batari korema gose gosimeka.

English: The king took Bethsura, and appointed a garrison there to keep it.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti akaira omochie o Beth-zuri na kwebekera abareendi baye aroro agwo.

English: He encamped against the sanctuary many days; and set there mounds to shoot from, and engines of war, and machines for throwing fire and stones, and weapons to throw darts, and slings.
Ekegusii: Akayeetanana na kogitera Hekalu ase ebiro ebitambe. Akaroberia na koroisia ebioge biogotagora chinyasi, chitinga chi’okoruta ebioge na ebinto biokoruta omorero amagena nechinsara boigo ebiraasi bi’okorutera amagena.

English: The Jews also made engines of war against their engines, and fought for many days.
Ekegusii: Abayahudi nabarabwo boigo bakeroiseria ase oboundi bwabo ebirwanero biokoamererania na biria biababisa. Okorwana okwo gokagenderera ase amatuko amange.

English: But there was no food in the sanctuary, because it was the seventh year, and those who fled for safety into Judea from among the Gentiles had eaten up the rest of the stores.
Ekegusii: Korende endagera tiyatigarete ekiagera engaki eyio yarenge omwaka bw’ogotimoka na abanto konye babatameire korwa ase abanto b’ebisaku na kwebisa Yudea konye bakoorire endaagera yonsi yagachire agwo Yudea.

English: There were only a few people left in the sanctuary, because the famine prevailed against them, and they were scattered, each man to his own place.
Ekegusii: Endaagera ekabora goika abanto bande bakabetererigwa koirana gochia ase chinka chiabo; bagatigara abanto bake igo ime ase Hekalu.

English: Lysias heard that Philip, whom Antiochus the king, while he was yet alive, appointed to raise his son Antiochus to be king,
Ekegusii: Ase ebiro ebio, Filipo oria ochooretwe nomorwoti Antioko buna omorere omwana oye goika obeire omorwoti,

English: had returned from Persia and Media, and with him the forces that went with the king, and that he was seeking to take control of the government.
Ekegusii: akairana korwa Perisi na Media. Nigo ere airanete na abarwani esegi b’omorwoti na igo nigo aroberetie kobogoria oborai bweserekari. Ekero Lisia aigwa amang’ana ayio,

English: He made haste, and gave orders to depart. He said to the king and the leaders of the army and to the men, “We get weaker daily, our food is scant, the place where we encamp is strong, and the affairs of the kingdom lie upon us.
Ekegusii: akarua ogochika barue agwo bwango. Akamoteebia omomura oria omosae amo na abanene baye: Kera rituko chinguru chiaito nigo chigendererete gokea. Titobwati endagera etoisaine, na aase aiga ase toonchokananete nakong’u mono. Goetania erio, amang’ana nareo yegeserekari atobetereretie gokora.

English: Now therefore let’s negotiate with these men, and make peace with them and with all their nation,
Ekegusii: Bono tiga tokore okobwatana na Abayahudi amo negesaku kiabo ekegima.

English: and covenant with them, that they may walk after their own laws, as before; for because of their laws which we abolished they were angered, and did all these things.”
Ekegusii: Tobaakere buya ase ogotunyana amachiiko na amorokererio abo buna barenge gokora omochakano. Emechaando eye yonsi nigo yachaagete ekero intwe twabachegetie Abayahudi ase okorusia na gotuguta amachiiko, amenario abo.

English: The speech pleased the king and the princes, and he sent to them to make peace; and they accepted it.
Ekegusii: Ekerengererio ekio kegancheranwa nomorwoti amo na abanene baye. Erio Lisia akabaa Abayahudi amachiiko y’omorembe, na barabwo bakayancherana.

English: The king and the princes swore to them. On these conditions, they came out from the stronghold.
Ekegusii: Ekero omorwoti na abarai baye banchete koyabwatia amachiiko ayio ase okoria chiira, Abayahudi bakarua ase oborendi bwabo.

English: Then the king entered into mount Zion. He saw the strength of the place, and broke the oath which he had sworn, and gave orders to pull down the wall all around.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero omorwoti asoete ase egetunwa gia Sayoni na korora buna orwaki orwo rwakong’ete, akabuna chiira chiaye echio konye ariire akarua ogochika chinyasi echio chiatananete orwaki chitagorwe.

English: Then he left in haste and returned to Antioch, and found Philip master of the city. He fought against him, and took the city by force.
Ekegusii: Erio agasoka ase obwango akageenda Antiokia. Agwo akamonyora Filipo obogoirie omochie, ere akarwana nere na koyoira omochie bwa Antiokia n’echinguru.

English: In the one hundred fifty first year, Demetrius the son of Seleucus came out of Rome, and went up with a few men to a city by the sea, and reigned there.
Ekegusii: Ase omwaka o 151, Demeturio mosinto o Seleuko akarua Rumi agaika ase omochie oyomo ase engegu yebisinga bie enyancha ya Mediterania ore na abanto bake igo. Akeraria koba omorwoti aroro agwo.

English: It came to pass, when he would go into the house of the kingdom of his fathers, that the army laid hands on Antiochus and Lysias, to bring them to him.
Ekegusii: Ekero aimogete kogenda ase enyomba y’oborwoti ya abagaaka baabo, abasikari bakababwata Antioko o gatano na Lisia na kobaira ase Demeturio.

English: The thing became known to him, and he said, “Don’t show me their faces!”
Ekegusii: Korende ekero Demeturio aigwete omoroberio oyio agateeba: “Inche tindigeti korora amasio abo.”

English: So the army killed them. Then Demetrius sat upon the throne of his kingdom.
Ekegusii: Ekaba abasikari bagaita Antioko o gatano na Lisia na ere Demeturio agaikaransa ase ekerogo kioborwoti.

English: All the lawless and ungodly men of Israel came to him. Alcimus was their leader, desiring to be high priest.
Ekegusii: Ekaba Abayahudi baria ababe na batamosigete Omonene, ase oborai bwa Alikimo oyio oganetie koba Omokuani omonene, bakamochiera Demeturio.

English: They accused the people to the king, saying, “Judas and his kindred have destroyed all your friends, and have scattered us from our own land.
Ekegusii: Bakabasoera Abayahudi bamwabo bakoboora: “Yuda amo na bamura bamwabo babaitire abasani bao bonsi nabarabwo batoseririe intwe korwa ase ense yaito.

English: Now therefore send a man whom you trust, and let him go and see all the destruction which he has brought on us and the king’s country, and how he has punished them and all who helped them.”
Ekegusii: Bono aye motome monto onde bwensi omwegenete arore buna barabwo basambete chinibo chiaito na buna ense yomorwoti yasaretigwe erio aye obae egesusuro Yuda na bamura bamwabo na abakoonyi baabo bonsi.”

English: So the king chose Bacchides, one of the king’s friends, who was ruler in the country beyond the river, and was a great man in the kingdom, and faithful to the king.
Ekegusii: Ekaba omorwoti akamochoora Bakide, oyomo ase abaseemia baye oyio orenge omogabana bw’orogongo rwa ng’umbu y’orooche. Ere Bakide nigo arenge omonto bw’engeencho enene naende omwegenwa kegima ase omorwoti.

English: He sent him and that ungodly Alcimus, whom he made the high priest; and he commanded him to take vengeance upon the children of Israel.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti akamotoma kogeenda noria omotwambu Alikimo, oyio ochooretwe nomorwoti koba Omokuani omonene; akabachiika goakana egesiomba ase Abayahudi.

English: They marched away and came with a great army into the land of Judah. He sent messengers to Judas and his kindred with words of peace deceitfully.
Ekegusii: Barabwo bakarua Antiokia, bagaika Yudea bare na abarwani be esegi abange. Bakide agateema kobang’aina Yuda na bamura bamwabo ase okobatoma abanto na amang’ana yokorigia omorembe.

English: They paid no attention to their words; for they saw that they had come with a great army.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero Yuda amo na abamwabo barooche buna aba nigo bachicha bare na abarwani be esegi abange, barabwo tibeegena amang’ana ya baria batometwe.

English: A group of scribes gathered together to Alcimus and Bacchides to seek just terms.
Ekegusii: Bono ekeombe kiabamanyi ba amachiiko gekamochiera Alikimo na Bakide kogania amachiiko yoboronge.

English: The Hasidaeans were the first among the children of Israel who sought peace from them,
Ekegusii: Abaasidimo abwo nabwo Abayahudi b’eritang’ani bateemete korigia omorembe korwa ase Alikimo na Bakide.

English: for they said, “One who is a priest of the seed of Aaron has come with the army, and he will do us no wrong.”
Ekegusii: Barabwo nigo barengereretie buna Alikimo oyio orenge Omokuani omonene ase ororeria rwa Aroni nonya ochete na abarwani be esegi, ase nchera ende yonsi, tarenge gochia kobakorera bobe.

English: He spoke with them words of peace, and swore to them, saying, “We won’t seek to harm you or your friends.”
Ekegusii: Alikimo agakwana na barabwo amang’ana y’omorembe na koria chiira ase ogotiana ogoteeba: “Intwe titokobakorera bobe inwe abanyene gose abasani baino.”

English: They trusted him. Then he seized sixty men of them, and killed them in one day, according to the word which was written,
Ekegusii: Barabwo bakamwegena. Korende erio kegima akababwata abanto 60 ase egati yaabo na kobaita rituko erio erio, buna eriikire:

English: The flesh of your saints and their blood was shed all around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them.
Ekegusii: “Amanyinga ya abegenwa bao agaiterwa, emebere yaaboegatugutwa aa na aaria Yerusalemu; tatigarete oyo orenge gotindeka ebitondo.”

English: The fear and the dread of them fell upon all the people, for they said, “There is neither truth nor justice in them; for they have broken the covenant and the oath which they swore.”
Ekegusii: Abanto bonsi bakaboboa Bakide na Alikimo bagoteeba: “Barabwo tibamanyeti engencho ye ekeene na oboronge. Nigo batianete ase chiira na barabwo bakabuna chiira chiabo barabwo abanyene!”

English: Bacchides withdrew from Jerusalem, and encamped in Bezeth. He sent and seized many of the deserters who were with him, and some of the people, and he killed them, throwing them into a large pit.
Ekegusii: Bakide akarua Yerusalemu na koroisia obomenyo bwaye agwo Beth-zaithi. Erio agachiika barigigwe na kobwatwa Abayahudi baria bamotamete na akabaita na koruta emebere yaabo engoro ime abande ase egati yaabo.

English: He placed Alcimus in charge of the country and left with him a force to aid him. Then Bacchides went away to the king.
Ekegusii: Erio ere akamotigera Alikimo oborai bw’ense eyio. Akamotigera ebiombe bia abarwani be esegi bamokonye, ere akairana gochia ase omorwoti.

English: Alcimus struggled to maintain his high priesthood.
Ekegusii: Erio Alikimo agachaaka emeroberio yogokiinia obokuani bwaye obonene.

English: All those who troubled their people joined him, and they took control of the land of Judah, and did great damage in Israel.
Ekegusii: Abanto bonsi abachege bakabwatana nere. Bayebwata na koyebetereria ense ya Yudea koigwera bakarenta ogosiria okonene ase Israeli.

English: Judas saw all the wrongs that Alcimus and his company had done among the children of Israel, even more than the Gentiles.
Ekegusii: Yuda akarora amabe ayio Alikimo na abamwabo bakorete ase egati ya Abaisraeli; ayio nigo arenge amabe kobua aria akoretwe na abanto bebeisaku binde.

English: He went out into all the borders of Judea and took vengeance on the men who had deserted from him, and they were restrained from going out into the country.
Ekegusii: Erio Yuda agaetanana ase ense yonsi ya Yedea, agaakana egesiomba ase abanto bonsi baria bamotamete na kobwatana na Alikimo, akabagitera tibarwa ase omochie kogeenda mogondo.

English: But when Alcimus saw that Judas and his company had grown strong, and knew that he was not able to withstand them, he returned to the king, and brought evil accusations against them.
Ekegusii: Ekero Alikimo arooche buna Yuda amo na abanto baye, bamentekanire chinguru, na komanya buna takonyaara koamererania na barabwo, ere akairana ase omorwoti na kobateebera baabo Yuda oborimo.

English: Then the king sent Nicanor, one of his honorable princes, a man who hated Israel and was their enemy, and commanded him to destroy the people.
Ekegusii: Errio omorwoti akamotoma Nikanori oyomo bwa abanene baye abasike otyio boigo ageechete, Abayahudi mono na komochiika abaite na kobasiria Abayahudi.

English: Nicanor came to Jerusalem with a great army. He sent to Judas and his kindred deceitfully with words of peace, saying,
Ekegusii: Nikanori agaika Yerusalemu na abarwani be esegi abange ogokumia. Agateema boigo komong’aina Yuda amo na abamwabo na amang’ana yomorembe,

English: “Let there be no battle between me and you; I will come with a few men, that I may see your faces in peace.”
Ekegusii: ogoteeba: Engencho teiyo nonya nenke yogokora esegi gati yaino naintwe. Inche ninchiche na abanto bake igo agwo obosio ase obosio ase chinkwana chimorembe.

English: He came to Judas, and they saluted one another peaceably. The enemies were ready to seize Judas by violence.
Ekegusii: Nikanori akamochiera Yuda na gokwanania nere kebosaani. Ani ababisa nigo beariganetie komobwata Yuda.

English: This was known to Judas, that he came to him with deceit, and he was very afraid of him, and would see his face no more.
Ekegusii: Ekero amanya buna ogoocha kwa Nikanori nigo kore okwobong’ainereria bwokomorigia, Yuda akamoiroka na kwanga koumerana nere eria kabere.

English: Nicanor found out that his plan was disclosed; and he went out to meet Judas in battle beside Capharsalama.
Ekegusii: Nikanori akamanya buna omoroberio oye omanyekanire. Erio akarua Yerusalemu na kogenda korwana na Yuda ang’e na Kafari-salama.

English: About five hundred men of Nicanor’s army fell, and the rest fled into the city of David.
Ekegusii: Abanto koreng’ana 500 ase abarwani be esegi ba Nikanori bagaitwa, na baria baminchoretie bagatama gochia ase orwaki rwa Daudi.

English: After these things, Nicanor went up to mount Zion. Some of the priests came out of the sanctuary, with some of the elders of the people, to salute him peaceably, and to show him the whole burned sacrifice that was being offered for the king.
Ekegusii: Magega ya amang’ana ayio gakorekanire, Nikanori akageenda ase egetunwa gia Sayoni. Abande ase egati ya abakuani na abagaaka ba abanto bakamoarigania na amang’ana yomorembe, boigo bakamworokia ekeng’wanso kiogosaambwa ekio kiarenge koruugwa ase engencho yomorwoti.

English: He mocked them, laughed at them, derided them shamefully, spoke arrogantly,
Ekegusii: Korende Nikanori akabachaaya na kobasaria erio ere agakwana nobwetogia bosio bwabo.

English: and swore in a rage, saying, “Unless Judas and his army are now delivered into my hands, it shall be that, if I return safely, I will burn up this house!” And he went out in a great rage.
Ekegusii: Agakorera gotiana: “Onye Yuda amo na abarwani be esegi baye tibagotiga abanyene esegi na gonsika bono, inche ninsaambe omorero Hekalu eye kegima ekero nabuire esegi nkoirana goocha.” Akarwa agwo nekeririanda.

English: The priests entered in, and stood before the altar and the temple; and they wept, and said,
Ekegusii: Abakuani baria bakairana gochia ime ye Hekalu na gotenena bosio bw’egesasiimero bakarera bagoteeba:

English: “You chose this house to be called by your name, to be a house of prayer and supplication for your people.
Ekegusii: “Omonene naye gwachoorete Hekalu eye erokwe ase erieta riao, boigo ebe enyomba yogosaba na ogosorora ase engencho ya abanto bao.

English: Take vengeance on this man and his army, and let them fall by the sword. Remember their blasphemies, and don’t allow them to live any longer.”
Ekegusii: Bono moe egesusuro omonto oyo amo na abarwani be esegi baye; na bonsi baitwe ase omoro. Inyora okorama kwabo; aye tobatiga bagenderere komenya naende.”

English: Then Nicanor went out from Jerusalem and encamped in Bethhoron, and there the Syrian army met him.
Ekegusii: Nikanaori akarua Yerusalemu, akabeeka ekambi yaye agwo Beth-horoni na agwo abarwani be esegi ba Siria bakabwatana amo nere.

English: Judas encamped in Adasa with three thousand men. Judas prayed and said,
Ekegusii: Yuda nere akabeeka ekambi yaye Adasa, ore na abanto 3,000. Ere agasaba okobora:

English: “When those who came from the king blasphemed, your angel went out, and struck among them one hundred eighty-five thousand.
Ekegusii: “Omonene, ekero abanto baria batometwe bakoraamete, omomalaika oo nigo abaitete Abaashuru 185,000.

English: Even so, crush this army before us today, and let all the rest know that he has spoken wickedly against your sanctuary. Judge him according to his wickedness.”
Ekegusii: Bono ase enchera eyio eyio, reero osegenyesegenye abarwani be esegi bare ase obosio bwaito. Erio kera omonto amanye buna Nikanori nigo akoegwa egesusuro ase engencho achaayete Hekalu yao enchenu. Aye omoe egesusuro koreng’ana nobobe bwaye.”

English: On the thirteenth day of the month Adar, the armies met in battle. Nicanor’s army was defeated, and he himself was the first to fall in the battle.
Ekegusii: Ase rituko ria ikomi na gatato ase omotienyi bwa Adari, abarwani esegi bakarwana esegi endito. Abarwani esegi ba Nikanori bakabugwa. Nikanori akaba omonto bw’eritang’ani goitwa ase esegi,

English: Now when his army saw that Nicanor had fallen, they threw away their weapons and fled.
Ekegusii: na ekero abasikari baye barooche buna ere oitirwe, bakuruta ebirwanero biabo inse bagatama.

English: They pursued them a day’s journey from Adasa until you come to Gazara, and they sounded an alarm after them with the signal trumpets.
Ekegusii: Abayahudi bakabamonyokia omobaso boira, korwa Adasa goika Gazara na ekero bagendererete kobaminyokia bakaba bakobugia egetuureri gieseegi.

English: Men came out of all the surrounding villages of Judea, and outflanked them. These turned them back on those, and they all fell by the sword. There wasn’t one of them left.
Ekegusii: Abanto bababebekaine korwa ase ebinyoro bionsi bia Yudea bigasooka na kobagwera ababisa abwo barenge gotama. Ababisa bakabetererigwa koirana magega na koumerana na abarwani be esegi abwo barenge kobamonyokia. Ababisa bonsi bagaitwa ase esegi eyio; tatigara nonya n’omonto obo oyomo.

English: The Jews took the spoils and the booty, and they cut off Nicanor’s head and his right hand, which he had stretched out so arrogantly, and brought them, and hung them up beside Jerusalem.
Ekegusii: Erio Abayahudi bakabogoria ebisakore na abooswa baabo. Bakamonacha Nikanori omotwe nokoboko kwaye gwokorio koria aramborete noboenenu bakabiira Yersalemu na kobitonga isiko.

English: The people were exceedingly glad, and they kept that day as a day of great gladness.
Ekegusii: Abayahudi bakagooka mono na gochengera rituko erio buna rituko riomogooko omonene,

English: They ordained to keep this day year by year on the thirteenth day of Adar.
Ekegusii: na gochiika boigo richengerwe kera omwaka, riruko ria ikomi na gatato riomotienyi bwa Adari.

English: So the land of Judah had rest a few days.
Ekegusii: Ase ebiro ebike, ense ya Yudea ekaba nomorembe.

English: Judas heard of the fame of the Romans, that they are valiant men, and have pleasure in all who join themselves to them, and make friends with all who come to them,
Ekegusii: Konye Yuda oiguure chinkuma chia Abaroma, buna barabwo nigo bare nechinguru chinene chi’abasikari be esegi. Ere namanyete buna barabwo nkoarigania bareenge bonsi baria bakorigia kobwatana nabarabwo na boigo buna bonsi abwo bagosoa ase bare nabo barenge kobanyoora buna abasani b’ekeene ba Rumi.

English: and that they are valiant men. They told him of their wars and exploits which they do among the Gauls, and how they conquered them, and forced them to pay tribute;
Ekegusii: Boigo abanto mbamoteebetie Yudaigoro ye esegi ya Abaroma yarwanete, na buna bababuete Abagalatia noboremu na kobetereria abanto baabo kobaruera ebango.

English: and what things they did in the land of Spain, that they might take control of the silver and gold mines which were there;
Ekegusii: Nateebetigwe boigo buna Abaroma bakorete aria ase Isipania na buna babwatete chingoro chi’efeta ne etaabu.

English: and how by their policy and persistence they conquered all the place (and the place was exceedingly far from them), and the kings who came against them from the uttermost part of the earth, until they had defeated them, and struck them severely; and how the rest give them tribute year by year.
Ekegusii: Ase emeroberio yaabo na okoganya, nigo bayebwatete ense yonsi ya Isipania nonya ero yarenge oboare korwa Rumi. Boigo barabwo mbababuete abarwoti babachierete ase esegi korwa ase chinse chia aare, bakabamoinogora na kobabua goika nonya mbaria batakwete ekebabetereria kobaruera Abaroma ebango kera omwaka.

English: Philip, and Perseus, king of Chittim, and those who lifted up themselves against them, they defeated in battle, and conquered them.
Ekegusii: Konye barabwo barwanire esegi na kobua Filipo, Pereseo, omorwoti o Makedonia, na bonsi abwo babwatanete na aba ase okorwania Rumi.

English: Antiochus also, the great king of Asia, came against them to battle, having one hundred twenty elephants, with cavalry, chariots, and an exceedingly great army, and he was defeated by them.
Ekegusii: Konye babuire ninya na Omosike Antioko, omorwoti o Asia oyio obagwerete Abaroma ne chinchogu 120, chibaarasi, chigari ne emeganda ya abarwani esegi.

English: They took him alive, and decreed that both he and those who reigned after him should give them a great tribute, and should give hostages, and a parcel of land from the best of their provinces:
Ekegusii: Bakamobwata Antioko ore moyo, bakamobetereria ere amo na abarwoti abwo bamobwatisetie korwa ebango enene, koira abooswa sobo, boigo korwa na koira ensemo ere engiya ye chingongo chiabo.

English: the countries of India, Media, and Lydia. They took them from him, and gave them to King Eumenes.
Ekegusii: Buna ense ya India, Media na Lidia. Bakaira chinsemo echio na komoa omorwoti Eumene.

English: Judas heard how the Greeks planned to come and destroy them,
Ekegusii: Ekero Abagiriki bakorete emeroberio yokobaumokera na kobasiria,

English: but this became known to them, and they sent against them a general who fought against them, and many of them fell down wounded to death, and they made captive their wives and their children, and plundered them, and conquered their land, and pulled down their strongholds, and plundered them, and brought them into bondage to this day.
Ekegusii: Abaroma bagategora emeroberio eyio, bakaira ejamadari eyemo ekabaonchia. Abaroma bakabaita Abagiriki ase obonge, bakabaira abakungu na abana baabo koba abasomba, bakabasakora na gotwara ense yaabo, bagatagora chinyasi chiabo na barabwo boigo bakabakora koba abasomba buna bare ase rituko eri.

English: The remaining kingdoms and islands, as many as rose up against them at any time, they destroyed and made them to be their servants;
Ekegusii: Boigo mbabaitete na kobakora abatomwa abanto ba amarwoti ande ase chinse chire chingegu ye enyancha na onde bwensi origetie korwana na barabwo.

English: but with their friends and those who relied on them they stayed friends. They conquered the kingdoms that were near and those that were far off, and all that heard of their fame were afraid of them.
Ekegusii: Korende mbagendereretie obosaani ase ababwatani baabo baria babetigerete ase oborendi. Bakabaita na kobabua abarwoti ba ang’e na abaare na kera omonto oigwete chinkuma chia Abaroma nigo abairogete.

English: Moreover, whoever they desired to help and to make kings, these they make kings; and whoever they desired, they depose. They are exalted exceedingly.
Ekegusii: Barabwo mbabakoonyete abanto bande koba abarwoti, na ase ensemo ende bakabarusia abande ase oborwoti. Ekeene Abaroma nigo barenge nokobua ase ebisaku bionsi bi’ense.

English: For all this, none of them ever put on a crown, neither did they clothe themselves with purple, as a display of grandeur.
Ekegusii: Nonya nabo, tarenge Omoroma oyomo origetie gokiinia ekerogo kiaye ere omonyene gose kweboyia chianga chi’abarwoti chimonyinga ase ogwetang’anania.

English: Judas heard how they had made for themselves a senate house, and day by day, three hundred twenty men sat in council, consulting always for the people, to the end they might be well governed,
Ekegusii: Barabwo nigo baroisetie egeikaranso kiabagaaka 320 abwo barenge goikaransa na goetia amang’ana yogokinigwa kwabo.

English: and how they commit their government to one man year by year, that he should rule over them, and control all their country, and all are obedient to that one, and there is neither envy nor emulation among them.
Ekegusii: Ase kera omwaka nigo barenge komoa omonto oyomo emeremo yokoyeraa ense engima. Kera omonto nigo arenge komoigwera omorai oyio na onde tarenge nonya noyomo ore komoigwera endamwamu gose ribero.

English: So Judas chose Eupolemus the son of John, the son of Accos, and Jason the son of Eleazar, and sent them to Rome, to establish friendship and alliance with them,
Ekegusii: Bono Yuda, akabachoora Eupolemo mosinto o Yohana omoochokoro bwa Akosi, Yasoni mosinto bwe Eliezari, akabatoma Rumi koroisia okobwatana bw’obosani na okobwaterana na Abaroma.

English: and that they should free the yoke from themselves; for they saw that the kingdom of the Greeks kept Israel in bondage.
Ekegusii: Ere nigo akorete ayio erio gwesibora korwa ase obosomba bwa Abagiriki, boigo ase engencho Abayahudi konye barorire buna ngokorwa bare koba abasomba.

English: Then they went to Rome, a very long journey, and they entered into the senate house, and said,
Ekegusii: Yasoni na Eupolemo bagaika Rumi nyuma y’orogendo orotaambe na orokong’u. Bakabanyoora egeikaranso kia abagaaka na kobateebia iga:

English: “Judas, who is also called Maccabaeus, and his kindred, and the people of the Jews, have sent us to you, to make an alliance and peace with you, and that we might be registered as your allies and friends.”
Ekegusii: “Yuda Makabi, bamura bamwabo, na egesaku kia Abayahudi batotomire ase more erio toroisie okobwatana kwomorembe noborendi nainwe erio tonyaare koriikwa koba ababwatani baino boronge.”

English: This thing was pleasing to them.
Ekegusii: Abaroma bagancherana ogosaba okwo,

English: This is the copy of the writing which they wrote back again on tables of brass, and sent to Jerusalem, that it might be with them there for a memorial of peace and alliance:
Ekegusii: na aya naro amariiko ye ekaratasi eyio arigetwe ase ebisamunye bie etai, akairwa Yerusalemu erio abe ekeinyorio giokobwatana okwmbe na okobwaterana:

English: “Good success be to the Romans, and to the nation of the Jews, by sea and by land forever. May the sword and the enemy be far from them.
Ekegusii: Obobui bobeo botambe ase Abaroma na egesaku kia Abayahudi, ase ense na ase enyancha! Omoro tobakuna; omobisa tabaika ang’e.

English: But if war arises for Rome first, or any of their allies in all their dominion,
Ekegusii: Ekero esegi eraabe yarariigwe ase Abaroma, gose omobwatani oye onde bwensi ande onsi aria,

English: the nation of the Jews shall help them as allies, as the occasion shall indicate to them, with all their heart.
Ekegusii: egesaku kia Abayahudi nkerue ogokoonya gwokwerwa ne chinibo koreng’ana nokogania korabeo.

English: To those who make war upon them, they shall not give supplies, food, weapons, money, or ships, as it has seemed good to Rome, and they shall keep their ordinances without taking anything in return.
Ekegusii: Na ababisa abwo barakore esegi, Abayahudi tibabaa gose kobaereria endagera, ebirwanero gose chimeeri buna twancheranire na Rumi. Abayahudi mbaikeranie amachiiko ayio batari goakanwa.

English: In the same way, moreover, if war comes first upon the nation of the Jews, the Romans shall willingly help them as allies, as the occasion shall indicate to them;
Ekegusii: Boigo kerabeo esegi ekorarigwa ase Abayahudi, Abarumi mbarue ogokoonya bwechiniibo na okwerua, koreng’ana nokogania korabeo.

English: and to those who are fighting with them, there shall not be given food, weapons, money, or ships, as it has seemed good to Rome. They shall keep these ordinances, and that without deceit.
Ekegusii: Na ababisa abwo barakore esegi, Abarumi tibabaa gose kobaereria endagera, ebirwanero gose chimeeri buna twancheranire na Rumi. Abayahudi mbaikeranie amachiiko ayio komocha gotaiyo.

English: According to these terms, the Romans made a treaty with the Jewish people.
Ekegusii: “Aya naro amachiiko yokobwatana Abaroma bakorire n’egesaku kia Abayahudi.

English: But if hereafter the one party and the other shall determine to add or diminish anything, they shall do it at their pleasure, and whatever they add or take away shall be ratified.
Ekegusii: Korende, kerabe agwo motwe, chinsemo echi ibere chiaganirie komenta gose korusia ekeng’ese kende gionsi, n’yaancherwe gokora boigo na kende gionsi kerarusigwe gose komentwa nkebe giancheire.

English: Concerning the evils which King Demetrius is doing to them, we have written to him, saying, ‘Why have you made your yoke heavy on our friends and allies the Jews?
Ekegusii: Naende boigo, ase amabe ayio omorwoti Demeturio abakoreire Abayahudi, twamoriikeire Demeturio buna ekobwatia: Nase ki okobakorera bobe na kobarianania bobe igo abasani na ababwatani baito Abayahudi?

English: If therefore they plead any more against you, we will do them justice, and fight with you on sea and on land.’”
Ekegusii: Ekero barabe bachire ase tore na kwemurungania ase engencho yaino naende, intwe ntobabwatesie Abayahudi, ntokoranie nainwe ase amaache na ase ense enyomo.”

English: Demetrius heard that Nicanor had fallen with his forces in battle, and he sent Bacchides and Alcimus again into the land of Judah a second time, and the right wing of his army with them.
Ekegusii: Ekero Demeturio aigwete buna Nikanori amo na abarwani esegi baye basiriigwe ase esegi, akabairania naende Alikimo na Bakide amo na ebiombe bi’abarwani esegi baye bokorio Yudea.

English: They went by the way that leads to Gilgal, and encamped against Mesaloth, which is in Arbela, and took possession of it, and killed many people.
Ekegusii: Bagaetera enchera egochia Giligali na kobeeka ekambi yaabo agwo Aribela, Bakayoira omochie o Mesalothi na kobaita abanto abange.

English: The first month of the one hundred fifty-second year, they encamped against Jerusalem.
Ekegusii: Ase omotienyi bw’eritang’ani bw’omwaka 152, bakabeeka ekambi yaabo chimbebe chia Yerusalemu.

English: Then they marched away and went to Berea with twenty thousand infantry and two thousand cavalry.
Ekegusii: Korwa ime ye ekambi bakageenda Beroya na abasikari bagochiera amagoro 20,000, na abagochiera chibaarasi 2,000.

English: Judas was encamped at Elasa with three thousand chosen men.
Ekegusii: Yuda nigo abaegete ekambi Elasa, ore na abasikari 3,000 bachoorire.

English: They saw the multitude of the forces, that they were many, and they were terrified. Many slipped away out of the army. There were not left of them more than eight hundred men.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero barora obonge bwa abarwani esegi ba ababisa, bakabwatwa nobwoba obonene. Abange ase bare bagatama korwa ekambi erio bagatigara abanto 800 boka.

English: Judas saw that his army slipped away and that the battle pressed upon him, and he was very troubled in spirit, because he had no time to gather them together, and he became faint.
Ekegusii: Ekero Yuda arooche buna abarwani esegi baye bagendereire gokea naende buna ere tabwati ebiro aranyare kobasangereria ase esegi konye yabereire ang’e, agakwa omoyo.

English: He said to those who were left, “Let’s arise and go up against our adversaries, if perhaps we may be able to fight with them.”
Ekegusii: Konye ere okuure omoyo. Korende akabateebia abarwani esegi baria batigarete nere: “Tweariganie ase esegi; nabo eranyaarekane tobue ababisa.”

English: They tried to dissuade him, saying, “There is no way we are able; but let’s rather save our lives now. Let’s return again with our kindred, and fight against them; but we are too few.”
Ekegusii: Korende abanto baye bagatema komotanga bakoboora, “Intwe titokonyaara kobabua. Onye torigetie gotooria obogima bwaito, tiga intwe bono toirane gochia seito. Erio intwe ntochiche amo na abaminto; erio tobarwanie ababisa. Ase bono intwe nabake mono.”

English: Judas said, “Let it not be so that I should do this thing, to flee from them. If our time has come, let’s die in a manly way for our kindred’s sake, and not leave a cause of reproach against our honor.”
Ekegusii: Yuda akabairaneria: “Yaaya, tekoba! Nigo ere obosooku ase tore intwe gokora boigo gotama esegi. Kerabe omoerio oito oikire, tiga intwe tokwe ase engencho y’Abayahudi baminto. Intwe titosaria erieta riaito!”

English: The army marched out from the camp, and stood to encounter them. The cavalry was divided into two companies, and the slingers and the archers went before the army, and all the mighty men that fought in the front of the battle.
Ekegusii: Agwo abarwani be esegi ba Bakide bagasoka na kweroberia kobarwania Abayahudi esegi. Abasikari bakoira chibaarasi bakaroberigwa ase ebiombe bibere. Abasikari ebiata bakabekwa motwe, korende abasikari bakoruta chinsara amo na abebirasi bagatang’anigwa motwe kegima.

English: Bacchides was in the right wing. The phalanx advanced on the two parts, and they blew with their trumpets.
Ekegusii: Bakide omonyene akeroberia ase okoboko gwokorio. Abasikari bagochiera amagoro bagachaaka gosuka motwe barabwo bagiteire korwa chinsemo ibere na baria bariinete chibaarasi. Ebituureri bi’eseegi biakabugigwa na abasikari ba Yuda nabarabwo bakabugia ebituureri biabo.

English: The men by Judas’ side sounded with their trumpets, and the earth shook with the shout of the armies, and the battle was joined, and continued from morning until evening.
Ekegusii: Ekero abarwani abwo be esegi baumeranete, ense egatengecha. Bakarwana korwa mabia goika mogoroba.

English: Judas saw that Bacchides and the strength of his army were on the right side, and all that were brave in heart went with him,
Ekegusii: Yuda akamanya buna Bakide na abasikari ebiata nigo bare ase okoboko gw’okorio. Erio baria abaremu na ebiata bakabwatana amo nere,

English: and the right wing was defeated by them, and he pursued after them to the mount Azotus.
Ekegusii: Bakabasenyentasenyenta abasikari bokorio ba Bakide na kobaminyokia goika egetunwa gia Azoto.

English: Those who were on the left wing saw that the right wing was defeated, and they turned and followed in the footsteps of Judas and of those who were with him.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero abarwani be esegi ba Siria ba komosi barooche buna abamwabo bokorio baitirwe mono, bagekiora na komobwatia Yuda na abarwani baye be esegi korwa magega.

English: The battle became desperate, and many on both sides fell wounded to death.
Ekegusii: Esegi ekaba endoro mono. Abasikari abange bechinsemo chionsi bagasiria obogima bwabo.

English: Judas fell, and the rest fled.
Ekegusii: Omoerio Yuda omonyene agaitwa erio abanto baye bonsi bagatama.

English: Jonathan and Simon took Judas their brother, and buried him in the tomb of his ancestors at Modin.
Ekegusii: Yonathani na Simioni bakabogoria omobere oye na koyotindeka ase chimbeera chi’echisokoro chiabo agwo Modeini.

English: They wept for him. All Israel made great lamentation for him, and mourned many days, and said,
Ekegusii: Bagaikaransa agwo ase embeera na komoreera Yuda. Abaisraeli bonsi bakamoreera ase amatuko amange bagoteeba:

English: “How the mighty has fallen, the savior of Israel!”
Ekegusii: “Inaki omonyanguru agwa ere orenge omotooria bwa Abaisraeli!”

English: The rest of the acts of Judas, and his wars, and the valiant deeds which he did, and his greatness, are not written; for they were exceedingly many.
Ekegusii: Amakora ande a Yuda, esegi arwanete, oboremu bwaye, na okobua kwaye okonene tibianyaarete koriikwa egekogera biarenge ebiinge mono.

English: It came to pass after the death of Judas, that the lawless emerged within all the borders of Israel. All those who did iniquity rose up.
Ekegusii: Magega yogokwa kwa Yuda, abatwambu baria batabwatete amachiiko bagachaaka kororekana kera ensemo ase ense ya Yudea na ababe bonsi bakarorekana naende.

English: In those days there was an exceedingly great famine, and the country went over to their side.
Ekegusii: Ase engaki eyio, enchara enene ekaba ase ense na ense engima ekaba ase ensemo ya ababe abwo.

English: Bacchides chose the ungodly men and made them rulers of the country.
Ekegusii: Erio Bakide ase ogwancha akabachoora abanto abwo ababe korwa ase Abayahudi babe abarain b’ense.

English: They inquired and searched for the friends of Judas, and brought them to Bacchides, and he took vengeance on them and used them spitefully.
Ekegusii: Erio bakabarigia abasani ba Yuda na kobaira ase obosio bwa Bakide. Bakide akabachaanda na kobairania inse kegima.

English: There was great suffering in Israel, such as was not since the time prophets stopped appearing to them.
Ekegusii: Engaki eyio nigo yarenge e yogochaandwa na obororo obonge kobua ekero ababani bachaagete kobora ase egati ya Abaisraeli.

English: All the friends of Judas were gathered together, and they said to Jonathan,
Ekegusii: Erio abasani bonsi ba Yuda bakaumerana na komoteebia Yonathani:

English: “Since your brother Judas has died, we have no man like him to go out against our enemies and Bacchides, and among those of our nation who hate us.
Ekegusii: “Korwa momura omino Yuda akwete, taratoka naende onde omogwekaine oratorae mamincha ya ababisa baito, mamincha ya Bakide amo na Abayahudi baito abwo bagotoengereria.

English: Now therefore we have chosen you this day to be our prince and leader in his place, that you may fight our battles.”
Ekegusii: Ase igo reero intwe twagochoorire aye koba omorai oito na omoteneneri bwe esegi ribaga riaye erio intwe togendererie esegi yaito.”

English: So Jonathan took the governance upon him at that time, and rose up in the place of his brother Judas.
Ekegusii: Yonathani akabogoria oborai ase rituko erio na kobogoria ensemo ya Yuda momura omwabo.

English: When Bacchides found out, he tried to kill him.
Ekegusii: Ekero Bakide amanyete ring’ana erio, agaetia amoite Yonathani.

English: Jonathan, and Simon his brother, and all who were with him, knew it; and they fled into the wilderness of Tekoah, and encamped by the water of the pool of Asphar.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero Yonathani amanya emeroberio eyio, agatama gochia ase erooro ya Tekoa, ere amo na momura omwabo, Simioni amo na abanto baabo. Agwo bakabeeka ekambi ange neritibo ria Asifari.

English: Bacchides found this out on the Sabbath day, and came—he and all his army—over the Jordan.
Ekegusii: (Bakide akanyoora amang’ana ayio ase rituko ri’Esabato, akaamboka orooche ere amo na abarwani baye be esegi bonsi.)

English: Jonathan sent his brother, a leader of the multitude, and implored his friends the Nabathaeans, that they might store their baggage, which was much, with them.
Ekegusii: Yonathani akamotoma momura omwabo Yohana oyio orenge gokorera chiamate chi’abasikari abasabe Ababetea, abasani ba Yonathani ribaga riokogacha ebinto biabo ebinge bachete nabio ase ekiage kiabo.

English: The children of Jambri came out of Medaba, and seized John and all that he had, and went their way with it.
Ekegusii: Korende abanto be eamate ya Yamburi korwa Medeba bakamogwera Yohana bakamobwata na koira ebinto bionsi arenge nabio.

English: But after these things, they brought word to Jonathan and Simon his brother that the children of Jambri were celebrating a great wedding, and were bringing the bride, a daughter of one of the great nobles of Canaan, from Nadabath with a large escort.
Ekegusii: Ase ebiro ebike Yonathani na momura omwabo Simioni bakaigwa buna eamate ya Yamburi nigo yebegete ang’e gochengera enyangi enene. Boigo buna barabwo nigo barenge goci gotwara okorobera okonene gwokomokooba omoriakari korwa ase omochie o Nadabathi. Omoriakari nigo arenge omoiseke bw’oyomo bwa abanene ba Kaanani.

English: They remembered John their brother, and went up, and hid themselves under the cover of the mountain.
Ekegusii: Yonathani na momura omwabo bagaetia koirania egesiomba ase engencho ya amanyinga a momura omwabo Yohana ayio aiteretwe. Barabwo amo na abanto baabo bakariina egetunwa ekemo na kwebisa.

English: They lifted up their eyes and looked, and saw a great procession with much baggage. The bridegroom came out with his friends and his kindred to meet them with timbrels, musicians, and many weapons.
Ekegusii: Bakarigereria na korora abanto babogoretie chigurube bagoeta na goaka egeturi. Omonyanyaangi, abasani baye, ne eamate yaye konye bachire koumerana na barabwo. Nigo babogoretie ebirwanero naboigo bakobugia chikonu na ebinto binde biogoteera.

English: They rose up against them from their ambush and killed them, and many fell wounded to death. The remnant fled into the mountain, and the Jews took all their spoils.
Ekegusii: Agwo Abayahudi bakarwa ase obwebisero bwabo bakabagwera na kobaita abange baabo; abaminchoretie bagatama gochia ebitunwa. Abayahudi bakaira obotenenku bwabo bwonsi.

English: So the wedding was turned into mourning, and the voice of their musicians into lamentation.
Ekegusii: Erio enyaangi eyio akaonchoka koba ebirero na amateera yomochengo akaonchoka akaba ay’ebirero na okweumia.

English: They avenged fully the blood of their brother, and turned back to the marshes of the Jordan.
Ekegusii: Ekero Yonathani na Simioni bakoorete goakana egesiomba ase amanyinga a momura omwabo, bakairana gochia ase amatibo a Yorodani.

English: Bacchides heard it, and he came on the Sabbath day to the banks of the Jordan with a great army.
Ekegusii: Bakide akanyoora amang’ana igoro yayio akoregete. Ase rituko ri’Esabato agaika na abarwani baye be esegi goika ase engegu yorooche rwa Yorodani.

English: Jonathan said to his company, “Let’s stand up now and fight for our lives, for things are different today than they were yesterday and the day before.
Ekegusii: Yonathani akabateebia abanto baye: “Bono goika torwane esegi yogokwa no okoba. Twaonchokananirwe mono kobua ngaki ende yonsi.

English: For, behold, the battle is before us and behind us. Moreover the water of the Jordan is on this side and on that side, and marsh and thicket. There is no place to escape.
Ekegusii: Ababisa nigo bare bosio bwaito. Magega yaito norooche. Borio na bonosi bwaito nebisarara namatibo. Ng’ai intwe toratamere gochia?

English: Now therefore cry to heaven, that you may be delivered out of the hand of your enemies.”
Ekegusii: Bono saba Omonene atotoorie korwa ase chinchara chi’ababisa baito.”

English: So the battle was joined, and Jonathan stretched out his hand to strike Bacchides, and he turned away back from him.
Ekegusii: Esegi egachaaka. Yonathani akarambora okoboko kwaye erio amoite Bakide. Korende Bakide akebacha agatama gochia magega ya abarwani baye be esegi.

English: Jonathan and those who were with him leapt into the Jordan, and swam over to the other side. The enemy didn’t pass over the Jordan against them.
Ekegusii: Erio Yonathani na abanto baye bagasoa ime yorooche rwa Yorodani. Bagaaka obari goika ng’umbu erio banyaare gotama. Korende abanto ba Bakide tibaabogete kobabwatia.

English: About a thousand men of Bacchides’ company fell that day;
Ekegusii: Bakide agasiria abanto baye ang’e 1,000.

English: and he returned to Jerusalem. They built strong cities in Judea, the stronghold that was in Jericho, and Emmaus, Bethhoron, Bethel, Timnath, Pharathon, and Tephon, with high walls and gates and bars.
Ekegusii: Magega yokoirana goika Yerusalemu, Bakide akaagacha chinyasi chintambe na ebisieri ebikong’u ase chinyomba chiaye ase omochie o Yudea: Emau, Beth-horoni, Betheli, Timunati, Farathoni, Tefoni; na ase orwaki rwa Yeriko.

English: He set garrisons in them to harass Israel.
Ekegusii: Ase emechie eyio yonsi, Bakideakabeeka ebiombe bia abasikari erio barabwo babakorere bobe Abayahudi.

English: He fortified the city Bethsura, Gazara, and the citadel, and put troops and stores of food in them.
Ekegusii: Agakong’ia boigo chinyomba chia Beth-zuri na Gazara naboigo eburi ya Yerusalemu. Akabeeka aroro ebiombe bia abarwani be esegi ne ebiage bie endagera.

English: He took the sons of the chief men of the country for hostages, and put them under guard in the citadel at Jerusalem.
Ekegusii: Erio akababwata abana ba abanto basikire ase omochie na kobakora abooswa na kobasiekera ime ase eburi ya Yerusalemu.

English: And in the one hundred fifty-third year, in the second month, Alcimus gave orders to pull down the wall of the inner court of the sanctuary. He also pulled down the works of the prophets.
Ekegusii: Ase omotienyi o kabere ase omwaka o 153, Omokuani omonene, Alikimo agachiika enyasi ya ime ye Hekalu etaagorwe. Gokora boigo nigo konga buna ogosaria keria ababani bakoorete; ekero bachia gochaaka ogotagora enyasi,

English: He began to pull down. At that time was Alcimus stricken, and his works were hindered; and his mouth was stopped, and he was taken with a palsy, and he could no more speak anything and give orders concerning his house.
Ekegusii: Alikimo akanyoora amaakwa na emeremo egatenena. Omonwa oye okagataa agasinywa koyomumora, gokwana gose koriera abanto baye omwando.

English: Alcimus died at that time with great torment.
Ekegusii: Agakwa ore n’obosareru obonene.

English: Bacchides saw that Alcimus was dead, and he returned to the king. Then the land of Judah had rest for two years.
Ekegusii: Ekero Bakide anyorete amang’ana yo ogokwa okwo, akairana gochia ase omorwoti Demeturio na ense ya Yudea ekaba n’omorembe ase emiaka ebere.

English: Then all the lawless men took counsel, saying, “Behold, Jonathan and his men are dwelling at ease and in security. Now therefore we will bring Bacchides, and he will capture them all in one night.
Ekegusii: Erio abakaayayu bonsi bagateeba: “Rora, Yonathani na abanto baye nigo bare n’omorembe amo nobuya. Toise komorenta Bakide aiga, ere nigo arababwate bonsi ase obotuko obomo.”

English: They went and consulted with him.
Ekegusii: Barabwo bakageenda gokora ebigambo na Bakide.

English: He marched out and came with a great army, and sent letters secretly to all his allies who were in Judea, that they should seize Jonathan and those who were with him; but they couldn’t, because their plan was known to them.
Ekegusii: Bakide akaimokia na abarwani esegi baye abange kegima na kibariikera amarube abobisi abasani baye bonsi bareenge ase ense ya Yudea, okobaboria bamobwate Yonathani na abanto baye. Korende barabwo tibanyaara goikerania ayio ase engencho omoroberio obo omanyekanete mapema.

English: Jonathan’s men seized about fifty of the men of the country who were authors of the wickedness, and he killed them.
Ekegusii: Yonathani na abanto baye bakababwata abarua abwo 60 na kobaita.

English: Jonathan, Simon, and those who were with him, went away to Bethbasi, which is in the wilderness, and he built up that which had been pulled down, and they made it strong.
Ekegusii: Kegima Yonathani, Simioni na abarwani esegi baabo bagasooka kogenda Beth-basi ase ense y’erooro. Agwo bagachuka amatombe yechinyomba na gotenenia oborendi bwo omochie o Beth-basi.

English: Bacchides found out about it, and he gathered together all his multitude, and sent orders to those who were of Judea.
Ekegusii: Ekero Bakide ayanyoorete ayio onsi, agasangereria abarwani be esegi baye bonsi na kobabeeka amo bonsi baria barenge komobwatesia ase ense ya Yudea.

English: He went and encamped against Bethbasi and fought against it many days, and made engines of war.
Ekegusii: Erio ere akageenda na koyogwera omochie o Beth-basi korwa chinsemo chionsi. Akaagacha etinga ye esegi. Ekero esegi yagenderera ase amatuko amange,

English: Jonathan left his brother Simon in the city, and went out into the country, and he went with a few men.
Ekegusii: Yonathani akamotiga momura omwabo ime yomochie, akageenda ensemo ye emegondo ase ense eyio ore nekeombe kia abanto abake igo.

English: He struck Odomera and his kindred, and the children of Phasiron in their tents.
Ekegusii: Agwo Yonathani akamobua Odomera na abanto baye erio akabagwera eamate ya Fasironi ase chiema chiabo. Abwo babuetwe bakabwatana nere ase okorwana.

English: They began to strike them, and to go up with their forces. Then Simon and those who were with him went out of the city, and set the engines of war on fire,
Ekegusii: Ase chingaki echio echio, Simioni na abanto baye bagatama korwa ase omochie o Beth-basi bakayesamba etinga eria ye esegi.

English: and fought against Bacchides, and he was defeated by them. They afflicted him severely; for his counsel and expedition was in vain.
Ekegusii: Ase esegi eyio, Bakide akabwatwa bobe mono goika emeroberio yaye yonsi egatantanigwa. Ere akabugwa ae esegi.

English: They were very angry with the lawless men who gave him counsel to come into the country, and they killed many of them. Then he decided to depart into his own land.
Ekegusii: Ere akababea mono Abayahudi baria bamoseemetie na komosegeta agende Yudea; akabaita abange baabo. Erio ere Bakide agaetia koirana gochia ense yaye.

English: Jonathan learned of this and sent ambassadors to him, to the end that they should make peace with him, and that he should restore to them the captives.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero Yonathani anyora amang’ana ayio, akabatoma abanto baye gochia ase Bakide igoro yokoroisia emeroberio ya amachiiko yomorembe na koirania abasibwa ba Boyahudi.

English: He accepted the thing, and did according to his words, and swore to him that he would not seek his harm all the days of his life.
Ekegusii: Bakide agaitabera gokora kobwatekana nokoboria kwa Yonathani na gotiana ase chiira buna takomokorera bobe ase obogima bwaye bwonsi.

English: He restored to him the captives which he had taken before out of the land of Judah, and he returned and departed into his own land, and didn’t come any more into their borders.
Ekegusii: Bakide akamoiraneria Yonathani abasibwa bonsi Abayahudi konye abwatire na kobaira korwa ense ya Yudea.

English: Thus the sword ceased from Israel. Jonathan lived at Michmash. Jonathan began to judge the people; and he destroyed the ungodly out of Israel.
Ekegusii: Agwo esegi egatiga korwana ase ense ya Israeli. Yonathani agakora obomenyo bwaye Mikimashi, agachaaka kobaraa Abaisraeli, na kobaseria baria ababe bonsi korwa ense eyio.

English: In the one hundred sixtieth year, Alexander Epiphanes, the son of Antiochus, went up and took possession of Ptolemais. They received him, and he reigned there.
Ekegusii: Ase omwaka o 160, Alekisanda Epifane, mosinto bwa Antioko o kane agaika Tolemai na koyoira omochie oyio. Abanto bakamoarigania nere akaba omorwoti obo.

English: King Demetrius heard about this, and he gathered together exceedingly great forces, and went out to meet him in battle.
Ekegusii: Ekero omorwoti Demeturio anyorete amang’ana ayio, ere agasangereria abarwani esegi abange, agasooka kogenda korwana na Alekisanda Epifane.

English: Demetrius sent a letter to Jonathan with words of peace, so as to honor him.
Ekegusii: Ase engaki eyio Demeturio akamoirera Yonathani riruube riobosaani ribwate amang’ana amange yokoebereria,

English: For he said, “Let’s go beforehand to make peace with them, before he makes peace with Alexander against us;
Ekegusii: ere nigo asemeretie amonyoore na boigo koroisia omoroberio bw’omorembe amo na Abayahudi erio Alekisanda ataraika koroisia okobwatana nabwo mamincha yaye.

English: for he will remember all the evils that we have done against him, and to his kindred and to his nation.”
Ekegusii: Demeturio akarengereria buna Yonathani nkoinyora areenge amabe onsi aria amokorerete ere na bamura bamwabo na ase egesaku ekegima kia Abayahudi.

English: So he gave him authority to gather together forces, and to provide weapons, and that he should be his ally. He also commanded that they should release the hostages that were in the citadel to him.
Ekegusii: Igo Demeturio akamoroisia Yonathani koba omobwatani nere ase esegi, akamoa okobua gwokoroisia ekeombe kia abarwani be esegi na kobaa ebirwanero. Boigo agachiika buna Yonathani aegwe abasibwa abwo basiekeire ime yeburi ya Yerusalemu.

English: Jonathan came to Jerusalem, and read the letter in the hearing of all the people, and of those who were in the citadel.
Ekegusii: Yonathani akageenda Yerusalemu gosooma riruube erio ase obosio bwa abanto abwo barenge ime y’eburi.

English: They were very afraid when they heard that the king had given him authority to gather together an army.
Ekegusii: Abanto abwo bakairoka mono ekero baigwete buna omorwoti omoeire Yonathani okobua gwokoroisia ekeombe kia abarwani be esegi.

English: Those in the citadel released the hostages to Jonathan, and he restored them to their parents.
Ekegusii: Bakamoa Yonathani abasibwa nere akabairania gochia ase abaibori baabo.

English: Jonathan lived in Jerusalem and began to build and renew the city.
Ekegusii: Yonathani akaroisia obomenyo bwaye obonene ase omochie o Yerusalemu. Ere agachaaka koyoagaacha boyia na koyobareera.

English: He commanded those who did the work to build the walls and encircle Mount Zion with square stones for defense; and they did so.
Ekegusii: Akabachiika abaagachi koagaachera amagena agosungoka ase chinyasi chi’omochie na enyasi egoetanana egetunwa gia Sayoni. Ayio agakoreka boigo.

English: The foreigners who were in the strongholds which Bacchides had built fled away.
Ekegusii: Abamenyi abwo barenge ase chiburi chiaagachetwe na Bakide bagatama;

English: Each man left his place and departed into his own land.
Ekegusii: kera omonto agatiga emeremo yaye na koirana gochia sobo.

English: Only at Bethsura, there were left some of those who had forsaken the law and the commandments, for it was a place of refuge to them.
Ekegusii: Korende Abayahudi baria konye batigire gotunyana amachiiko bakagenderera komenya Beth-zuri; ekiagera omochie oyio noro orenge obotamero bwabo bwo omoerio.

English: King Alexander heard all the promises which Demetrius had sent to Jonathan. They told him of the battles and the valiant deeds which he and his kindred had done, and of the troubles which they had endured.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti Alekisanda akanyoora amang’ana igoro ye chiira chionsi Demeturio amoete Yonathani, igoro ya Yonathani omonyene, chiseegi konye arwanire, amakora aye yoboremu, na obokong’u konye ere anyoorire amo na abamura bamwabo.

English: So he said, “Could we find another man like him? Now we will make him our friend and ally.”
Ekegusii: Akamanya ekeene buna ere takomonyora omonto onde onga buna Yonathani. Ekaba omorwoti Alekisanda akagania amokore Yonathani koba omobwatani oye.

English: He wrote a letter and sent it to him, in these words, saying,
Ekegusii: Eri nario riruube ere amoriikerete Yonathani:

English: “King Alexander to his brother Jonathan, greetings.
Ekegusii: “Omorwoti Alekisanda ase omosaani oye Yonathani, amakwania ayio!

English: We have heard of you, that you are a mighty man of valour, and worthy to be our friend.
Ekegusii: Naigure buna aye nomonto omoremu. Ase igo aye nore noboronge bw’okoba omosaani bw’omorwoti.

English: Now we have appointed you this day to be high priest of your nation, and to be called the king’s friend, and to take our side, and to keep friendship with us.” He also sent to him a purple robe and a golden crown.
Ekegusii: Ase rituko eri ria reero inche nagochoorire koba Omokuani omonene ase egesaku kiao, na nigo orarokwe Omosaani bw’Omorwoti. Aye noobe omobwatani oito oratoe ogokoonya.” Amo neriruube erio, omorwoti akamotomera Yonathani eyanga emonyiinga amo negutwa yetaabu.

English: And Jonathan put on the holy garments in the seventh month of the one hundred sixtieth year, at the feast of tabernacles; and he gathered together forces and provided weapons in abundance.
Ekegusii: Ase omotienyi o gatano na kabere omwaka o 160, ase rituko rinene riebigutu, Yonathani akeboyia emiambaro eyio yo Omokuani omonene. Akaroisia ekeombe kia abarwani be esegi na kobaa ebirwanero ebinge.

English: When Demetrius heard these things, he was grieved and said,
