Ekegusii: Ekero Demeturio aigwete ayio, akegosa ase omoyo oye erio agateeba:

English: “What is this that we have done, that Alexander has gotten ahead of us in establishing friendship with the Jews to strengthen himself?
Ekegusii: “Ninki togokora bono? Twamotigire Alekisanda gototang’anera na gokong’a ase okoroisia obosaani na Abayahudi!

English: I also will write to them words of encouragement and of honor and of gifts, that they may be with me to aid me.”
Ekegusii: Bona nainche nigo nkobariikera Abayahudi riruube riobosani. Nimbariere chiira chiokobaa oborai ao ao, erio barabwo bang’e ogokoonya ebiro binde bionsi erabetererie.”

English: So he sent to them this message: “King Demetrius to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
Ekegusii: Erio akariika: Omorwoti Demeturio, ase egesaku kia Abayahudi, Amakwania ayio!

English: Since as you have kept your covenants with us, and continued in our friendship, and have not joined yourselves to our enemies, we have heard of this, and are glad.
Ekegusii: Intwe ntore nomogooko koigwa buna mwatunyanire okobwatana gwaito. Inwe mwatigaire koba abegenwa ase tore nabo buna inwe timorabwatana na ababisa baito.

English: Now continue still to keep faith with us, and we will repay you with good in return for your dealings with us.
Ekegusii: Ekero eraabe buna inwe mwagendereire koba abegenwa ase tore, intwe ntobae ekeegwa ekenene.

English: We will grant you many immunities and give you gifts.
Ekegusii: Intwe intobaruuserie ebango enyinge na kobaa ogwanchererigwa ase ebinto ao ao.

English: “Now I free you and release all the Jews from the tributes, from the salt tax, and from the crown levies.
Ekegusii: Ase riruube eri, natugutire ebango yomotwe, n’eyomonyo nechibaango chinde chiechingeencho chinde.

English: Instead of the third part of the seed, and instead of half of the fruit of the trees, which falls to me to receive, I release it from this day and henceforth, so that I will not take it from the land of Judah, and from the three districts which are added to it from the country of Samaria and Galilee, from this day forth and for all time.
Ekegusii: Boigo, gochaakera ase rituko eri ria reero, inche nabaruuseirie okong’akana gw’enseemo eyemo ya isato yokogesa kwaino gwechintetere na ekeng’ese ase okwama kwa amatunda. Gochakera rituko eri kogenderera, inche tingotura ogoakana okwo korwa Yudea nechinsemo isato chiria chiabwatanetigwe na Yudea korwa Samaria amo na Galili.

English: Let Jerusalem be holy and free, with her borders, tithes, and taxes.
Ekegusii: Yerusalemu amo ne ebichie biaye bionsi inabimanyekane buna omochie omochenu na oro tokoganerigwa korua ebaango ende yonsi.

English: I yield up also my authority over the citadel which is at Jerusalem, and give it to the high priest, that he may appoint in it men whom he chooses to keep it.
Ekegusii: Korwa reero inche tindi nokobua ase eburi ya Yerusalemu; nayobeekire inse yoborai bw’Omokuani omonene, oyio boigo oraabe nokobua gwokomochoora onde bwensi ere omonyene araanche koba omorendi aroro agwo.

English: Every soul of the Jews who has been carried captive from the land of Judah into any part of my kingdom, I set at liberty without payment. Let all officials also cancel the taxes on their livestock.
Ekegusii: Inche nabaigoreire abasibwa bonsi be esegi bare ande onsi ase oborwoti bwane. Abwo bonsi babeirwe korwa ase chibaango nonya nebaango ase chitugo chiabo.

English: “All the feasts, the Sabbaths, new moons, appointed days, three days before a feast, and three days after a feast, let them all be days of immunity and release for all the Jews who are in my kingdom.
Ekegusii: Tari Omoyahudi nonya n’oyomo ande onsi ase agotooka oraruusigwe ebaango ase rituko ri’Esabato, ase amatuko amanene y’omotienyi, oboyia bw’omotienyi na ase amatuko ande amanene. Boigo, ebaango tegosangererigwa ase amatuko atato magega na motwe ya amatuko ayio amanene.

English: No man shall have authority to exact anything from any of them, or to trouble them concerning any matter.
Ekegusii: Ase amatuko ayio onde tagwancherwa kobatura ase amaakano gose kobachaanda ase enchera ende yonsi.

English: “Let there be enrolled among the king’s forces about thirty thousand men of the Jews, and pay shall be given to them, as is due to all the king’s forces.
Ekegusii: Abayahudi goika 30,000 mbancheire kweriika ase ekeombe gieseegi kiomorwoti nabarabwo mbaakanwe buna abasikari bande b’omorwoti.

English: Of them, some shall be placed in the king’s great strongholds, and some of them shall be placed over the affairs of the kingdom, which are positions of trust. Let those who are over them and their rulers be of themselves, and let them walk after their own laws, even as the king has commanded in the land of Judah.
Ekegusii: Ase egati yaabo nabo baranyare kobeekwa ase chiburi chinene chi’omorwoti na abande koegwa obonene ao ase eserekari. Abarai na abanene baabo inababe Abayahudi bamwabo nabo barabwo inabaancherwe gotunyana amenaria na amachiiko abo buna omorwoti boigo ancherete abanto ba Yudea.

English: “The three districts that have been added to Judea from the country of Samaria, let them be annexed to Judea, that they may be reckoned to be under one ruler, that they may not obey any other authority than the high priest’s.
Ekegusii: Chinsemo chiria isato chi’ense ya Samaria chibwatanetigwe na Yudea, inachibarwe koba ensemo ya Yudea na kobekwa inse yobobui bw’Omokuani omonene.

English: As for Ptolemais and its land, I have given it as a gift to the sanctuary that is at Jerusalem, for the expenses of the sanctuary.
Ekegusii: Ebitoki bi’omochie Tolemai ne endemero yaye inabikore emeremo yokogendereria Hekalu ya Yerusalemu.

English: I also give every year fifteen thousand shekels of silver from the king’s revenues from the places that are appropriate.
Ekegusii: Boigo nariire eira yokorua ebiegwa 15,000 bi’efeta kera omwaka korwa kera ensemo ebwatekanete yekegancha kiomorwoti.

English: And all the additional funds which those who manage the king’s affairs didn’t pay as in the first years, they shall give from now on toward the works of the temple.
Ekegusii: Omobaro bwonsi bwogokoonya bwefeta korwa ase eserekari, eyio inwe totanyaarete korwa ase emiaka ya magega, neakanwe kegima korwa bono na kogenderera erio ekoonye emeremo ye Hekalu.

English: Besides this, the five thousand shekels of silver which they received from the uses of the sanctuary from the revenue year by year is also released, because it belongs to the priests who minister there.
Ekegusii: Komenta nayio, titori gochia gotura ebing’ese biria 5,000 bi’efeta korwa ase okonyoora gwe Hekalu. Efeta eyio nigo ebatungetie abakuani baria bagokorera Hekalu.

English: Whoever flees to the temple that is at Jerusalem, and within all of its borders, whether owing money to the king, or any other matter, let them go free, along with all that they have in my kingdom.
Ekegusii: Onde bwensi oriete kende gionsi agoturwa nomorwoti gose obwate ogoturwa egento kende gionsi, ekero araabe otameire Hekalu ya Yerusalemu gose ase ensemo eyemo ende yonsi ye Hekalu eyio, goika ere aberwe na koegwa enibo yaye ere ande onsi ase oborwoti bwane.

English: For the building and renewing of the structures of the sanctuary, the expense shall also be given out of the king’s revenue.
Ekegusii: “Rigori riokoagaacha Hekalu ase oboyia inariakanerwe korwa ase ekegancha kiomorwoti.

English: For the building of the walls of Jerusalem and fortifying it all around, the expense shall also be given out of the king’s revenue, also for the building of the walls in Judea.”
Ekegusii: Boigo, oboagaachi oboyia na okobareera ase chinyasi chia Yerusalemu na ase emechie emechoore ime ya Yudea, nigo biraabe bigoakanerwa korwa ase ekegancha kiomorwoti.”

English: Now when Jonathan and the people heard these words, they gave no credence to them, and didn’t accept them, because they remembered the great evil which he had done in Israel, and that he had afflicted them very severely.
Ekegusii: Ekero Yonathani amo na abanto baye baigwete ebirengererio ebio bi’omorwoti Demeturio, bagasinywa kobiegena gose kobiitaba ase engencho bainyorete buna ere abakorerete bobe na kobatiringera inse goetania ekerengo.

English: They were well pleased with Alexander, because he was the first who spoke words of peace to them, and they were allies with him always.
Ekegusii: Barabwo bakabwatana na Alekisanda, ekiagera ere abeete oyo bw’eritang’ani korwa ebirengererio bi’okobwatana na barabwo ase omorembe; bagatigara koba ababwatani nere goika ekero ere akwete.

English: King Alexander gathered together great forces and encamped near Demetrius.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti Alekisanda akaroisia ekeombe ekenene na kweroberia korwana na Demeturio.

English: The two kings joined battle, and the army of Alexander fled; and Demetrius followed after him, and prevailed against them.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero abarwani esegi ba abarwoti abwo babere baumeranete ase esegi, abarwani esegi ba Alekisanda bagekiora bagataama. Erio Demeturio akabamonyokia na akabua esegi.

English: He strengthened the battle exceedingly until the sun went down; and Demetrius fell that day.
Ekegusii: Nonya nabo, Alekisanda akarwana ogokwa nokoba goika risase rikarimera na Demeturio agaitwa ase rituko erio.

English: Alexander sent ambassadors to Ptolemy king of Egypt with this message:
Ekegusii: Erio Alekisanda agatoma amang’ana gochia ase Tolemai o gatano narimo omoruot o Misiri agoteeba iga:

English: “Since I have returned to my kingdom, and am seated on the throne of my fathers, and have established my dominion, and have overthrown Demetrius, and have taken possession of our country—
Ekegusii: “Inche nairanire ase borwoti bwane na goikaransera ekerogo kiobonene giechisokoro chiane. Namobuire Demeturio na goonchora eserekari na bono ense nigo ere ase amaboko ane.

English: yes, I joined the battle with him, and he and his army were defeated by us, and we sat on the throne of his kingdom—
Ekegusii: Ee inche nigo namorwanetie goika nkamobua ere amo na abarwani baye be esegi, erio inche ngaikaransera ekerogo kiobonene kioborwoti bwaye.

English: now also let’s make friends with one another. Give me now your daughter as my wife. I will be joined with you, and will give both you and her gifts worthy of you.”
Ekegusii: Bono inche ninde nokogania gokora okobwatana kwobosaani naye; ing’a omoiseke oo inche imonywome, nainche ninkoe aye amo nomoiseke oo ekeegwa kebaisaine inwe mwensi.”

English: Ptolemy the king answered, saying, “Happy is the day you returned to the land of your ancestors and sat on the throne of their kingdom.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti Tolemai akamoiraneria: “Erio nigo riabeete rituko riomogooko, ekero kwairanete ase ense yao na kogeikaransera ekerogo kiobonene giechisokoro chiao!

English: Now I will do to you as you have written, but meet me at Ptolemais, that we may see one another; and I will join with you, even as you have said.”
Ekegusii: Inche nancheranire nokoboria kwao, korende tiga ritang’ani tororane inche amo naye ase omochie o Tolemai, agwo inatoigwane nainche ninkonywomerie omoiseke one.”

English: So Ptolemy went out of Egypt, himself and Cleopatra his daughter, and came to Ptolemais in the one hundred sixty-second year.
Ekegusii: Igo ase omwaka 162, Tolemai nomoiseke oye, Kileopatura bagasooka korwa Misiri na goika Tolemai.

English: King Alexander met him, and he gave him his daughter Cleopatra, and celebrated her wedding at Ptolemais with great pomp, as kings do.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti Alekisanda akaumerana nabarabwo, nere Tolemai akamonywomeria Alekisanda omoiseke oye Kileopatura. Enyangi egachengerwa agwo Tolemai ase omogooko kobwatekana nobonene amo nechingeencho chia abarwoti.

English: King Alexander wrote to Jonathan, that he should come to meet him.
Ekegusii: Erio omorwoti Alekisanda akamoriikera Yonathani riruube achiche barorane amo nere.

English: He went with pomp to Ptolemais, and met the two kings. He gave them and their friends silver and gold, and many gifts, and found favor in their sight.
Ekegusii: Yonathani akageenda Tolemai nesiko na koumerana na abarwoti abwo babere.

English: Some malcontents out of Israel, men who were transgressors of the law, gathered together against him to complain against him; but the king paid no attention to them.
Ekegusii: Ase ebiro ebio ekeombe ekemo kia Abayahudi bamwangete Yonathani kegataka komorentera Yonathani esegi. Gekamorentera amasoero nokwemurungania ase are korende omorwoti Alekisanda akaanga kogetegerera.

English: The king commanded that they take off Jonathan’s garments and clothe him in purple, and they did so.
Ekegusii: Ere Alekisanda agachiika Yonathani aaborigwe chianga chiaye na koboyigwa chianga chi’oborwoti chiimonyinga. Ayio agakoreka boigo.

English: The king made him sit with him, and said to his princes, “Go out with him into the midst of the city, and proclaim that no man may complain against him of any matter, and let no man trouble him for any reason.”
Ekegusii: Naboigo omorwoti akamoikaransia Yonathani ensemo yesiko ang’e nere. Erio akabateebi abanene baye, “Mobogorie Yonathani momotaarie goika omochie omonene na koraria buna monto onde tancheiri komosoera Yonathani ase ing’ana rinde rionsi, na monto onde bwensi tabaisa goteema komorosia ase engencho ende yonsi.”

English: It came to pass, when those who complained against him saw his honor according to the proclamation, and saw him clothed in purple, they all fled away.
Ekegusii: Ekero okorari okwo kwabete na baria bonsi baroberetie komosoera barooche buna Yonathani aeirwe esiko na koimokererigwa igoro boigo kobekerwa egutwa yoborwoti, bagatama.

English: The king gave him honor, and enrolled him among his chief friends, and made him a captain and governor of a province.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti akagenderera koa Yonathani esiko goika akamobeka ase omobaro bw’eritang’ani ase “Abasani b’omorwoti,” na komokora koba omochiki bw’eseegi omogabana ase orogongo rwaye.

English: Then Jonathan returned to Jerusalem with peace and gladness.
Ekegusii: Erio Yonathani akairana gochia Yerusalemu, ore n’omogooko omonge n’okonyoora okonene.

English: In the one hundred sixty-fifth year, Demetrius, son of Demetrius, came out of Crete into the land of his ancestors.
Ekegusii: Ase omwaka o 165 Demeturio o kabare mosinto o Demeturio bw’eritang’ani, akarua Kirete na goika ase ense yechisokoro chiaye.

English: When King Alexander heard of it, he grieved exceedingly and returned to Antioch.
Ekegusii: Ekero omorwoti Alekisanda anyoorete amang’ana ayio, akegosa mono, akairana gochia Antiokia.

English: Demetrius appointed Apollonius, who was over Coelesyria, and he gathered together a great army, and encamped against Jamnia, and sent to Jonathan the high priest, saying,
Ekegusii: Erio Demeturio akamochoora Apolonio koba omogabana bw’orogongo rwa Siiria. Apolonio akaroisia ekeombe ekenene kia abarwani baye be esegi na kobeeka ekambi ang’e nomochie o Yamunia. Erio akamotomera Yonathani Omokuani omonene amang’ana akobwatia:

English: “You alone lift up yourself against us, but I am ridiculed and in reproach because of you. Why do you assume authority against us in the mountains?
Ekegusii: “Aye naye bweka orachiche goteema gotorwania. Ninki rende gekogera aye ogendererete gokora ogweatanana agwo ase ebitunwa naye tobwati onde ogokobwatesia?

English: Now therefore, if you trust in your forces, come down to us into the plain, and let’s match strength with each other there; for the power of the cities is with me.
Ekegusii: Onye ekeene aye bwegenete abarwani bao be esegi, tirimboka goocha aiga ense omweya erio torengane chinguru. Ring’ana rireo neri buna ebiombe bionsi bia abarwani be esegi ase emechie nigo bire magega yane.

English: Ask and learn who I am, and the rest who help us. They say, ‘Your foot can’t stand before our face; for your ancestors have been put to flight twice in their own land.’
Ekegusii: Aye mbwemanyere buna inche ning’o na abasani baane mbarabi naboigo nomanye buna tokobua kende ase obosio bwaito. Baria bagotangarete aye babeire bagoitwa ase riroba riabo abanyene;

English: Now you won’t be able to withstand the cavalry and such an army as this in the plain, where there is no stone or pebble, or place to flee.”
Ekegusii: inaki aye orasemerie kobabua abariini chibaarasi baane amo na abarwani esegi baane bengeencho eye inche mbwate ase ense eye yomweya? Oinyore inse aiga taiyo amagena gose ebigena bikogoto oranyaare aye kwebiserera boigo tobwati enchera oratamere.”

English: Now when Jonathan heard the words of Apollonius, he was moved in his mind, and he chose ten thousand men, and went out from Jerusalem; and Simon his brother met him to help him.
Ekegusii: Ekero Yonathani anyoorete amang’ana ayio korwa ase Apolonio, akabea mono. Agachoora abasikari 10,000 korwa Yerusalemu na Simioni momura omwabo nere akarenta abasikari bande. Ebiombe ebio

English: Then he encamped against Joppa. The people of the city shut him out, because Apollonius had a garrison in Joppa.
Ekegusii: bikabeeka ekambi isiko ya Yopa. Abanto b’omochie oyio bakanga kobaigorera basoe ase omochie oyio egekogera ekeombe kia abarwani esegi ba Apolonio nao barenge ime agwo. Yonathani agachaaka esegi.

English: So they fought against it. The people of the city were afraid, and opened to him; and Jonathan became master of Joppa.
Ekegusii: Abanto b’omochie oyio bakaba nobwoba, bakaigora ebisieri bi’omochie. Yonathani akayoira omochie o Yopa.

English: Apollonius heard about that, and he gathered an army of three thousand cavalry, and a great army, and went to Azotus as though he were on a journey, and at the same time advanced onward into the plain, because he had a multitude of cavalry which he trusted.
Ekegusii: Ekero Apolonio aigwete aria agendererete, akabogoria abarwani baye be esegi be chibaarasi 3,000 na abasikari abange bagochira amagoro akageenda Ashidodi, buna ere agendererete ase orogendo rwaye. Ere kagendererete gwetogeria abarwani baye be chibaarasi, agasuka motwe goika ense yomweya.

English: He pursued him to Azotus, and the armies joined battle.
Ekegusii: Yonathani akamobwatia Apolonio goika Ashidodi ne esegi egachaaka.

English: Apollonius had secretly left a thousand cavalry behind them.
Ekegusii: Kani Apolonio nabwate abarwani baye be esegi be chibaarasi 1,000 abisete korwa magega.

English: Jonathan learned that there was an ambush behind him. They surrounded his army, and shot their arrows at the people, from morning until evening;
Ekegusii: Goika agwo konye Yonathani tamanyete buna otegeirwe. Ekaba mobasokano abarwani baye be esegi bakaonchokanwa. Erio chinsara chi’ababisa chikabatonyera korwa igoro buna embura korwa mambia goika mogoroba.

English: but the people stood fast, as Jonathan commanded them; and the enemy’s horses grew tired.
Ekegusii: Nonya nabo, abarwani ba Yonathani be esegi bagatenena bokong’u, buna ere abachiigete goika abariini chibarasi ababisa bagachaaka kogoya.

English: Then Simon brought forward his army and joined battle with the phalanx (for the cavalry were exhausted), and they were defeated by him and fled.
Ekegusii: Goika ekero abariini chibaarasi abwo bagoya kegima, Simioni akaoroka ase egetii gieseegi ore ne ebiombe bia abarwani baye be esegi. Ere akabagwera rimo rioka na kobabua abarwani be esegi ba amagoro ababisa erio barabwo bakang’ea gotama chimbero.

English: The cavalry were scattered in the plain. They fled to Azotus and entered into Beth-dagon, their idol’s temple, to save themselves.
Ekegusii: Abariini chibarasi abwo bachong’ononete ase egetii giosi gieseegi, bagatama gochia Ashidodi, agwo na barabwo bakebisa ase Hekalu ye enyasae yaabo ekorokwa Beth-dagoni.

English: Jonathan burned Azotus and the cities around it and took their spoils. He burned the temple of Dagon and those who fled into it with fire.
Ekegusii: Korende ere Yonathani akayosamba omochi o Ahidodi boigo ne Hekalu ya Beth-dagoni, akabaita na kobasamba abwo bonsi batamete gochia aroro. Boigo akayesamba emechie yabebekaine na koyesakora.

English: Those who had fallen by the sword plus those who were burned were about eight thousand men.
Ekegusii: Ase rituko erio, abanto goika 8,000 bagaitwa goetera ase omoro gose omorero.

English: From there, Jonathan left and encamped against Ascalon. The people of the city came out to meet him with great pomp.
Ekegusii: Magega yayio Yonathani agasoka akageenda na kobeka ekambi yaye Asikeloni, na abanto b’omochie oyio bagasooka komoarigania nomochengo omonene.

English: Jonathan, with those who were on his side, returned to Jerusalem, having many spoils.
Ekegusii: Yonathani na abanto baye bakairana Yerusalemu na abooswa abange.

English: It came to pass, when King Alexander heard these things, he honored Jonathan even more.
Ekegusii: Ekero omorwoti Alekisanda anyoorete amang’ana ayio, akamoa Yonathani esiko enene kobua.

English: He sent him a gold buckle, as the custom is to give to the king’s kindred. He gave him Ekron and all its land for a possession.
Ekegusii: Akamotomera egetita gietaabu buna engencho ere ase omorwoti komokorera omorwoti onde boigo akamoa omochie o Ekironi ne chitaano chiaye.

English: Then the king of Egypt gathered together great forces, as the sand which is by the sea shore, and many ships, and sought to make himself master of Alexander’s kingdom by deceit, and to add it to his own kingdom.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti Tolemai o gata’narimo agasangereria ekeombe kia abarwani be esegi abasikari abange kobua omukenye o nyancha akaarigania ne chimeri chinyinge. Ekerenga kiaye nigo kiarenge okomobwata Alekisanda, aire oborwoti bwaye na kwementera ere omonyene ase arenge kogaamba.

English: He went out into Syria with words of peace, and the people of the cities opened their gates to him and met him; for King Alexander’s command was that they should meet him, because he was his father-in-law.
Ekegusii: Igo ere akagenda Siria na kobarira chiira gokora omorembe ase abanto agwo. Abamenyi ba Siria bakamoigorera ebisieri na koarigania. Omorwoti Alekisanda nere obachiigete gokora boigo ekiagera Tolemai omonywomerete.

English: Now as he entered into the cities of Ptolemais, he set his forces for a garrison in each city.
Ekegusii: Korende ekero Tolemai ageenda Irianyi agaeta kagotiga ekeombe kia abasikari kera ase.

English: But when he came near to Azotus, they showed him the temple of Dagon burned with fire, and Azotus and its pasture lands destroyed, and the bodies cast out, and those who had been burned, whom he burned in the war, for they had made heaps of them in his way.
Ekegusii: Ekero aika Ashidodi, abanto bakamworokia ritombe rie Hekalu ya Dagoni eyio yasambetwe nomorero na ogosaria gwonsi gwakoretwe Ashidodi ne chinsinyo chiaye. Ebitondo nigo biatindigaine kera aase. Emebere ya abanto abwo baitetwe na Yonathani nigo yarareranete mbarabare ase enchera egoeta Tolemai.

English: They told the king what Jonathan had done, that they might cast blame on him; but the king kept silent.
Ekegusii: Abanto bakamotebia boigo amabe Yonathani akorete bare nogosemeria buna ere nabekerwe amamocho; korende takwana gento kende.

English: Jonathan met the king with pomp at Joppa, and they greeted one another, and they slept there.
Ekegusii: Yonathani akagenda nobonene kororana na Tolemai. Bagakwanania na koraara agwo.

English: Jonathan went with the king as far as the river that is called Eleutherus, then returned to Jerusalem.
Ekegusii: Yonathani akamokooba goika orooche rwa Eleuthero erio ere akairana gochia Yerusalemu.

English: But King Ptolemy took control of the cities along the sea coast, to Selucia which is by the sea, and he devised evil plans concerning Alexander.
Ekegusii: Ase enchera eyio yobong’ainereria Tolemai akenyoorera emechie yonsi engegu yenyancha goika ekiambokero gia Selukia.

English: He sent ambassadors to King Demetrius, saying, “Come! Let’s make a covenant with one another, and I will give you my daughter whom Alexander has, and you shall reign over your father’s kingdom;
Ekegusii: Korwa agwo Tolemai akamoirera omorwoti Alekisanda amang’ana yokomoteebia iga: Tiga intwe tokore okobwatana kwomorembe. Bono iga omoiseke one n’omokungu bwa Alekisanda. Korende inche nimoire na gokomonywomeria erio inche ningokore obe omorwoti ase oborwoti bwa iso.

English: for I regret that I gave my daughter to him, for he tried to kill me.
Ekegusii: Nigo ngweitia eki kiagerete inche inkamoa Alekisanda omoiseke one, ekiagera ere nigo akorigia chinchera chiokong’ita.

English: He accused him, because he coveted his kingdom.
Ekegusii: Tolemai akamomochia Alekisanda ase enchera eyio ekiagera ere nigo atagete amoure oborwoti bwaye.

English: Taking his daughter from him, he gave her to Demetrius, and was estranged from Alexander, and their enmity was openly seen.
Ekegusii: Erio ere akamoura omiseke oye na komonywomeria Demeturio; agasiria oboamate bwonsi na Alekisanda na igo obobisa bwabo bokaba maiso marore.

English: Ptolemy entered into Antioch, and put on himself the crown of Asia. He put two crowns upon his head, the crown of Egypt and that of Asia.
Ekegusii: Tolemai agasoa Antiokia na kwebogoreria oborai bwa Asia; igo akaba omorai o Misiri na Asia.

English: But King Alexander was in Cilicia at that time, because the people of that region were in revolt.
Ekegusii: Ase ebiro ebio omorwoti Alekisanda nigo arenge Kilikia, ase engencho babwate chiburuburu.

English: When Alexander heard of it, he came against him in war. Ptolemy marched out and met him with a strong force, and put him to flight.
Ekegusii: Korende akero aigwete igoro ogouchanana gwa Tolemai, agasooka kegima na komogwera Tolemai. Ase obokoonyi bwa abarwani be esegi abange abwate, Tolemai akamoengera na komobua Alekisanda kegima.

English: Alexander fled into Arabia, that he might be sheltered there; but King Ptolemy was triumphant.
Ekegusii: Alekisanda agatama gochia kwebisa Arabia,

English: Zabdiel the Arabian took off Alexander’s head, and sent it to Ptolemy.
Ekegusii: korende Omoarbu oyomo okorokwa Sabidieli akamonacha omotwe na koyoirera Tolemai.

English: King Ptolemy died the third day after, and those who were in his strongholds were slain by the inhabitants of the strongholds.
Ekegusii: Ase amatuko abere abwatetie, Tolemai nere agakwa naboigo abasikari baye atigete ase chiburi ao ao bagaitwa na abanyene emechie eyio.

English: Demetrius became king in the one hundred sixty-seventh year.
Ekegusii: Erio Demeturio o kabaere akaba omorwoti ase omwaka o 167.

English: In those days Jonathan gathered together the Judeans to take the citadel that was at Jerusalem. He made many engines of war to use against it.
Ekegusii: Ase amatuko ayio ayio Yonathani agasangereria abanto ba Yudea erio koyerwania eburi ya Yerusalemu. Barabwo bakaroisia chitinga chinyinge chiiogokorera esegi ase ebiro ebio.

English: Some lawless men who hated their own nation went to the king and reported to him that Jonathan was besieging the citadel.
Ekegusii: Korende Abayahudi bande abwo bagechete egesaku kiabo abanyene, bakabasareria ase okogenda ase omorwoti Demeturio o kabere buna Yonathani nigo ere anaaretie eburi ya Yerusalemu.

English: He heard, and was angry, but when he heard it, he set out immediately, and came to Ptolemais, and wrote to Jonathan, that he should not besiege it, and that he should meet him and speak with him at Ptolemais with all speed.
Ekegusii: Ekero Demeturio aigwete aya ere akagechigwa mono goika akang’anyia obomenyo bwaye obonene goika Tolemai. Erio akamoriikera Yonathani riruube na komotebia atige koyonaaria omochie o Yerusalemu na ageende kororana nere agwo Tolemai ase obwango.

English: But when Jonathan heard this, he gave orders to continue the siege. He chose some of the elders of Israel and of the priests, and put himself in peril
Ekegusii: Ekero Yonathani anyoorete amang’ana ayio, akabachiika abanto baye babeo ase okoyonaaria omochie o Yerusalemu. Erio ere akabachoora bake korwa ase abarai na abakuani ba Abayahudi bamokoobe. Ere taegerera obogima bwaye

English: by taking silver, gold, clothing, and various other presents, and went to Ptolemais to the king. Then he found favor in his sight.
Ekegusii: akagenda Tolemai ase omorwoti na komoirera chianga, chifeta ne etaabu amo nebiegwa ebinge. Omorwoti akamogookera mono.

English: Some lawless men of those who were of the nation made complaints against him,
Ekegusii: Nonya yarenge buna abasaria gete konye bamosoereire na komobekera Yonathani amamocho,

English: and the king did to him even as his predecessors had done to him, and exalted him in the sight of all his friends,
Ekegusii: omorwoti akamokorera Yonathani buna abarwoti bande abatang’ani konye bamokoreire. Ere akamoa esiko ase obosio bwa abaseemia baye bonsi,

English: and confirmed to him the high priesthood, and all the other honors that he had before, and gave him preeminence among his chief friends.
Ekegusii: na komotenenia buna Omokuani Omonene ase ekerogo kiaye keria abwate agwo omochakano, akamoimokereria igoro kegima ase omobaro bwa “Abasani bo Omorwoti.”

English: And Jonathan requested of the king that he would make Judea free from tribute, along with the three provinces and the country of Samaria, and promised him three hundred talents.
Ekegusii: Erio Yonathani akamosaba omorwoti atugute okorwa ebango ase abanto ba Yudea n’echinsemo chiaye isato chia Samaria. Yonathani akamoriera eira yokomoa omosomogooko oyomo bwe ekerengo gie chitaabu chikiro 10,000 ekero abaruseirie ebango eyio.

English: The king consented, and wrote letters to Jonathan concerning all these things as follows:
Ekegusii: Omorwoti agaitaba na komoriikera Yonathani riruube riogoikerania eira eyio buna ekobwatia:

English: “King Demetrius to his brother Jonathan, and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti Demeturio, ase omomura omwabo Yonathani na momura omwabo amo na abanto bonsi be egesaku kia Abayahudi: Amaiga ayio!

English: The copy of the letter which we wrote to Lasthenes our kinsman concerning you, we have written also to you, that you may see it.
Ekegusii: Aiga inche nigo nkobwatania ase amang’ana aao na ensemo yeriruube namoriikerete oyominto Lasithene igoro yao.

English: ‘King Demetrius to Lasthenes his father, greetings.
Ekegusii: Omorwoti Demeturio ase omosike oyominto Lasithene: Amaiga ayio!

English: We have determined to do good to the nation of the Jews, who are our friends, and observe what is just toward us, because of their good will toward us.
Ekegusii: Inche naetirie gokea egesaku kia Abayahudi okwaberwa kwa amang’ana gete ase engencho barabwo nabasaani baito abeegenwa naende nigo babwatete buya ensemo yabo yamachiiko yokobwatana gwaito kwomorembe.

English: We have confirmed therefore to them the borders of Judea, and also the three governments of Aphaerema, Lydda, and Ramathaim (these were added to Judea from the country of Samaria), and all their territory to them, for all who do sacrifice in Jerusalem, instead of the king’s dues which the king received of them yearly before from the produce of the earth and the fruits of trees.
Ekegusii: Inche nancheranire buna egesaku kia Abayahudi nkere noboronge ase ense ya Yudea ne chinsemo chiaye isato chia Afairema, Luda na Rathamini eyio bono ekong’anyigwa korwa Samaria gochia Yuda ero amo ne endemero yonsi etungetie chingingo echio. Bonsi abwo barabe bakorwa ebing’wanso biabo ase omochie o Yerusalemu tibakoba bakomoruera omorwoti ebaango eyio omorwoti erenge kobarusia ase kera omwaka agwo omochakano korwa ase rigesa riechinyeke na amatunda: ebango eyio bono nigo eraabe kegokoonya emeroberio ye Hekalu.

English: As for the other payments to us from henceforth, of the tithes and the taxes that pertain to us, and the salt pits, and the crown taxes due to us, all these we will give back to them.
Ekegusii: Boigo inche inkobaruseria nde ogoakana gwonsi koria nkobatura ase ensemo ya ikomi, ebango na amaakano ande yengeencho.

English: Not one of these grants shall be annulled from this time forth and forever.
Ekegusii: Ebingese bionsi bie riruube eri nigo birabeo bitari koonchorerigwa kare na kare.

English: Now therefore be careful to make a copy of these things, and let it be given to Jonathan, and let it be set up on the holy mountain in a suitable and conspicuous place.’”
Ekegusii: “Bono rora buna riruube eri riariikirwe buya ase obwegenwa na egesamunye ekio kiabekirwe ase amaboko a Yonathani, erio kebeekwe ase agwenerete igoro ase egetunwa gie Hekalu, ase kerarorekane maiso marore ase abanto bonsi.”

English: When King Demetrius saw that the land was quiet before him, and that no resistance was made to him, he sent away all his troops, each man to his own place, except the foreign troops, which he had raised from the islands of the Gentiles. So all the troops of his fathers hated him.
Ekegusii: Ekero omorwoti Demeturio aroche buna ense yategereire inse yoborwoti bwaye, na buna ere tabwati naende abanto bakorwana nere, akabuna ebiombe bia abarwani be esegi bionsi na kobairania gochia inka abasikari baye bonsi otatiga baria akomboete korwa ase ebisinga bia Bogiriki. Ogokora okwo gokabagechia abasikari bonsi abwo bariikire na abarwoti abwo bamotang’anerete Demeturio, na ase engencho bono batarenge nenchera yokwenyorera eng’eria barabwo bakamogecha omorwoti.

English: Now Tryphon was one of those who previously had been on Alexander’s side, and he saw that all the forces murmured against Demetrius. So he went to Imalcue the Arabian, who was raising up Antiochus the young child of Alexander,
Ekegusii: Turifo oyio agwo ritang’ani orenge ase omorwoti Alekisanda, ekero arooche abasikari bonsi bakwemurungania ase engencho ya Demeturio, akamochira Imalikue omwarabu oyio omorerete na komorenda Antioko mosinto bwa Alekisanda.

English: and urgently insisted to him that he should deliver him to him, that he might reign in his father’s place. He told him all that Demetrius had done, and the hatred with which his forces hated him; and he stayed there many days.
Ekegusii: Turifo aba agwo ase ebiro ebitambe ase okomosorora Imalikue amotigere omwana oyio omoke bwa Alekisanda erio ere amokore koba omorwoti ase ribaga ria ise. Boigo er akamomanyia Imalikue kwobwatekana na amakora a Demeturio, na buna abasikari bamogechete.

English: Now Jonathan sent to King Demetrius, that he should remove the troops of the citadel from Jerusalem, and the troops who were in the strongholds; for they fought against Israel continually.
Ekegusii: Ase chingaki echi Yonathani akamotomera amang’ana omorwoti Demeturio komosaba arusie ebiombe bia abasikari baye korwa ime ase eburi ya Yerusalemu amao nebichi binde bia Yudea ekiagera barabwo barenge kobachaanda Abayahudi.

English: Demetrius sent to Jonathan, saying, “I will not only do this for you and your nation, but I will greatly honor you and your nation, if I find an opportunity.
Ekegusii: Demeturio akairaneria: “Inche ninkore okogania kwao, na ekero ebiro biraabe ebiya, inche ninkoe esiko enene kegima.

English: Now therefore you shall do well if you send me men who will fight for me; for all my forces have revolted.”
Ekegusii: Korende bono nigo ngokoboria ondetere abasikari baranwanerere ekiagera abaane bonsi banyangire.”

English: So Jonathan sent him three thousand valiant men to Antioch. They came to the king, and the king was glad at their coming.
Ekegusii: Erio Yonathani akaira abasikari ebiata 3,000 goika Antiokia. Omorwoti akagooka mono ekero barabwo baigete,

English: The people of the city gathered themselves together into the midst of the city, to the number of one hundred and twenty thousand men, and they wanted to kill the king.
Ekegusii: ekiagera konye omsangererekano bwa abanto 120,000 babwatanire bamoite omorwoti.

English: The king fled into the court of the palace, and the people of the city seized the main streets of the city and began to fight.
Ekegusii: Erio omorwoti agatama korwa ase enyomba yoborwoti, ekero abanto babwatete chinchera chi’omochie na gochaaka chiburuburu.

English: The king called the Jews to help him, and they were gathered together to him all at once, and they dispersed themselves in the city, and killed that day about one hundred thousand.
Ekegusii: Agwo omorwoti akarangeria abarwani esegi ba Boyahudi bamokoonye na barabwo bagaikerana bwango bagoeta omochie ase omochie na kobaita abanto goika ekerengo gie chilifu rigana erimo (100,000).

English: They set the city on fire, and seized many spoils that day, and saved the king.
Ekegusii: Barabwo bakamotooria omorwoti korende bakoyosakora koyobeka omochie oyio omorero.

English: The people of the city saw that the Jews had taken control of the city as they pleased, and they became faint in their hearts, and they cried out to the king with supplication, saying,
Ekegusii: Ekero abanto barooche buna Abayahudi bayogomirie omochie kegima, bagakwa omoyo erio bakamochiera omorwoti na komosorora bagoteeba:

English: “Give us your right hand, and let the Jews cease from fighting against us and the city.”
Ekegusii: “Koranche otoe intwe omorembe na otenenie ogoita kwa Abayahudi ase tore na omochie oito.”

English: They threw away their weapons and made peace. The Jews were glorified in the sight of the king, and before all who were in his kingdom. Then they returned to Jerusalem, having much plunder.
Ekegusii: Abaengereria abwo bakabeeka ebirwanero inse na koimokereria amaboko abo igoro. Omorwoti na abanto bare inse yaye bagatwara amasikani amanene ase Abayahudi. Erio Abayahudi bakairana gochia Yerusalemu bating’ete obonge bwa abooswa.

English: So King Demetrius sat on the throne of his kingdom, and the land was quiet before him.
Ekegusii: Ekero omorwoti Demeturio aboigete naende ase oborwoti bwaye, na boigo ense yonsi egatwara omorembe,

English: He lied in all that he spoke, and estranged himself from Jonathan, and didn’t repay him according to the benefits with which he had repaid him, and treated him very harshly.
Ekegusii: akabuna chiira chiaye chionsi na konacha oboamate bwaye na Yonathani; ribaga riokomoa esiko buna yagwenerete koba, ere na komororeria bobe kegima.

English: Now after this, Tryphon returned, and with him the young child Antiochus, who reigned and put on a crown.
Ekegusii: Magega yebiro ebike, Turifo akairana amo nomwana oria Antioko, akamobekera ekegowa na komobeeka ase ekerogo kioborwoti.

English: All the forces which Demetrius had sent away with disgrace were gathered to him, and they fought against him, and he fled and was routed.
Ekegusii: Abasikari baria bonsi batigetigwe emeremo bakamobwatesia omorwoti omoyia. Bakamorwania Demeturio esegi na komobua erio ere agatama.

English: Tryphon took the elephants, and took control of Antioch.
Ekegusii: Turifo agachiira chinchogu chi’eseegi na koyoira omochie bwa Antiokia.

English: The young Antiochus wrote to Jonathan, saying, “I confirm to you the high priesthood, and appoint you over the four districts, and to be one of the king’s friends.”
Ekegusii: Omorwoti omosae Antioko akamoriikera Yonathani na komwanchera ase ekerogo kiaye ki’Omokuani omonene na ekio obonene bwe chingongo chiria inye, akamochoora koba “Omosaani bw’Omorwoti”.

English: He sent to him golden vessels and furniture for the table, and gave him permission to drink in golden vessels, and to be clothed in purple, and to have a golden buckle.
Ekegusii: Akamotomera ebibekerero bitaabu biogokorera emeremo ase emesa, akamoa ribaga riokonywera ebikobe bi’etaabu, kweboyia chianga chi’oborwoti na kobeeka omootoro bw’etaabu.

English: He made his brother Simon governor from the Ladder of Tyre to the borders of Egypt.
Ekegusii: Boigo akamochoora Simioni momura omwabo Yonathani koba omogabana bwenseemo yonsi korwa egetunwa gia Turo goika chimbeebe chia Misiri.

English: Jonathan went out and took his journey beyond the river and through the cities. All the forces of Syria gathered themselves to him to be his allies. He came to Ascalon, and the people of the city met him honorably.
Ekegusii: Erio Yonathani agaeta gati yemechie emenene ya Siria, abarwani be esegi bonsi ba siria bakabwatana nere. Ekero aigete Asikeloni, abamenyi b’omochie oyio bakamoarigania na komoa esiko enene.

English: He departed from there to Gaza, and the people of Gaza shut him out. So he besieged it and burned its pasture lands with fire, and plundered them.
Ekegusii: Akarwa agwo, akageenda Gaza korende abamenyi ba aroro agwo bagasieka, ebiita biabo na komosiekera isiko. Erio Yonathani akayogitera omochie oyio akayobeeka omorero na koira emechie yarenge ase chinsinyo chiaye.

English: The people of Gaza pleaded with Jonathan, and he gave them his right hand, and took the sons of their princes for hostages, and sent them away to Jerusalem. Then he passed through the country as far as Damascus.
Ekegusii: Erio abanto ba Gaza bakamosaba omorembe, nere akaroisia omoroberio bw’omorembe. Ere ekababogoria abana bonsi ba abarai na kobaira Yerusalemu erio barabwo bae abooswa.

English: Then Jonathan heard that Demetrius’ princes had come to Kedesh, which is in Galilee, with a great army, intending to remove him from his office.
Ekegusii: Yonathani akaigwa buna abanene ba Demeturio konye baikire Kadeshi, Galili, amo na abarwani be esegi abange mono erio bamorusie Yonathani ase obonene bwaye.

English: He went to meet them, but he left Simon his brother in the country.
Ekegusii: Ere akamotiga momura omwabo Simioni ase ense ya Yudea na kogenda korwana na abarwani be esegi ba Demeturio.

English: Simon encamped against Bethsura, and fought against it many days, and hemmed it in.
Ekegusii: Simioni akayonaaria omochie o Beth-zuri na koyorwania esegi ase ebiro ebitambe.

English: They asked him to give them his right hand, and he gave it to them. He removed them from there, took possession of the city, and set a garrison over it.
Ekegusii: Erio abamenyi ba aroro bagasaba amachiiko yomorembe, nere Simioni agaitaba. Ere akayoira omochie oyio, akabaseria abanyene na kobeeka aroro ekeombe kiaye kia abasikari.

English: Jonathan and his army encamped at the water of Gennesareth, and early in the morning they marched to the plain of Hazor.
Ekegusii: Yonathani amo na abarwani be esegi baye bakabeka ekambi yaabo ase chingegu chi’enyama ya Genesareti. Mambia chuni botarakiamoka, akabaraa abarwani be esegi baye goika ense yomweya ya Hazori,

English: Behold, an army of foreigners met him in the plain. They laid an ambush for him in the mountains, but they themselves met him face to face.
Ekegusii: agwo ase ensemo enene ya abarwani be esegi ba isiko barenge gosuka gocha erio bamorwanie. Kani omobisa konye obisire ekeombe kende kia abarwani be esegi gekona konyenyeka ime yebitunwa, erio bakaumerana obosio ase obosio.

English: But those who lay in ambush rose out of their places and joined battle. All those who were on Jonathan’s side fled.
Ekegusii: Abasikari abwo bebeisete bagasoka na gochaaka korwana.

English: Not one of them was left, except Mattathias the son of Absalom, and Judas the son of Chalphi, captains of the forces.
Ekegusii: Abarwani be esegi ba Yonathani bakaonchoka gotama. Tatigara onde bwensi otataiga abanene babere: Matathia mosinto bwa Abisalomu na Yuda mosinto o Kalifi abateneneri be esegi.

English: Jonathan tore his clothes, put dirt on his head, and prayed.
Ekegusii: Yonathani agachweria chianga chiaye ase obororo, akeaka orotu rwa amaroba ase omotwe oye agasaba.

English: He turned again to them in battle, and routed them, and they fled.
Ekegusii: Ere akairana ase esegi na korwania ababisa goika bagatama.

English: When the men on his side who had fled saw this, they returned to him and pursued with him to Kedesh to their camp, and they encamped there.
Ekegusii: Ekero abasikari baye abwo konye batamire baroche ayio, bakairana na kobwatana nere kobamonyokia ababisa. Bakabamonyokia goika bakabasoyia ase ekambi yaabo ya Kadeshi, erio bakaira ekambi eyio.

English: About three thousand men of the foreigners fell on that day. Then Jonathan returned to Jerusalem.
Ekegusii: Abasikari ba ababisa abwo batari inse ya 3,000 bagaitwa ase rituko erio. Erio Yonathani akairana goika Yerusalemu.

English: Jonathan saw that the time was favorable for him, so he chose men and sent them to Rome to confirm and renew the friendship that they had with them.
Ekegusii: Ekero Yonathani arooche amang’ana abeire amaya asare, ere agachoora abatomwa erio bagende Rumi kobokia obwanchani na abanto ba Rumi.

English: He also sent similar letters to the Spartans, and to other places.
Ekegusii: Ere boigo agatoma amarube abwate amang’ana yokogania okwo goika Siparta ne chinsemo chinde.

English: They went to Rome, entered into the senate house, and said, “Jonathan the high priest and the nation of the Jews have sent us to renew for them the friendship and the alliance, as in former time.”
Ekegusii: Abatomwa abwo bakagenda Rumi agwo ase baariganetigwe negeikaranso ekenene kia abagaaka. Bagateeba: Ere Yonathani Omokuani omoneneamo na egesaku gionsi kia Abayahudi batotomire erio tonyaare kobokia oboamate boria bwaito bw’eritang’ani na Abaroma.

English: They gave them letters to the men in every place, that they should provide safe conduct for them on their way to the land of Judah.
Ekegusii: Abaroma bakabaa amarube yokobamanyekania ase kera omonene ba kera ense erio banyore ogwancherwa kwogoeta na koirana gochia sobo ase obuya.

English: This is the copy of the letters which Jonathan wrote to the Spartans:
Ekegusii: Eri nario riruube Yonathani abariikerete Abasiparta:

English: “Jonathan the high priest, and the senate of the nation, and the priests, and the rest of the people of the Jews, to their kindred the Spartans, greetings.
Ekegusii: “Omokuani omonene Yonathani, ase Egeikaranso Ekenene giense, abakuani bonsi, na abanto bonsi ba Yudea, ase abaminto ba Siparta: Amaiga ase more.

English: Even before this time letters were sent to Onias the high priest from Arius, who was reigning among you, to signify that you are our kindred, as the copy written below shows.
Ekegusii: Ase amatuko a magega, omorwoti oino erio namoriikerete Omokuani oito omonene Onia, komomanyia buna ebisaku ebi biaito mbire noboamate buna riruube eri rimanteranetigwe rikoorokia.

English: Onias welcomed honorably the man who was sent and received the letters, wherein declaration was made of alliance and friendship.
Ekegusii: Erio Onia akamoarigania omotomwa oria na amasikani amanene na koiraneria riruube riaino koraria maiso marore oboamate nobosaani bore gati yaito.

English: Therefore we also, even though we need none of these things, having for our encouragement the holy books which are in our hands,
Ekegusii: Nabo bono nonya titori noboamate buna obwo, ase engencho chinguru chiaito chikorwa ase amariiko amachenu ayio are ase amaboko aito,

English: have undertaken to send that we might renew our brotherhood and friendship with you, to the end that we should not become estranged from you altogether; for a long time has passed since you sent your letter to us.
Ekegusii: bono nigo tokobariikera ase okobokia oboamate bwaito bw’obosani na obomwabo tore nabwo amo nainwe. Titotageti gosaria oboamate bwaito; emiaka nemenge yaetire korwa twanyorete riruube riaino.

English: We therefore at all times without ceasing, both in our feasts, and on the other convenient days, remember you in the sacrifices which we offer, and in our prayers, as it is right and proper to be mindful of kindred.
Ekegusii: Intwe nigo tokobainyora kera engaki ekero tobwate ribaga: ase amatuko aito amanene na ayande agwenerete, ase chisadaka na amasabo aito, buna eganeirie abamwabo koinyorana.

English: Moreover, we are glad for your glory.
Ekegusii: Boigo nomogooko oito buna inwe mwenyoreire ogkiina.

English: But as for ourselves, many afflictions and many wars have encompassed us, and the kings who are around us have fought against us.
Ekegusii: Korende intwe twabeire togotwara obokong’u ne emechando boigo chiseegi kera engaki, ase engencho ebisaku bitoetanaine biabeire bigotorwania.

English: We were unwilling to be troublesome to you, and to the rest of our allies and friends, in these wars;
Ekegusii: Ase chingaki echio chi’eseegi intwe titwaganetie kobachaanda inwe gose abande ase abasani baito.

English: for we have the help which is from heaven to help us, and we have been delivered from our enemies, and our enemies have been humbled.
Ekegusii: Ekiagera obokonyi bwaito nigo bokorwa ase Omonene, ere oyionotobuereire ababisa baito na gototooria korwa ase chinchara chiabo.

English: We chose therefore Numenius the son of Antiochus and Antipater the son of Jason, and have sent them to the Romans, to renew the friendship that we had with them, and the former alliance.
Ekegusii: Nigo twabachorire Numenio mosinto bwa Antioko na Antipata mosinto o Yasoni, na kobatoma Rumi kogenda kobokia obosani na okobwatana gwaito na Abaroma.

English: We commanded them therefore to go also to you, and to salute you, and to deliver you our letters concerning the renewing of friendship and our brotherhood.
Ekegusii: Boigo twabatomire baike ase more na korenta amaiga aito boigo riruube eri rigokwanera okobokigwa kwoboamate bwaito bw’obomwabo.

English: And now you will do well if you give us a reply.”
Ekegusii: Intwe twasemeirie buna intonyoore amairanerio ase riruube eri.”

English: And this is the copy of the letters which they sent to Onias:
Ekegusii: Eri rikobwatia neriruube riaino ritang’ani gochia ase Onia:

English: “Arius king of the Spartans to Onias the chief priest, greetings.
Ekegusii: “Omorwoti Ario o Siparta ase Omokuani omonene Onia, amaiga ayio.

English: It has been found in writing, concerning the Spartans and the Jews, that they are kindred, and that they are of the descendants of Abraham.
Ekegusii: Nigo yarorekanire ase amariiko gete buna intwe Abasiparta amo nainwe Abayahudi ntobwate oboamate, naboigo buna ebisaku biaito bibere na ababiare ba Aburahamu.

English: Now, since this has come to our knowledge, you will do well to write to us of your prosperity.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho twamanyire ayio, twabasabire komoranche inwe motoe amang’ana aino.

English: We moreover write on our part to you, that your livestock and goods are ours, and ours are yours. We do command therefore that they make report to you accordingly.”
Ekegusii: Naintwe nigo tokobariikera kobamanyia buna intwe ntore ang’e gosanga nainwe chinibo chiaito amo ne chitugo chiaito ekero nainwe morakore boigo. Twabachiikire abatomwa baito babamanyie amange kobua ase amang’ana ayio.”

English: Now Jonathan heard that Demetrius’ princes had returned to fight against him with a greater army than before,
Ekegusii: Erio Yonathani akanyoora amang’ana buna abanene ba Demeturio konye bachire naende bare na abarwani esegi abange ase ogocha komorwania.

English: so he marched away from Jerusalem, and met them in the country of Hamath; for he gave them no opportunity to set foot in his country.
Ekegusii: Yonathani tatagete kobaa ribaga koyesoanana ense yaye. Ere akarwa Yerusalemu akageenda korwana na barabwo ase ensemo ya Hamathi.

English: He sent spies into his camp, and they came again, and reported to him that they were preparing to attack them at night.
Ekegusii: Agatoma chiroti ime ase ekambi yababisa, chirochio chikairana na komoteebia buna ababisa nigo babwate omoroberio bw’okobaachera Abayahudi ase obotuko.

English: But as soon as the sun was down, Jonathan commanded his men to watch, and to be armed, that all the night long they might be ready for battle. He stationed sentinels around the camp.
Ekegusii: Ekero erioba riagwa, Yonathani akabachiika abasikari baye bonsi kwebeeka ang’e, nebirwanero bire koboko, ase esegi ende yonsi eratuboke mosiabano ase obotuko. Boigo akabeeka abasikari barende chinsinyo chionsi chiekambi.

English: The adversaries heard that Jonathan and his men were ready for battle, and they feared, and trembled in their hearts, and they kindled fires in their camp then withdrew.
Ekegusii: Ekero ababisa baigwete buna Yonathani na abanto baye bebekire ang’e ase esegi, bagasogwa nobwoba obonene, bagatama na gotiga emerero kegwoka ime yekambi.

English: But Jonathan and his men didn’t know it until the morning; for they saw the fires burning.
Ekegusii: Yonathani amo na abanto baye bakarora emerero eyio ime yekambi korende barabwo tibamanya aria agendererete goika bogakia mambia.

English: Jonathan pursued after them, but didn’t overtake them; for they had gone over the river Eleutherus.
Ekegusii: Erio Yonathani agasoka kobwatia ababisa. Korende tanyara kobaikeera ekiagera baigete kwamboka orooche rwa Eleuthero.

English: Then Jonathan turned toward the Arabians, who are called Zabadaeans, and struck them, and took their spoils.
Ekegusii: Ekaba Yonathani agekiora akabwatia enchera ye ensemo na kobarwania Abazabadea, ekemo kiebisaku bia Abaarabu. Akababua na gosakora chinibo chiabo.

English: He came out from there, and came to Damascus, and took his journey through all the country.
Ekegusii: Erio akarwa agwo akageenda goika Damesiki, ase okwemanyia ensemo eyio yonsi.

English: Simon went out, and took his journey as far as Ascalon, and the strongholds that were near it. Then he turned toward Joppa and took possession of it;
Ekegusii: Simioni nere agasooka agaeta ase ense eria akagenda motwe goika Asikeloni ne chiburi chietanaineo. Naende agekiora akagenda Yopa, akayoira omochie oyio mosiabano,

English: for he had heard that they were planning to hand over the stronghold to Demetrius’ men. He set a garrison there to guard it.
Ekegusii: ekiagera aigwete buna abamenyi be ensemo eyio mbarenge ang’e kobatigera abasikari batometwe na Demeturio eburi ya Yopa. Simioni akabeeka ekeombe kia abasikari koyerenda eburi eyio.

English: Then Jonathan returned and called the elders of the people together. He planned with them to build strongholds in Judea,
Ekegusii: Ekero Yonathani airanete akarangeria egeikaranso kia abagaaka ba abanto koroberia gochia koagaacha emechie ase Yudea,

English: and to make the walls of Jerusalem higher, and to raise a great mound between the citadel and the city, to separate it from the city, that so it might be isolated, that its garrison might neither buy nor sell.
Ekegusii: komenta obotambe bwechinyasi chia Yerusalemu na koagaacha enyasi entambe gati yeburi nomochie, erio gwatanana eburi eyio erio ababisa tibanyaara koonia gose kogora kende gionsi.

English: They were gathered together to build the city. Part of the wall of the brook that is on the east side had fallen down, and he repaired the section called Chaphenatha.
Ekegusii: Abanto bagakora emeremo amo ase ogokong’ia enyasi yomochie, ase engencho ensemo yenyasi ya moocha konye yagure; akayeriosia boigo ensemo yarenge korokwa Kefenatha.

English: Simon also built Adida in the plain country, made it strong, and set up gates and bars.
Ekegusii: Simioni nere akaywagaacha boyia omochie bwa Adida ase eraaro ya Shefela, akayokong’ia na koyobeekera ebisieri nechiboriti.

English: And Tryphon sought to reign over Asia and to crown himself, and to stretch out his hand against Antiochus the king.
Ekegusii: Magega yayio, turifo akaroisia chinchera chi’okomiyeria Antioko erio ere abe omorwoti o Asia.

English: He was afraid that Jonathan wouldn’t allow him, and that he would fight against him; and he sought a way to seize him, that he might destroy him. So he marched out and came to Bethshan.
Ekegusii: Nonye nabo, akoboa buna Yonathani tarenge gochia gwancherana nere kobwatekana nomoroberio oyio, boigo buna ere nabo arenge gochaakia esegi erio gotanga ring’ana erio. Igo Turifo akaba okomorigia amobwate na komoita; erio ere agasoka akagenda Beth-sheani.

English: Jonathan came out to meet him with forty thousand men chosen for battle, and came to Bethshan.
Ekegusii: Korende Yonathani agasoka na kogenda komorwania agwo Beth-sheani ore na absikari bachooretwe 40,000.

English: Tryphon saw that he came with a great army, and he was afraid to stretch out his hand against him.
Ekegusii: Ekero Turifo arooche obonge bwa abarwani esegi ba Yonathani, akoboa gchaaka obochege.

English: He received him honorably, and commended him to all his friends, and gave him gifts, and commanded his forces to be obedient to him, as to himself.
Ekegusii: Erio akamoarigania Yonathani ase amasikani onsi, akamomanyekania ase abaseemia baye bonsi, akamoa ebiegwa na kobachiika abaseemia baye na abasikari baye bamoigwere Yonathani buna barabwo barenge komoigwera ere omonyene.

English: He said to Jonathan, “Why have you put all these people to so much trouble, seeing there is no war between us?
Ekegusii: Erio akamobooria Yonathani: “Ninki gekogera kwabachaandete abasikari aba abange iga naye nomanyete buna intwe titobwati esegi ase egati yaito?

English: Now send them away to their homes, but choose for yourself a few men who shall be with you, and come with me to Ptolemais, and I will give it to you, and the rest of the strongholds and the rest of the forces, and all the king’s officers. Then I will turn around and depart; for this is why I came.”
Ekegusii: Ninki keragere aye tobairania gochia inka? Aye chora abanto bake batigare amo naye erio aye onkobe inche gochia Tolemai. Ekero ndakoe omochie oyio o Tolemai, amo nechiburi chinde, na abasikari, na abanene baabo bonsi. Erio inche ningende inka k’obwane. Ekio nakio kiandetete aiga.”

English: He put his trust in him, and did even as he said, and sent away his forces, and they departed into the land of Judah.
Ekegusii: Yonathani akamwegena. Erio ere akabatoma gochia inka abarwani baye be esegi gochia Yudea.

English: But he reserved to himself three thousand men, of whom he left two thousand in Galilee, but one thousand went with him.
Ekegusii: Agetigareria abanto 3,000; 2,000 akabatiga agwo Galili na 1,000 boka bagatigara nere.

English: Now as soon as Jonathan entered into Ptolemais, the people of Ptolemais shut the gates and seized him. They killed all those who came in with him with the sword.
Ekegusii: Korende buna Yonathani achia gosoa Tolemai, abamenyi ba aroro bagasieka ebiita bi’omochie bakamobwata ere na goita bonsi baria atigarete nabarabwo.

English: Tryphon sent troops and cavalry into Galilee, and into the Great Plain, to destroy all Jonathan’s men.
Ekegusii: Erio Turifo akaimokia ebiombe bia abasikari baye bagochiera amagoro na baria bakoriina chibarasi goika Galili na ase rikura ria Yesireeli gochia kobaita abasikari baria ba Yonathani batigarete.

English: They perceived that he had been seized and had perished, along with those who were with him. They encouraged one another and went on their way close together, prepared to fight.
Ekegusii: Ase amanyinga abo, abasikari baria ba Yonathani bakamanya buna Yonathani amo na abasikari abwo atigarete nabwo babwatirwe na goitwa. Bakabeekana chinguru na kweroberia ase esegi.

English: Those who followed them saw that they were ready to fight for their lives, and turned back again.
Ekegusii: Ekero abarwani aasikari ba Yonathani berobeirie gokora esegi ase okoranerera obogima bwabo, bakairana magega.

English: They all came in peace into the land of Judah, and they mourned for Jonathan and those who were with him, and they were very afraid. All Israel mourned with a great mourning.
Ekegusii: Erio abasikari baria Abayahudi bakairana Yudea bare buya, korende bare nobwoba. Egesaku ekegima gekarusia egekuuro ekenene giokomoreera Yonathani amo na ababwatani baye.

English: And all the Gentiles who were around them sought to destroy them utterly; for they said, “They have no ruler nor anyone to help them. Now therefore let’s fight against them, and take away their memory from among men.”
Ekegusii: Naboigo ebesaku biabebekaine bono bigachaaka goteema kobasiria Abayahudi. Barabwo nigo bakagete buna Abayahudi tibari na morai onde gose omokoonyi oye naende. Bagateeba: “Bono tiga inwe tobaite na gosiria okoinyorwa kwabo korwa ase oboiko bw’ense.”

English: Simon heard that Tryphon had gathered together a mighty army to come into the land of Judah and destroy it utterly.
Ekegusii: Simioni akaigwa buna Turifo konye osangereirie riicho rinene riabarwani esegi, erio koyerwania ense ya Yudea na koyesiria.

English: He saw that the people were trembling in great fear. So he went up to Jerusalem and gathered the people together.
Ekegusii: Akarora boigo buna abanto batengechiigwe nobwoba. Erio akageenda Yerusalemu akarangeria egeikaranso,

English: He encouraged them, and said to them, “You yourselves know all the things that I, my kindred, and my father’s house have done for the laws and the sanctuary, and the battles and the distresses which we have seen.
Ekegusii: na goteema kobaremia abanto, ogoteeba: “Inwe imomanyete amang’ana amanene inche amo na momura ominto neamate yonsi ya tata twakorire ase engencho ya amachiiko na Hekalu. Boigo, imomanyete igoro ye esegi eyio twakorire na buna twachaandegete.

English: Because of this, all my brothers have perished for Israel’s sake, and I am left alone.
Ekegusii: Bamura baminto bonsi baitirwe ase okorwanerera amachiiko, Hekalu negesaku kia Abaisraeli; niche bweka ntigarete.

English: Now be it far from me, that I should spare my own life in any time of affliction, for I am not better than my kindred.
Ekegusii: Na bono tindi gochia korigia korwanerera obogima bwane ase chingaki chinde chionsi chi’obokong’u, ase engencho inche tinyeroochi koba omuya kobua abamura abwo baminto.

English: However, I will take vengeance for my nation, for the sanctuary, and for our wives and children, because all the Gentiles have gathered out of hatred to destroy us.”
Ekegusii: Inche ning’akane egesiomba ase engencho yegesaku kiane, Hekalu, abakungu na abana baino ekiagera ebisaku bionsi biasangererekanire amo ase obobisa erio bitosirie.”

English: The spirit of the people revived as soon as they heard these words.
Ekegusii: Amang’ana ayio akabaremia abanto kegima,

English: They answered with a loud voice, saying, “You are our leader in the place of Judas and Jonathan your brothers.
Ekegusii: nabarabwo bakairaneria ase eriogi rinene: “Aye naye bono omorai oito ase ribaga ria momura omino Yuda na Yonathani.

English: Fight our battles, and we will do all that you tell us to do.”
Ekegusii: Gendereria esegi yaito, naintwe ng’a tokore kende gionsi keria aye oratoteebie.”

English: He gathered together all the men of war, and hurried to finish the walls of Jerusalem. He fortified it all around.
Ekegusii: Erio Simioni akabasangereria abasikari bonsi agakora bwango gokora chinyasi chia Yerusalemu na gokong’ia oborendi bwaye.

English: He sent Jonathan the son of Absalom, and with him a great army, to Joppa. He threw out those who were in it, and lived there.
Ekegusii: Akamotoma Yonathani mosinto bwa Abisalomu kogenda Yopa, ere amo nabarwani esegi abange. Yonathani akabaseria abanto barenge Yopa akayoira omochie oyio.

English: Tryphon left Ptolemais with a mighty army to enter into the land of Judah, and Jonathan was with him under guard.
Ekegusii: Turifo akaimokia abarwani esegi abange akagenda gosagaana Yudea. Ere nigo amoimogetie Yonathani, momura omwabo Simioni buna omosibwa.

English: But Simon encamped at Adida, near the plain.
Ekegusii: Simioni nigo abagete ekambi yaye agwo Adida ase arochie omweya.

English: Tryphon knew that Simon had risen up in the place of his brother Jonathan, and meant to join battle with him, so he sent ambassadors to him, saying,
Ekegusii: Ekero Turifo aigwete buna Simioni obogoirie oborai ase ribaga ria momura omwabo Yonathani, na buna bwebekire ang’e korwana esegi amo nere, akamotomera amang’ana abwatetie:

English: “It is for money which Jonathan your brother owed to the king’s treasury, by reason of the offices which he had, that we are detaining him.
Ekegusii: Nigo imobeegete momura omino inse yoborendi ekiagera ere taakanete amadeni ase ekegancha kiomorwoti ase chingaki chioborai bwaye.

English: Now send one hundred talents of silver and two of his sons for hostages, so that when he is released he may not revolt against us, and we will release him.”
Ekegusii: Bono intomere chitaabu chikiro 3,000 na abana baye babere babe abooswa erio intwe tokomoigorera ere tabaisa gotioyeria. Agwo intwe ng’a tomoigorere.

English: Simon knew that they spoke to him deceitfully, but he sent to get the money and the children, lest perhaps he would arouse great hostility among the people,
Ekegusii: Ekiagera ere atatagete korenta obobisa ase egati ya Abayahudi, nonya omanyete buna nigo bakomong’aina, agachiika arenterwe chibeesa echio na abana babere ba Yonathani,

English: who might say, “Because I didn’t send him the money and the children, he perished.”
Ekegusii: erio magega yaye tibacha goteeba buna: “Onye ndiria Simioni amoete chifeta na abana baria baye babere anga Yonathani tarenge goitwa.”

English: So he sent the children and the hundred talents, but Tryphon lied, and didn’t release Jonathan.
Ekegusii: Erio Simioni agakora buna Turifo aboretie korende Turifo akabuna chiira chiaye na kogenderera komosiba Yonathani.

English: After this, Tryphon came to invade the land and destroy it, and he went around by the way that leads to Adora. Simon and his army marched near him to every place, wherever he went.
Ekegusii: Naende Turifo akagenda motwe ase ogosagaana na koyesamba ense ya Yudea akayeetanana Yudea yonsi goetera enchera ekogenda Adora. Korende Simioni na abarwani esegi baye bakaba bakomotunyana kera ase ere arenge kogenda.

English: Now the people of the citadel sent to Tryphon ambassadors, urging him to come to them through the wilderness, and to send them food.
Ekegusii: Ase ebiro ebio bionsi, Abasikari baria ababisa bareenge ime ye eburi ya Yerusalemu bakaba bakobatoma abatomwa baabo komomanyia Turifo achiche bwango ase ogoetera enchera yerooro erio abarentere endaagera.

English: So Tryphon prepared all his cavalry to come, but on that night a very heavy snow fell, and he didn’t come because of the snow. He marched off and went into the land of Gilead.
Ekegusii: Turifo akabaarigania abariini chibaarasi baye bonsi ase engencho yorogendo, korende ase obotuko obwo obokendu bokaba obonge mono goika agasinywa koriina egetunwa. Ere agatenenia orogendo orwo, akagenda bwoye Gileadi.

English: When he came near to Bascama, he killed Jonathan, and he was buried there.
Ekegusii: Ekero aigete ang’e na Basikama, agachiika Yonathani aitwe; Yonathani agatindekwa aroro agwo.

English: Then Tryphon turned back, and went away into his own land.
Ekegusii: Erio Turifo akairana gochia bwoye.

English: Simon sent, and took the bones of Jonathan his brother, and buried him at Modin, the city of his fathers.
Ekegusii: Simioni akabatoma abanto bagende koywoyia omobere o Yonathani ere akamotindeka momura omwabo agwo Modeini omochie bw’echisokoro chiaye.

English: All Israel made great lamentation over him, and mourned for him many days.
Ekegusii: Kera oyomo ase Abaisraeli bonsi akamoreera ase obororo obonene na komokumeria ase amatuko amange.

English: Simon built a monument on the tomb of his father and his kindred, and raised it high so that it could be seen, with polished stone on the front and back.
Ekegusii: Simioni akaagacha omorobiri bwokoinyoria igoro ase chimbeera chia ise na abamura bamwabo. Omorobiri oyio ogatubwa bosio na magega ne rigena riasenirie buya na nigo orenge kororekana korwa are.

English: He also set up seven pyramids, one near another, for his father, his mother, and his four brothers.
Ekegusii: Boigo akaagacha Emerobiri etano na ebere ase engencho ya ise, na ng’ina na abamura bamwabo bane.

English: For these, he made an elaborate setting, erecting great pillars around them, and upon the pillars he made suits of armor for a perpetual memorial, and beside the suits of armor, he carved ships, so that they could be seen by all who sail on the sea.
Ekegusii: Akaagacha chitinga chiogotenenia emetobwa emetambe emetambe mbarabare ye Emerobiri eyio. Na igoro ye emetobwa eyio akabeeka ebirwanero biechingeencho ao ao, erio bibe ebimanyererio bitasire kare na kare. Mbarabare yebirwanero ebio, akabeeka chimeli chikobaachwa. Abanto bonsi barenge goeta ase enyaancha nabo barenge korora ebimanyererio ebio.

English: This is the tomb which he made at Modin. It remains to this day.
Ekegusii: Embeera eyio Simioni aagachete agwo Modeini nao ere nonya ngoika reero.

English: Now Tryphon deceived the young King Antiochus and killed him,
Ekegusii: Turifo akamokorera bobe omorwoti oria omosae Antioko o gata’narimo, akamoita,

English: and reigned in his place. He put on himself the crown of Asia and brought a great calamity upon the land.
Ekegusii: na kogamba ase ribaga riaye igo akaba omorwoti o Asia. Omorwoti Turifo akarenta obokong’u obonene aroro agwo.

English: Simon built up the strongholds of Judea, and walled them all around with high towers, great walls, gates, and bars; and he stored food in the strongholds.
Ekegusii: Simioni agachiagaacha boyia chiburi chia Yudea agachionchokaneria chinyasi chinkong’u chire ne emetobwa emetambe, ebisieri ne chiboriti. Boigo akabeeka emonga yendagera ime yeburi.

English: Simon chose men, and sent to King Demetrius with a request that he grant the country an immunity, because all that Tryphon did was to plunder.
Ekegusii: Akabatoma abatomwa ase omorwoti Demeturio o kabere gosaba ense yaye yaberwe terwa ebaango ase engencho Turifo agendererete kobanyunyunta amanyinga.

English: King Demetrius sent to him according to these words, and answered him, and wrote a letter to him, as follows:
Ekegusii: Demeturio akairaneria ase riruube rikobwatia:

English: “King Demetrius to Simon the high priest and friend of kings, and to the elders and nation of the Jews, greetings.
Ekegusii: “Omorwoti Demeturio ase Omokuani omonene Simioni, omosaani bw’omorwoti, ase egesaku kia Abayahudi na abarai baye: Amaiga ayio!

English: The golden crown and the palm branch, which you sent, we have received. We are ready to make a steadfast peace with you, yes, and to write to our officers to release you from tribute.
Ekegusii: Nanyorire egutwa yetaabu nerito riemokendo mwantomera, nainche nigo nde ang’e kegima gokora nainwe okobwatana kwomorembe na kobateebia abariiki baito be ebaango babaabere inwe timorwa ebaango.

English: Whatever things we confirmed to you, they are confirmed. The strongholds, which you have built, let them be your own.
Ekegusii: Ebiteebanio biaito bi’eritang’ani biancheranirwe na chiburi mweagacheire ng’a chibe enibo yaino.

English: As for any oversights and faults committed to this day, we forgive them, and the crown tax which you owed us. If there were any other tax collected in Jerusalem, let it be collected no longer.
Ekegusii: Nababeire amamocho yogotamboka okobwatana gwakoregete goika etariki ya reero, na inche nababeire ogoakana mogosabwa okwo gotigarete kwe ebaango yengeencho nechibaango chinde chionsi echio chiabeire chigosangererigwa agwo Yerusalemu goika reero.

English: If any among you are qualified to be enrolled in our court, let them be enrolled, and let there be peace between us.”
Ekegusii: Abayahudi bonsi bare ne chimbwa chiganeirie ase obokoreri ase enyomba yomorwoti nabo bakoriikwa. Tiga obeo omorembe ase egati yaito.”

English: In the one hundred seventieth year, the yoke of the Gentiles was taken away from Israel.
Ekegusii: Ase omwaka o 170, chingatare chi’okobatindachera inse abanto be ebisaku binde chikarusigwa ase Abayahudi.

English: The people began to write in their instruments and contracts, “In the first year of Simon, the great high priest and captain and leader of the Jews.”
Ekegusii: Abanto bagachaaka koriika amang’ana nokobwatana kwabo ase amang’ana akobwatia: “Ase omwaka o Simioni bw’eritang’ani, Omokuani omonene, omochiki bw’eseegi na omorai bwa Abayahudi.”

English: In those days Simon encamped against Gazara, and surrounded it with troops. He made a siege engine, and brought it up to the city, and struck a tower, and captured it.
Ekegusii: Ase amatuko ayio, Simioni akabeeka ekambi eragete Gazara, akayoetanana omochie na abarwani baye be esegi. Akaroisia etinga yeseegi, agasukia orobebe goika chinyasi chi’omochie. Erio akayesagaana eyemo ye chiburi chiaye na koyeira.

English: Those who were in the engine leaped out into the city; and there was a great uproar in the city.
Ekegusii: Abanto barenge ase etinga eria yeseegi bagacharoka na gosoa ime yomochie na ogokururana okonene gokaba ime ya Gazara.

English: The people of the city tore their clothes, and went up on the walls with their wives and children, and cried with a loud voice, asking Simon to give them his right hand.
Ekegusii: Abasacha, abakungu baabo, abana baabo bagatandora chianga chiabo na koriina ase chinyasi chi’omochie. Ase eriogi rinene bakamosorora Simioni achiike omorembe obe,

English: They said, “Don’t deal with us according to our wickednesses, but according to your mercy.”
Ekegusii: bagoteeba: “Otwabere gaki, totokorera buna etogwenerete intwe!”

English: So Simon was reconciled to them, and didn’t fight against them; but he expelled them from the city and cleansed the houses where the idols were, and then entered into it with singing and giving praise.
Ekegusii: Ere Simioni agaitaberana nabarabwo na gochiika esegi etenene. Korende ere akabarusia abamenyi bonsi korwa ime yomochie erio agachichena chinyomba chiabo echio chiabwate emegwekano yogosasiima chinyasae. Simioni na abanto baye bagasoa aroro bagoteera chingero na amateera yogotogia.

English: He removed all uncleanness out of it, and placed in it men who would keep the law, and made it stronger than it was before, and built a dwelling place for himself in it.
Ekegusii: Agasokia kende gionsi kiarenge korenta ogotacheneka ase omochie na kobanchera komenya ime ase omochie oyio abanto baria barenge kobwatia amachiiko boka.

English: But the people of the citadel in Jerusalem were hindered from going out and from going into the country, and from buying and selling. So they were very hungry, and a great number of them perished from famine.
Ekegusii: Abanto barenge ase eburi ya Yerusalemu bono nigo barenge batangire kogenda koonia gose kogora kende gionsi. Enchara enene ekababwata na abange bagakwa ase enchara.

English: Then they cried out to Simon, that he should give them his right hand; and he gave it to them; but he expelled them from there, and he cleansed the citadel from its pollutions.
Ekegusii: Erio bakamosaba Simioni anchere omorembe. Simioni agancherana, akabarusia ime yeburi eyio na koyechena.

English: He entered into it on the twenty-third day of the second month, in the one hundred seventy-first year, with praise and palm branches, with harps, with cymbals, and with stringed instruments, with hymns, and with songs, because a great enemy had been destroyed out of Israel.
Ekegusii: Ase rituko riemerongo ebere nagatato na ase omotienyi o kabere omwaka bwe rigana erimo na merongo eta’nebere noyomo (171), okaba omoyega omonene bwokoiraneria mbuya mono ase omochie o Yerusalemu ekiagera okwoboyia gwokoondokia kwaruusetigwe aroro. Simioni na abanto baye bagasoa ime yeburi eria bakobugia ebinubi, ebita na amakano boigo chitebe bagoteera chingeero chi’ogotogia na koiraneria mbuya mono barabwo babogoretie amato yemekendo.

English: Simon ordained that they should keep that day every year with gladness. He made the hill of the temple that was by the citadel stronger than before, and he lived there with his men.
Ekegusii: Erio Simioni agachiika buna rituko erio ribe rigochengerwa kera omwaka. Agakong’ia oborendi bw’egetunwa na Hekalu, ensemo erigereranetie neburi, akayoroisia omochie o Yerusalemu oboikaro bwaye ere amo na abanto baye.

English: Simon saw that his son John was a man, so he made him leader of all his forces; and he lived in Gazara.
Ekegusii: Yohana omomura oye bono konye obeire omonto omonene. Erio Simioni akamokora koba Omochiki bw’eseegi ase abarwani esegi baye bonsi, nere Yohana agaetia koba ime yomochie o Gazara.

English: In the one hundred seventy-second year, King Demetrius gathered his forces together, and went into Media to get help, that he might fight against Tryphon.
Ekegusii: Omwaka o 172, omorwoti Demeturio o Kabere agasangereria abarwani baye be esegi na kogenda Media gosaba obokoonyi bonde erio agende korwania Turifo esegi.

English: When Arsaces, the king of Persia and Media, heard that Demetrius had come into his borders, he sent one of his princes to take him alive.
Ekegusii: Ekero Arisake o Gata’narimo, omorwoti o Persia na Media aigwete buna Demeturio osaaganire ense yaye akamotoma oyomo bwabachiiki baye be esegi agende amo na abasikari baye bake bamobwate Demeturio na komomorentera kare moyo.

English: He went and struck the army of Demetrius, and seized him and brought him to Arsaces, who put him under guard.
Ekegusii: Abasikari bakabasagaana na kobabua abarwani be esegi ba Demeturio na komoira Demeturio ase omorwoti Arisake. Omorwoti akamobeka Demeturio ime ase echeera.

English: The land had rest all the days of Simon. He sought the good of his nation. His authority and his honor was pleasing to them all his days.
Ekegusii: Ebiro bionsi Simioni arenge moyo, ense ekaba nomorembe. Nere agatakera egesaku kiaye obobui; oborai bwaye bokabagookia abanto nesiko ere anyorete ase obogima bwaye.

English: Amid all his honors, he took Joppa for a harbor, and made it an entrance for the islands of the sea.
Ekegusii: Ogotogigwa kw’obonene bwaye bokaba ekero airete chingegu chia Yopa, akaigora enchera yogoika ebisinga bia Mediterania.

English: He enlarged the borders of his nation and took possession of the country.
Ekegusii: Akamenta oboagare bwechimbebe chi’egesaku kiaye na gotwara obobui bw’ekeene ase ekerogo kiaye.

English: He gathered together a great number of captives, and took control of Gazara, Bethsura, and the citadel, and he removed its uncleannesses from it. There was no one who resisted him.
Ekegusii: Akabairania abasibwa abange bechiseegi goocha ense yaabo; akayogambera omochie o Gazara na Beth-zuri amo neburi ya Yerusalemu. Akayechena eburi eyio na tarengeo omonto onde orenge komoamererania nere.

English: They tilled their land in peace, and the land gave her increase, and the trees of the plains gave their fruit.
Ekegusii: Abayahudi bakarema ase emegondo yaabo ase omorembe, ense ekarua okwama kwaye na amatunda akaama ase obonge.

English: The old men sat in the streets; they all conversed together about good things. The young men put on glorious and warlike apparel.
Ekegusii: Abagaaka bakaba baikaransete ase chieero, abanto bonsi bagakwanera amang’ana amaya; na abasae nabarabwo bakeboyia chianga chi’eseegi chikomekameka.

English: He provided food for the cities and furnished them with means of defense, until the glory of his name was known to the end of the earth.
Ekegusii: Simioni akayoa omochie endaagera na kwementera ebirwanero biokwerendera. Chinkuma chiaye chigaika chinsinyo chionsi chi’ense.

English: He made peace in the land, and Israel rejoiced with great joy.
Ekegusii: Akarenta omorembe ase ense na omogooko bwa Abaisraeli torenge nekerengo.

English: Each man sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was no one to make them afraid.
Ekegusii: Bonsi bagaikaransa nomorembe inse yemesabibu nemete yaabo na onde tarengeo okobagosa.

English: No one was left in the land who fought against them. The kings were defeated in those days.
Ekegusii: Tatigarete monto onde ase ense orekobarwania, abarwoti ababisa bonsi bakarimigwa ase engaki eyio.

English: He strengthened all those of his people who were humble. He searched out the law, and every lawless and wicked person he took away.
Ekegusii: Simioni akaba gakobakoonya abataka bonsi ase egesaku kiaye, agatunyana amachiiko na korusia obobe na abasaria bonsi aroro.

English: He glorified the sanctuary, and added to the vessels of the temple.
Ekegusii: Agachabera Hekalu egatogigwa na akameenta ebibeekerero biogosasiimera.

English: It was heard at Rome that Jonathan was dead, and even in Sparta, and they were exceedingly grieved.
