Ekegusii: Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com.

English: Published [January] 12, 2016.
Ekegusii: Engatiato [January] 12, 2016.

English: The elders and their children who gathered together were discussing a matter concerning the son of Omogaka Sokoro, Omogaka Ombongi. Return again, the son will tell you about Rero Ndero Itimbo Riegonkire. What is this gathering about? Listen, the son says that the story will spread throughout the land and reach many people.
Ekegusii: Amatimbo nabo agachiete agachaka gosaria chibao chi' ekerama ki' enyomba y' omogaka sokoro omogaka Ombongi. Korora iga, omogaka okare goteba buna Rero Ndero Itimbo Riegonkire. Bono ninki eng'encho y' omorabaro oyo? Ritang'ani, omogaka sokoro nigo antebetie buna ritimbo nigo rigokora kende gionsi n' omokia omonene.

English: Yesterday morning, they brought a black goat and slaughtered it, and there was celebration. That goat which was sacrificed, it was very beautiful, resembling a young goat with a large horn. Remember well, resemble that goat so it doesn’t get lost.
Ekegusii: Nonya rire risiniini, nabo rikobochora omote omokung'u pa pa na kobeka engoro enene, naende entambe. Engoro eye etaraba, nigo rigokwerekerera, goikera riikie ekerengo ki' engoro eyio ritagete. Gotimoka tikoiyo, goikera engoro eye yaikeranire buna ritagete.

English: What if the story is forgotten over time?
Ekegusii: Bono nabo ritimbo rirasarerigwe emeroberio yaye.

English: And when the rain came, it fell heavily, like a flood. Over time, she understood everything. But truly, the woman whose house burned down, and because of the story of the story, everyone has been angered and cursed !! You people should be enough with this gathering, those who know things should speak truthfully.
Ekegusii: Nabo embura erachake gotwa, ari ase riakunyire egekamago. Emeroberio yaye yamanya gosareka. Ase boigo, nabo omonyene enyomba eye arayeake erangi, na gosaria emeroberio y' ritimbo eri gose ariaake na koriita rikwe !! Mwanyagetinge ominto nigo arenge gokwanera omorabaro oyo ase ogweitia ekero ebinto ebibe biabeire.

English: This is a very important message !!
Ekegusii: Simbiri nyamoibi oyio !!

English: And investigate thoroughly what is happening with those who haven’t understood. And let them prepare their belongings to leave. Let everyone show clearly all the small details. Hurry now, find a good path to follow, don’t wander aimlessly, let that foolish person return home quickly, taking all his possessions with him !! This is a very important message, so let it be known to anyone who wants to understand, knowing that it will be difficult. But encourage each other, let the story be completed so that her history is remembered.
Ekegusii: Nabo korabe ogweitia gose okonyorwa n' aya otakagerete. Buna nabo oragende mogondo, na gosimeka endagera yao buya. Chibando chimanye kobereka bibere bibere gose bitato bitato. Koru igabwo, oganye rigesa rigiya korende ekero rigesa riaikire, tata omoibi egiata agende mogondo kwao, aibe endagera yago yonsi pi !! Bono simbiri nyamoibi oyo ekero akoibeire koru aaaria ase gwasemereti, kwamanya gotigara bosa. Ase enchera ende, aye ritimbo tobwati ase ogosemeria gochi ekiagera emeroberio yao yasariigwe.

English: Her history is also important. And Matiebo was discussing something earlier.
Ekegusii: Emeroberie eri yao emiya nabo egosareka. Nabo Matiebo agosaria kera egento

English: Hurry to Omogaka Ombongi’s people, this is our plan for this week. Goodbye now and thank you for listening.
Ekegusii: Koru ase omogaka Ombong'i ominto, oyo noro omobayeno oito for this week. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

English: Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. December 31, 2011.
Ekegusii: Na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. Egesunte-Egesunte Kia Masaba (December) 31, 2011.

English: These are greetings:
Ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya:

English: Oh! How has the year passed? Children of people, the leader has finished and given life throughout the year 2011 and it has ended well. Let us thank God and remember all the good things that have happened.
Ekegusii: Obe! Omwaka toengekaneti bori? Abana baminto, Omonguru otorendire na gotoa obomoyo ase omwaka O 2011 onyarire koera buya. Tiga tomotogie Omonene na komobaka amatuko onsi ase aya atoire.

English: This is how we celebrate our friends and the community of Gusii.com so that we can continue together in the year 2011. It is good to remember. Whoever doesn't have time, let them visit the website there.
Ekegusii: Bono ntwe nigo tokobairaneria abasani n' eamate ya Gusii.com buna mbuya mono ase okobwaterana nainwe ase omwaka o 2011. Mbuya mono ase kera egento. Onye tari igoro yainwe, nanga ewebusaiti eye teiyo.

English: Goodbye Mr. and Mrs. 2011. It is good to remember in 2011. May God bless you and give you strength to face tomorrow.
Ekegusii: Bye bye Mr. and Mrs. 2011. Mbuya mono ase kera egento in 2011. Nyasae abaseseni mwesi na kobaagata kera engaki gochia motwe.

English: The website is always alive, whoever comes does not get tired. You should visit the blog there to learn more. It is good to write stories that encourage others.
Ekegusii: Ewebusaiti ende yonsi teri moyo, onye onde bwensi tari koyetarera. Ninwe mwagerire ebulogi eye yakinire goikera igaa. Mbuya mono ase okonyora ribaga gototarera kera rituko.

English: For this new year 2012, we ask for peace and love for everyone, home and the culture of Gusii. And since we are celebrating great achievements in this country of Kenya, let us seek peace to face tomorrow. For this coming year, we wish prosperity and blessings to those who work hard.
Ekegusii: Ase omwaka oyo omoyia 2012, nigo togosaba omorembe obuche ase tore, ime na isiko ya Gusii. Na buna torigereretie obochori obonene ase ense yaito ya Kenya, tiga tosegete omorembe ase kera engaki. Ase omwaka oyo omoyia ogoansa aakio, nigo tokobasaba mosange na bari batabwati.

English: Let us be strong in faith, write down the good things about March next month. We will unite, so that we may work hard. The year 2012 will be successful if we cooperate, and the people of Gusii and will continue to cooperate with the community of Gusii.com. May God bless you and give you strength.
Ekegusii: Keri egeke obwate, inyora abande ekiagera Mechi maburu. Twensi ntoikeraneti, korende tiga toe bari batabwati. Omwaka O 2012 ntogenderere gosemania buna twakabeire, na ay' are Gusii yaito na togenderere kobwaterana buna eamate eyemo ya Gusii.com. Nyasae abaseseni mwesi na kobaagata kera engaki.

English: In the year 2011, many things happened, contributing to the development of Gusii.com. We present the top 10 for you below for your enjoyment. Good luck, and may you live many years.
Ekegusii: Ase omwaka oyo o 2011, amariko narengeo anchire mono, kobwatekana no obotari gocha ase Gusii.com. Twabekire the top 10 for you below for your enjoyment. Mbuya mono, naende monywe mache maya.

English: Good luck and thank you for listening.
Ekegusii: Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

English: Rarely did Matiang'i realize that people would support him so much; Gusii people have chosen Raila
Ekegusii: raria matiang’i buna nachie gotigara obowaziri buna abande barariigwe; abasomu ba Gusii babooririe Raila

English: Prominent leaders and professionals have supported the development of the Gusii community because they fear the consequences of supporting Azimio Raila Odinga and Interior Minister Fred Matiang'i, which has caused a lot of division.
Ekegusii: Ekeombe kiabanto abasomu gose professionals baaboririe abarai korwa Gusii baria bakonya koba ebigocha ase omorai o Azimio Raila Odinga korwa komochoora Matiang’I buna omowaziri bwoborendi ase eserekali yaye, gotiga rimo rioka.

English: They met with lawyer Danstan Omari and also spoke with West Mugirango MP Stephene Mogaka, and they agreed to help Raila's supporters because they believe that Matiang'i was unfairly targeted in that matter concerning Raila.
Ekegusii: Bakorau na Omowakili Danstan Omari amo noyokorigia ekerogo kia obojumbe West Mogirango Stephene Mogaka, nigo batebire mbamaete abasani ba Raila nabange bare ase orogongo rwa Gusii korende tiga batige Matiang’I aenekerigwe ekerogo ekio ribaga riokonyagokaania Raila.

English: They said that this issue should be addressed by those from the Gusii region and the election of Martha Karua should be celebrated. They praised Karua for visiting her home in Kisii and saying that there is no dog belonging to the Gusii people.
Ekegusii: Nigo boigo bairete ribaga erio kogikeria aria aba ase egetii kia Gusii ase omosangererekano o Martha Karua aturubanetigwe. Baganirie Karua koroberia boyia esbari yaaye Kisii ase keria eyuo teri embwa yomogusii

English: Stephene Mogaka spoke about the constituency of West Mugirango and asked people to stop spreading false information. He said that this problem and its effects will be resolved soon.
Ekegusii: Stephene Mogaka nigo akoboria ekerogo kiobojumbe bwa West Mogirango ase abasabire abanto bensemo eyuo komobwatesia koreta amaonchorerio. ase keria orogongo orwo ase engaki bono, rwatigarire maega.

English: Three supporters of things
Ekegusii: Tiga gotokongeria ebinto

English: Is there an Ekegusii-English Dictionary?" A person asked. That thing is very good. Is someone looking for a big book so people can learn how to read? Very well. Don't bother with the dictionary. What is it? It seems we haven't understood. Hurry up and be careful.
Ekegusii: Imobwate Ekegusii-English Dictionary?" Nyamusi ominto. Abwo aroro nigo gwacha. Nigo omineti ritabu riria rineene ase abanto bakorigia amarieta? Intwe yaya. Titobwati e dictionary. Eyaki? Intwe nigo tokorika buna tweigwete. Goaka inse na kogororoka.

English: This matter is difficult to understand all the words of the Ekegusii language which are written, so it causes sadness to those who speak the language. The father of Saringi was wise, so he didn't forget to teach his children the language. Those people, they don't teach their children the language. Those children have ruined everything because of it. Someone who doesn't support education, they don't value money.
Ekegusii: Ekero totagete komanya erieta rinde rionsi rie Ekegusii riatosinyire, nigo togochwatera magokoro omongina Saringi esimi. Onye baba Saringi taiyo, nigo togoakera sokoro Nyankuru korwa bomame esimi. Abwo bakobora, nigo togoakera abagisangio baito esimi. Abagisangio bari twachiete iburu nabwo. Onye abagisangio bagotongaina na gototebia ukora, basi nigo togodiliti amarieta ayio.

English: Are we learning the Ekegusii dictionary now?" A child asked. Do you know that a degree from college takes about 12 years? Why hasn't someone taught people how to use the dictionary for 40 years? It's unbelievable how foolish we are. Because they gain nothing from it. Yes. Find me a dictionary quickly. This one is the wealth of the community. It seems this wealth won't last. Someone whose heart is bad, misfortune. This head is not right.
Ekegusii: Timokoroisia e dictionaty ye Ekegusii rende?" Mwana ominto. Nomanyete inga edigrii entangani nigo yatoirete emiaka 12? Yaani igo nigo otagete abanto baito baganye e dictionary ase emiaka 40? Intwe intomanyete oboremerwa bwaito. Intori bangaini moono buna aye okagerete. Yaya. Mangana a dictionary intoiyo. Eyio ne egasi ya abande. Intwe egasi yaito no okorika tu. Onye amagoso kare aroro, bahati mbaya. Intwe imotwe torigereretie.

English: Why are you questioning the spelling of this thing?" Father Nyamusi. But don't you understand? Maybe you don't understand? People.
Ekegusii: Inaki mogochekia spelling ero rende?" Baba Nyamusi. Naye tokabwati amangana? Nayio onsi nigo otagete komanya? Baminto.

English: Imagine if someone like Bill Gates from Microsoft created a Spellcheck for Ekegusii. Do you know what he would say? "Someone who types websites and menus that aren't correct and makes mistakes, you are on your own." That's what it means. Bill said, "No spellcheck for you".
Ekegusii: Rakini intwaboretie Bill Gates korwa Microsoft atobekere Spellcheck ye Ekegusii. Nomanyete inaki atebete? "Onye mokona korika chiwebu saiti ne ebimenu ebio biaino onde atari koigwa, you are on your own". Tari igo rioka. Bill nigo atebete inga, "No spellcheck for you".

English: That's why Nyamusi asked. This is what I found regarding my spelling on the website. Come here little child.
Ekegusii: Oigwe bono Nyamusi ominto. Ekio nakio kegerete amagoso amange a spelling are ase ewebu saiti eye. Kanywe mache maya mwana ominto.

English: These are the reasons:
Ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya:

English: When the sun rises beautifully, it reveals a mystery.
Ekegusii: Onde taiyo orenge kobibeka ase ense engima

English: The elders and fathers have hearts that understand little. It is a small thing, and not much. The elders and fathers remember well those days of old, revealing a mystery beautifully. Yes, truly. Traditions. Customs (preserved) traditions are beautiful and important to all people, especially the Gusii.
Ekegusii: Omongina baba magokoro ominto nabwate eng'ana. Nigo ere eng'ana enke, ko n' endito. Nigo omongina baba agoteba buna gesaku kende nkeiyo ase ense eng'ima kiare kobibeka. Eee bono. Ebitinge. Ogotimigwa (okobekerwa) ebitinge nigo kiarenge egento gesaku kende gionsi ase ense engima getare gokora, otatiga Abagusii.

English: My fellow Gusii people, let us cherish and protect these customs and traditions. The Gusii tradition is beautiful and strong, able to solve problems and be respected by generations.
Ekegusii: Mwamogusii bweka, naende bene, nere okabekire gose gotimigwa ebitinge. Omosubati Omogusii nigo arenge gotimigwa egetinge ekero are gosoka gochia bwoye, na gokorerwa enyangi y' bitinge.

English: The children of Mwanyagetinge should respect their heritage. Kemunto, Kerubo, Moraa and Kwamboka also honor our traditions. On the far right, the elder shows respect during a ceremony, the tradition Kwamboka preserves traditions. Picture with Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com files.
Ekegusii: Abana ba Mwanyagetinge babekire emeyabo. Kemunto, Kerubo, Moraa amo na Kwamboka nao bare ase omoyega bwe enyangi. On the far right, omongina bwe esiko ase ekenyoro, omosubati kwamboka otimigwe ebitinge. Picture na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com files.

English: Therefore, the fathers remember that preserving something beautifully is a strong tradition. What kind of tradition is this? It is a great tradition, so that when something is preserved, it can bring about positive change!
Ekegusii: Ase boigo, nigo baba agoteba buna omoiseke orenge kobibekerwa nigo arenge omosubati bw'e esiko ase ekenyoro. Esiko eng'ana buna ki? Nigo yarenge esiko enene, mbaka omoiseke obibekeirwe nigo arenge gochora erieta ri' okwebaka!

English: The wealth of traditions is very significant!
Ekegusii: Amarieta y' ebitinge nigo are ane oka!

English: Comment on this, the elders remember that the Gusii people can achieve great wealth, but they must preserve traditions. Connected to the heart, this wealth which is important to the Gusii can be achieved through: Kemunto, Kerubo, Moraa and Kwamboka.
Ekegusii: Komenta nayio, nigo omongina baba agoteba buna abasubati ba Gusii nigo barenge kwebaka amarieta ane oka, ko batimigwe ebitinge. Kobwatekana na magokoro, amarieta ayio ane omoriakari o Gusii arenge kwebaka nigo are: Kemunto, Kerubo, Moraa amo na Kwamboka.

English: Traditions are beautifully preserved, and the initiation process is done carefully, meticulously. This Egetinge tradition teaches responsibility, “Responsibility.” Furthermore, the tradition is strengthened through unity (collaboration). This tradition (customs) of Egetinge originates from Nyagetinge, extending to the present day Mwanyagetinge.
Ekegusii: Egetinge nigo kiare kobekwa magoro, ase egeting'iro korwa igoro, asiniiini. Erieta Egetinge ndibwate omoreng'anio, "Tinga". Eng'encho ende, omosubati nigo areng'e goting'wa kogoro (obwatanigwa). Bono oyo okobekerwa (ogotimigwa) egetinge orokwa Nyagetinge, erinde egesaku eke nakio Mwanyagetinge.

English: The elders also say that we should embrace this truth, and strive for progress. Thank you very much for listening.
Ekegusii: Omongina baba nabo ateba buna bwatera abwo bono, ase okwegera ase twarwete. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

English: Embarambamba is very high up. Mwanyagetinge and his family, Nyang'wara Mosioma too.
Ekegusii: Embarambamba iko juu sana. Mwanyagetinge amo n' omwana omino, Nyang'wara Mosioma eyio.

English: They have visited Nyamira county, those who know how to manage.
Ekegusii: obokoreri obobe nyamira,abamenyi kwemurungania

English: Written by Hyline Major on February 21, 2022
Ekegusii: Written by Hyline Major on February 21, 2022

English: Those who know the Nyamira county account are the ones who went to visit that county.
Ekegusii: Abamenyi ase ekaunti ya Nyamira nigo bagikerie obokoreri obobe ase ekaunti eyio

English: The people of Bonyunyu ward of Kiabonyoru constituency went and found that the parents were working hard to cultivate so that they could work together and also ensure that the children get education in Borabu and North Mugirango constituencies so that they can benefit from what they learn from the knowledgeable people and their families are supported.
Ekegusii: Gokwana ime ya Bonyunyu eward ya Kiabonyoru nigo batebire buna abarai bachorete mbanya gokora kende gekororekana ase batebire buna nonya imbari barikire ase chiestate echio chire ime ya Borabu na North Mugirango mbanya gokonyeka nachio egekogera abamenyi borogongo orwo imbari koegwa ribaga ritang’ana ase abana babo korikwa

English: So they managed to convene a meeting with the company's management and about that and they found out that some children dropped out of school and continued to engage in activities and they were encouraged to return to school.
Ekegusii: Nigo boigo bemurunganeiri ogochandwa amor nechikampani chiestate yechae ase ensemo eyio ase batebire buna nigop abaa bachiete chisukuru bagasomka ase ensemo eyio korende mbanaya korigerererigwa nonya

English: So they found out about the machine that was rented in that estate and the people there took it and used it to earn income and then they requested the governor of Nyamira James Kemoni and he promised that the company would build good houses which will be distributed among the residents of that area and the people welcomed this news happily.
Ekegusii: Nigo boigo batebire igoro yechimashine echio chiarentetwe ase estate eyio ase abange abwo bare gotora echae basiretie emeremo yabo engana eyio nigo boigo bagikeirie noyokorigia ekerogo kiobogavana Nyamira James Kemoni ase atebire buna nere buya chikampani echio chirusie ebiita ebio bibekire egatagati yechiestate echio erio korwa ribaga ase abamenyi goeta aroro buna yakabeire agwo ritang’ani

English: The History of the Gusii People: Cattle and Small Livestock are a Blessing, They Strengthen the Knees of Children, They Provide Food for the Poor, They Bring Joy to the Home!!
Ekegusii: Emebayeno Ya Abagusii: Ng'ombe Na Mbori Chikane Korigia Magega Yaya, Korera Tarera Boreri Bobe, Bwoye Tagochongeria Mobere Osinye Bikoe !!

English: It is said that in ancient times during the time of Buyaki, they migrated from Kegogi, Bosamaro, Omongina with heavy hearts, but cattle and small livestock remained a blessing, providing food for the poor, bringing joy to the home.
Ekegusii: Tokare kogenda ase enyangi ya Buyaki aaria Kegogi, Bosamaro, Omongina magokoro baba ominto nantebetie buna Ng'ombe Na Mbori Chikane Korigia Magega Yaya, Korera Tarera Boreri Bobe, Bwoye Tagochongeria Mobere Osinye Bikoe.

English: Why does this tradition of wealth persist among the Gusii people? Perhaps, this is because it is considered important to have enough resources to avoid poverty and hardship. Having enough resources to avoid poverty and hardship is considered a sign of respect and honor, and prevents unnecessary wandering. But also, it is good to remember that having resources can bring about challenges.
Ekegusii: Bono ninki eng'encho y' omorabaro oyo ase ntwe Abagusii? Aaiga, aya nigo arenge gokwanerwa ekero omoiseke arenge gosoka na kogenda bwoye. Ekero omoiseke arenge kogenda bwoye, nigo arenge gotebigwa aremereri komenya abwo ase enka yaye enyia, naende tabaisa konya kong'anyang'anya. Ase enchera ende, nigo ere buya amanye buna akomenya.

English: To prevent disputes over property, let us maintain peace.
Ekegusii: Konara kong'anya korwa bwoye, tikiarenge gento kiya

English: These matters are being discussed according to their traditions, and with great wisdom. Anyone who forgets them will not be able to stand on their feet, and their house will collapse like a termite mound. It is not right to cause disputes over property. True wealth lies in unity and cooperation so that everyone benefits.
Ekegusii: Amangana aya nigo aregotebigwa ekero ki'enyangi yaye, na ng'ina omoiborete. Onye ochire bwoye teri buya arigie magega, ekiagera chimbori amo ne chiombe chiaakanirwe. Bono tagwenereti kong'anya korwa bwoye. Okomenya okuya nigo gokogokia ng'ina biara na koorokia buna ng'ina omoibori mbuya amorerete.

English: And those who lack resources are often seen as vulnerable and unable to sustain life.
Ekegusii: Na ngina biara nere nigo arenge gotebigwa buna takongeria moka momura obogima

English: But sometimes, those who have little are respected more than those who possess abundant wealth. Wealth, when misused, can lead to arrogance and disrespect, causing problems and ultimately leading to its downfall.
Ekegusii: Ase boigo, ng'ina biara omoiseke nere ngotenbigwa arenge buna takong'eria omosubati oyo obogima erinde asinywe komenya ase enka eye enyia. Omosubati, ekero agochongerigwa, nigo agoichana, goikera oita ebikoe ekiagera nigo agosinywa buna ense eye achiete naki ere gose.

English: I come from Buyaki in Keumbu, Kisii County. Respect and humility are my guiding principles. The community should strive to ensure that no one suffers due to lack of basic necessities.
Ekegusii: Nka sobo Buyaki aaria Keumbu, Kisii County. Komenya n' omorembe n' egento ekiya. Chikorera nigo chiarenge koborigwa buna tichikongeria moka momura obogima.

English: This message is intended to reach those who understand and appreciate our traditions, and to remind the older generation of the Gusii people about the importance of cattle and small livestock as a blessing, providing food for the poor, bringing joy to the home.
Ekegusii: Obosemia obo bwarenge korwegwa gochia ase omoikeke na ng'ina biara ekero ki enyangi, nabio biagerete Abagusii abakoro bagateba buna Ng'ombe Na Mbori Chikane Korigia Magega Yaya, Korera Tarera Boreri Bobe, Bwoye Tagochongeria Mobere Osinye Bikoe.

English: That is the end of this story today. Thank you for listening.
Ekegusii: Oyo noro omobayeno oito ase ewiki eye. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

English: These are the conclusions:
Ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya:

English: The residents of Bobasi are mourning the death of Mr. Bichang'a
Ekegusii: Abarisia Bobasi koemurunganeria okorusigwa abisi kwa Bichang’a

English: Written by RadioVuna on June 15, 2020
Ekegusii: Written by RadioVuna on June 15, 2020

English: The leaders have praised the Adventist church members of Bobasi for electing their leader, the President of South Kenya Adventist Church, Dr. Julius Bichanga, whose term has ended
Ekegusii: Ensemo yabarisia bekanisa yege adventista korwa Bobasi bagikeirie enchera omo president bwensemo ya SOUTH Kenya ase chikanisa chiege adventista Dr Julius Bichanga bwango iga arusigwa abisi

English: We thank God, those people have participated greatly in supporting the work of Pastor Bichanga throughout his leadership during the conference period (Bobasi)
Ekegusii: Gokwana nabariki amang’ana, abarai abwo nigo batebete ekerenga nkereo kiabobisi kiairera Bichanga goakwa isiko chingaki obochori bwe conference boberete ang’e(Bobasi)

English: Those from OGEMBO division, the leaders of that church and also from that sub-county have participated greatly in supporting the work of that meeting so that they can take care of things at the conference level and be appointed accordingly (Looking at Bobasi)
Ekegusii: Bagokwana ime ya OGEMBO, abarisia abwo korwa chi kanisa ao ao ase e sub-county eyio nigo batebete abarai abange korwa ensemo eyio babeire bagotwara ebitari ase e conference nigo babeire bakorusigwa abisi ase obotutukanu(Koonera omobasi)

English: They discussed the challenges facing that church regarding the issue of restoring those who left and returning them
Ekegusii: Nigo baganirie oboteneneri bwekanisa eyio korigia chinchera chiokobagorora abarai baye anene abarandia rika riokobabuta

English: Therefore, they agreed to continue working with the church in Bobasi to cooperate with the conference and discuss this matter further
Ekegusii: Nigo boigo bagosereirie gochia koraa chikanisa korwa BObasi kwerusia ase e conference eyio ase banaganirie omorandia oyio amang’ana aye arigererigwe ase omroebrio

English: Those people also discussed how they will assist in the government's efforts to combat the disease affecting Kenya and related to CORONA (Prayer)
Ekegusii: Abarai abwo nigo baganirie baria bare abisi kwerita korwa siasa yoborai anene chingaki echi Kenya egendererete kominana na CORONA(Prayer)

English: The Story of the Gusii People LXXXI: "Oh!! These White Dogs Are Crazy, Their Hearts Are Full of Pride" This story is about the events of the past concerning the people of Nyabitunwa Bine.
Ekegusii: Emegano Ya Abagusii LXXXI: "Kai !! Ani Bwanchi Mbwa Maiso, Mioyo Etamanyaini" Egioto Ekemo Korwa Aaria Nyabitunwa Bine

English: These days are like this:
Ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya:

English: Long ago, the people lived peacefully among the people of Nyabitunwa Bine. The people who were there used to live happily and peacefully. They would gather together, and the people would fall asleep in the shade of trees and wander around.
Ekegusii: Abwo kare kare ebioto mbiarenge aroro aaria Nyabitunwa Bine. Ebioto ebi nigo biarenge goeta ase emete emenge yarenge. Kibigedererete goeta, ebioto ebi bibere bikagwa ime ye engoro yarenge etambe.

English: Details of the eyes: Gusii.com at home among the people of Nyabitunwa Bine, South Mugirango, Kisii County. Mwanyagetinge.com/2014
Ekegusii: Amaridadi ya amaiso: Gusii.com at home aaria Nyabitunwa Bine, South Mugirango, Kisii County. Mwanyagetinge.com/2014

English: Some people say that those things happened because of the things they did, which caused them to fall asleep in the shade and wake up confused and unable to understand what was happening. Others say that those things happened because of their actions, which led to confusion and trouble, causing them to suffer greatly. The people who fell asleep in the shade had no life, and it seemed as though they were being punished, leading to suffering and wandering around.
Ekegusii: Bono ebioto binde ekero biachiete korora ebi biamwabo bibere bigwete engoro ime bikabisekerera na kobitebia buna mbigosoka korwa engoro eyio ime bire moyo. Aaiga nario ebioto ebi bibere biekorete buna mbigweti aya yokobisekereria na gotema buna biare konyara erinde birwe engoro eye ime. Ebioto ebi biagwete engoro ime mbiakwete moyo, ekiagera nigo bierwete kerage, gosoka korwa engoro eye yarenge etambe mono.

English: This story is full of sadness and pain, back and forth.
Ekegusii: Egioto ekemo gekarosa na goaka inse na gokwa, abuo abuo.

English: This story is carefully crafted to reveal the truth and expose the secrets, so that it can be understood. Every now and then, the people remember the events of the past and try to understand this story, hoping to find peace in the shade.
Ekegusii: Egioto keri giatigarete engoro ime kegatema gocharoka gose ngesoke korwa engoro eye ime, korende gekaba kegosinywa. Erio erio, ebioto biri binde nigo biare goseka na goita egioto kiamwabo omoyo, bigoteba buna egioto ekio nagetiga gwechanda ekiagera ngokwera kere engoro eye ime.

English: Some of the stories that have been told, are said to be untrue and fabricated, causing great anger!!
Ekegusii: Bono ebioto ebi biamwabo, biagokire buna egioto eke tikiaigwete buna biagetakerete amabe !!

English: Some of this story, if revealed, will lead to suffering and hardship. Some people believe that it is better to remain silent than to speak out, fearing that it will cause more harm. This story has been hidden for a long time, and its details are shocking!! The people who reveal it will face consequences and suffer greatly.
Ekegusii: Bono egioto eke kegatema igo, goikera kegasoka korwa engoro eye ime. Biri binde kibiachia korora aya bikamoboria buna gose nkoigwa arenge buna biare gokwana. Egioto eke gekabatebia buna ime y' engoro eyio ime, nigo amato atinete !! Ebioto ebio bikagoka buna taigwete buna biamotakerete amabe.

English: This story is very important, knowing that White Dogs Are Crazy, Their Hearts Are Full of Pride.
Ekegusii: Egioto eke korwa erio, gekamanya buna Bwanchi Mbwa Maiso, Mioyo Etamanyaini.

English: These are my wishes:
Ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya:

English: May God bless you all with peace and joy: Merry Christmas 2012! May this happiness reach everyone, young and old, children who are there, children of the village and those from afar, God bless you!
Ekegusii: Ase Mwanyagetinge abeta ase chintanda chionsi: Merry Christmas 2012! Naki omogoko ekero tokoyechengera engaki ye esuguku n’ omorembe amo n’ obwanchani buna abana abamo, abana b’omong’ina n’omogaka oyomo, Mwanyagetinge!

English: Indeed, how can we forget this year of prosperity as we celebrate Christmas again? As we finish the year, let us remember the hardships we faced, the difficulties we went through, the great road of Kenya and the rough roads. Let all people everywhere praise the Lord who has brought us peace and joy this year.
Ekegusii: Inee aye ninki okoinyora ekero kie engaki eye y’ omoyega bw’ esuguku gose? Buna twachagete omwaka, nabo twarorire amange akorekanire ase chinka chiaito, ebinyoro biato, ense yaito ya Kenya amo n ’ense engima. Abe amang’ana aria amaya gose amabe nigo tokomotogia Omonguru ase ogotoikia engaki ende y’ ogochengera ekero Yeso aiboretwe.

English: Praise the Lord who has been with us always. May He continue to protect the children of God. Merry Christmas 2012.
Ekegusii: Tiga Omonguru atogigwe ase kera egento. Ogochenga okuya ase abana ba Mwanyagetinge. Merry Christmas 2012.

English: This is a great blessing that brings prosperity this Christmas season. Remember my friends who may not have the opportunity to celebrate their lives well, remember them as they struggle to find ways to improve their lives, remember those who are poor and unable to afford everything they need.
Ekegusii: Oyo n’omogoko omonene ekero togochengera omoyega oyo bw’esuguku naende. Inyora mbare batari koyochengera ase ching’encho ao ao korende onye aye kore n’ egesio kio ogokora omoyega ase omenyete, inyora bari abataka batari kwenyara onyare kobasira ase enchera ende yonsi oranyare.

English: My friends, let us share what little we have so that others may also be happy and grateful! They should appreciate this year of prosperity and remember that they will never lack anything in their future endeavors.
Ekegusii: Mbare bare chinyagitari ao ao ase eng’echo y’ oborwaire ao ao. Nabarabuo nere buya tobatarere erinde tobae ogosemeria ng’a nabo bakobwena! Bari bakwereire engaki eye y’ omoyega bw’ esuguku nabarabuo nabo tokobatarera erinde tobaremi nario baraigwe buya ase chinkoro chiabo ime.

English: Let us all work hard together to overcome our challenges. We thank you for giving us strength and courage, and we pray that you will continue to guide us in all that we do!
Ekegusii: Abaminto esegeto enene neri buna timoria bobe gose konywa bobe mbaka ching’endo chibe chimbe, erinde oiche gweitia ekero omoyega oyo oeriere. Inyora gochenga na komogokia Omonguru ase chinchera chionsi engaki eye y’ esuguku.

English: People gather greatly because they want to drink and enjoy themselves until the end of time, and may this prosperity last forever. Remember to give thanks to God for all His blessings this Christmas season.
Ekegusii: Abaminto timweba gosabera omorembe ime na iisiko ya ase tore, chinyomba chiaito, amo na bari tobebekaine nabwo. Ense yaito yonsi toyesabere, ekiagera omwaka bw’ obochori ng’aange’e ore. Inyora tomosabe Omonguru atoe chisemi erinde tonyare gochora abarai abaya bari bamoirogete Omonene otongete ebinto bionsi bire n’ obomoyo mbaka Mwanyabanto.

English: People come together to offer gifts and respect, good deeds, and those who are present. All roads lead to celebration, marking the end of the year with great enthusiasm. Let us thank God for granting us life and enabling us to live happily with our families and communities.
Ekegusii: Tiga Omonguru atorende na tomobake engaki yonsi. Esuguku 2012 engiiya, ase kera oyomo, minto Mwanyagetinge!!!!!!!!

English: Goodbye 2013. May Mwanyagetinge people be well, the world is also ours and with relatives may we finish the year 2013 and welcome 2014. We thank God very much for his blessings, let us remember the year 2013 and welcome the new year 2014.
Ekegusii: Bye bye 2013. Ase Mwanyagetinge abeta, twensi nigo tore n' omogoko ase ogokora o mwaka o 2013 na gochaka 2014. Nigo tokomoiraneria Omonguru oito buna mbuya mono ase oborendi bwaye, goikera twayokumbire omwaka 2013 na gochaka omwaka omoyia 2014.

English: Welcome to 2014. Happy new year to all families of Mwanyagetinge with peace.
Ekegusii: Welcome to 2014. Happy new year gochia ase eamate yonsi ya Mwanyagetinge ense engima

English: May good things happen, may all bad things from this past year disappear. Continue with these words, we thank God very much. The website of Gusii.com has been improved so that people can easily find information and news about Mwanyagetinge.
Ekegusii: Amange akorekanire, amaya gose amabe ase omwaka oyo o oera. Korende ase aya onsi, nigo tokomwakera Omonguru ng'a mbuya mono. Ekebute eke kia Gusii.com, nigo giachire nguma ase engencho aaiga nao tokonyora amang'ana amaaya, naende amaansu a Mwanyagetinge.

English: We will continue working hard for the development of the culture of Mwanyagetinge. Find there stories, traditions, customs of Gusii, history and other cultural aspects of the Gusii people.
Ekegusii: Nigo togotema gokora obotuki igoro ye ching'encho chia Mwanyagetinge. Aiga nao tokonyora Emegano emiansu, Ebitandawiri ao ao, Emebayeno yaito ya Gusii, Egekoro giato, amo n' ching'encho ao ao chi'Omogusii.

English: Through the Gusii.com website we will help many people very much with information about the website and encourage them to read and understand everything. As we welcome the new year we will strive to unite all children of Mwanyagetinge together so that we can work towards developing their culture and we will ensure reading and understanding knowledge is widespread and we will be happy.
Ekegusii: Ntwe aaiga ase Gusii.com nigo togoakera abasani baito bonsi buna mbuya mono ase ogotarera ase ekebute eke na gosanga ase ogosoma na koboria amaboria ao ao. Buna togochaka omwaka omoyia nigo tokobariera eira bari bonsi banchete omonwa o Mwanyagetinge o chabumbe buna nigo togocha kogenderera korika omonwa aoito buna ere botambe na nigo toanchete gosoma amaboria korwa ase more na twayairaneria.

English: The year 2013 brought many challenges to the entire country of Kenya and because of that year being over we have experienced difficulties in life and it is hoped that it will be possible to overcome all obstacles.
Ekegusii: Omwaka 2013 nigo otwara amakong'u ao ao ase ense yaito ya Kenya na inyora omwaka oyo oera nari twachora eserekari enyia inse ye richiko eri rinyia na nigo ere buya togenderere koyesabera erinde esaboke chingaki chionsi.

English: Therefore, my friends, let us remember all the problems that happened in the whole country of Kenya, those who were affected suffered greatly and those who weren't helped, the problems that occurred everywhere and we hope the whole country will be peaceful. This is my wish for peace and prosperity in the new year 2014 with the grace of God and everything will be alright.
Ekegusii: Ase boigo, tiga toinyore twarora emebasokano ao ao kegokorekana ase ense yaito ya Kenya, ababegwa bagatocherera na goita abanto batari bake, emebasokano emebe ya para nero yakorekana na nigo togosabera ense yaito amaya kera engaki. Bono nigo nkoira engaki eye kobaganeria omwaka omoyia o 2014 omuuya bwa amasesenio na Omonguru abe na inwe chingaki chionsi.

English: Happy new year to all families of Mwanyagetinge through Gusii.com.
Ekegusii: Happy new year eamate yonsi ya Mwanyagetinge ime ya Gusii.com.

English: Let us discuss this matter and make it clear. Gusii.com is a good website where people can share their thoughts and ideas. Contact the administrator Mr. Keen Nyamwange: email@example.com.
Ekegusii: Engana ekobwatia ne eyo obosemia. Gusii.com intori komenta monyo onde bwensi ase engana engiya buna eye. Ogotebererani korwa ase omogaka Keen Nyamwange: email@example.com.

English: Welcome friends. Welcome everyone. A good friend is someone who helps you when you are in trouble and stands with you through thick and thin. Let us appreciate our friendship. Welcome friends.
Ekegusii: Tochaya oyomino. Ogochaya no okobe. Ekero ogochaya ekerema igo aye nigo ogoteba buna tokoremara. Nigo okweng’aina aye omonyene ekiagera oborema igoro bore. Tosekera kerema kende. Tochaya oyomino.

English: Welcome child, may God bless you and give you wisdom so that you grow up knowing how to respect others. God knows everything about what we do and what we don't do.
Ekegusii: Tochaya mwana omonto ekiagera aye tomanyeti ekio omwana oyio arache koba ekero abeire omonene. Nyasae bweka nere omanyete naende nere omotongete.

English: Welcome leader, let him lead us well and guide us on the right path. The proverb says: A strong tree does not bend easily. This is something to remember. Welcome friends.
Ekegusii: Tochaya mogaka onde gose mongina onde na komotinyeria inse na komoroka akagaka gose akangina akariri. Inyora iga: Bogotu ingesango no ogokina kore okuya. Eki ogosimeka nakio okogesa. Tochaya oyomino.

English: Welcome things, let us examine them carefully and understand that some things are good and others are bad. Remember to welcome things with an open mind.
Ekegusii: Tochaya binto bionde na kobitinyeria inse tokomanya ekero ebinto ebio ebio birakoiyore aye omonyene korwa ase obokong’u. Koranche tochaya binto bionde bwensi.

English: Welcome parents, they are always there for us. And they teach us how to live and how to behave. God created Adam and Eve and placed them in the Garden of Eden. God knows everything about our hearts. Welcome very much.
Ekegusii: Tochaya morugi gose mosacha bw’ onde. Aye tokaga buna oyo obwate ne riraika. Nyasae agatonga Adamu na Awa bare abanuke kegima nomanyete ekio bakorete aaria Edeni. Nyasae nere bweka omanyete chinkoro chiaito. Tochaya monto o’monto.

English: Welcome seed, let us plant it. God works with seeds. They grew and flourished. Welcome everyone. Seed is precious like gold.
Ekegusii: Tochaya semi chionde. Nyasae nere okorwa chisemi. Tokaga buna aye naye kemanyi. Ogochaya no okobe. Semi tiching’ana nguru.

English: Welcome knowledge, let us seek it diligently. They grew and understood and became wise people who were respected by all. There is only one truth, welcome everyone.
Ekegusii: Tochaya obomenyo bw’ omonto onde. Tokaga buna aye ase omenyete aye ne baresi enene gose ekalu. Nonya mbwoo ebinyinyi imbire aroro Ogochaya nokobe.

English: Welcome journey, let us embark on it together. They grew and learned and discovered new things. God knows everything about our future.
Ekegusii: Tochaya dini yonde. Tokaga buna aye naye okeroche. Nyasae nere bweka omanyete emioyo yaito.

English: Welcome prayer, let us offer it sincerely. And pray for peace and harmony among all people, and let us be grateful for all that we have. Welcome everyone.
Ekegusii: Tochaya emeremo oyomino agokora. Aye oyorengereretie buna emeromo yao nero namba-wani nabande namanamba nigo okweng’aina. Ogochaya nokobe.

English: Jesus said: "He who rejects me and does not accept my message rejects God himself; and he who accepts me accepts God." (Luke 10:16)
Ekegusii: Yeso agateba iga: “Ere oyo okoigwa aria mogoteba onyigure nainche; nere oria okobachaya inwe igo ninche aeire ogochaya; noria ogochaya igo nigo agochaya oria ontomete.” (Luka 10:16)

English: Welcome everyone. Welcome today.
Ekegusii: Ogochaya nokobe. Tochaya onde.

English: Keen Nyamwange.
Ekegusii: Keen Nyamwange.

English: These are the issues:
Ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya:

English: The person who drew the boundaries in Kenya really created too many constituencies, we are getting more. It seems 80 new constituencies will be included in the current constitution. Indeed those constituencies and the changes to the constitution we made say that we have to create more.
Ekegusii: Onye gokagete inga Kenya nigo ebwate too many constituencies, we are getting more. Intoche toegwe 80 new constituencies kobwatekana ne Ekatiba enyia. Eee chikonstichwensi echio ne chinyinge rakini Ekatiba eye twaetia nabo egoteba inga we have to create more.

English: With those 80 constituencies, Gusii has very few, included in the report in the Standard. Included in what we saw, only two constituencies in Gusii will benefit from that review. These constituencies that will benefit include North Mugirango Borabu and Kitutu Chache.
Ekegusii: Gati ye chikonstichwensi echio 80, Gusii neche enyore ibere, kobwatekana ne engana korwa ase e Standard. Kobwatekana na aya twaigure, only two constituencies in Gusii chigocha go benefit korwa ase okobutoranwa okwo. Kiabeire inga chikonstichwensi echio chigocha kobutoranwa nigo chire North Mugirango Borabu amo na Kitutu Chache.

English: So how did the Interim Independent Boundaries Commission (IIBRC) allocate those numbers to Gusii? Perhaps they were compromised? We don't know. The reason is that they allocated numbers to people exceeding per constituency.
Ekegusii: Yaani how did the Interim Independent Boundaries Commission (IIBRC) yaikerete enamba eyio ase Gusii? Obotaalamu ki batumiete? Intwe intomanyeti amange. who are we to know? Rakini nigo toroche inga nigo batumiete enamba ya abaaki chikura per constichwensi.

English: Based on the number of registered voters from 2007, North Mugirango/Borabu and Kitutu Chache had the most voters thus deserving:
Ekegusii: Ase okobwatia chinamba chia registered voters korwa ase omwaka o 2007, North Mugirango/Borabu amo na Kitutu Chache nachio chibwate the most voters buna ekobwatia:

English: So what does this mean for 2012? It is concerning. It is bad especially for our people who want to vote more. In North Mugirango Borabu, people are saying the MP Wilkista Onsando wants to retain his seat.
Ekegusii: Bono what does this mean as 2012? Oboke imboreo. Oboke no obonge especially ase abasubati baria batagete koboria chikura. Korwa North Mugirango Borabu, ribaga indiroo onye omongina Wilkista Onsando otagete koboria obojumbe.

English: MP Onsando is popular in Borabu. North Mugirango Borabu was divided into North Mugirango and Borabu, there is a good chance that MP Wilkista will also win in Borabu.
Ekegusii: Omongina Onsando nigo amenyete ase ensemo ya Borabu. North Mugirango Borabu eise kobutorwa ebe North Mugirango na Borabu, there is a good chance inga omongina Wilkista nabo araborie chikura korwa Borabu.

English: What about Kitutu Chache? In Kitutu Chache, there is a possibility that Dr. Jane Onsongo from KACC will also win the seat. There are several candidates available. Also the Senate seat for Gusii is wide open. In addition to those candidates, people are showing interest including The Chairman of Nyansiongo Tea Factory, Mayor Claire Omanga and ODM Chief Executive Officer, businesswoman Janet Ong'era.
Ekegusii: Kitutu Chache rende? Ase Kitutu Chache, there is a possibility inga Dr. Jane Onsongo korwa KACC nabo araborie obojumbe. Tari obobunge bwoka bore available. Egasi yo Oboseneta nero korwa Gusii is wide open. In addition ya abagaka abange baraborie ekerogo ekio, abasubati bande baratware interest nigo bare The Chairman of Nyansiongo Tea Factory, Mayor Claire Omanga amo na ODM Chief Executive Officer, omosubati Janet Ong'era.

English: What now? The people of Gusii are waiting eagerly. This is the best opportunity for us to get things done for 2012. Let us seize this moment.
Ekegusii: Ase igo? Abasubati ba Gusii imokerera igoro. This is the best chance indoche mobwate for 2012. Timotiga echiere inse.

English: These are her words:
Ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya:

English: Welcome Gusii.com Proverbs And Customs Editor, Petronillah Ogoti.
Ekegusii: Welcome Gusii.com Proverbs And Customs Editor, Petronillah Ogoti.

English: People. Back in December (December month), they were looking for someone to edit stories on the website. We wanted to edit stories specifically knowing the Ekegusii language well and understanding Ekegusii culture. Then we realized some people had already shown interest. These people.
Ekegusii: Abaminto. Back in December (Egesunte Kende), intwarwete okoboria aaiga ase ekeoreri tokorigia omoriki onde. Nigo twarenge korigia omoriki specifically omanyete Ekegusii gose bwanchete korika na gokwana Ekegusii. Nigo togoaka inga imbuya mono ase abaminto abange baria mwatomete interest. Imbuya mono.

English: Then she came highly recommended as the Gusii.com Folk Tales And Proverbs Editor. Now we have been told that some people didn't know how to write well in Ekegusii. Anyone who wants to learn, now we will teach them.
Ekegusii: Nigo yaba egasi enkongu sana ase ogochora the Gusii.com Folk Tales And Proverbs Editor. Intwe nigo twagokigwa inga abaminto abange nigo mwanchete omonwa oito bwe Ekegusii mono. Onye indiria yarenge konyarekana, intwe nigo twarenge koira kera oyomo.

English: But this time we won't teach. We have left the stories as they are for now. But if God allows, there will be more opportunities. People are eager to contribute stories like proverbs, riddles, myths and the history of the Gusii.
Ekegusii: Rakini bono gaki tiyarenge konyarekana. Nigo twachorete omoriki oyomo ase ogototenenera ase ensemo eyio for now. Buna omonene Nyasae akona gotobokia, there will be more opportunities. Abaminto eariganie koumera Omoriki omoyia bwe Emegano, Ebitendawili, Emebayeno amo ne Ekemira kia Abagusii.

English: She also knows how to speak and write Ekegusii. She has skills and experience. Welcome our editor Petronillah Ogoti from Gusii.com. In addition to speaking Ekegusii, Petronillah studied Hospitality and Tourism Administration.
Ekegusii: Nigo anchete korika na gosoma Ekegusii. Tari korwa ase ngina na ise koro. Karibuni omosubati Petronillah Ogoti ase Gusii.com. In addition yo ogwancha Ekegusii, Petronillah nigo asomerete Hospitality and Tourism Administration.

English: We have found someone to work on the ground. Petronillah fits that requirement. She comes from Ichuni Sub Location, Nyamagesa Location, Nyaribari Masaba, Kisii County. Petronillah is going to fill a big gap at Gusii.com.
Ekegusii: Nigo twaboretie omoriki ore in the ground. Petronillah fits that request. Enka nigo ere Ichuni Sub Location, Nyamagesa Location, Nyaribari Masaba, Kisii County. Petronillah nigo agocha go fill a gap enene sana ase Gusii.com.

English: But if you don't understand Ekegusii. We will try to explain things here and there, but this time Petronillah will correct us. Because of you, we haven't stopped wondering why we accepted to edit these stories. It is because of you. The Gusii readers.
Ekegusii: Buna tore iga titomanyeti Ekegusii. Nigo tokona gokamba kambageria here and there rakini bono Petronillah will straighten us out. Nonya nabo igo, titokweba why naende twatwarire omoriki onde. It is because of you. Abagusii readers.

English: These people and their continued support and encouragement are very helpful. We appreciate and thank you. In the coming days, you will see articles written by Petronillah.
Ekegusii: Imbuya mono ase ogotosindigisa and constant support ase ogototarera kera rituko. We appreciate and Thank you. Ase amatuko agocha, you will see articles chia Petronillah.

English: Anyone with suggestions on how to improve the website, feel free to share. Petronillah, welcome to the Abagusii.com family. These people.
Ekegusii: Onye onde obwate suggestions ase oko improve ewebusaiti eye, gaki totebie. Petronillah, Welcome to the Abagusii.com family. Imbuya mono.

English: The results have been released by various sources including the Kenya National Examinations Council. This was announced. The results of the Kenya Certificate Of Secondary Education [ KCSE ] 2012, from Nyabururu Girls High School which is in Kisii County were therefore released.
Ekegusii: Nigo amachibu ayio atangwa goetania ase omotienyi oyomo, amo na Kenya National Examinations Council. Bono asokigwe. Amachibu y' amatemwa a kenya Certificate Of Secondary Education [ KCSE ] 2012, y' esukuru ya Nyabururu Girls High School aaria Kisii County nasokigwa rero.

English: Speaking to Robert Nyasato of Standard, Kisii County Director Of Education, Mr. Konchora Chepe said they will work hard and carefully so that all students get their results correctly, especially those from Nyabururu Girls.
Ekegusii: Kobwatenana na Robert Nyasato bw' Standard, Kisii County Director Of Education, omosike Konchora Chepe nigo ateba buna bakorire obotuki na konyora buna bobe bonde tiboiyo ase amatemwa ayio, korwa ase Nyabururu Girls.

English: Below: Students of St. Joseph's Nyabigena Boys. Very good. Thus Nyabururu Girls High School joins Kisii High School, St. Joseph's Nyabigena Boys, Moi Gesusu and Kereri Girls among the top schools in the larger Gusii Counties. We congratulate them. Again, congratulations to Nyabururu Girls. Photo by Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files.
Ekegusii: Below: Students of St. Joseph's Nyabigena Boys. Mbuya mono. Bono Nyabururu Girls High School joins Kisii High School, St. Joseph's Nyabigena Boys, Moi Gesusu and Kereri Girls among the top schools in the larger Gusii Counties. Ntwe twagokiigwe. Again, pongezi ase Nyabururu Girls. Picture na Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files.

English: Of these results, 250 students passed and most of them will go to university. Mr. Chepe said:
Ekegusii: Ase amachibu ayio, abana 250 nigo baeta buya, naende nabo baragende ase chiyunivasiti. Nigo omosike Chepe ateba buna:

English: [ I ]. 266 is the total number of students who did the exams at Nyabururu Girls.
Ekegusii: [ I ]. 266 nero enamba y' abana bonsi bakorete amatemwa ayio korwa ase Nyabururu Girls.

English: [ II ]. 250 is the number of students who passed and will go to university
Ekegusii: [ II ]. 250 Nero enamba y' abana baria baetete buya, naende baragende eyunivasiti

English: [ III ]. A plain means a student got an average grade.
Ekegusii: [ III ]. A Plain nigo enyorire n' omwana oyomo.

English: [ IV ]. A- means there are 30 such students.
Ekegusii: [ IV ]. A- nigo enyorire na abana 30.

English: [ V ]. B+ means there are 44 such students
Ekegusii: [ V ]. B+ nigo enyorire na abana 44

English: [ VI ]. B Plain means there are 61 such students
Ekegusii: [ VI ]. B Plain nigo enyorire na abana 61

English: [ VII ]. C+ represents 49 students.
Ekegusii: [ VII ]. C+ nigo ere ase abana 49.

English: [ VIII ]. C Plain was attained by 7 students.
Ekegusii: [ VIII ]. C Plain nigo yanyorekanete ase abana 7.

English: Commenting on this, the Mean Score is 8.7. It has improved from 8.3 in 2011. We celebrate this very good result and congratulations to Nyabururu Girls High School, for its performance in KCSE 2012. May God continue to bless Kenya.
Ekegusii: Komenta nayio, the Mean Score nigo ere 8.7. Nigo yatiira korwa ase 8.3 ase omwaka o 2011. Ntwe nigo togoteba buna mbuya mono and congratulations ase Nyabururu Girls High School, ase egasi engiya ase KCSE 2012. May God continue to bless Kenya.

English: The History of Mwanyagetinge: Abande Namokwanwa, Leader of the Maeba Clan, The Famous Warrior!
Ekegusii: Emebayeno Ya Mwanyagetinge: Abande Namokwanwa, Timonga Chinkore Chia Maeba, Chigocha Chiaichora Enyongo!

English: People with good intentions who understand this history are asked to come forward and share it with Mwanyagetinge, which has been passed down through generations and elders: Petronilla Ogoti, Gusii.com
Ekegusii: Abaminto omorabaro oyo okobwatia nigo ore oyomo ase emebayeno eri yainto ntwe Mwanyagetinge, eri yateretwe ase enchera y' omoino amo na abagaka baito abakoro: Petronilla Ogoti, Gusii.com

English: Good people should work together to make things easier, so that Abande Namokwanwa, Leader of the Maeba Clan, The Famous Warrior can be remembered. Is this the reason for this story on Mwamogusii?
Ekegusii: Omogaso oyomo tokare koria ritoke omogoye, omogaka sokoro ominto nigo antebetie buna Abande Namokwanwa Timonga Chinkore Chia Maeba, Chigocha Chiaichora enyongo. Bono ninki eng'encho y' omorabaro oyo o Mwamogusii?

English: Gusii Proverbs: Are people discussing this with advice? Returning respect to the family of Maeba, who lived in Kebura Nchogu, South Mugirango, Kisii County. Pictures with Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files.
Ekegusii: Amaridadi a Gusii: Baminto motakomenta echae n' amandasi naende? Kobweria endagera ase enka y' omogaka Maeba, aaria Kebura Nchogu, South Mugirango, Kisii County. Picture na Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files.

English: Truly, gather around, everyone, so that the story of this history can be heard. It is also important to remember that the elder got tired of being disturbed by Maeba. This elder is known to be wise and knowledgeable, and they always have wisdom to share with those who seek it. Furthermore, this elder is still alive today and remembers everything clearly, and their respect for their ancestors remains strong.
Ekegusii: Aaiga, ritangani, sokoro nigo antebetie buna omogano bw' omorabaro yo nore aroro. Nigo sokoro antebetie buna abwo kare kare, omogaka gete narengeo orenge korokwa Maeba. Bono omogaka oyo nigo amanyekanete koba omuya ase ekenyoro kiaye, naende nigo arenge omogaka bw' amasikani ase eng'encho arenge korwa obokonyi bonde bwensi gocha ase ekenyoro eke kiaye. Ase boigo, omogaka oyo nigo ekiage kiaye giachire kera engaki, naende endagera tiyarenge kobora ase enka yaye.

English: Elder Maeba has spoken.
Ekegusii: Omogaka Maeba nigo achiete nguma

English: So Maeba spoke and his children listened carefully. His children were grateful, and they continued to live according to his teachings, and the wisdom he shared helped them overcome challenges and succeed because of Maeba. That person is always helping others, and whenever they see someone struggling, they help them and encourage them to persevere.
Ekegusii: Bono Maeba nigo anchete korageria na koa abaamate baye ebinyugwa. Abaamate baye ekero baigotire, nigo barenge komotera n' omoino bakomotogia, ase eng'encho onde taiyo orenge kobakonya na kobarageria buna Maeba. Omoyega oyo oye nigo orenge korenta abanto oroche, gocha bwoye ekiagera nigo bare koragera na konywa ebinto ao ao.

English: Those who listen to him, their lives will be blessed, just like the clan that benefited from the knowledge. So let the children learn and continue to live according to the traditions of Abande Namokwanwa, Leader of the Maeba Clan, The Famous Warrior!!
Ekegusii: Abanto kibaikire bwoye, nigo enyongo yarenge goterekwa n' amarwa, kere ne chinkore erinde abanto banya gosiberia n' omogoko. Bono ekero abaamate barageire na konywa buya, nigo barenge gotera omoino bagoteba buna Abande Namokwanwa Timonga Chinkore Chia Maeba, Chigocha Chiaichora Enyongo !!

English: Consider this, this story is worth sharing! Respect the elders and people, who tell stories about this week. Goodbye now and thank you for listening.
Ekegusii: Gochakera abwo, omobayeno oyo okaba ogotebwa! Koru ase omogaka sokoro ominto, oyo noro omobayeno oito for this week. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

English: The language of the Gusii people is rich and has a large vocabulary used by both elders and children, including various names. The home is also rich in traditions passed down from parents and grandparents to their children and grandchildren, which are carefully preserved over time.
Ekegusii: Enyangi y’Omogusii nigo yarenge n’engencho enene ase abamura na abaiseke amo ne’chiamate chiabo. Enywomo nero yarenge egetambokero ase omomura n’omoiseke korua ase amaboko abaibori babo na gochaka koagacha omochie obo.

English: In ancient times, the home was not like what it is today. In the past of the Gusii people, skilled craftsmen and builders built houses with their own hands and decorated them beautifully.
Ekegusii: Engaki eyuo, enywomo tiyare koba onye enyangi teraba. Engaki ya kare ase Gusii, omosubati obegete ebitinge nigo are koegwa amasikani amanene kegima, ekiagera oyuo ’ng’ina ’monto (‘banto) okoagacha egesaku. Yare gotoka buna oirerwe kare nchera, nigo are gokobwa goika mwaye, koenekia buna oikire buya.

English: These stories tell us about the history of the Gusii people; these stories of old are told during important ceremonies, which bring joy and unity ('people') together and create a sense of community. It happened that when someone died, they were mourned greatly, and songs were sung to comfort them, hoping they would return.
Ekegusii: Egetabu eke nigo kebwate obosemia obuya kegima ase engaki ya rero; obo obosemia obonene bw’okoagacha emechie, mono kobwatekana buna ense yaonchokire ekero abange batari korora buna enywomo n’egento ki’engencho enene buna egwenerete.

English: Uhuru has been communicating with the government throughout the entire period; Col (rtd) Cyrus Oguna
Ekegusii: Uhuru tabwateraniri na gokong’a kwobogima ime yense; Col (rtd) Cyrus Oguna

English: Written by Zachary Mayieka on July 6, 2022
Ekegusii: Written by Zachary Mayieka on July 6, 2022

English: The spokesperson, Cyrus Oguna, stated that President Uhuru Kenyatta should not be allowed to continue interfering with the affairs of the entire country of Kenya
Ekegusii: Omonogeri bwe eserekali Cyrus Oguna otebire omorai bwense Uhuru Kenyatta tabwenereti gotamerwa ase ogokina kwa amagori yebinto ime yense ya Kenya

English: According to reports from various media outlets, Oguna explained that interference with the affairs and continuous communication secretly causes more harm than good to Kenya under Uhuru.
Ekegusii: Gokwana ne egetaseni ekemo kioboraria , Oguna nigo aenekia buna ogokina kwa amagori nomochando obwateraneti chinse chinyinge aseigo mochando oywo tori o’ Kenya gose Uhuru.

English: He further stated that Uhuru Kenyatta does not want to take responsibility for his actions regarding the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine which has caused great suffering to the people of Kenya.
Ekegusii: Nigo Oguna amentire goteba buna Uhuru Kenyatta tabwati kobua konde gwensi ase chisegi chigendererete gati yense ya Russia na Ukraine eyu egerete anene mono ase ogokina kwobogima bwa abakenya.

English: They are now discussing the differences between Deputy President William Ruto and the allegations that the relationship between President Uhuru and Raila Odinga which was established through a handshake in 2018, led to interference in the affairs of the entire country of Kenya.
Ekegusii: Boigo nairaneria amang’ana yoomokonyi bwomorai bwense omosike William Ruto ase atebete buna ogokwanania gati yomorai bwense omosike Uhuru na Raila odinga okwo komanyekanete buna handshake omwaka bwe chiribu ibere na ikomi na isano na isato (2018), nenchera eyemo esegetete ogokina kwamagori yebinto ime yense ya Kenya.

English: He urged politicians to stop making statements that they cannot fulfill and to focus on uniting the country. He also explained that it is important for leaders to work together, peacefully and with clear goals.
Ekegusii: Obaboririe abanasiasa batige gotumeka amang’ana buna aywo atabwati bokeene bonde bwensi ase okogania kwemanyekani . Boigo naenekia buna koru abarai abwo babere bakwanani, omorembe na amagenderero arorekanire.

English: Bono went to visit his mother in Bitutu village, Manga Esikimu, who is very sick and needs help from Bwanchi Bwamang'eire, Ntengora Bokorigia. Is this the reason he went to see Mwanyagetinge?
Ekegusii: Bono tokare nchera kogenda ase enyangi ya Bitutu aaria Manga Esikimu, omong'ina magokoro baba ominto okare goteba buna Bwanchi Bwamang'eire, Ntengora Bokorigia. Bono ninki eng'encho y' omorabaro oyo gocha ase tore ntwe Mwanyagetinge?

English: Website address: Gusii.com at home in Metamaywa, Borabu, Nyamira County. They say people should compete to help their neighbors who are suffering, so they can get assistance when they need it. When people help each other and work together, it brings joy to everyone!! Mwanyagetinge.com/2014
Ekegusii: Amaridadi ya amaiso: Gusii.com at home aaria Metamaywa, Borabu, Nyamira County. Nabo omoiseke arenge koanga gosiganwa gochia ase omomura oria atancheti. Kobaorokia abamura aba bachire ase ekerorano buna ere tatageti momura oyio, nigo arenge koabusa ekeoreri, riria baikaransire. Bono riria abamura aba baikaransire bakagete buna nkogenigwa bare, enyaroka yachaka koabusa omochi obo !! Mwanyagetinge.com/2014

English: This matter should be investigated further. Yes.
Ekegusii: Chinyangi tichiarenge gokorerwa nchera. Yaya.

English: Friends, these things happen, and life is full of surprises, including challenges. Come on, people, let this issue be resolved quickly!! People should compete, striving to help others.
Ekegusii: Aaiga, aya akwaneire, n' enyangi gati y' moiseke, amo n' omomura. Ritang'ani, baminto manya ng'a chinyangi chia kare nchiagakoreirwe nchera !! Omoiseke nigo arenge gosiganwa, goetera ase okorigia obochege.

English: Bono wants people to compete, and leaders and elders should come together to solve this problem completely, looking at both sides of the story. The truth will prevail, and it will bring peace to the community.
Ekegusii: Bono nonya omoiseke osiganirwe, nigo abagaka amo na abang'ina abanene barenge kounenkia emechie eye ebere, koenekia gose emecheie eyio n' emiya. Emechie emebe, bigo yarenge gotwara obokongu konyora omomura, gose omoiseke omuya.

English: In Ekegusii culture, Okomang'ana always helps those in need, offering support and encouragement. It is important to respect traditions and customs, and to maintain unity and harmony.
Ekegusii: Ase Ekegusii ki' omobayeno oyo, Okomang'ana nakw' ogochoka obwanchani ase enchera endonge, gose okoria oboko. Ekero okonyora ase okonywoma korwa, nigo okonyora kwamang'ire omochi okonywoma koru boikeranu, naende gwatwara obomaene buna oboiri obo n'obuya.

English: The old Gusii people were known for their kindness. It is good to remember the past and learn from our ancestors, so we can continue to live in peace.
Ekegusii: Abagusii abakoro mbamanyete kare. Nigo ere buya kounenkia omochie oria otagete konywoma, gose konywomwa gochi

English: As we look ahead, we should strive to create a better future for our children, ensuring they have access to education and opportunities. This tradition has been passed down through generations, and we must uphold it.
Ekegusii: Ase okoenekia, nigo okoboria abanto erinde otware omogano omuya naende omoikeranu. Enchera ende omobayeno oyo n' ogosegeta buna ekero otagete konywoma, nere buya oenekie kegima buna enyomba okonywoma gose okonywomwa gochi, teri mbe.

English: In the past, the Gusii people did not tolerate injustice, and they stood up against oppression. Today, we must honor their legacy by supporting Bwanchi Bwamang'eire, Ntengora Bokorigia. Let us unite and help those in need, remembering the importance of compassion and empathy.
Ekegusii: Ase engencho Omogusii omokoro atagete chinywomo chitari gosiboka, naende chire n' obwanchani, ekagera agatoa omobayeno oyo ogoteba buna Bwanchi Bwamang'eire, Ntengora Bokorigia. Korwa ase omongina magokoro baba ominto, oyo noro omobayeno oito ase ewiki eye.

English: Thank you very much for listening.
Ekegusii: Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

English: Little children's stories
Ekegusii: Chianga chiane chiesukuru

English: This story is about a child who learns something, big and small. This story is adapted from the "SEED story" developed by the University of KwaZulu-Natal.
Ekegusii: Ase omogano oyo omwana nigo akoerengia chianaga chinge, chinene na echi chimoisane. Omogano oyo nigo orwete ase “SEED story” korwa eyunibasiti ya Kwazulu-Natal.

English: The mother and the pot
Ekegusii: Omotugi n’enasari yaye

English: The story tells of a woman who finds a beautiful pot while walking in the forest. The pot is made of clay and decorated by skilled craftsmen.
Ekegusii: Omogano igora ya ogokonya ebirerwa bieching’iti chikoretwa ase enasari ye chitangana. Ebirerwa ebio nigo bikorerwa nomonto obene na abakonyi bande.

English: How can we make peace?
Ekegusii: Ning’o orobare goika ikomi?

English: How can a person solve a difficult problem through wisdom and intelligence?
Ekegusii: Ning’o orabe omoruoti bweching’iti chiorosana maega yeechui korwa oboruoti?

English: Anansi asks the sky god for stories
Ekegusii: Anansi orenteire abanto emegano

English: Opening a difficult lock
Ekegusii: Kobara chinyang’au chiorosana

English: The lock is very strong and hard to open, but it can be opened with skill and effort.
Ekegusii: Chinyang’au nigo chire nerang’o aseigo chibare buna chigochia konywa amache.

English: A generous person
Ekegusii: Omonto omotambe mono

English: That person who shares this story is a generous person and someone who always helps others and does good deeds. That person is known for their ability to understand and appreciate everything around them.
Ekegusii: Omonto oyo ore ase omogano oyo nigoare omontambe mono na ase igo keregento nigokere ekieng’e na egeke asare. Omonto oyo nigo agotatora obokong’u goetera ase okoreng’ania ebinto bionsi bimoreng’ane.

English: The greedy giant
Ekegusii: Omoguko ogokwana

English: Gusii Culture And Customs CXIX: Is Petronillah Indeed a Daughter, a Woman of Character and Good Reputation?
Ekegusii: Abagusii Culture And Customs CXIX: Bono Petronillah Inee, Omokungu Ngosereta Arenge Na Kobuna Enyomba?

English: Mwanyagetinge.com has been thoroughly investigated. It is through this investigation that we have understood the character of the Gusii woman, her reputation and her household. This investigation reveals things that were hidden, and I now understand how to approach and investigate further. Perhaps, it is because the elder approaches people with kindness that the Gusii community respects them greatly, their reputation and their possessions.
Ekegusii: Mwanyagetinge.com ntwaborigwa riborio. Bono nigo twaborigwa gose omokungu Omogusii ngosereta arenge enyomba. Bono riborio eri kiriaba riikongu, nche nigo naimogete nkagenda o sokoro, koboria. Kinaboria, nigo omogaka sokoro ominto antebetie buna Gusii yaito amang'ana y' egekoro narengeo, ayio arenge ay' eng'encho mono.

English: Sources of information: Gusii.com at home is located at Menyinkwa Market, Nyaribari Chache, Kisii County. Pictures from Petronillah Ogoti, Mwanyagetinge.com files.
Ekegusii: Amaridadi y' amaiso: Gusii.com at home aaria Menyinkwa Market, Nyaribari Chache, Kisii County. Picture na Petronillah Ogoti, Mwanyagetinge.com files.

English: A woman who appreciates good manners is respected!
Ekegusii: Omokungu komumekeria egechuuri nigo yarenge chimuuma!

English: If someone does not want these things to be done, then let things happen as they may, let them be. However, a person should not despise another’s household, but rather appreciate their efforts, so that they can appreciate their own household in return. Yes. Appreciating others is like appreciating the elder’s household.
Ekegusii: Bono onye amang'ana aya tare koba takorwa, nigo ebinto gete ebibe, biare koba. Ase omobwekano, ekero omokungu akoagacha enyomba ebe, naende aseerete obonyansi, tarenge komumekeri enyomba igoro. Yaya. Okomumekeria nigo kwarenge kw' omogaka bw' enyomba.

English: Moreover, remember that when an elder matures, good manners become apparent! This honest person in the household, always appreciates good manners, and the household is well regarded. But if someone doesn’t care, the reputation will not be appreciated. Work hard at it, and you will be praised, people will respect you.
Ekegusii: Naboigo, inyora buna omogaka gakuure, nigo egechuri kiarenge kobunwa! Bono omosacha nyene enyomba, nere orenge komumekeri egechuuri, enyomba keyakorirwe goseretwa. Bono ko onye taiyo, nigo omosereti akoyemumekeri. Korwa abwo, etwani yanyenywa, abanto baragera.

English: It is the elder who is honored, who receives gifts and blessings, even in old age!
Ekegusii: Nigo omogaka akaganyirwe, goikera ekero akoirana bwoye, neba n' emiaka ikomi!

English: However, also know that if an elder is not present, their wisdom still prevails, and they are remembered, receiving gifts and blessings even in old age!
Ekegusii: Ase boigo, nabo yarenge koba buna omogaka nyene tari aange, gose nigo akameneyete aare. Aaiga, onye omogaka oyo tari aang'e, nigo akoganywa, goikera kaa ekero akworoka bwoye, neba n' emiaka ikomi!

English: Comment also on the reputation of the household, so that the reputation of the household is maintained (respect for the household’s foundation). If you work hard at it, it shows that this woman is a good person, possessing qualities, and she won’t lack anything. An honest person in the household always appreciates and works hard to maintain its reputation!
Ekegusii: Komenta nayio omosereti enyomba tarenge gosereta enyomba akore, tatigari orogoma (ensemo gotira y' enyomba ekona ). Aise gokora igo, nigo yarenge boba buna nigo omokungu oyio akoima omosacha oye, eng'encho ende, atagete akwe. Omosacha nyene enyomba nere orenge gosereta na gokora orogoma rwe enyomba!

English: Mr. Amos Wako has been given respect. America has refused that the Constitution of Kenya will not be American. What is it? It seems there is no intention of amending the constitution of Kenya and amending citizens. Truly Mr. Amos Wako fell ill, and he went until he reached Charles Njonjo. He went to wear the suit of the attorney general Njonjo which was very old and almost torn, so it wasn't good to be seen by Americans because they were suspicious. Many leaders of Kenyan politics wore that suit. It was a terrible thing. And now the British have come. Then Mr. Wako calmed down and went to the area near the American Embassy and also the American representative office in Kenya, and the following things happened: 1. Kenyans were angered. They contributed Ksh. 1.7 million for the campaign. But they haven't yet received legal assistance. We don't want the leadership of this politics. He disagreed with Eric Holder with a stamp.
Ekegusii: Mhe. Amos Wako osiekeirwe isiko. Amerika yakanire inga Omonene Bwa Amachiko a Kenya tatacha Amerika. Ase ki? Kiabeire inga tari gokora gasi ya okorenda amachiko a Kenya na korenda Abananchi. Ekero Mhe. Amos Wako aigwa igo, nigo aimoka ogenda impaka o Charles Njonjo. Nigo agenda kwoyia esuti yo omogaka Njonjo ekiagera eyaye konyora terainagwa korwa Amerika ase yachiete gosibigwa. Momanyete abanene ba amachiko Kenya nigo bakobeka esuti eyemo. Ebwate chinchwara. Erio ne richiko Abangeresa baetetie. Nigo Mhe. Wako aminyoka na amagoro impaka aaria ase Embasi Ya Amerika na koa Omotenenri bwa Amerika ime ya Kenya, riuko rikobwatia:1.Abakenya nigo banganchete. Nigo bakongakana Ksh. 1.7 millioni kera omotienyi. Igo bado tibaramenta chialawensi. Inwe timwancheti omonene bwa amachiko aino. Nigo mogoakana Eric Holder chifudi sitampu chioka.

English: 2.We had 50 states. We remember commenting about joining Hawaii in 1959! This matter is confusing. Mention the states. Currently Kenya has 210 constituencies. And we continue with this government.
Ekegusii: 2.Inwe nigo mobwate chistate 50 chioka. Timwanya komenta kende gesa mobeka Hawaii omwaka 1959! Chingaki chiachenchirie. Menta chistate. Intwe Kenya nigo tobwate chikonstituensi 210. Naende intomente echinde.

English: 3.We have many workers from different homes who are Kenyans. The workers of Eric Holder are from Mexico.
Ekegusii: 3.Nimbwate abakori emeremo ba nyomba bonsi bare AbaKenya. Abakori emeremo ba Eric Holder nigo barwete Mexico.

English: 4.There is a suit that goes around the area. And there is trouble with the suit and the cloth coming from Zimbabwe and Sudan. That cloth troubled the citizens. America goes around the area.
Ekegusii: 4.Ira chisuti chiano gochia aaria. Nabo inkogora chisuti amo ne chianga chiane korwa Zimbabwe gose Sudan. Chinse chingiya chianchete Abananchi babo. AmeriKa genda gochia aaria.

English: 5.Kenya has problems. There is no peace anywhere since the politics are disturbed. That is what causes trouble and hardship for the citizens. However, America, it is stable and prosperous. It causes trouble until it reaches the president. Is this good for people? Does history show that the hardship of the citizens is forgotten? Will we forget this president?
Ekegusii: 5.Kenya nigo ebwate omorembe. Teri gosoera onde ase ekoti ekero amachiko abunirwe. Okwo no ogosaria chinsa ne chibesa chia Abananchi. Rakini inwe Amerika, ebina botuko na mogaso. Nigo mogosoera impaka nonya ne presidenti. Imbato ki aba more? Timorochi inga echio ne chibesa chia Abananchi mogotuguta? Imosigete e presidenti yaino?

English: 6.Kenya has 42 ministries. America has 15. Let us not compare them. Okay. Mention the ministries.
Ekegusii: 6.Kenya nigo ebwate chiministri 42. Amerika nigo ebwate 15 chioka. Tiga gotoigwera endamwamu. Kina. Menta chiministri.

English: 7.Let us finish this discussion. Goodbye.
Ekegusii: 7.Kende tikeiyo morankorere. Kwaheri.

English: Petronillah Ogoti, Mwanyagetinge.com
Ekegusii: Petroniilah Ogoti, Mwanyagetinge.com

English: Long ago, years and years ago, Mansamu and Ogasusu had a very big problem. Because of this, they searched for solutions to their problems, and finally they found some peace. With this peace, they found it with their mothers, and then they lived happily.
Ekegusii: Abwo kare kare, emiaka n' emiaka, Mansamu n' Ogasusu mbarenge aroro. Bono aba babere nigo banchaine ekianda gia ikomi, naende nigo bamenyete aamo orosana ime. Aaiga orosana ime, aba babere nigo bamenyete na abamama babo, abwo konye bagotire kegima.

English: When they asked their mothers, Mansamu and Ogasusu were told a strange story, a very strange story. It was surprising, Mansamu said, “What kind of story is this, and what does this story mean?” Below, Mansamu listened carefully to the story they were told.
Ekegusii: Ko baonia abamama babo, Mansamu n' Ogasusu bakagora endagera egotonontera baire nka, koinagera. Ogoitera chindende, Mansamu nigo eboretie buna, "Ndi ngocha goika nka, na kobweria endagera eye?" Below, Mansamu oyio okoayerera gochi nka n' endagera bagorire.

English: That day the weather was very good, and everything looked beautiful. After that, the pot began to boil. Ogasusu and Mansamu wanted something, like the contents of the pot. But Mansamu took a closer look at what was happening, so people wouldn't blame the pot.
Ekegusii: Engaki eyemo omorakera okaba omotindi, n' ebimeri bikaoma mogondo. Korwa abwo, enchara egacha etindi. Ogasusu na Mansamu bakarea mono, ase eng'encho ye enchara. Bono Mansamu agatwara ekerengererio gio okoonia ng'ina, erinde banyore eng'eria tibakwa enchara.

English: They gathered their friends and relatives together, to help them with their work. Ogasusu told Mansamu that she would finish the work. However, despite this, Ogasusu went ahead and did things her own way, and put the leftovers aside.
Ekegusii: Bagatebania babeke abaibori babo chigunia ime na babaire echiro, kobakorera oboonchoreria. Ogasusu akang'aina Mansamu buna mbakunora chigunia echi. Nonya nabo igo, Ogasusu akagenda akabisa ng'ina, na kobeka ebichanchabe eguni eyio ime.

English: When it was time to leave, they asked their mothers, and Ogasusu refused to tell them the secrets of the things they knew, saying they should stop bothering her with those matters! But they insisted on asking their friends and kept searching. When they met, they told each other different stories.
Ekegusii: Ko baika echiro, bakaoni abamama babo, korende Oogasusu agakana buna mbaigora ebinyorini ebi egekogera nigo barabaise kominchoka batame korwa ebinyorini ime! Bono aba bakaonia abaibori babo na koegwa chibesa. Ko bakoirana, bakagora chindagera ao ao.

English: But again Ogasusu just continued to be stubborn!!
Ekegusii: Bono ng'ina Ogasusu oyio okare kwerindori gocha !!

English: They went back to their homes, and remembered the strange story. Quickly, when the story ended, Mansamu grabbed his belongings and ran towards Ogasusu who was still being stubborn, rushing home so they could remember the story!! But Mansamu realized something, which Ogasusu noticed and refused to share.
Ekegusii: Bagoika riabo nyomba, bakarosia endagera egotonontera. Keri keri, riria endagera yayire iga, Mansamu agaakwa n' ekeondoko ekero aroche ng'ina Ogasusu okare kwerindori, gosoa nyomba erinde basange endagera !! Bono Mansamu agasinyua eki agokora, ekiagera nigo Ogasusu among'ainete akaonia ng'ina.

English: After that, Ogasusu and Mansamu became very close.
Ekegusii: Korwa erio, Ogasusu amo n' Mansamu mbachieti koigwana.

English: This is a true story, a story from the heart, a story about kindness. Thank you very much and thank you for listening.
Ekegusii: Oyo noro omogano oito, korwa ase magokoro, ase omokubio oyo. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

Ekegusii: Na Joshua Araka: Gusii.com, Kisii Town. Esagati (October) 23, 2010.

English: Kisii Town. Gusii.com photo file.
Ekegusii: Kisii Town. Gusii.com photo file.

English: Kisii Municipal Council Deputy Mayor Patrick Aming'a Siro lost his seat due to an election petition. Kisii Resident Magistrate Njeri Thuku ruled that the petition was valid because Siro was accused of bribery and influencing voters in Nyaura Ward.
Ekegusii: Kisii Municipal Council Deputy Mayor Patrick Aming'a Siro lost his seat rituko ria igoro. Kisii Resident Magistrate Njeri Thuku nigo arwete obogambi inga Siro taakeretwe kura buya na kobua korwa Nyaura Ward.

English: Kisii Resident Magistrate Thuku ruled that the case was strong enough because there were witnesses, including Charles Ombuna. Witness Ombuna testified that there were irregularities during the 2007 elections, which led to Patrick Siro being elected.
Ekegusii: Kisii Resident Magistrate Thuku nigo arwete obogambi obwo ase ekina kiabegetwe ase ekoti no omokansora omokoro, omosike Charles Ombuna. Kansora Ombuna nigo agoteba inga amagoso narenge aroro ase chikura chio omwaka o 2007, echio chiagerete omosike Patrick Siro akaba omobui.

English: Resident Judge Njeri Thuku stated that “the Nyaura Ward election was free and fair.
