English: Welwitschia (Welwitschia mirabilis) is a unique plant found in the deserts of Namibia and Angola in Africa. Welwitschia itself is very strange because it only has two leaves throughout its life. The plant grows slowly and lives for a very long time, with some specimens living for over a thousand years, appearing like large, old piles. Welwitschia is a plant that survives through fog.
Ekegusii: Welwitscha (Welwitscha mirabilis) nigo kere ekemeri kiamete amatuko amatang’ani amwanyabanto, egekwama ase asinine ase ekengeka ki’enyancha ime ya Namibia na Angola ya maate. Welwitschia maene nigo ore omote korende tori kororekana boigo ekero okororekana ritang’ani. Ekemeri ekegima nigo kebwate ritina erimo rinene ribwate amato abere amanene akwama-aya akororekana buna ebisicha ebinene bieringete bikaba ebigare. Welwitschia ndire ekororekana buna egetunwa ki’eubi.

English: The plant also has a strong stem (like a trunk, woody) - which does not branch like other plants. Welwitschia is a plant that grows from the ground, with its roots (deep and shallow) spreading widely to absorb moisture. The leaves are always green (even when they are old) and have many small ridges on them.
Ekegusii: Ekemeri eke nigo botambe kere ase engaki y’okomera (nonyen’enkaki y, obotobu) – eyio etari gokoreka mono ase ebimeri. Welwitschia n’ekemeri getari koibora gioka, igo ebimeri bibere (egesacha n’egekungu) mbiganeiri korosia entetere. Ebisicha nigo bire buna chichuba (buna biri bie chipaini gose chisikadi)bire gati gati y’amato.

English: This unusual plant can survive extreme heat and drought, and it stores water in its stem and roots.
Ekegusii: Chikoni chinsubati echikwerusekani ekero chiakinire korusia chinteretere chiabo chire chingusu, echio chigosiaru bwango n’embeo.

English: It belongs to the group of plants called Gnetophyta which are related to conifers (Pinophyta). Gnetophyta has three families with similar characteristics: Gnetum vines with shiny leaves, Ephedra - with branches resembling Welwitschia's stems.
Ekegusii: Nigo chigotoka ase ekemeri egekoro gia Gnetophyta ebi bire oboiribwang’e ne chikonifa chikorokwa (Pinophyta). Gnetophyta ebwate ebisaku bitato ebing’ao ekero okorigereri okororekana kwabo: Gnetum lianas ebwate amato amororo, Ephedra – ebwate amagwa amona Welwitschia enyene.

English: Welwitschia is named after the Austrian botanist Friedrich Welwitsch who discovered it in 1860. Welwitschia is also a symbol of Namibia.
Ekegusii: Welwitscha nigo yanyorete erieta riaye korwa ase omonyamete korwa Slovenia okorokwa Friedeich Welwitscha oomwaka o 1860. Welwitschia nkwama ere ase ebendera ya Namibia.

English: Welwitschia also tolerates harsh conditions and is able to live. It needs little rain but also endures strong winds from the ocean. These adaptations allow it to survive in the harsh environment of Welwitschia. A major reason this plant doesn't die is because it has deep roots that reach underground. Its roots spread wide (sometimes up to 2–5 meters wide) absorbing moisture from the soil. It takes Welwitschia a long time to grow and develop, but once established it becomes very strong. The root system is strong and helps support the plant. Also, it continues to grow slowly and remains stable for many years. To survive, Welwitschia relies heavily on fog, which provides moisture to the plant, even though it lives in a dry area. This plant is truly remarkable and shows how plants can adapt to survive in difficult environments.
Ekegusii: Welwitscha nabo ekoigwana bwango n’ase are aomo mono.Tari buna nigo etegemeete embura mono naende nabo ekonyoraamache aisaine korwa ase amare agocha korwa nyancha. Aya n’amang’ana atakeire oinyore ekero okoyosimeka omote o Welwitschia. Esababu enene omote oyo o Welwitschia otari kwama buya n’ekero aobekeire amache amange egereogunda. Igo netakeire chintetere chiasimekea ase omochanga (wchinyeke chibe chimirimita 2–5 ase obogare) ekiagwera amarabaakogacha amache egeka gtari maya ase ogokinna kwaye. Netakeire Welwitschia eumoreru amache n’okorenda okonene gose ebekerwe omoika. Chintetere echikomera ase echuma eyemo. Nabo naende chirasimekwe chibekwe ase etirisa igoro chirigererie maate. Ekero ogosimeka Welwitscha, goika obe omoremereria mono ekiagera ekemeri eke nigo gekwama ng’ora mono nigo ere e dainosa ase ogokwana ekeene. Eise koegwa oborabu obonge moono amo n’amache amange, kemer eke ngekwama gekaokwe ogetige.

English: Long ago, spirits lived amongst people. These spirits were very clever, they started a war, causing great suffering. Quickly, these spirits began to destroy homes and property, leaving people destitute and helpless.
Ekegusii: Abwo kare kare, ebimoni bibere mbiarengeo. Bono ebimoni ebi emaambia eyemo, ngotamboka biare rikori, gochia ekeng'umbu. Keri keri, ebimoni ebi bikarora obooro bogwete inse y' omote, oyio orenge mbarabare.

Through this, the ancestor has destroyed countless homes, causing widespread devastation.

English: Oh! Spirits destroy homes, leading to the collapse of the entire community.
Ekegusii: Kai! Ebimoni bikarora obooro bogasaine gokea kera engaki Ogakondo akoboroma ensemo eyemo, gose nereng'ane eyende.

English: Oh! The ancestor’s actions have caused immense problems indeed!
Ekegusii: Kai! Ogakondo okwerekereire gotiachora obooro bwensi pi!

English: The ancestor tried to rebuild what was destroyed, restoring the homes. He also promised to help the spirits find peace, saying, “Let me assist you, so that you may live together peacefully and restore what has been lost.”
Ekegusii: Ogakondo agakwerekerera koroma ensemo yatigarete, obooro bokaera. Aaiga nario Ogakondo aimogete na gosaba ebimoni ebi okwabera, ogoteba buna "Gaki nyabere, nigo yabeire akong'u koreng'anania obooro obo erinde kera oyomo aire boreng'aine

English: The situation is tense and uncertain near Parliament, there is a lot of commotion and excitement. It involves Kitutu Chache North MP Hon Jimmy Angwenyi, a lot of commotion and excitement is happening, and it seems they are planning something to help.

English: It is time to move forward. This practice which continues to perpetuate FGM and child marriage, shames Kenya. Nyamira County Women's Representative, Hon Alice Chae said that we should forget about the past and encourage the Abagusii people to move on, so that this harmful tradition does not continue.
Ekegusii: It is time to move on. Ching'ong'o chiria still chikwerekererete FGM ase obotindi, Kenya engima. Nyamira County Women's Representative, Mhe Alice Chae nigo agotosemia buna bono yaikire engaki ase intwe Abagusii to move on, korwa ase chinchera chiria chitatokonye gochia ase amatuko a motwe.

English: We need to thank the government for taking action against those who commit these crimes, both current and former officials, including leaders and former leaders, and all those involved in this bad behavior," Hon Angwenyi added. “The future of the Abagusii people depends on ensuring our children are safe” Hon Angwenyi concluded.
Ekegusii: Inche tiindochi buna ninki gekogera eserikali etagete goetia amachiko ayio agoita ekemira, abwo ase ntwe totaraetia richiko rigokana obwanchani gati ya abasacha amo na abasacha bande, gose abakungu am na abakungu bande, ebio bire ebimira bie chinse chinde" Nabo Mhe Angwenyi atebete. "Egekoro kia Abagusii nigo kegoteba buna abaiseke nkonintwa bare aake" Nabo Mhe Angwenyi amentete naende.

English: This matter also concerns Mwingi North MP Hon John Munuve, who supported Hon. Angwenyi and urged everyone to be careful, and emphasized that our children deserve protection. This was also echoed by Nyamira County Women's Representative Hon Alice Chae who agreed and stated she will continue to fight for their rights.
Ekegusii: Bono abwo nario riberera riamentekanete ekero Mwingi North MP Mhe John Munuve, aboretie Mhe. Angwenyi gose ere onintirwe, naende gose n' ekeene buna abaiseke baye banintirwe. Abwo abwo bono nario Nyamira County Women's Representative Mhe Alice Chae aimogete na goteba buna ere nachiete magotwa motwe.

English: And further, Hon Chae added that the law is already in place, and she respects the traditions of her people. "I urge Hon Angwenyi to continue speaking out, to protect our children, and to save lives. And I ask Hon Angwenyi to show compassion to the people, so they don't blame leaders for this harmful tradition,” Hon Chae concluded.
Ekegusii: Ase boigo, nigo Mhe Chae atebete buna ekemira eke nigo kere ekebe, naende giateire amatuko aye. "Nigo ngosaba buna nanga Mhe Angwenyi nigo are omosubati buna inche, oyio ochiete maguta motwe, korende ore moyo. Ase boigo, tiga Mhe Angwenyi atoenekerie buna abasacha bagototama, erinde bagenda konywoma abakungu korwa chinsemo chiria chitari kogenda maguta motwe" Nabo Mhe Chae amentete.

English: Hon. Angwenyi, who is seeking re-election, was escorted out of Parliament. Ekegusii: Omoremi oyo agaansa gokura, ogochachana na gotumatuma gaansa korurwa. Korwa abwo, omoyo okaamba gokwa nga tagenda mogondo, airane gochia bwoye. Nonya nabo igo, mbarabare abwo, omogaka oyomo narengeo oyatengerete amakore aya onsi.

English: Continue investigating and find out what this person’s value is so that people don’t take advantage of them. Little money is enough to make someone forget everything and abandon their responsibilities, so that they can fulfill their desires.

English: By Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com Proverbs, Culture And Customs Editor. February 15, 2011.

English: One who doesn't hurry won't get far." The elders say they can't wait to get old.
Ekegusii: Nintagete kogenda bware" Ebimura binde can't wait kogenda iburu.

English: Old age, wisdom comes with gray hair and experience in the Ekegusii language of our ancestors. People often live for many years, up to eighty or ninety years, before they prepare to become old. But nowadays, old age is celebrated during the month of December at the end of the year.
Ekegusii: Iburu, maguta motwe no okwaroka na amarieta ye Ekegusii yo ogosara. Abaisia ki baikire emiaka ikomi mbaka ikomi ne ebere nigo bare goisanera kogenda iburu. Mara enyinge, iburu nigo yare gochiegwa ase engaki yo omotienyi bwe Egesunte kende (December) ase kera omwaka.

English: People strive for good health so that it may benefit them. They build houses and acquire possessions and livestock so that their homes are beautiful. A home without wealth is not admirable.
Ekegusii: Abaisia nigo bare kwearigania ase omoyega oyo buna ekobwatia. Nigo bare korigia chingoko bagochia konyenya ne ebitugi bio ogouta omorero ekero bare nyomba. Inyora inga morero bwo omware tonya korima.

English: The community gathers to help those who are sick and the youth assist the elderly in preparing for old age. The tradition of honoring the months of old age, those months are when people and relatives visit the aged and share stories.
Ekegusii: Omosari nigo arenge koba oyomo ase ekenyoro ekegima na abasae bataranywoma nabwo bare kobira abaisia ekero bare gochia iburu. Obotuko bwo ogokiera rituko rie enyangi ya iburu, aba be enyangi nigo bare korara na abamura barie bachiete iburu banyenya chingoko.

English: Truly speaking, it is the elderly who remember past events and are reminded through songs and dances about the months of old age. The young ones respect traditions and appreciate gifts.
Ekegusii: Mambia maaambia, nigo abaisia aba bare koirwa roche gwesibia amache amakendu na korurwa ne chinyanduri ne risa egere beariganie ase enyangi eye. Abasegi nigo bare kobogoria amatimo na kweboyia amayo.

English: Poverty is said to prevent someone from understanding things fully. Sometimes, they are given assistance so that they may recover and become strong. Before something valuable is lost, it is better to prepare to become old and strengthen oneself to gather knowledge so that it remains.
Ekegusii: Egetono nigo kiare korosigwa kiamanya koruma buna endo. Aaiga, nigo bare gotebigwa buna endo igo yare kobamera nande yabaroka. Ekero kio ogosarwa gwaikire nigo oyo ore kogenda iburu are gotarera omote gochia magega egere tarora amanyinga buna agoiteka.

English: Work done by women and men is carried out to improve the home. Wealth should be used wisely to ensure that everything is well within the home. If it is not managed properly, it will diminish and disappear quickly.
Ekegusii: Korwa aiga amatera yo obware aterwa kwagachia ase omware are koirwa. Omorero nigo ore gosegeswa bwoka amatuko onsi pi omware are nyomba. Ki yare komochani orime, nigo yare koba chimuma naende yare kobetereria okorerane chisokoro.

English: A person should work hard and diligently, always striving to achieve success. Work alone, however, is not enough; one must also have blessings. A person who has blessings receives gifts and remembers the past.
Ekegusii: Omware nigo are gosoa saiga na korwa gesieri korende tare koirorera goeta gesieri eke. Korwa bono, nigo are gotumia etirisa. Omware nao agasokeire etirisa ochia gwota ensakia korende kera rituko nigo are kweyaka ribu.

English: A home should be protected against thieves until it becomes established. People often save money. That savings, when used to rebuild the home, ensures that the home is secure and work continues.
Ekegusii: Mware tare korora gose gwesibia mache mpaka arwe nyomba. Abare nigo bare kobeka egesena. Abwo nyomba, nigo bare gokora emekubio ene. Engaki eyio ye emekubio ene kiyaerire, nigo yare gokagerwa buna omware obwenire na korwa nyomba.

English: Before starting new work, a person should first assess their resources. They should then begin slowly and carefully. Work done by a person who plans ahead is successful because they know how to manage their time.
Ekegusii: Ekero akorwa nyomba, mware tare gweeta gesierie keri asoerete. Nigo are kogenda roche bwesibia na kweboyia buya. Korwa aiga mware tare korara saiga aria ase arenge nyomba. Nigo are korara ase eamate amatuko abere omanya koirana sobo.

English: Preparing for tomorrow requires a person to be diligent and work consistently, always striving to succeed. Work today, therefore, is important.
Ekegusii: Goansera aiga omware bono nigo are no obosiborwe bwo ogotumia gesieri kende gionsi gia saiga. Bono gochakera engaki eye, momura bwarogete tare gosoa ase abaibori bare korara. Echio ne chimuma. Inee rero enyangi eye nereo?

English: The heart feels like a person who has been troubled and does not understand how to continue studying the matter of the elders and their customs. Let them cry, the heart remembers the elders and their time. So, people say that the elders have power and can cause harm:
Ekegusii: Omongina magokoro baba ominto nigo antebia buna nigo atagete kogenderera gotosomia igoro y' emegiro ende meke aase rituko ria rero. Ase okoinyora, magokoro natotebetie emegiro meke igoro. Ase rero, baba nigo agoteba buna emegiro ende nigo ekobwatia iga:

English: 19. Did he delay coming from Heaven, and when he came down, did he appear like a foolish child? What reason makes him sit quietly and listen to advice: A wise person who understands things well knows how to listen to advice from someone who speaks truthfully and wisely. Why? A wise person needs to learn things. And again, therefore he listens to advice carefully, a leader who knows what is good, knows how to choose good things over bad ones! It is very important.
Ekegusii: 19. Nigo gwatindera aaria bw' Ombati, na gotumbaga kwagachia, gwaiika nka bwoo morogoba botuko? Aye rirorio goika oturere mokao korwa etirisa: Omosacha otamereti chinderu nigo agotura mokaye korwa etirisa onye oikire nka bwoye ekero chinyomba chiasiekirwe. Ninki? Ekiagera omosacha nigo agwenerete komera chinderu. Ase eng’encho ende, ere nigo agotura korwa sukunyuma, omokungu omanya koigora, omanya goeta korwa omorangu boronge! Emeremo emekong'u.

English: That is why: Tradition preserves the history of ancestors. And also this: The truth is that some people do not want others to live a righteous life. But what is the problem? They will be ashamed. The problem is a life that is not aligned with the ways of the ancestors, which has been corrupted by modern times. [ righteousness ]. In ancient Kisii, a person truly respected those who were disciplined. Consider how a parent treats a child, teaching them respect. This is the strength of Kisii culture, which has endured through hardship. Picture and Petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files.
Ekegusii: Abwo nse: Egesanda kebekire erongori y' obori echiete aroro. Naende nse yaye: Ekemunwa keri omogaka sokoro ominto agocha kobekerwa obokima obotongore. Bono egesero ninki? Nabo oraborie. Egesero n’ obokima boria obotang’ani bw’o bori ekero bwagesirwe korwa aase endemero. [ obotongore ]. Aase Ekegusii gia kare, omogaka nyene omochie nere ogatongoire ritangani. Kerabe buna omogaka taaiyo aase omochie oyio, omomura omotangi nere ogatongoire. Gokora magega y' Ekegusii eke nigo yarenge chimuuma. Picture na petronillah Ogoti, Gusii.com files.

English: 21. The problem of old times always remains: Anyone who disrespects the ancestors [ righteousness ], a person who does not value tradition. Similarly, anyone who disrespects parents also does not value tradition. But what is the problem? The problem is a life that is not aligned with the ways of the ancestors, which has been corrupted by modern times [ righteousness ].
Ekegusii: 21. Egesero ngekare miinto rero mogoroba: Onye omosubati ore mwaye ogesire obori [ obotongoire], omogaka nere ogotanga koegwa egesero. Korende onye mogaka taaiyo ase enka eyio, omomura omotangi nere okoegwa egesero. Bono egesero ninki? Egesero n’ obokima obotang’ani bw’obori ekero bwagesiru korwa mogondo [ obotongore ].

English: 22. Remember this point: A wise person does not reveal secrets carelessly. Be careful, and let wisdom guide you. Also, a leader should not be careless, lest they regret it. Let everyone carry their own burden, Kisii people know how to bear it.
Ekegusii: 22. Koramera tikoiyo: Omosacha otanywometi tanya koramera ebwate. Naramera, ere n' chingaki asaretie. Naboigo, omokungu otasogeti nere naramera tirikobwata. Goika aba bonsi baratwara chinka chiabo, Ekegusii kemanye kobwata.

English: 23. I finish speaking these important words: A person carries a heavy burden when they travel and find themselves in a difficult situation. Let them go slowly. Why? Because it is better to be cautious than reckless.
Ekegusii: 23. Nainche nimbwate rikobu rineene: Omonto obwate rikobu rineene tanya kogenda ase ekegege gie chintuga. Agende igo mbobe. Ninki? Nigo chigosira ekero chiabokire.

English: This message brings comfort to the heart. He says that if they accept it, let them remember this thing. Drink these waters, and thank you for listening.
Ekegusii: Chitoro chiabwatire magokoro naende. Nigo ateba buna bwatera abwo, goikera chingaki chiinde. Monywe mache maya, and thank you for listening.

English: Don't despise a small beginning lest you stumble on a large rock, a good heart among people is what helps someone so that the traditions of our ancestors don't disappear completely. Yes. Cherish your family, so that it remembers its roots.
Ekegusii: Tokare kwaa enderema erinde toiyeke igoro morogoba, omong'ina magokoro baba ominto nigo antebetie buna enywomo ya kare tiyarenge eya nchera. Yaya. Konyora omoiseke omuya, nigo yarenge koira amatuko amange.

English: And people remember good things from their families. It is said that one should be careful, and also respect work, so that visitors don't find fault. It is important to help each other always and share problems, so that they can be solved.
Ekegusii: Nigo abairi barenge gotomwa korigia omorabera omuya. Emechi nigo yarenge kounenkigwa, amo n' obotuki bwakorwa, erinde ogweiiti tigocha koba. Nigo omosacha arenge goeta kera aase gose nanyore omokungu ori baranchane, erinde banywomane.

English: This person who helps and shares with others from their family, knows how to cherish their home, understands that cherishing one's children is a good thing for those who haven't matured yet!!
Ekegusii: Bono omosacha oyo gaetire na goetanana kera aase komorigia omokungu oyo omuya, omoerio oye, omanya konyora omwanchwa oye korwa ase atakagerete !!

English: Many people have liked this on Facebook today because of the rock. So let this message reach both young and old so that they come together and support each other in building a strong foundation, and maintain their culture!! For Mwanyagetinge people are many, their families remember well. And anyone who hears this message, let them not lie about it to those who haven't matured. Below: Our Sub-Editors
Ekegusii: Bakaumeranete aaria Facebook igoro moiso onde morogoba, kare kare tata banywomanire. Bono rero nario chingaki chianchokire abamura n' abaiseke baukomerana ase entunde entang'ani, na kobaserana obotuko obwo obwo!! Ase Mwanyagetinge ominto omokoro, omoiseke omuya tarenge gotoka bwango igo. Ase engencho y' okoira chingaki chintambe, nabo omomura arenge konywoma koru aari ase atakagereti. English: So cherish your home, knowing that it is the source of life. The source of life exists, this person will remember the whip, so that they can protect their family, which strengthens the family and makes it more united.
Ekegusii: Bono kanyorire omwanchi oye, omanya gochaka emeroberio y' enyangi. Emeroberio gekoera, omosacha oyo nigo arenge koimokia ritimo, erinde achie kwoyia omokungu oye, ekiagera omokungu nere ogocha korenda enibo.

English: Good hearts among people help those whose homes remember the strong foundation, the land where Mwanyagetinge people live abundantly, Good Tidings From The Land, The Wise Woman, And The Wise Woman Suguta Who Started With A Whip, Wonderful News!!
Ekegusii: Magokoro ominto nigo antebetie buna ase eng'encho kwarenge koira chingaki chintambe, okorigia omokungu omuya nigo kwagerete Mwanyagetinge ominto omokoro agateba buna Amatira Tira Nkorigia, Nyakobitinge, Ani Nyakobitinge Suguta Ogotamboka Na Itimo Koboko, Amanda Agitere !!

English: And in that home, the family's strength is built upon customs and traditions [ Good tidings from the land...] which are remembered. And further, it is built upon maturity. So let it be known, this family will continue to grow stronger, and also the wealth of its members [ Wonderful news...].
Ekegusii: Ase eng'encho ende, omokungu bw' enyangi nigo akorigigwa ase ebitiro amo na ebitirimboko [ Amatira tira Nkorigia..] goikera onyorwa. Ase enchera ende, nigo arenge korigigwa kera aase. Bono kanyorirwe, omokungu oyo nere orenge korenda enibo, amo n' obonda bw' enka yaye [ Amanda agitere..].

English: Work with good hearts Bitutu people, who bring good news eight times this week. Goodbye now and thank you for listening.
Ekegusii: Korwa ase omong'ina magokoro Bitutu ominto, oyo noro omorabaro oito for this week. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

English: 1. A child who cries a lot causes trouble and also causes annoyance. In our Gusii culture, people cry a lot when they are happy and when they cry because of sadness. Anyone who doesn't know how to cry, let them learn how to cry so that when they cry because of sadness, they will be lucky.
Ekegusii: 1. Tori korora risase ase rikorwa na ase rikogenda. Aye nigo ogocha gotaboboka onyore inga bwairire. Ekero ore Gusii, nabo okorora buna omogaso ogoansa mambia naende buna risase rikorimera morogoba. Onye kore ase chinse chinde, goika oakane chibesa otarigwe impaka ase atambe erinde ororore buna risase rikorimera, onye kore ne bahati.

English: Anyone who is a true Gusii person, cries a lot when they are sad.
Ekegusii: Onye tori nka Gusii, tori korora buna risase rikorimera

English: 2. Rats don't have respect. This world is full of people who cause trouble.
Ekegusii: 2. Mache tari gwansa. Ekio nakio egento egetangani okorora.

English: 3. Old men don't have respect. Sometimes old men say things that hurt others, and it is considered bad manners. Let old men speak only good things and avoid saying hurtful words.
Ekegusii: 3. Mabere tari gwansa. Nobeka amabere angana inaki ase echae, aye ne chinsa ogosaria. Egento amabere ye chinse chinde are, nigo abekire ebinto bigokobotia.

English: 4. A foolish person boasts and says, “Today is my day.” In our tradition as Gusii people, boasting is discouraged and said like, “I have finished working at Manoti… Manoti is very far away…”.
Ekegusii: 4. Onde bwensi mokoumerana nigo agokoboria inga, "Aye seino ingai" Korende ekero ore nka seino Gusii, nigo okoborigwa inga, "Aye tori mochokoro o Manoti......Manoti nomosani one.....

English: 5. A lazy person does not succeed. Our ancestors said that laziness leads to poverty, and one should work hard to earn sugar. Don't be idle. Lazy people always complain about their lives like a boat without an oarsman…don’t bother the oarsman…
Ekegusii: 5. Nyoko koro tari gokobisera kende. Ekero okogenda gokwania nyokokoro, nigo agoikoinekera naende okobisera ebisukari. Onde takobikuna. Nyokorome nigo agokonyenyera engoko oteba inga ekebwato eke neki omoigwa....onde tasumbua omoigwa...

English: 6. Birds chirp while pecking at grains in the field. These are small birds. It is appropriate to listen to them and watch them.
Ekegusii: 6. Nyoni tichiri kogoterera rimaambia echuni. Nyoni tichiyo. Nigo obwenerete gweterera aye bweka.

English: 7. People boast as if they own everything. They speak carelessly. In Gusii culture, people brag about owning large farms…they boast about being wealthy and having many wives…what is the benefit of bragging?
Ekegusii: 7. Nigo okona korenda inga ne chinsa irenga chire. Aye negetongu giensa. Ekero ore Gusii okona goaka oboche aaria etuka maate..... gose okona gosiswa etuki na abasani bao... ningo ore na acha n' chinsa?

English: 8. A good custom is a good thing, and a bad custom is a bad thing. A bad custom and a good custom of the Gusii people can ruin someone. Be careful when dealing with people who behave strangely.
Ekegusii: 8. Omogaso ekero ochire, oyio no omogaso. Obokendu ekero bwachire, obwo no obokendu. Obokendu na omogaso o Gusii tona goita onde. Ekero ore ase chinse chinde naende batebe inga ense neche ekende, wewe chunga sana.

English: 9. Greetings. Small birds. Old men who cry. This is a curse. Salt, soda, sugar, cooking fat, millet, sorghum…all those things are not free. Learn from wise people who understand life and appreciate valuable things.
Ekegusii: 9. Chinsaga. Tichiyo. Amabere amaroranu. Echio ne chindoto. Rinagu, risosa, ebisukari, erongori yobori, egesare, rikuneni.. ebio bionsi tibiyo. Goika origi obongaini bonde konyora ebinto ebio.

English: 10. Christmas has come with its joy (remember what was said in point 7 above). In our Gusii culture, Christmas is a time for eating meat and drinking beer.
Ekegusii: 10. Ekerisimasi nerituko erimo rioka (inyora buna aye negetongu giensa - namba 7 igoro). Ekero ore nka Gusii, ekerisimasi nomotienyi omogima na gochi igoro.

English: 11. I remember this Gusii land. Again and again, people boast as if they are Gusii people, associating themselves with the elders.
Ekegusii: 11. Narotire kinde Gusii. Nankio nankio, nigo okona korota buna nao ore nka Gusii, kore amo na abasani bao.

English: Gusii is a land of abundance.
Ekegusii: Gusii n' erwenyi y' omwando.

English: The first Thanksgiving was celebrated by Aida Morgan
Ekegusii: Amaoga a Thanksgiving korwa ase Aida Morgan

English: They wrote about it on November 6th, the pilgrims of England (United Kingdom), in the year 1620. They traveled from another country to a new land. They arrived in Massachusetts, a beautiful place of arrival and rest (America). After a few days, they built houses and prepared to plant. On November 11th, they landed on a rock (American shore), and they remembered their journey to this area called Plymouth Rock. After writing and building boats, the group of 102 passengers thanked God greatly. It was difficult. Sickness and Indians. Hunger. They came to America seeking freedom. In 1607, the colony of Jamestown (Virginia) almost failed, and only half of the 102 passengers survived. But God helped them, and they established a strong colony in Virginia. The colony thrived. And because of God's grace, those people and the Indians became friends and lived together peacefully, thanking God for his help. That tradition of giving thanks continued. In 1789, President George Washington declared that day as a national day of thanksgiving. Later, in 1941, Congress officially designated the fourth Thursday of November as a major American holiday.
Ekegusii: Nigo barwete Bongeresa chitariki 6, omotienyi o Kianda (Tureti ya Kebaki), omwaka 1620. Bagatara ase enyancha ase emetienyi ebere. Bagaika Massachusetts omoerio bwo omotienyi o ikomi na rimo (Egesunte). Nonya nabo igo, ase tarenge aroro agiya ase obwato bwarenge kobekwa. Rakini ase chitariki 11 chio omotienyi o ikomi na kabere (Egesunte Kende), bakanyora ase agiya aaria Plymouth Rock. Nonya banyorete ase bakobeka obwato, emechando ya abanganyi aba 102 korwa Bongeresa konyora teraera. Amarwaire. Chisegi na Abaindi. Enchara. Nigo baigete Amerika engaki yo obokendu. Ekero omotienyi o Kane (Rigwata) omwaka 1607 ochiete goika, konyora enusu ya abanganyi aba 102 bakure. Buna Nyasae abangete, bagasimeka endagera engaki eyio ye Rigwata. Endagera ekama buya. Ase ogoakera Nyase inga imbuya mono, abanganyi aba amo na Abaindi bari barenge abasani bagateba inga tiga omoyega obe aroro bwo ogoakera Nyasae asante. Rituko rio ogoaka inga imbuya mono rikaiborwa. Omwaka o 1789, Omogambi George Washington agateba inga tiga rituko rio ogoaka imbuya mono ribekwe. Rakini nigo yairete impaka omwaka o 1941 ekero Bunge yaetetie inga kera Tichi Kane yo omoerio bwe Egesunte obe eholidei enene Amerika.

English: Today we celebrate that day of thanksgiving and remember God. We celebrate that day remembering the events of that year. Recently, Barack Obama, son of Nyaberi Orongo Manyange, was inaugurated president that year (America). The leaders of the church and the pastor Nyaberi were present. This event was widely publicized and celebrated as a blessing from God in 2009. Greetings, thanksgiving to the readers of Gusii.com. Anyone who has information should visit the website. Share this story with others. Let us thank God for the gift of speaking Ekegusii.
Ekegusii: Inche nigo ingoaka inga imbuya mono ase obomoyo korwa ase Nyasae. Nigo ingoaka inga imbuya mono ase ebisio nanyorire ase omwaka oyo. Akamoisia gaito, Barack Obama Ochwoga Nyaberi Orongo Manyange nigo kaiborwa omotienyi omotangani (Engatiato) omwaka oyo. Abachokoro bo omongina Kerubo no omogaka Nyaberi inkona komentekana bare. Ekio nakio ekeegwa ekenene sana ase inche korwa ase Nyasae ase omwaka o 2009. Eria Kabere, imbuya mono ase abasomi ba Gusii.com. Onye tari inwe nanga ewebusaiti eye teiyo. Ninwe mogotoa omokia kera rituko. Nigo ingoakera Nyasae inga imbuya mono ase okobaa ribaga rio ogosoma Ekegusii.

English: What now? Are you there? Can you hear me clearly? What about resting? Is everything alright? What about building a boat? What about peace and prosperity? How is life going? Come back soon. Praise Jesus for his blessings. The preacher speaks. Let us pray diligently to God. Happy Thanksgiving Day. America celebrates. Kenya celebrates.
Ekegusii: Inee? Aye rende? Inkwaboka bono mambia? Nobwate ase okorara? Kwarire kende rero? Nobwate agachanchabe okona kobeka? Nobwate mosani onde? Moiri onde rende? Buya sana. Tebia Yeso inga imbuya mono. Omonguru bweka. Intobwati kende otatiga korwa ase Nyasae. Rituko rigiya ria Thanksgiving. Amerika Egenderere. Kenya Egenderere.

English: The story of Thanksgiving from Christian Answers.
Ekegusii: Omogano o Thanksgiving korwa ase Christian Answers.

English: The black mulberry tree is a fruit tree belonging to the fig family (Moraceae). It originates from Asia and the islands of the Pacific Ocean. The black mulberry tree grows well in warm climates. The breadfruit tree is closely related to Artocarpus altilis. Artocarpus integer (Cempedak), Artocarpus heterophyllus (Jackfruit, Nangka) and also Artocarpus odoratissimus (Marang) are all members of the breadfruit family.
Ekegusii: Egesaku Omogati bw’amatunda ebwate ang’e chimbego 60 chi’emete machani ye chitropiki korwa ase omochia o Moraceae (omochie o mulberry gose chifigi). Nigo chigotoka ase Asia n’ebisinga bi’enyancha ya pacific. Omogati bw’amatunda nigo ore ang’e kobwakana chifigi. Omogati bwe ritunda osimekire mono nigo ore Artocarpus altilis. Artocarpus integer (Cempedak), Artocarpus heterophyllus (Jackfruit, Nangka) amo amo na Artocarpus odoratissimus (Marang) chionsi echire ase omochie bw’omogati bwa amatunda.

English: Parajubaea torallyi is a palm tree native to South America. Currently, it is mainly cultivated as an ornamental plant by collectors, Bolivia, where it has a significant economic importance due to its large seeds, which are used for oil extraction on the coast.
Ekegusii: Parajubaea torallyi n’omote omuya korwa Amerika ya maate. Korende, tori gosimekwa mono isiko y’ase yachakerete na abaremi, Bolivia, esengencho y’echintetere chiaye chinene, eyio emoneti rigori rinene ase ogoetigwa enyancha.

English: Native to Bolivia, it grows in humid forests and montane forests of the Inter-Andean region at altitudes between 2700–3400 meters above sea level; however, it can also grow at lower altitudes in drier areas. It requires approximately 20 years to reach maturity and a trunk diameter of up to one meter. A mature tree can produce around 7 kilograms of seeds annually (approximately 500 seeds per kilogram) and requires about 550 millimeters of rainfall per year.
Ekegusii: Oiboreire Bolivia, igo okwama ase aome naende are n’ebuse , emetaroekorakwa Inter-Andean chire n’oboigoro bwe chimita 2700–3400 igoro ya nyancha; aseigo, epamu eye nero eimogete igoro ase chikabira chionsi ense engima. Iberera ndiri goetania chidigiri 20 n’obokendu bwa botuko mbioyo. Reberera ngogenda rire inse gioka chidigiri 7 are emetienyi y’obokendu (omotienyi ogatano na kabere na omotienyi o gatano na gatato) n’embura egotwa omwaka omogima nigo ere chi mirimita 550 chioka.

English: Welwitschia (Welwitscha mirabilis) is a unique desert plant endemic to the Namib and Angolan deserts in southwestern Africa. Welwitschia plants are dioecious, meaning they have separate male and female individuals. The adult plant consists of a short stem with two continuously growing leaves that become twisted and shredded over time, forming a massive, tangled mass. Welwitschia reproduces sexually through cones.
Ekegusii: Welwitscha (Welwitscha mirabilis) nigo kere ekemeri kiamete amatuko amatang’ani amwanyabanto, egekwama ase asinine ase ekengeka ki’enyancha ime ya Namibia na Angola ya maate. Welwitschia maene nigo ore omote korende tori kororekana boigo ekero okororekana ritang’ani. Ekemeri ekegima nigo kebwate ritina erimo rinene ribwate amato abere amanene akwama-aya akororekana buna ebisicha ebinene bieringete bikaba ebigare. Welwitschia ndire ekororekana buna egetunwa ki’eubi.

English: Khasi pine (Pinus kesiya) originates from Asia and grows well in mountainous regions, but it is also found in plantations. It reaches heights of 30–35 meters with a trunk diameter of up to one meter. It has small, needle-like leaves arranged in bundles of two, and its bark is reddish-brown. The cones of this pine tree are 5 to 9 centimeters long and 1.5 to 2.5 centimeters wide.
Ekegusii: Ekemeri giepaini ya Khasi (Pinus kesiya) korwa Asia nigo gekwama bwago mono, naende nkeri gotoka raisi isiko ya sobo. Emete nigo egoika chimita 30–35 ase obotambe n’amatina agoika emita eyemo ase obonetu. Kera egesabo ekebwate amagwa amato akobeta atato, kera erimo rire chisentimita 15 goika 20 ase abotambe. Amatunda korwa aekemeri eke nigo are chisentimita 5 goika 9 ne chintetereechire chisentimita 1,5 goika 2,5 ase abotambe.

English: Kalimantan mango (Mangifera casturi) is commonly known as Kasturi mango, a tropical fruit tree reaching heights of 10–30 meters, originating from lowland forests and cultivated near Banjarmasin in Borneo (Indonesia). This type of mango is known for its fragrant aroma. Currently, it is also being grown commercially for its delicious fruits.
Ekegusii: Riembe ria Kalimantan (Mangifera casturi) rimanyire buna Kasturi srire rotunda rie chitripiki ang’e chimita 10–30 ase obotambe erigotoka ase asinine ase akorokwa Banjarmasin ase Borneo ya maate (Indonesia). Amatuko aya riasire gosira ekiagera rikonachwa mono. Korende, nabo rikonya gosimekwa aiga asengencho y’amatunda aye agwansa.

English: It is said this day, the government is good, seeking help from people so that the Gusii nation may be remembered by the Government. We request that the government remember the Gusii nation who have helped the Kisii people.
Ekegusii: Ase omokubio oyo oera, omogaka sokoro ominto natosemia igoro y' Omogusii oria orenge korokwa Omorominta. Ntwarora buna omorominta nigo are Omogusii oria oitete Omosigisi.

English: It is also said, we request that you bring gifts like the Gusii and their clans so that they can remember those clans which were forgotten, they will not fail to assist. Therefore, a person with a good heart should not fail to help them because they have assisted.
Ekegusii: Ase boigo, tokarora buna ogoitana gwaito ntwe Abagusii n' ebisaku binde nigo kwarengeo ase engencho ebisaku ebi binde biatoetanaine, biatagete gotoita. Ase rero, omongina magokoro ominto nigo atagete kobwatera abwo korwa ase sokoro atigerete.

English: Are we understanding correctly? The matter does not exceed showing respect and honoring the differences among the communities and their cultures. Those who understand well are found in Keumbu. Picture with Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com files.
Ekegusii: Tigwachiete nyangi? Rirorio tiyarenge konyarekana ogende ase ekeigoroigoro gi' okoremera ebiranya ase engaki eyio. Abangina nkoiririata bare aaria Keumbu. Picture na Petronillah Ogoti. Gusii.com files.

English: A person who loves people understands that there is a meeting with the Kisii people, differences are being honored greatly. Why honor the differences now? They are asking about it. Differences are greatly honored especially the Kisii people who show kindness to others and their generosity. Also concerning this, we request that you remember the culture of our ancestors during March of this year, so that differences are honored until the Kisii elders are called upon from Esegi Y' Osaosao and Kabianga.
Ekegusii: Omongina baba ominto nigo agoteba buna ase chisegi chiato amo n' Abasigisi, ebiranya nkoremerwa biare. Bono okoremera ebiranya ninki? Nabo oraborie. Ebiranya nigo biare koremerwa erinde Abasigisi aba ababisa baitwe ase obonge. Ase okoinyora, ntwaroche ase eganki y' omotienyi bw' Egetamo (March) omwaka oyo, buna ebiranya biaremeretwe mbaka Abasigisi abange bagaitwa ase Esegi Y' Osaosao amo na Kabianga.

English: Differences are greatly honored indeed. They know how to cooperate with the leaders.
Ekegusii: Ebiranya nigo biare koremerwa nse. Biamanya koragererigwa n' abagaka abanene

English: Therefore, people understand that you should go and see the problems facing the people so that you can help them overcome those challenges. What about these differences? It is about uniting with the people, and they are happy when they are helped. Let it not be forgotten, the leaders should remind the Kisii people.
Ekegusii: Bono baba nigo agoteba buna oyore gosicha ebiigoro igoro nere ore kogenda oremera ebiranya egere bing'use abasigisi. Bono ebiranya ninki? Kobwatekana n' baba ominto, eye n'emete yare gosunyuntwa baremera inse. Ko biaremeirwe nse, abagaka abakoro nigo bare koragereria Abasigisi.

English: Therefore, the Kisii people should rejoice and celebrate, they should sing songs of praise! These problems and the Gusii people who are suffering, it is said that they will be resolved quickly so that they don’t take too long. Comment on this, if they continue they will find solutions!
Ekegusii: Bono Abasigisi bakonyagoka baete rioka, nigo biare kobasiekera, baitwa baera pi! Ebiigoro igoro n'omong'ina Omogusii ogasichire oba buna egosori yare gokorwa botuko korende torenge borogi. Komenta nayio, bari bare koyokora nigo bare koba getirianda!

English: The youth should not be left behind! These problems will be solved by the leaders.
Ekegusii: Mosacha tatakeire igaa! Ebiigoro igoro nigo biare gokorwa n' abakungu boka.

English: People say that those with the leaders should continue. This one you did not understand, go and learn. It is not a small matter, you will understand later and be rewarded accordingly. Gossip is spreading, and all the bad news has been heard that the community’s traditions, customs and values of the Gusii people have been preserved and shown to everyone and their collaborators. They also pray for assistance in resolving the differences and ensuring it doesn’t happen again. Until next time, people love and thank you for listening.
Ekegusii: Abaminto inyora buna aba n' abakungu boka bare koyokora. Oyo otamanyete, tare kogenda. Tari igo rioka, oyotachieti nyangi, taregochi aroro na torekoirwa nka. Chinyabubu nigo chiare gosicha, na aiga obosemi obonge nigo bware koregwa buna enyangi ye ebitinge, kera ekemo kie ebimira bio Omogusii na nigo yaregosicherwa orosana ime na abakorerani ao ao. Nabo omoyega bw' okoremera ebiranya orenge gokorwa igo. Until next time, omongina baba nigo ateba buna bwatera abwo and thank you for listening.

English: Long ago there was a child named Matieko, who greatly loved his mother and father. This child often went to the river to play, sometimes falling and getting hurt. But this child could also go to the river alone, avoiding dangers and carefully watching over himself. Because of this, this child and his parents were happy with that river.
Ekegusii: Abwo ase rinani ria Matieko, ogasusu narenge aroro amo n' ebimanu biaye. Bono Ogasusu gakonya gotara rinani eri ime, akaigwa enchara na gochaka korigia endagera. Buna Ogasusu akonya goeta ase rinani eri iime, akaumera omong'anyi okororekana omotambe gochia ime. Korwa abwo, Ogasusu amo n' ebimanu biaye bigasoa omong'anyi oyo ime.

English: When this child grew up, this child said, “Children who are too young should not be sent.” The first child was small, and the other children followed him closely, and this child watched over himself near the river of Matieko.
Ekegusii: Omwango ase ogoaka esabu, Ogasusu nigo atebete buna "Ebimwana ebi rero goika toigote" Omwana oyomo ore kwaa, n' ebimwana biinde biikomotunyana koru magega, Ogasusu okare korigia endagera aaria ase orosana rwa Matieko.

English: That river was also known as Omansamu. This famous Omansamu always had a way of helping people. When this child reached the river, this child quickly jumped across the water and then climbed a tall tree, and Omansamu was very surprised. He did not expect this child to cross the river like that, so this child made Omansamu laugh.
Ekegusii: Omong'anyi oyo kumbe n' obwe Omansamu. Bono konyora Omansamu osokire isiko gochia koratara. Aaiga ase omong'anyi ime, Ogasusu tanyorete kende giokori korende nyuma ye chintunde chiinke igo, Omansamu akaba oiranire. Konyora atarasoa omong'anyi oye ime, konye Ogasusu okare korora Omansamu gakoirana.

English: This child then went to grow up.
Ekegusii: Ogasusu okare goaka esabu ase obwango

English: This child became very scared, and he went to grow up with fear and thought about what he had done to make Omansamu happy with that river, and he wanted to help this child and his parents.
Ekegusii: Ogasusu akaba n' obwoba obonene, korende agaaka esabu ya bwango na korengereria eki arakore ekiagera Omansamu arenge gosoa omong'anyi oyo ime, nigo arenge gocha koria Ogasusu oyo amo n' ebimanu biaye bionsi pi.

English: This fear caused this child to repeatedly say, “Four children have come and they will drown. That is why I will take this Omansamu and protect him from danger” Omansamu heard these words, and he ran away quickly and began to think about what happened with that river!!
Ekegusii: Obwango obwo obwo, Ogasusu okare goteba goteba buna "Abana bane tiga takwoboa. Bono nigo nkobaitera Omansamu oyo erinde monyare komoria" Omansamu koigwa aya, akaondoka kerage na gochaka gotama korwa ase omong'anyi oyo !!

English: Finally, Omansamu met Okabwe and told him that the river had been causing problems for that river and that he needed to find a way to protect those children from harm. Because of this, Okabwe promised Omansamu to help him, and he vowed to use his power to prevent such things from happening again.
Ekegusii: Keri keri, nario Omansamu aumerete Okabwe na komotebia buna omonto nare osoire omong'anyi oye ime na nigo atagete komoita erinde oyo n' abana baye banyore endagera bakoria. Obwango obwo, Okabwe agatebia Omansamu taoboa nonya, na komotebia amokobe gochia ase omong'anyi oye erinde arore oyo okomoseria korwa bwoye.

English: “Four children, they should not be sent.”
Ekegusii: Abana bane, rero goika toigote

English: Okabwe remembered his kindness towards Omansamu. So when they came to the river, they fell down and started saying, “Four children, we have brought Omansamu and his family to Okabwe. They should not be sent.”
Ekegusii: Okabwe agasibera ekemincha kiaye gochia ase Omansamu. Bono buna bare aang'e n' omong'anyi, bakaigwa eriogi rigosoka korwa ime rigoteba ibuna "Abana bane bono nari twareteirwe Omansamu n' omosani oye Okabwe. Rero goika toigote

English: But when Omansamu heard this, he ran away alone and realized that Okabwe was deceiving him. However, Omansamu didn't understand. When he looked around, he saw a shadow that had been cast upon him, which made Okabwe's tree shake violently!!
Ekegusii: Omansamu buna aigwete aya akaondoka mono na komanya buna Okabwe nigo among'ainete. Aaiga nario Omansamu atagete atame. Buna agasaine gotama, akanyora engori eye asiberetwe nigo yare komong'usa bobe, ekairera ekemincha gi' Okabwe kobutuka amo n' engori !!

English: Omansamu was frightened and ran back to Ogasusu and his children, and they all fled quickly from that river.
Ekegusii: Omansamu akaminchori agatama kwagachia n' Ogasusu amo n' abana baye bakanyora ribaga bagatama korwa omong'anyi oyo.

English: Goodbye my friends. I am going goodbye my messengers who are gathering the Abananchi people this year and next year including the fruits of bananas which are very sweet to the Gusii people. All the messengers of Gusii. Very quickly. Let us carry our baskets together including the fruits of bananas from Gusii. Go and clear the area. The elders of Gusii refused because they did not want to share the profits of farming. Nyambega Gisesa said that the elders of Nyangorora Banana Youth Group agreed to contribute a small amount each towards the bananas and clearing the land. They contributed Ksh. 300. They realized the little contribution they had collected was equivalent to Ksh.1,680. There were also some chips that they contributed. For the bananas, they contributed willingly, eagerly, generously, happily, respectfully, honestly and with cooperation. Is the total value of the fruits and the contributions more than Ksh.6 million?
Ekegusii: Kwaheri ase obotaka.Naende kwaheri ase abajumbe bari bakongaina Abananchi omwaka ase kera omwaka inga emasini ya amatoke neche erosigwe Gusii. Abajumbe bonsi ba Gusii. Obosoku sana. Twatwarire chimbuche toganyete emasini ya amatoke Gusii. Genda gochia aaria. Abasae ba Gusii bakanire inga tibari koganya amangana yo oborimo. Nyambega Gisesa nigo agoteba inga abasae ba Nyangorora Banana Youth Group baansire korosia chindagera ao ao korwa ase amatoke na gochionia ase efaida. ase omobwekano, nigo bakogora ritoke ase Ksh. 300. Bamanya koroisia chichip echio bakoonia ase rigori ria Ksh.1,680. Tari chips chioka bakoroisia. Korwa ase amatoke, nigo bakoroisia obosie,chikeki,ejamu,echuisi,amarwa,chingori,amajambe amo ne chogopia. Emasini eye ne chibesa irenga yaira? Ksh.chimillioni 6.

English: For many years, the farmers of Gusii have been exploited by banana traders who sell them at high prices in major cities of Kenya and make huge profits. Bananas are transported to areas like Kisumu, Kitale, Mombasa, Nairobi, Nakuru and others. The members of Nyangorora Banana Youth Group work hard in their farm near Miriri. Mr. James Omiso and his assistant went to inspect the farm. Near Miriri is about 23 kilometers from Bosongo. Does the road reach Miriri easily? Yes. Are there fences? No. Is there water? There is none. Many birds disturb the farmers. The inspection team visited approximately 44 farmers. Most of them filled out the forms properly. They were grateful for the support from Farm Africa, Kenya Industrial Research Development Institute (Kirdi), International Service for Acquisition of Agri-biotechnology Application (Isaaa) and Kenya Gatsby Trust. The Kirdi office provided seeds. Kitutu Masaba CDF is also working to help improve the storage facilities for bananas. Very good.
Ekegusii: Ase emiaka emenge sana, abaremi ba Gusii nigo bakoriegwa chibesa na abagori ba amatoke abwo bakoyaira ase emechie emenene ya Kenya na koyaonia ase efaida enene sana. Amatoke nigo akoonigwa aaria Kisumu, Kitale, Mombasa, Nairobi, Nakuru na kera ase. Abasae aba ba Nyangorora Banana Youth Goup nigo bagokorera egasi yabo aaria ase omochie o Miriri. Omosike James Omiso nere omonyakerogo bwe ekeombe eke. Omochie o Miriri nigo ore chikilomita 23 korwa Bosongo. Ebara ye ramu nechiete impaka Miriri? Yaya. Amache nangusire? Nonya. Omorero rende? Hakuna. Ayio onsi taratanga abasae aba baito. Ekeombe eke nigo kebwate abasae ange 44. Bonsi nigo baigete fomu fo yoka. Banyorire ogokonywa korwa ase Farm Africa, Kenya Industrial Research Development Institute (Kirdi), International Service for Acquisition of Agri-biotechnology Application (Isaaa) na Kenya Gatsby Trust. Ekeombe kia Kirdi nakio kiabaete emasini. Kitutu Masaba CDF nero iyakora buya ase okobakomboera enyomba ase bakogacha amatoke. Buya sana.

English: In addition, the farmers have formed groups to address the challenges facing banana farming. It's not easy, I am going to try and ensure that the small contribution helps to cover the costs of transporting the bananas. In terms of banana production, we need to invest heavily and rent large farms. We need to encourage innovation. The efforts of the Nyangorora Banana Youth Group are commendable.
Ekegusii: Ase bono iga, abasae abaiga imbaganetie ebara engiya ase chigari chigoetera na amatoke. Tari igo rioka, naende okogania ingotakeire kwa amasakara ya okobeka chindagera echi ekero chiarosigwe korwa ase amatoke. Ase amatuko a motwe, neganeiri gotwara enyomba enene na korenta emasini enene. Intwe nigo togosaba amaya. Egasi engiya abasae ba Nyangorora Banana Youth Group.

English: Rhapidophyllum hystrix is a plant from the large palm family of the palm tree. The leaf is a typical leaf of the genus Rhapidophyllum. It originates from the forests of the southeastern United States. The seed is collected and planted so that about 20 seeds can be transported to Europe each year.
Ekegusii: Rhapidophyllum hystrix n’eyemo ye Chipamu chikoremerereia obokendu obonene ase chimbego chie chipamu. Embego n’eyemo yoka ere ase egesaku kia Rhapidophyllum. Igoogosimekwa ase akendu ase chinsemo chia USA ya maate- moino. Korene n’gesio ase okoremeriria kwaye kw’obokendu bore inse buna chidigiri 20 igo yaanchire monoe getich mono imeya Yuropu.

English: It is also a fan palm, reaching a height of 1–3 meters with a trunk diameter of up to 17.8 cm. Rhapidophyllum Hystrix is a relatively easy-to-grow plant, its roots grow well in shady areas. On fertile soil, the roots become very large. The fan palm does not have climbing roots, but rather roots that reach a length of 1.2 m and a depth of 17.8 cm. The roots are brown, fibrous, and branched. They spread widely, forming a dense network. Once established, they can tolerate drought conditions. The leaves are arranged in a fan shape and are deeply divided. They are green in color and take about 3 years to mature. They are resistant to pests. The fan palm grows well in shade and can withstand cold temperatures. It reproduces through suckers. The fan palm usually grows in moist soils and can also grow in slightly acidic soils. It adapts well to different environments. Its growth rate depends on soil quality, moisture, and temperature. It takes about 3 years for the seedlings to develop a strong root system. However, the palm requires fertile soil to grow quickly and thrive. A healthy palm that is not stressed will produce more shoots. Cold tolerance varies depending on the variety, but most varieties can tolerate temperatures down to -15 to -20 degrees Celsius. Extremely low temperatures below -28 degrees Celsius can cause damage.
Ekegusii: Nigo ere embego y’epamu enkong’u, naende ekwama chimita 1–3 chioka ase obotambe n’amagwa amaya ase ritina. Rhapidophyllum Hystrix igo ere enke ekorusia chimbande raisi, amatina amange akorosia ekemeri ekegare mono. Ase engaki entambe, amatina ayio narosi orosana oronene. Epamu y’esindani teri korosi matina korende ekobi erakine goika chimita 1,2 ase obotambe goika 17,8 ase obogare. Amatina nigo abwate amato amakoro, amatwaro, n’amagwa amatanyerere amatambe. Nigo atirete buya , gose aarare inse ekiagere chikorwanerera oborabu gose ekiriri. Chintetere nigo chigosimekwa ase abwate amache. Ase amiaka 3 ametang’ani. Nigo etakeire chibe are n’obokendu. Epamu y’esindani igo egotaka ase are n’omoika bwa amache naende ebekwe ase omogaso gose ekiriri ementwe omogaso buna egokina. Eekororekana buya ekero chibekire ase ekiriri akeigo. Ekero chiamete ase omogaso omogima, ekobi ekobwatana n’amato asitia ekara machani. Ebimeri bietaneti emiaka 3 nabo bikogachwa isiko y’egeticha ase omwaka omogima onye komenyete ase riberera ritari goetania chidigiri 10. Buna enkendu, epamu ekoremereria obokendu nigo etakeire gosimekwa ase riroba rieteti amache buya naende ebekwemaate. Omobisa omonene bw’epamu eye tari bokendu korende riroba ribwate amache amange. Ribererea riainse mono amo n’eriroba ribwate amache amange nigo agosaria emerio. Epamu eye nabo ekonyara komenyera obokendu chidigiri –15 goika –20. Riberera ria inse mono rimanyire yamenyerete riarenge chidigiri –28.

English: The Clans of the Gusii People, the Council of Elders, they speak like the Gusii.
Ekegusii: Abagambi Ba Abagusii Ekero Omosongo Aigete Nka Gusii

English: They travel far and gather little things, the Gusii people don't understand how to save small amounts of money at all. They are wasteful, but traditions remain strong so they can save something. What is this? My mother tells us about the tradition of saving small amounts of money from time immemorial? But it is said, the Gusii people have forgotten those old ways of saving:
Ekegusii: Ase orogendo amo n' okong'anya gwaito, Abagusii ntwaigete ase tokwebaka amarieta y' ching'iti ao ao. Ase okoboria, ntoratebigwa buna ninki kiagerete tokeebaka iga. Ninki gose? Mbuya ki twaroche ase chingiti echi ekagera tokeebaka amarieta abo? Buna togotebigwa, Abagusii mbebagete amarieta ayio akobwatia:

English: (I). The Herdsmen, they save, Zebras and Wild Animals. Comment on this, it is said that the Herdsmen and the Farmers! The Herdsman who herds cattle is like a Gusii man whose cow has calves! The Gusii people today no longer bother to milk cows until their udders are full! Despite this, they say that the Herdsmen saved enough wealth to buy things:
Ekegusii: (I). Ababasi nigo bebagete, Enchage (Zebra ase Ekenyamorero). Komenta nayio, nigo togotebigwa buna Omobasi n' omongaini! Omobasi nere oorogeti Omogusii buna eng'ombe ekobaswa korwa ebigoti! Abagusii bande nigo barenge konyenya eng'ombe korwa omogongo! Nonya nabo igo, abande nigo bagoteba buna Ababasi nigo babasete eng'era korua omogong'o rika rie ritana, erio bakarokwa Ababasi!

English: (II). The Hunters. Leopards and Wild Animals. The Hunter hunts for leopards. This one also goes to the forest to become a Gusii, and is feared by the Leopard Clan!
Ekegusii: (II). Abagirango. Engo (leopard ase Ekenyamorero). Omogirango nigo agirete koria engo. Oyo nere naende omomura okabere ase Omogusii, naende okorokwa Omogirango Omosweta!

English: (III). The Gatherers. These ones also know that the Baboons and Wild Animals. Comment on this, they also know that the Gatherers are skilled! These ones collect firewood to cook food for the elders, but it is said. It is not always easy. The Gatherer is respected, what does it mean to be a Gusii person among those who are knowledgeable? The clans were respected by the Gusii people and they fought against the Gatherers.
Ekegusii: (III). Abanyaribari. Aba nabwo naende bamanyire buna Abasweta ((Baboon ase Ekenyamorero). Komenta nayio, naende bamanyire buna Abanyaribari Amang'eng'a! Aba nabwo bagatangire esegi ko yatindiire korwa Bomanyi, buna togotebigwa. Tari igo rioka. Omonyaribari nere obarete, gose kobaga Omogusii bwensi ase abeta ritangani. Abagambi bari babarete Abagusii ritangani nao barwete Nyaribari.

English: (IV). The Machoge Clan. It is not the Gatherers who bother to fear the Baboons. The Machoge clan also respect the Baboons and Wild Animals.
Ekegusii: (IV). Abamachoge. Tari Abanyaribari boka barenge kweroka Abasweta. Abamachoge nabarabwo nigo bebagete Abasweta (Baboon ase Ekenyamorero).

English: (V). The Chari Clan. The Shield. The Chari person is the Shield of the Bokendu family! The shield protects the entire Bokendu homestead. I don't know what makes them think that the Chari people will abandon their inheritance.
Ekegusii: (V). Abanchari. Engubo. Omonchari nere Engubo Y' Ndiba chia Bokendu! Engubo nigo yanchete komenya aase amache amakendu ime. Ntwe ntomanyeti gose eke nakio kiagerete Abanchari bakeeroka erieta eri.

English: (VI). The Getutu Clan. These ones are the Baboons who fight (Wild Animals). The Getutu person is a very large man. This one also fears the Land of the Enchogu people, his relatives!
Ekegusii: (VI). Abagetutu. Aba nabwo Abasweta abatang'ani (Baboon ase Ekenyamorero). Omogetutu nere omomura omonene. Oyo nere naende okorokwa Enda Y' Enchogu nyabana bange!

English: From the hearts of our ancestors Kwamboka Mireri and the elder Samuel Omare Nyambisa and Kenyanya Marube, my mother says and thank you for listening.
Ekegusii: Korwa ase omongina magokoro Kwamboka Mireri amo na abagaka chisokoro Samuel Omare Nyambisa amo n' Kenyanya Marube, mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

English: Yes mother. 500 years from now. Our ancestors will remember and cherish this land of Omogusii forever. It is Omogusii who will protect the secrets of our ancestry from Bomanyi, extending to Tabaka through the plains, up to Bogere. Omogusii will move forward and never backward. Below, the plains reach Tabaka Town.
Ekegusii: Eee mbuya. 500 years from now. Abachokororia amo ne ebichembene bonsi mbamanye buna Omogusii narengeo. Nigo Omogusii agambete erwenyi engima korwa Bomanyi, goetera Tabaka ase chigware, mbaka Bogere. Mogusii tarenge mworo naende tarenge kwegesa. Below, kobacha chigware aaria Tabaka Town.

English: Clemencia’s question: How can we get rid of this old culture, customs and traditions? What things bother me?
Ekegusii: Omong'ina Clemencia: Bono ninki mokonya korikera igoro ya outdated culture, customs and traditions? Ebinto ebi mbibakonye?

English: Jared Nyaberi: Really! Mother, what should we do?
Ekegusii: Jared Nyaberi: Obe! Omongina baba ominto, Nintwe bono okoboria?

English: Clemencia’s question: Yes my child. Isn't it good to learn about Gusii.com?
Ekegusii: Omong'ina Clemencia: Ee mwana. Gete ninwe mokorika abw' ase Gusii.com?

English: Jared Nyaberi: Yes mother, some traditions and customs seem outdated, but we need to respect and preserve them, so that future generations know the history of Omogusii. This land of Omogusii forever. The plains extend to the hills and valleys of Abagusii.
Ekegusii: Jared Nyaberi: Ee gaki omong'ina nonye some traditions and customs chiabeire outdated, ntwe okogania gwaito n' ogochirika nse, erinde abande bagotobwatia nario barache komanya buna Omogusii akamenyire. Buna Omogusii narengeo. Kogacha amariko y' Abagusii ase ebigori ebike.

English: Clemencia’s question: Okay, I understand, but how can we achieve this and progress?
Ekegusii: Omong'ina Clemencia: Nche ndoche buna ne chinsa mosaretie. Igo bono timobwati gasi ende mogokora?

English: Jared Nyaberi: Mother, don't worry, we will make progress. If we work hard today, we will be able to manage our affairs well, and develop Ekegusii.
Ekegusii: Jared Nyaberi: Gaki omongina mako moke, ntobwate chigasi togokora. Ekero twakorire chigasi echio, nario togocha twamanya kona konanageria aaiga, ase Ekegusii.

Ekegusii: Amorokererio y'ogoteba ng'a ebinto nigo bikororekana koreng'ana buna Nyasae achorete omonyene, ogocheneka omonto akona konyora ng'ora ng'ora, ayio naro amorokererio amanene y'obokristo naro arentete obotantanu, na ogoiserwa ime ase chinkoro chi'abegeni. English: Many good things have been said, people say that when someone has many children they feel happy because those children bring honor to their home. Also, concerning marriage, our mothers say that a woman who has cattle, goats, and cows feels proud and respects her husband. She also says that a person should raise a child and teach their siblings so that they grow up well. Many mothers today no longer want to listen to advice, a child nowadays does not respect elders anymore.
Ekegusii: Nonya bono chingaki chiaonchokire, omogaka sokoro ominto nigo antebetie buna abakoro baito nigo barenge gokora ebinto buya omono. Bono onye moamate onde narengeo otarenge gocha goikerana, omwana naende nigo arenge koegwa egetari, omoirera.

Ekegusii: Abagusii abakoronigo banchete oboamate obuya amo n' omorembe.

English: Behold, I declare unto you, concerning all things, both spiritual and temporal: Hearken, ye heavens, and give ear to the words of my servant, Jesus Christ, we bear record of this church which is built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, yea, and also of the people of Nephi and their brethren, and also of the people of Jared, who were spared because of their faithfulness. And we know that they were preserved by the power of God, which was manifested in them through the workings of miracles; and also we know that they were led by him through the wilderness, and he provided for them in all their needs. And it came to pass that we bear witness of the truth of these things which are written; and also that they were delivered by the hand of God, and also by his power, and also by his grace. And we testify that we have seen with our eyes and heard with our ears, and we have felt the power of God working within us to bring about these wondrous events, and to strengthen our faith in the work of salvation, and to fill our hearts with joy. And we testify that we know that the gospel of God, our Father, and of his Son Jesus Christ, is true and will be established throughout the earth, and that all men shall come unto him and be saved. And we exhort you to open your hearts and receive the truth, and to forsake your sins and turn unto God, that you may find peace and eternal life. And let the glory of the Lord be upon you. And also, the kingdom of God shall be revealed unto you, that you may understand the mysteries of his plan, and that you may prepare yourselves for the day when he shall return to reign in glory. And we testify that whosoever believeth on Jesus Christ shall be saved, and shall receive remission of his sins, and shall inherit eternal life, and shall dwell with God forever and ever, and shall rejoice in the blessings of his kingdom, and shall know that he is blessed. And honor be unto the Father, and the Son, and unto the Holy Ghost, who are one God. Amen.
Ekegusii: Komanyekana ase chinse chionsi, ebisaku, emenwa ao ao na abanto: Erinde intwe, ase obuya bwa Nyasae tata na omotoria oito Yeso Kristo, twarorire chibao echio chiyabwate amang’ana aya, ayio are amang’ana ya abanto ba Nephi naboigo aya AbaLamani, nabamura bamwabo, naboigo na abanto ba Jaredi, oria obeire ogokwanwa. Na twamanyire ng’a nabete agoonchorerigwa ase ekeegwa na chinguru chia Nyasae, ekiagera eriogi riaigwegete na korwa amang’ana aya ase tore; ase ayio nigo tomanyete na tore nekeene ng’a emeremo eye ney’ekeene. Na boigo nigo tokoorokia ng’a twarorire obweng’e bwa amariko aya ane ase chibao echi; naboigo obeire akworokigwa ase tore goetera ase chinguru chia Nyasae, na tari omonto. Na nigo togoteba ase amang’ana y’obwororo, ng’a omomaraika onyasae nachete inse korwa igoro, na akayareta na koyabeka ase tore ase obogima bwaito tokarigereria na korora chibao chiamariko, na obwenge boria boreo; na nigo tomanyete ng’a nase engencho y’obuya bwa Nyasae Tata na Omonene Yeso Kristo, bwagerete tokarigereria nakorwa amang’ana aya ng’a nigo are ayekeene. Na nigo kore ogoichana ase amaiso aito. Naboigo eriogi ri’Omonene nigo riatochigete ng’a tobe tokoboorokia oborori bwaito igoro ya amang’ana aya asayio, koba omoigweri ase amachiko a Nyasae, tokarwa oborori obo ase igoro yebinto ebi. Na nigo tomanyete ng’a onye tore abegenwa ase Yeso Kristo, goika toorokie chiganchwa chiaito chia, amanyinga a mwanyabanto bonsi, na chinyorekane chitari na kemoa ase obosio bw’ekerogo giekina gia Kristo, na tomenye nere kare na kare igoro. Na obonene bobe ase Tata, na Omwana, na ase Omoika Omochenu, abwe bare Nyasae oyomo. Amina.

English: This strength of the people should be recognized, and discussed by the elders of Etureti, especially those with wisdom and experience. In Etureti, the elders should stop hiding the children from the world, so they can speak about what is happening!
Ekegusii: Bono omosacha oyo omonyaka nigo arenge korobekanigwa, na kogambigwa n' abagaka aba b' Etureti, abwo ase chingaki echio chinkoro. Gaikigwe ase Etureti, nigo abagaka aba barenge kobeka ebinyuso ase chimioro chiabo, erinde bagamba ekina eke ki' obonyaka!

It is connected to the elder, the true meaning of this history is revealed over time, and it benefits both present and future generations.
Ekegusii: Bono ebinyunso n' ebiaki tata? Ase omorabaro oyo, okobeka ebinyunso chimioro nigo ere omobwekano bw' ogwetanga koru ase obotioku obo bwabeire ase ekenyoro, kobwatekana n' obonyaka bwo omosacha oyo. Ekegusii: Oyo noro omobayeno oito korwa ase sokoro gochia ase abana ba Mwanyagetinge for this week. Mbuya mono and thank you for listening.

English: So if you meet that grandfather who has good stories, remember the time when he raised his child and taught him how to respect others, so he could walk on the right path. So that grandfather succeeded, because those good stories helped the child understand things and learn from them.
Ekegusii: Buna ere botambe omoremi oyo agatiga esese yaye egesumwa ime mbarabare nase aarereti omwana oye anchete kerage, akagende echiro korigia endagera. English: Those stories, which brought joy to both him and the child, were important and made the child feel safe and secure. Those people fought sometimes, making the child afraid.
