English: They celebrated with the saying “A good seed grows well during a field trip”, so with joy and enthusiasm they visited the area of The Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Festival, Keroka Town, recently. Initially, I was hesitant, but when I saw it, I liked it, and I felt proud of our culture and heritage because the Abagusii people were represented, and things were done well.
Ekegusii: Bagoteba ng'a "Rero mochokoro goika tokoire e field trip", sokoro amo na magokoro nigo bangira aaria ase The Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Festival, Keroka Town, recently. Initially, nigo narutete chintacho, korende ki naika aroro, nigo nabete no omogoko ase ogosomigwa na kwoorokigwa buna Abagusii twakabeire, ne ebinto twagatumiire.

English: Unless we visit the museum which displays our artifacts and our customs of the Abagusii people, and this is the best repository we have for now, with The Otenyo Cultural Group, and others scattered online too. It is possible that artifacts of Omogusii are elsewhere, and they are scattered in many places. Therefore we have no central repository. We hope that things will change in the next few years with the establishment of the Omogusii Museum and Cultural Center.
Ekegusii: Unless twaagachire e museum yaito ekogacha our artifacts amo no omogano oito bwa Abagusii, eye nero the best repository we have for now, with The Otenyo Cultural Group, and others scattered online buna eye. It is possible nga artifacts chio Omogusii ne chinyinge, and they are scattered in many places. Korende we have no central repository. We hope that things will change in the next few years with the establishment of the Omogusii Museum and Cultural Center.

English: Also, praise to the Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Troupe for their efforts to preserve the few artifacts that are left with us. In addition, the Otenyo Troupe has been instrumental in teaching us our history and traditions which are being forgotten fast. Thank you for your selfless efforts.
Ekegusii: Ase boigo, mbuya mono to the Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Troupe ase efforts babwate to preserve the few artifacts that are left with us. In addition, the Otenyo Troupe has been instrumental in teaching us our history and traditions which are being forgotten fast. Thank you for your selfless efforts.

English: And to our readers, thank you for visiting and our cultural feature follows. Enjoy.
Ekegusii: And to our readers, thank you for visiting and our cultural feature follows. Enjoy.

English: Stories
Ekegusii: Ebitinge

English: The life of the Omogusii person is incomplete without stories. Without stories, life is empty. The ancestors of Gusii greatly valued stories and their importance. Stories also served as a way of entertainment.
Ekegusii: Enywomo yo Omogusii tiyare koera onye bitinge tibiyo. Without ebitinge, igo nywomo teraba. Omosubati o Gusii nigo arenge gotimigwa ebitinge ase ekero kie enyangi. Ebitinge nabio biare koba buna chibeta echi chie ekerero.

English: Why are stories disappearing? This issue is becoming increasingly difficult to address. Ancestors used to tell stories at night and in the evenings. People who had time would gather in the evening and listen. Those who had time in the afternoon would also gather and listen.
Ekegusii: Inaki ebitinge biare koroisigwa? Chintere chie etarimbo nigo chiare kobutorwa ebing'ese ebingese. Omosubati obwate okogoro okogare nigo are konacherwa ebing'ese bitano na kemo. Oyo obwate okogoro ogosiniini nigo are are konachera ebing'ese bitano.

English: To understand properly, be careful. Do this, a bull is slaughtered. Share among yourselves the meat. Whoever steals, let them be taken to the river to be cleansed. Be mindful. Do this, people know how to respect a beautiful calf that doesn't wander off.
Ekegusii: Kwamanya korambora okogoro, bia bekwa. Korwa abwo, risangwa rie eng'ombe rianachwa. Barietanani ase okogoro ime. Onye ebibao bigotigara, nigo bare kobeka emurwa yaticha. Mangana taraera. Korwa abwo, bamanya koyeaka egetinya egere kiororobe.

English: And nowadays, people want to know whether a story is true or false.
Ekegusii: Ase omoerio, nigo bare goaka etago kiamanya koba egetinge na koba ekieni.

English: Below, some stories of Omogusii and their meanings are presented.
Ekegusii: Below, egetinge kio Omogusii buna kiarenge kororekana.

English: Ceremonies Ao Ao
Ekegusii: Ebibekerero Ao Ao

English: The Omogusii people greatly value ceremonies that are performed and celebrations with their peers. Let us see a few, starting with the picture below. Look and remember: Oroteru. Oroteru was a special container for storing millet, beans, and other grains.
Ekegusii: Omogusii nigo arenge koroisia ebibekero ebinge kobwatekana buna okogania ne egasi yabo. Let us see a few, starting with the picture below. Gochakera ase okobee motwe: Oroteru. Oroteru narwo rware koirura obori, amaemba, ching'ende gose chibando.

English: Comment further, Oroteru also was used to display items temporarily. The lid of Oroteru was strong. The grain and beans were carefully stored, the lid, together with its handle were also made to last.
Ekegusii: Komenta nayio, oroteru nabo rware gotumeka ase okogachera endagera temporarily. Ime yo oroteru oro nigo toroche ensio. Ekero obori gose amaemba arenge gosiegwa, ensio, together with orogena nabio biare gotumeka ase ogosia.

English: The handle and the lid were made from wood and skillfully carved so that the container wouldn't fall and break. The elders also used to say this. Anyone who didn't appreciate it, knew that the handle was made to protect the container and its contents, knowing how important it was.
Ekegusii: Orogena amo ne ensio nigo are koiywa korwa ase egetare gose rigena ritari koburoka riamanya goturwa. Abasacha nabwo bare gokora aya. Onye aye ki bwanchete ributi, manya ng'a orogena narwo rware gosia obori ne ememera, yamanya koroisia ributi rigwansa.

English: Behind Oroteru to the left is Egekabu. Egekabu was a place to put items temporarily, like a shelf where things could be placed. Comment further, Egekabu also was made to last and serve generations, being used to store various items.
Ekegusii: Behind oroteru to the left ne egekabu. Egekabu nakio kiare kobeka endagera buna chinyeni ekero chikwau korwa mogondo. Komenta nayio, egekabu nabo kiarenge gotumeka kobeka kende gionsi kiarenge koirwa ase obogeni gose echiro.

English: The seat of Ebundo
Ekegusii: Riroba rie ebundo

English: Next to Egekabu on the left is Enyongo. Enyongo was used for grinding, especially during the preparation of Ebundo. Enyongo was also made to display tools, knives...
Ekegusii: Magega ye egekabu on the left ne enyongo. Enyongo nigo yare koroisigwa korwa ase riroba rie ebundo, riamanya gosambwa. Enyongo nigo yare gotumeka kogacha amache, amarwa, ributi....

English: Immediately behind Oroteru is Ekebari. The opening of Ekebari is for displaying items. But if the shelf was full, it was used to hold Ekebari itself. Ekebari and its surroundings (not pictured) were also used to display items.
Ekegusii: Immediately behind oroteru nigo tobwate ekebari. Emeremo ye ekebari no okogacha endagera. Buna bono ekero endagera yagesirwe, nigo yare kobekwa ekebari ime korwa mogondo. Ekebari amo ne egetonga (not pictured) nabio biare korusia endagera mogondo.

English: Right behind Ekebari towards the center left are Ebirandi. A discussion about Ebirandi is further down in this article. Next to Ebirandi, we have Chinyakaruga. Chinyakaruga was used to store various items for safekeeping. These included medicine, animal hides, clothing… all sorts of things were kept inside Chinyakaruga. There is more discussion about Chinyakaruga further down.
Ekegusii: Right behind ekebari gochia center left ,ne ebirandi. E discussion ye ebirandi is further down in this article. Magega ye ebirandi, we have chinyakaruga. Enyakaruga nero yarenge gokora egasi yo okoiyeka endagera. Endagera eng'asu buna enyama ya nda, obokima bwo obori, erongori yo obori..... ebitoche ebi bionsi nigo biakaiyekeirwe ime ye enyakaruga. There is more discussion ye enyakaruga further down.

English: For remembrance, and for future generations, let those with knowledge and wisdom also teach others what they have learned.
Ekegusii: Ase okorigereria, nabo okorora nga, abamagokoro amo ne chisokoro chiato nabo chiaroisetie ebinto bio okwerenda buya egere togaika igaa.

English: The Handle And Lid Of Mwamogusii
Ekegusii: Orogena Ne Ensio ya Mwamogusii

English: Animal hides, knife sheaths, containers… everything needs a handle and lid. This is how things were originally done by the Gusii people. Our ancestors also valued tradition. It was backbreaking work making them at the time, our ancestors did not give up. Below, the handle and lid of Omogusii can be seen.
Ekegusii: Obokima bwo obori, ememera ya amarwa, obosie bwe erongori.....Ebi bionsi tibiare koba without orogena ne ensio. Eye nero etinga entangani naende original yo Omogusii. Abasubati nabwo bagasire obosie. It was backbreaking work korende at the time, abasubati tibare gokumia. Below, orogena amo ne ensio yo Omogusii buna biare kororekana.

English: The Customs Of The Gusii People
Ekegusii: Obokano Bwo Omogusii

English: They were respected in ancient times. Ancient customs of the Gusii people. Children today, will they be able to inherit the wealth of their ancestors? Preserve the customs. Was Sarange remembered in the past? Remember to preserve the customs. Did Ogosi’s father get land from Obinge? Don’t let people forget the importance of preserving customs.
Ekegusii: Nabwo bakairirwe ase kera enyangi. Kera ase omoyega omuya bwo Omogusii. Abana nkogenda bare iburu gose kobekerwa maguta motwe? Renta obokano. Enyaroka Sarange nkoywomwa ekare? Sokoro renta obokano. Ntwaigwete ng'a omogeni natogete aaria bwo omogaka Obinge? Tata ominto tera omoino na kobugia obokano.

English: It was crafted using materials from the forest, including wood and bamboo. Why wood and bamboo? Because they were readily available. Below, the customs of the Gusii people are displayed. On the right, old men like Gesare are shown demonstrating.
Ekegusii: Nigo bwakaroserigwe korwa ase omote bwo omotembe, risangwa amo no obongori botano na botato. Why obongori botano na botato? Ntoranyora ichibu korende nkoririgia tore. Below, Obokano bwo Omogusii buna bwakabeire. On the right, omosubati Gesare nkonyegeria are amareko.

English: People were given a chance to showcase their skills with animal hides at Chinyakaruga. Also, they were allowed to display their crafts and artistry. People shouldn’t think that only important items are stored inside Chinyakaruga! Anyone who wants to learn should try it sometime.
Ekegusii: Abande ntwanyorete e chance yo okoiyekerwa enyama ya nda ase enyakaruga. Ase boigo, tokaiyekerwa engoko no omosori. Baminto gento tikeri ekiya buna ogosenyenta endagera eiyekire ime ye enyakaruga! Onye gotagete koragera buya pi, you should try it some time.

English: Chinyakaruga greatly helped the Gusii people secure their possessions. Below, showing how it was used, Chinyakaruga of the Gusii and its contents, containing animal hides inside.
Ekegusii: Enyakaruga nero yakinetie Abagusii abakoro ekagera togaika igaa. Below, buna yakarorekanire, enyakaruga yo Omogusii amo ne ekeburugo, biganyete enyama ya nda ebekwe ime.

English: When hides become dirty and worn out, they are taken to be cleaned thoroughly. And when cleaning the hides, the Gusii people use special stones. Once the hides have been cleaned with the stones, they become smooth.
Ekegusii: Ko obori gose amaemba amire na kwoma, goika arenge korusigwa echafu yonsi magega yo ogosiegwa. Ase okorusia obori gose amaemba echafu, nigo Abagusii barenge gotumia ekonu. Nigo obori bwakabekirwe ekonu ime, bwamanya gosunyuntwa.

English: After this process, they are dried and polished. Stones are used to polish them by skilled artisans. They say that everything about Gusii culture is unique. To the right of the stone, there is a grinding stone.
Ekegusii: Korwa abwo, bwamanya koirurwa no oroteru. Ekonu nigo yare koroisigwa na abasacha. Ase okoroisia ekonu, abasacha nigo barenge gotumia omote bwo omotembe. Timanyeti gose emetembe netigarete Gusii. Right nse ye ekonu, nigo toroche egesero.

English: What is a grinding stone? A grinding stone is made from wood, and used for grinding grains. It is strong and durable, and everything is ground using it. This includes millet. It is also used to grind maize so that it can be stored for future use. Below, that stone on top of the grinding stone to the left.
Ekegusii: Bono egesero ninki? Egesero ne risangwa rie embori, engombe gose engondi. Ge etugo yanyenyirwe, kende gionsi tikiare gotugutwa. This includes risankwa. Risangwa nabo riarenge gotumeka buna oboraro, kobekerera endagera ase ekeoreri ekero ekwoma gose teiteka gochia riroba nse. Below, ekonu eyio on top of egesero to the left.

English: Once the grain has been ground with the stone, it is dried and polished so that it doesn’t spoil. Grind the grain well, then store it inside a container so that it doesn’t spoil. What is a container?
Ekegusii: Ekero endagera yarosigwe ne ekonu, nigo yare koirurwa no oroteru erinde yamanya kogachwa irongo. Konyora etarairwa irongo, endagera nigo yare kobekwa ime yo omonyoncho ime yamanya kogachwa. Bono rende omonyoncho ninki?

English: A container is made from bark and is very large. Its sides are decorated, until the container is finished. How do you make a container? Artisans also create containers. After polishing it, the container is used to store hides and other valuables.
Ekegusii: Omonyoncho nigo orenge koroisigwa buna ekebari korende nigo orenge omonene. Ebirundu nabio biare gokorekanigwa, mbaka omonyoncho omanya koba. Ningo orenge koroisia omonyoncho? Abasacha nabwo bakarosirie emenyoncho. Ko oroisirie buya, omonyoncho nigo orenge kogacha obori ase amatuko amange.

English: The history of Mwamogusii
Ekegusii: Enduruche y' Mwamogusii

English: Because the Gusii people were surrounded by many enemies, and they didn’t understand each other, they decided to create defenses to protect themselves. We won’t give up. The Gusii people had weapons like spears, shields, clubs, arrows, and others.
Ekegusii: Because Abagusii twabebekaine ne ebisaku binde ebitindi, naende biatagete gotoita, goika twarenge koroisia ebibekerero bio okorwana. Titware gokira igo. Omogusii nigo abwate amatimo, chinsara, chinguba, chinungu, amo ne ebinde buna chinduruche.

English: History is used to remember events and teach future generations. Everything is remembered through history and passed down! Below, the history of the Gusii people will be explained.
Ekegusii: Enduruche nigo yarenge gotumeka koruta ebinto buna amagena gochia ase ababisa. Kende gionsi kiare korutwa ne enduruche nigo kiarenge kominyoka ne chimbero chimbariri! Below, enduruche yo Omogusii buna yarenge kororekana.

English: Traditions
Ekegusii: Obokombe

English: It is difficult to imagine how the customs of the Gusii people survived throughout all those years while facing challenges. We shouldn’t forget that the Gusii people were brave for many years. But now, we still have our traditions, which connect us to our ancestors who lived long ago.
Ekegusii: It is hard to imagine how ororeri rwo Omogusii survived ase emiaka eye yonsi kobwatekana ne ebibekeroro twabwate. Temanyekaneti nga Abagusii twabeire abaremi ase emiaka erenga. Korende nonya nabo igo, nao tore igaa ase engencho abangina na abagaka abakoro barigetie chinchera chio ogotorageria.

English: The Gusii and their neighbors.
Ekegusii: Omogusii no omong'aini.

English: In ancient times, the Gusii people defended their traditions fiercely. These traditions included things like ceremonies, dances, hides, clothing, songs…and more. Below, the traditions of the Gusii people will be described.
Ekegusii: Ase oboremi, Omogusii nigo aroisetie obokombe bwe rigena. Amakombe aya naro arenge gotumeka ase oboremi bwe chibando, amatoke, obori, amaemba, chinsaga....kera egento. Below, obokombe bwo Omogusii buna bwakabeire.

English: We were surrounded by enemies. We had many neighbors who fought against us, such as the Abamanyi, Abagere, Abamansae, and Abasigisi. These neighbors caused us a lot of trouble and tried to take our land and property.
Ekegusii: Nigo Mwanyagetinge twarenge surrounded by enemies. Nigo twabwate abanto bande babebekaine naintwe buna Abamanyi, Abagere, Abamansae amo na Abasigisi. Abanto aba be ebisaku ebi binde bionsi nigo barenge gotorwania ntwe, erinde baire etugo gose amaremo aito.

English: We refused to surrender.
Ekegusii: Ntwarenge kwegembera.

English: Along with the warriors, this is where the shield of Mwanyagetinge came in. The elders used the shield to defend the Gusii community. The shield was made from cowhide.
Ekegusii: Together with ebirwanero binde, this is where enguba y' Mwanyagetinge came in. Abamura ebisora korwa Gusii nigo bagatumiire chinguba ase esegi. Nigo enguba yare korosigwa korwa ase risangu rie engombe.

English: Below, the shield of the elders defending the Gusii community.
Ekegusii: Below, enguba ya abamura ebisore korwa Gusii.

English: The youth and their neighbors did not allow anyone to steal their livestock. Stealing livestock was considered a serious offense, and the thief would face consequences. Livestock, especially cattle, were very important.
Ekegusii: Abagaka amo na abangina abakoro tibare kobekerwa bokima ande onsi otatiga ase ekee. Kobeka obokima ase ekebekerero kende gionsi nigo yare koba amachayo. Ekee nakio kiare gotumeka ase okobeka obokima, especially obokima bwo obori.

English: Livestock were protected using traps made from cattle tails and intestines. The thieves also stole livestock. In the past, it wasn’t easy to recover stolen livestock. Yes. Livestock were able to graze peacefully for a long time. Below, the livestock of the Gusii people will be discussed.
Ekegusii: Nigo ekeee gekorosigwa korwa ase chimboba chio obori ne emegoye. Abasubati nabwo bare koroisia ebiee. Go keroisirie buya, ekee tikiare gokendia ndagera. Yaya. Ekee nigo kiare kogacha riberera rio obokima bwo obori for a long time. Below, ekee kio Omogusii buna kiare kororekana.

English: Circumcision among the Gusii
Ekegusii: Ekerandi Kio Omogusii

English: The Gusii people practice circumcision. It is true. The male genitals of cattle are cut during circumcision, just like humans. Circumcision is done using a special knife. Once the circumcision is complete, it is celebrated.
Ekegusii: Omogusii nigo anchete amabere. Eee bono. Amabere ye eng'ombe amaroranu abekire ekerandi ime Mose ominto. Ekerenadi nigo kiare korosigwa korwa ase risosa rie ekerandi. Ge ekerandi giakong'ire, nigo kiare kogeswa.

English: It is performed by traditionalists and young men. The leaders use a special stick to assist during circumcision so that it doesn’t hurt too much. Below, the circumcision of the Gusii people with its accompanying rituals.
Ekegusii: Giatigwa kioma na gosatwa amo na abasubati. Nigo abakungu bare gotumia ekebeya gosata ekerandi erinde kiaba amaridadi bori. Below, ekerandi kio Omogusii with ekemumeko gie ekeemba.

English: Sometimes, it is done differently in some places. It is very painful. However, nowadays, we use medicine and vehicles. But, it wasn’t always this way. The Gusii people were once strong enough to endure hardship!
Ekegusii: Eee gaki amache ang'usirwe in some places. Chigari nchiroo. Komenta nayio, ntobwate chibodaboda amo na mkokoteni. Korende, it was not always this way. Nigo Omogusii arenge kobogira kera egento gagokebeka motwe!

English: Pain was relieved by applying herbs to the wound. Spears, shields, cattle…and everything else. Now, the Gusii people devised a way to reduce the pain of removing items from the head.
Ekegusii: Amache nigo arenge kobuchwa korwa rooche abekwa omotwe igoro. Chinko, amatoke, obori...ndagera ende yonsi. Nonya nabo igo, Omogusii deviced a way to lessen pain yo okobogoria ebinto ase omotwe.

English: Finally.
Ekegusii: Engata.

English: This method was used to relieve pain on the head and even on parts of the body that had been injured. This method was applied to the head until it healed completely. It was created using the husks of bananas. Below. the final method of the Gusii people has been explained.
Ekegusii: Engata nero yare kobekwa gati yo omotwe oo amo ne egento keri obogoretie. Engata eye nero yare kobekwa motwe ekero ogwetweka. Nigo engata yare korosigwa korwa ase emegombo ya amatoke. Below. engata yo Omogusii buna yakabeire.

English: I remember that previously, young men would apply bandages to the forehead and temples. The forehead of the Gusii person should not have any scars because they affect the beauty of the head.
Ekegusii: Ntwarora above buna abasubati bare kobeka ebitinge ase enyangi ye enywomo. Enyangi yo Omogusii omokoro tiyare koba onye amaino ye embeche taratoka erinde omoywomi abekerwe motwe.

English: I don’t understand exactly the purpose of the gourds and horns that people carry when offering drinks to heal the head. But if we continue researching the gourds and horns that people carry, we will learn more. Let us investigate further; these things were never hidden. Below, the healing of the head (bandages) of the drink has been discussed.
Ekegusii: Ntoramanya exactly the purpose chisokoro amo na abamagokoro baito bateberete nga goika omonywomi abeke amaino ye embeche motwe oye. Buna tokona koboria chisokoro amo na abamagokoro baria baito batigarete, we will know more. Kabekire aamo iga, amaino aya nigo arenge korokwa ebibaga. Below, amaino ye embeche (ebibaga) yo omonywomi buna arenge kororekana.

English: The Ceremony of Mwanyagetinge
Ekegusii: Ekiore Kia Mwanyagetinge

English: In addition to applying bandages to the head, the Gusii people of old also practiced performing a ceremony on the head. The ceremony was usually carried out through divination. Below, the ceremony of the Gusii people will be described.
Ekegusii: In addition yo okobeka amaino ye embeche (ebibaga) ase omotwe oye, Omogusii omoywomi o kare nigo atakeire kobeka ekiore motwe oye. Ekiore nigo kiarenge koroisigwa korwa ase risankwa. Below, ekiore kio Omogusii buna giakarorekanire.

English: The Rituals of the Gusii
Ekegusii: Ritimo Rio Omogusii

English: As we have seen, there was no peace without war. I remember that the Gusii people had spears, shields, and clubs. And those who were brave enough, especially the elders and warriors, had their own rituals. This is in addition to shields, spears, etc. In the past, the Gusii people and their ancestors had standing armies.
Ekegusii: Buna twarorire, segi tiyare koba onye birwanero tibiyo. Ntwarora buna Omogusii abwate chinguba, chinsara amo na amatimo. Ase baria mogokina bono, tiga mbamanyie n'ga kera omogaka bwo omochie nigo abwate ritimo riaye. This is in addition to chinsara, enguba etc. Kera omogaka o Gusii amo na abamura be emechie bonsi, were standing armies.

English: They prepared well for battle.
Ekegusii: Baganyete ekero ekurate ekoba.

English: Below, the ancestral warriors of the Gusii people had their rituals. Behind him is the Assistant Minister for Culture and MP for North Mugirango Borabu, Hon. Wilfred Ombui and others at Keroka Cooperative Union Grounds recently during the Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Festival.
Ekegusii: Below, omomura egesora oyomo o Gusii kare ne ritimo riaye. Behind him is the Assistant Minister for Culture and MP for North Mugirango Borabu, Mhe. Wilfred Ombui and others aaria Keroka Cooperative Union Grounds recently during the Otenyo Omogusii Cultural Festival.

English: The Importance of Gourds
Ekegusii: Ekerangesa gia Sokoro

English: Anyone who sees a gourd being used for brewing, there is a reason why. Its importance. The great chiefs of old used to drink beer from gourds. The beer was poured into the gourd and then stirred. Because of this, the chiefs knew how to pour the beer into containers. But today, this is rarely done.
Ekegusii: Onye gokoigwa ekero sokoro agoasimora rimaambia, there is a reason why. Ekerangesa. Abagaka abanene ba kare nigo barenge konywa etumbato ye ekerangesa. Etumbato nigo yare kobekwa ase ekerangesa ime na gosunyuntwa. Korwa abwo, abagaka bamanya kobeka etumbato eyio ase chimioro. Basi bono tiga ogoasimora goanse.

English: What followed from there was continuous brewing. The contents of the gourd were poured into the gourd and were considered sacred. Continuous brewing led to prosperity and wealth!!
Ekegusii: What followed from there was ogoasimora kore successive. Amato ye etumbato arenge kobekwa ase ekerangesa ime nigo arenge koba amabese. Ogoasimora okonene nigo kwaminetie buna etumbato eyio n' engiya !!

English: The gourd was often made beautifully and carefully. As you can see, carpentry and arts and crafts of the Gusii people greatly depend on it. Below, the gourd of the Gusii people will be described.
Ekegusii: Ekerangesa nigo kiare koroisugwa korwa ase omote bwo omotembe. As you can see, omotembe nigo orenge important ase carpentry amo na arts and crafts yo Omogusii. Below, ekerangesa kio Omogusii buna giakarorekanire.

English: The Gusii people did not lack knowledge when faced with challenges. So what? The Gusii people were very skilled. They worked hard. Commenting on this, they worked hard and used tools to overcome challenges. Therefore, the skills of the Gusii people were praised.
Ekegusii: Omogusii tarenge gokira igo ka amarwaire achire. Ase ki? Omogusii nigo arenge omonyagitari. Abarwaria mbarengeo. Komenta nayio, abarwaria abwo mbabwate ebinto barenge gotumia ase okorwaria abarwaire. Ekemo kie ebibekerero bia abarwaria ba Gusii ne ekebwe.

English: But who praised them?
Ekegusii: Bono ekebwe ninki?

English: Anyone who understands well about medicine, knows that herbs are gathered and ground with medicine, the doctors use those skills to heal. If the herbs are mixed with medicine and the disease is cured, the cure is considered effective.
Ekegusii: Onye amanyinga akwereire emeki ime, gose omonto nigo aagetwe ase gete akabimba na amanyinga gokwera ime, abarwaria nigo barenge gotumia ekebwe koyang'usa. Ko omonto ang'usirwe amanyina ayio ne ekebwe, ensemo eyio yarwarete nigo yarenge gosusana.

English: Because of this, medicine is good. The skills are often developed through practice. People, below, have skills which will be described.
Ekegusii: Korwa abwo, omonto obwena. Ekebwe nigo kiare koroisigwa korwa ase orogunchara. Abaminto, below ne ekebwe buna giakarorekanire.

English: This Mwanyagetinge person, his field trip was successful. Let us wait for the next trip. For now, my heart is full of joy like a young bull grazing in the fields. But today I will briefly speak about it.
Ekegusii: Bono Mwanyagetinge ominto, e field trip nao yaereire igaa. Ntobatebie when the next trip comes. For now, magokoro nigo ateba ng'a enyama ya nda netigarete enyakaruga ime aaria nka. Bono tiga toraayerera gochia ase enka.

English: Jane Bosibori Obuchi
Ekegusii: Jane Bosibori Obuchi

English: When a person dies, relatives gather at the home with their hands, and they are mourned greatly throughout the homestead. Relatives also gather to lament and cry, and to show sorrow. The hands and arms are washed with water and various items: a calabash and its contents; bitter herbs and leaves; a grinding stone and pestle; a winnowing basket and fan. Washing the hands and washing the arms involves five types of seeds and five types of grains, each type being placed separately for the arm and the hand. All five types of seeds for the hands and arms, when the largest seed is put first, are scattered around the house. Also, from the remaining things, the largest seed for the hand is set aside with the other seeds for the hand, and the largest seed for the arm is set aside with the other seeds for the arm. The hands and arms are then rubbed with oil.
Ekegusii: Abwo kare kare, mwanyabanto nigo arenge gotaarera amagoro na’maboko, buna getongwa kende gionsi eke-nyamagoro ane. Mwanyabanto nigo arenge omwango kobua egesusu, endo, gose ekeobiria. Amagoro na’maoko nigo arenge aang’e mono ne’bimo binde: abwate chinenko chibwekaine: amareko ne’menyuma; ebigokoro na’maru; embaratero ne’nsanyi; egetinkiro no’koboko. Kera okoboko na kera okogoro nigo kwabwate ebiara bitano ne’bichara bitano, egechara ekemo ase kera ekiara gio’kogoro ne’giokoboko. Ebiara bionsi bitano bia’maboko na’magoro, korwa ekiara ekenene goika egeke, nigo biarobeirie enchera ebwekaine. Ase amatuko aria, ekiara ekeneene gio’koboko nigo kiarenge ang’e ne’biara binde bio’koboko buna ekiara ekeneene gio’kogoro kiarenge ang’e ne’biara binde bio’kogoro. Amagoro na’maboko nigo arenge korokana bwamwabo.

English: The hands and arms are then wiped with a cloth, and this is done so that when someone goes to walk, they do not stumble; the feet, ankles, knees and entire body are cleaned, and this is done so that they can be able to communicate well. And even with the eyes closed, they are able to wipe the face completely, and see all the things that are hidden. They are comforted and encouraged in their grief. They are asked to pray for blessings for themselves. They ask for forgiveness for all sins, asking for healing for illnesses, prosperity for wealth, success for children, and peace for eyes.
Ekegusii: Amagoro na’maboko nigo arenge gokonyana ase okobogoria omobere gochia ande onsi ore gotaka kogenda; echiro, chituka, korina na goika omote gose ebitunwa, ande onsi ase ogotaara kwaganeirie. Nonya na’se amache ime, nigo arenge kobwaterana buya mono gokonya omobere gocheng’enena, goaka ontimbu gose gotibogeria. Nigo asibogete na koigwana ase obwaamate bwabo. Nigo arenge gosaba obokonyi korwa ase ebimo binde buna; eriogi korwa ase omonwa, okoigwa korwa ase ogoto, okonyonka korwa ase emioro, amo no’korora korwa ase amaiso.

English: Their prayers and wiping are completed with respect for all sins. These sins are removed through cleansing and prayer for the sake of their ancestors. Together, they prepare food to offer, but the hands and arms may not touch it until it is finished. These sins cause problems for the hands and arms.
Ekegusii: Okoigwana na okobwaterana kwabo gokareta emoko ase ebimo binde. Ebimo ebi binde bikaanga korwa ogosemia na obokonyi gochia ase bwamwabo aba babere. Endamwamu ekabatuba gotarora buna amagoro na’maboko naro arenge kobaira ande onsi batagete. Ebimo binde bigachaka koroberia amabe ase amaboko na’magoro.

English: The elders request understanding from the mind and examine everything carefully. They begin to speak, “Eyes weep, the heart aches and the hands and arms tremble.” They want to know what caused the death and the reason for the great sadness. This gathering, these good things, the hands and arms, will stop speaking about the sadness once they have offered food and it has been eaten, and they will only remember the good deeds of the deceased. Finally, understanding comes with time; if one investigates, they will find the truth; the hands reveal what happened and the seeds are scattered, and they are able to understand the reasons for the scattering of the seeds of the arms, and they become calm and peaceful. Seeds of the arms are not mixed with bad things. And others investigate the causes of the weeping like the seeds of the hands. People, relatives, friends! This custom is observed by our ancestors, so let us continue to perform it properly for the benefit of our bodies and souls. The words spoken resemble the sound of thunder: Let these sins be cleansed and forgiven.
Ekegusii: Oromeme rogasaba ekerengererio korwa ase obongo na rokageikerania abwo abwo. Rogachaka gokumia, ‘maiso marore, igoro ye’chinguru ne’siko ya’maboko na’magoro. Rokarigia komanya ng’a ning’o obwate ekieni ne’siko enene kobua oyonde. Abwo ritang’ani, ’bimo ebi bibere, amaboko na’magoro, tibiarenge gokumia igoro ye’kioyonde abwate gose are gokora korende bono bigachaka gosaba eriogi korwa ase omonwa nabo igo bigachaka goteeba buna nigo bire ebie’ngencho mono ase omobere kobua ebimo binde. Keri keri, ekerengererio eke kegaonchoreria na koba; ning’o ochongororogete kobua oyonde; amaboko akerora ng’a aro na’re ne’ebiara ebinyerere, nabo igo agachaka gokwana na’machaya igoro ye’biara bia’magoro buna bire ebieng’e na ebinetu ebimigi. Biara bia’magoro tibigokirie na ‘nkwana eye. Na birobio bikairaneria ase amachaya igoro yo’bonyerere bwe’biara bia’maboko. Bakaba, bamwabo bachayaine, baankaine! Egento eke gekagenderera ase amatuko amange, goika kero kende kegasaria ogokora emereme ase obomo no’boikeranu. Omoerio oye egaikera ase riborio rie’chinguru: Bikaboria ebimo binde kogayana ring’ana eri.

English: The elders ask for understanding because of their inability to comprehend. Many people gather, but this is not the right understanding. Therefore, the question arises: Is this understanding true or false? Sins are cleansed through purification; some are remembered as being committed by our ancestors. Some are remembered as causing conflict, leading to trouble, therefore, let us look at the traditions that were established by our ancestors; let the hand and the arm work together. Regarding the skin of an animal, the elders request understanding from the mind, remembering the past. Concerning the hands and arms, let us look at the traditions that were established to ensure proper understanding. Relatives gather with this understanding.
Ekegusii: Oromeme rokarua ekerengererio ng’a babe no’kwamererania. Bonsi bagaancherana buna eke ne’kerengererio ekiya. Korende, obokong’u obomo no’bo: okoamererania oko inkoroki? Ebimo bigachaka korua ogosemia; ebinde bigateeba ng’a bamwabo aba bakinane enyameni. Ebinde bigateeba barwane ne’meyio, gose gotinkana chimbero, korende kera ekemo kie’birengererio ebi gekaangwa ng’a ne’gekong’u goikerania ase ebimo ebi bibere; okogoro gose okoboko. Ase entunde ya kabere, oromeme rogasaba ekerengererio korwa ase obongo, igoro yerichibu ria bwango. Ase amagoro na’maboko, nigo kera ekemo kie’bimo ebi kiarenge koreta okoamererania kwaye. Bwamwabo bagaancherana ne’kerengererio eke.

English: This misunderstanding is due to someone's arrogance and pride. All sins are hidden within, and everyone feels pain when they see the suffering of others, which affects their well-being. The eyes cry out for help. The legs carry burdens and walk far, but they may stumble, and the body becomes weak and tired, unable to see clearly, and the elders say that they can no longer endure.
Ekegusii: Okoamererania oko nigo gwakorekanete ase arabirie ime ye rinani, ang’e na rooche. Ebimo bionsi bikebeka ang’e ase kende gionsi gose mobasokano onde bwonsi orachere omobere, ekiagera bono ebimo bio’mobere nigo biarenge kong’usanana. Amaiso agachina are na’ng’e korora kende kebe kerache, korwa ‘nsinyo ende yonsi. Ekegusii: Jane Bosibori Obuchi is a writer, a researcher, and a teacher. English: Long ago, a story circulated around the area of Nyangweta. It is said that a certain person stole several items belonging to others, hiding them so they wouldn't be found by the owner.
Ekegusii: Chikura chinke chia Bonchari nigo chikare chitariki 2 Ebwagi [ June ], 2014.

English: Later, those who had stolen the items gathered and agreed to return everything, fearing the consequences. However, once the owner recovered their belongings, they refused to accept them back, claiming they were damaged beyond repair.
Ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya:

English: They claimed that the returned items were no longer useful and were completely broken, making them worthless. Those who had stolen the items regretted their actions and wished they hadn't bothered returning anything.
Ekegusii: Abwo kare kare, engoncho eyemo yamenyete aaria ase rinani ria Nyangweta. Aaiga, omoruoti nere ore kogamba nigo abwate abakori egasi baye, bagachire ase rinani eri batwara, erinde baretera omoruoti obo endagera.

English: Because the thief had taken everything and the returned items were severely damaged, the matter became complicated and caused problems throughout the Nyangweta area, leading to endless disputes.
Ekegusii: Rituko erimo, abatwari aba b' omoruoti bagatega chingoncho ekiagera nigo chiare gotera na kororekana buya amaritati oka. Ekero baika ase omoruoti amenyete, bakamooroki chingoncho echi bategete na kobwata na omoruoti akagokigwa ekianda gia ikomi.

English: Therefore, leaders should consult with traditions
Ekegusii: Kagokigwa, agateba buna chingoncho echi chiroserigwe egesumu ekiiya, erinde chimenye aroro na chiegwe endagera engiiya kera engaki tichibaisa kogenda kwerigeria endagera. Abanto bakagokigwa ne chinyoni echi na nigo bagachire bw' omoruoti erinde korora chingoncho echi kera rituko.

English: Those leaders and people involved in this issue should seek guidance from tradition. Tradition will advise them and help resolve the dispute. Again, the stolen items, guided by tradition, should be returned and the matter resolved peacefully.
Ekegusii: Bw' omoruoti egatwara abageni abange engaki eye yonsi ne chingoncho echi chikagokigwa kerage ekiagera nigo chiamenyete obogima obuya kobua bori chiamenyete ase rinani ria Nyangeta, ekiagera tichiare kwerigeria ndagera gose kweroseria ebisumu.

English: If the thief returns everything he stole, including the damaged items, and the matter becomes complicated in the Nyangweta area, it will lead to continuous arguments and disagreements.
Ekegusii: Bono abatwari basianyanire n' Ogakondo

English: However, if the traditional council intervenes, it will bring order and ensure fairness. They will investigate the matter thoroughly and determine what needs to be done.
Ekegusii: Bono abatwari b' omoruoti engaki ende ekero bare rinani ime, bagasianyana n' Ogakondo. Ogakondo oyo akabagokia na bakamobwata komoira ase omoruoti. Korora iga, omoruoti akagokigwa n' Ogakondo oyo na goteba buna nere buya aroserigwe ase akobera na koegwa endagera.

English: Finally, the agreement reached should be respected by everyone. Otherwise, the situation could worsen, and the initial agreement may be disregarded. This agreement should be upheld, otherwise, future issues may arise.
Ekegusii: Keri keri, Chingoncho echi chikaebwa bono ekaba buna Ogakondo oyo nere orenge kororwa n' abanto korwa aare. komenta nayio, nigo arenge koegwa endagera engiiya, goikera chingoncho chigacha chikaebwa. Chingoncho echi nigo chiebetwe, goikera amatuko ande nigo chiare korara nchara.

English: Important announcements regarding the traditional council!!
Ekegusii: Amamocho amanene mono, ase Ogakondo koruta chintacho !!

English: In this instance, the traditional council has made a significant decision, and it has spoken about the theft and its implications. If there is an apology, the person who was wronged should forgive. Furthermore, if a leader has a child, they should encourage their fellow leaders to support that child's upbringing.
Ekegusii: Bono engaki eyemo, Ogakondo oyo okare koruta chintacho, na goaka bw' omoruoti na koamoaka obosio. Ekero aakwa obosio, omowana oyo agokura mono. Bono omoruoti ekero aigwete egekuro ki' omwana oye, agatebia abatwari baye bagende barore ninki omwana oye agokurera.

English: Indeed, leaders who respect the traditional council will allow the child to benefit from the stolen property. The leader should ensure that the traditional council is honored, so they can protect their children.
Ekegusii: Ani, abatwari aba bakare konyora Ogakondo nigo aagete omwana bw' omoruoti obosio igoro. Omoruoti ekero aigwete aya, akagechigwa na goteba buna Ogakondo oyo airanigwe rinani ime ekiagera nigo arabaise goita abana baye.

English: Therefore, let the traditional council continue to work towards peace and harmony.
Ekegusii: Bono goika Ogakondo naende aanse kwerigeria aaiga orosana ime.

English: Leaders have praised the traditional council and its efforts in the Nyangweta area. This matter has been concluded successfully. If it remains successful, this agreement will be remembered by everyone, and it will be ensured that it is implemented fairly.
Ekegusii: Abatwari bakaimokia Ogakondo na komoirania rinani ria Nyangweta. Bono chingoncho chigatigara chioka. Ekero chiatigara chioka, chingoncho bono nachirochio chigachaka kororwa na abanto buna riri kare na chigachaka koegwa endagera buna chiare koegwa.

English: This story teaches us that forgiveness is essential, and reconciliation is possible. Therefore, it should be honored by everyone and help unite people.
Ekegusii: Chingoncho echi chikamanya buna chigosaria, nachirochio nigo chirairanigwe rinani ime. Bono chirochio chikaba chiingiya, chigotera na kogokia abanto kera engaki.

English: These are important points:
Ekegusii: Aya amwabo aya:

English: Respect and honor those who offer assistance and guidance. Let our ancestors remember the saying, “Let us find solutions together for the sake of our community.” Those who cause trouble should understand that their actions have consequences and that they must take responsibility for their mistakes.
Ekegusii: Okoamereria, n' ogwentukwaria ngwakabeire aroro korwa kare. Matuko make iga, omogaka sokoro ominto nantebetie buna "Ko’na Keene Buna Eki Omorogi Nyabamura" Aaiga, aya akwaneire n' omonto ogokora amabe, omanya kwamereria abanto moono buna ere tarakora kende kebe.

English: Like the Gusii people. Respect and honor those who offer assistance and guidance.
Ekegusii: Nka Gusii. Okoamererania ngwakabeire aroro korwa kare.

English: It is said that if someone does something wrong, they should seek forgiveness from the community, and the elders should help them reconcile with others. However, when things get difficult, people forget!
Ekegusii: Nigo sokoro antebetie buna ase chingaki chiria chi' kare, onye omonto omanyiru buna nigo arenge omorogi, nigo abanyakenyoro barenge komochobera botuko. Keri keri riria araire chitoro ekenyitita, bamong’enta atamanyeti!

English: Therefore, the community should support and educate its children, ensuring they grow up respecting traditions and values. Our ancestors also taught us to protect our heritage and culture.
Ekegusii: Korende omorogi orenge n’ abana abamura abange nigo arenge koirokwa na koobogwa, ekiagera abamura aba nabo bare gocha goita abanyakenyoro aba ekero bagochobera omoibori obo erinde bamong’ente.

English: Finally, those who cause trouble should understand that their actions have consequences and that they must take responsibility for their mistakes. They should seek forgiveness from the community and learn from their errors.
Ekegusii: Bono omonto ogokora amabe ase ekenyoro, omanya koamereria na gwetunkwaria buna ere tarakora kende, nere obwekanirie n' omororogi nyabamura bange. Koamereria abanto moono, nigo akobwekanigwa n’ omorogi oyo.

English: Protect our heritage, and let the Gusii people always remember the saying, “Let us find solutions together for the sake of our community!” Remember the importance of unity and cooperation within our community. This message is for everyone this week.
Ekegusii: Oboamereri, nabwo bwagerete Abagusii baito abakoro bagateba buna Ko’na keene buna eki’ omorogi nyabamura!! Korwa ase omogaka sokoro ominto, oyo noro omorabaro oito for this week.

English: John John 1
Ekegusii: YohanaYohana 1

English: 1 The beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. 2 This beginning was with God. 3 All things were made through him; without him nothing was made that has been made. 4 In him was life, and the life was the light of men. 5 The light shines in darkness, and darkness did not overcome it. 6 There came a man named John, sent from God, so that he might testify about the light. 7 He came to testify, to bear witness to the light, so that everyone who believes might have eternal life. 8 He was not the light, but bore witness to the light. 9 The true light which gives light to every man was coming into the world. 10 He was in the world, and the world was made through him, yet the world did not know him. 11 He came to his own people, and they did not receive him. 12 But to all who received him, he gave them the right to become children of God, to those who believe in his name: 13 who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God. 14 And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only begotten Son from the Father, full of grace and truth. 15 John testified concerning him, and cried out, saying, “This was he of whom I said, ‘He who comes after me ranks higher than I,’ because he existed before me.” 16 From his fullness we have all received, and grace upon grace. 17 For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. 18 No one has ever seen God; the only begotten Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, he has declared him. 19 And this is the testimony of John when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?” 20 He confessed, and did not deny, but said, “I am not the Christ.” 21 They asked him, “Then what are you? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” He answered, “No.” 22 So they said to him, “Then who are you, that we may give an answer to those who sent us?” 23 He said, “I am the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ as Isaiah the prophet wrote.” 24 Now the Pharisees also had come and questioned him, asking, 25 “Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?” 26 John answered them, saying, “I baptize with water, but there stands One among you whom you do not know. 27 He is the one who comes after me, and I am not worthy to untie his sandal strap.” 28 These things took place in Bethany beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing. 29 The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him, and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!” 30 This is he about whom I said, ‘After me comes one who is preferred over me, for he existed before me.’ 31 And I did not know him, but so that he might be revealed to Israel, therefore I came baptizing with water.” 32 John testified, saying, “I saw the Spirit descending like a dove from heaven and resting upon him. 33 And I have borne witness that he is the Son of God.” 34 I have seen and testified that this is the Chosen One of God.” 35 The next day again John stood with his disciples, and looked at Jesus as he walked by. 36 And he said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!” 37 The two disciples heard him speak, and followed Jesus. 38 Then Jesus turned, and seeing them following, said to them, “What do you seek?” They said, “Rabbi” (which means Teacher), “where are you staying?” 39 He said to them, “Come and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and remained with him that day, for it was about the tenth hour. 40 Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of those who heard him, and he told his brother Simon, 41 He first found his own brother Simon, and said to him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated, Christ). 42 And he brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “You are Simon the son of John, you shall be called Cephas” (which is translated, Peter). 43 The next day Jesus decided to go to Galilee, and he found Philip and said to him, “Follow me.” 44 Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter. 45 Philip found Nathanael and said to him, “We have found him about whom Moses in the Law and also the prophets wrote, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.” 46 Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come out of Nazareth?” Philip said to him, “Come and see.” 47 Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said of him, “Behold, an Israelite indeed, in whom there is no deceit!” 48 Nathanael said to him, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered him, “Before Philip told you, I saw you under the fig tree.” 49 Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!” 50 Jesus answered him, “Because I have told you that I saw you under the fig tree, do you believe? You will see greater things than these.” 51 And he said to him, “Truly, truly, I say to you, you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.”
Ekegusii: 1 Omochakano ndiarengeo Ring'ana, ne Ring'ana iga riarenge amo na Nyasaye, narirorio Ring'ana iga narenge Nyasaye. 2 Oyio omochakano igarenge amo na Nyasaye. 3 Bionsi bigakoreka as'oyio; gose onye tari ere anga tigiakoregete kende gionsi egiakoregete. 4 Ime yaye nao bwarenge obogima; naborobwo obogima iga bwarenge omobaso bw'abanto. 5 Noro omobaso obarire as'omosunte, erio omosunte toyonyara. 6 Akaoroka omonto, otometwe korwa ase Nyasaye, erieta riaye Yohana. 7 Oyo igachete abe kirori erinde atebe omobaso bonsi banyare gwancha asere. 8 Oyio tarenge oria omobaso, korende igachete as'oborori bw'omobaso. 9 Norengeo omobaso bw'ekeene, okomobeka omobaso ker'omonto ogocha as'ense, 10 Nao arenge as'ense ime, ense egakorwa asere, nense tiyamomanya. 11 Agacha as'abaye, nabarabwo abare abaye tibamwancha. 12 Korende bonsi abamwanchete, akabaa okobua babe abana ba Nyasaye, nabwo barianchire erieta riaye: 13 abaiboirwe, tari as'amanyinga, gose tari as'obwanchani bw'omobere, gose tari as'obwanchani bw'omonto, korende ase Nyasaye. 14 Narirorio Ring'ana rigakoreka omobere, agaikaransa asetore, (tokaborora obonene bwaye, obonene buna obw'omwana omomoima orure ase Tata), oichire obuya nekeene. 15 Yohana akamwatora, akaaka egeturi, akabora, Oyo nere natebete amang'ana aye, ng'a Oyorache nyuma yane igare ritang'ani asende: ekiagera arenge ritang'ani asende. 16 Naende as'ogoichora kwaye intwe twensi twanyorire, obuya igoro as'obuya. 17 Ekiagera amachiko aruetwe ase Musa; obuya nekeene iga bwachete ase Yesu Kristo, 18 Omonto onde tari omororire Nyasaye kero kende gionsi; Omwana bweka ore as'egekuba kia Tata nere omoorokirie. 19 Naende obwo nabwo oborori bwaye Yohana, ekero Abayahudi batomete abakuani n'Abalawi korwa Yerusalemu bamoborie, Aye naye ng'o? 20 Nere akaorokia, takana; agateba, Inche tari nche Kristo. 21 Bakamoboria, Naki rende? Naye Elija? Akabora, Inche tari ere. Aye naye omobani oria? Akairaneria, Yaya. 22 Nabo bakamotebia, Naye ng'o, tobae okoiraneria abatotomete. Naki ogweteba? 23 Akabora, Inche neriogi ri'omonto okoaka eriogi eroro ime, Rongeyia enchera y'Omonene, buna atebete omobani Isaya, 24 Nabarabwo abatometwe baruete as'Abafarisai. 25 Bakamoboria, bakamotebia, Naki rende okobatisa, onye aye tori Kristo, gose Elija, gose omobani oria? 26 Yohana akabairaneria akabora, Inche iga nkobatisa as'amache: egati yaino otenenire oyomotamanyeti inwe. 27 Nere ogocha nyuma yane, oyorenge ritang'ani asende, gose inche tingwenereti nyesibore enuga y'egekoroto kiaye. 28 Aya iga akoregete Bethania ng'umbu ya Yorodan, nao arenge Yohana okobatisa. 29 Rituko ria kabere riaye Yohana akamorora Yesu ogocha asare, akabora, Rora, Emanwa y'Eng'ondi ya Nyasaye, oyobogoretie ebibe bi'ense! 30 Oyo nere nare goteba amang'ana aye, Ngochare omonto nyuma yane, oyore ritang'ani asende, ekiagera arenge ritang'ani asende. 31 Nainche tinamomanyete; korende aorokigwe as'Abaisiraeli, nabo as'ayio ngacha nakobatisa as'amache. 32 Yohana agakwana, akabora, Nayororire Omoika ogoika korwa igoro buna riruma, rigaikaransa igoro asare. 33 Nainche tinamomanya: korende ere oyontomete kobatisa as'amache, oyio agantchia, Ere oyoranyare korora Omoika ogoika nagoikaransa igoro asere, oyio nere okobatisa n'Omoika Omochenu. 34 Nainche narorire, naende natebire ng'a oyo n'Omwana o Nyasaye. 35 Naende rituko ria kabere riaye Yohana igarenge otene ne nababere b'aborokigwa baye. 36 Akamorigereria Yesu ogotara, akabora, Rora, Emanwa y'Eng'ondi ya Nyasaye! 37 Baria aborokigwa babere bakamoigwa ogoteba, bakamotunyana Yesu. 38 Yesu ageonchora, akabarora bakomotunyana, akabatebia, Ninki mokorigia? Bakamotebia, Rabii (ogoonchorwa kwaye, Omworokia), ng'ai omenyete? 39 Akabatebia, inchuo morore. Bagacha, bakarora aas'amenyete; bakamenya asare rituko riria: iga yarenge ang'e chinsa ikomi. 40 Anderea, momura omwabo Simon Petero, igarenge oyomo bwa baria babere bamoigwete Yohana nakomotunyana. 41 Oyo akamonyora ritang'ani Simon momura omwabo omonyene, akamotebia, Twamonyorire Masihi, (ogoonchorwa kwaye Kristo). 42 Akamoira ase Yesu. Yesu akamorigere ria, akabora, Aye Simon, omwana o Yona, norokwe Kefa (ogoonchorwa kwaye, Petero). 43 Rituko ria kabere riaye Yesu akarigia koimoka kogenda Galili, akamonyora Filipo: akamotebia, Ntunyana. 44 Nere Filipo igarenge omonto o Bethisaida, omonto bw'omochie bw'Anderea na Petero. 45 Filipo akamonyora Nathaniel, akamotebia, Twamonyorire ere oyorikeretwe na Musa as'amachiko, nababani, Yesu omwana o Yusufu, omonto o Nazareti. 46 Nathaniel akamotebia, Nakenyare egento ekiya korua Nazareti? Filipo akamotebia, Inchuo orore. 47 Yesu akamorora Nathaniel ogocha asare, agakwana asare, Rora, oyo n'Omoisiraeli ekeene ekeene, otari nobong'ainereria ime yaye. 48 Nathaniel akamotebia, Ing'ai kwamanyera? Yesu akairaneria, akamotebia, Ritang'ani Filipo atarakorangeria, ekero kwarenge inse as'omoko, nakoroche. 49 Nathaniel akamoiraneria, akamotebia, Rabii, naye Omwana o Nyasaye, naye omoruoti bw'Abaisiraeli. 50 Yesu akairaneria, akamotebia, Ekiagera nagotebia, nakoroche inse as'omoko, gwanchire? Norore amang'ana amanene kobua aya. 51 Akamotebia, Ekeene, ekeene, nagotebirie, namoyerore igoro ekoigoka, namalaika a Nyasaye akorina, agoika igoro as'Omwana-o-mwanyabanto.

English: 1 On the third day there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there. 2 Jesus himself and his disciples were also invited to the wedding. 3 When the wine ran out, the mother of Jesus said to him, “They have no wine.” 4 Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does this have to do with me? My hour has not yet come.” 5 His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he tells you, do it.” 6 Now there were six stone water jars there for Jewish ceremonial washing, each containing twenty to thirty gallons. 7 Jesus said to them, “Fill the jars with water.” So they filled them up to the brim. 8 Then he told them, “Now draw some out and take it to the master of the banquet.” They did so, 9 and when the master of the banquet tasted the water that had been turned into wine, he did not know where it came from. But the servants who had drawn the water knew, and they testified, “This wine is from Cana in Galilee.” 10 Jesus said to her, “Every host serves the good wine first, and when people have drunk freely, then the poor wine. But you have kept the good wine until now.” 11 This, the first of his signs, Jesus did at Cana in Galilee, and manifested his glory. And his disciples believed in him. 12 After this he went down to Capernaum with his mother and brothers and his disciples, and they stayed there for a few days. 13 During the Jewish festival, Jesus went up to Jerusalem. 14 In the temple courts he found people selling cattle, sheep and doves, and money changers sitting there. 15 He made a whip out of cords, and drove all the animals and people out of the temple courts. He scattered the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables. 16 To those who were selling doves he said, “Get these out of here! Do not make my Father’s house a den of thieves!” 17 His disciples remembered that it was written, “Zeal for your house will consume me.” 18 The Jews demanded, “What sign can you show us to prove your authority to do this?” 19 Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and I will raise it again in three days.” 20 The Jews replied, “It has taken forty-six years to build this temple, and you are going to raise it in three days?” 21 But he was speaking about the temple of his body. 22 After he was raised from the dead, his disciples recalled that he had said this, and they understood that he was talking about the temple of his body. 23 As he was going to Jerusalem, many people believed in him because they saw the miracles he performed. 24 But Jesus would not entrust himself to them, for he knew all people. 25 He did not need anyone to testify about mankind, for he knew what was in their hearts.
Ekegusii: 1 Naende rituko ria gatato yarenge enyangi ase Kana ya Galili; na ng'ina Yesu nao arenge. 2 Yesu nere akarangerigwa amo naborokigwa baye as'enyangi. 3 Goika edivai egachia kobaremera, ng'ina Yesu akamotebia, Tibari nedivai. 4 Yesu akamotebia, Omokungu inki nde inche naye? Ensa yane teraika. 5 Ng'ina akabatebia abasomba, Rinde rionsi arabatebie, rikore. 6 Nchiarenge aroro chinsiongo isano nemo chi'amagena, chiabekire aroro as'engecho y'ogwesibia kwabo Abayahudi, ker'eyemo iga yarenge ang'e ekerengo kia chigallon emerongo ebere. 7 Yesu akabatebia, Ichoria chinsiongo namache. Bagachichoria goika igoro. 8 Akabatebia, bono taa, moirere omonene bw'omoyega. Bakaira. 9 Omonene bw'omoyega agachia koyaigwa amache akoregete koba edivai, tamanya ase yarua, (korende abasomba mbamanyete ababuchete amache), omonene bw'omoyega akamorangeria omonene bw'enyangi, 10 akamotebia, Kera omonto ritang'ani iga agochaka edivai ere engiya, goika abanto kobatiekire konywa mono, erio oreta eyetari engiya: aye kwagachire edivai engiya goika bono, 11 Oyio noro omochako bw'ebikone Yesu akorete Kana ya Galili, akaorokia obonene bwaye; aborokigwa baye bakamwancha. 12 Nyuma as'aya akagenda goika Kaperinaum, ere, na ng'ina, nabamwabo, naborokigwa baye: bakamenya aroro amatuko amake. 13 Naende epasaka y'Abayahudi iga yarenge ang'e, Yesu akarina goika Yerusalemu. 14 Akarora hekalu ime abanto barenge gotonda chiombe neching'ondi namaruma, nabanyene koonchora chifetha, baikaransete: 15 agakora orokini ase chingori, akabasokia bonsi korwa ase hekalu, neching'ondi nechiombe; agaitera chifetha chiabo abanyene goonchora chifetha,agachionchora chimesa chiabo; 16 akabatebia baria barenge gotonda amaruma, Yatigerie aya; timokora enyomba ya Tata one koba enyomba y'ebiasara. 17 Aborokigwa baye bakainyora ng'a nerikire, Risemi ri'enyomba yao riandire. 18 Nabo Abayahudi bakairaneria bakamotebia, Ngekone ki ogotworokia, ekiagera ogokora aya? 19 Yesu akairaneria, akabatebia, Yetagore hekalu eye, nainche as'amatuko atato ninyetenenie. 20 Abayahudi bakabora, Hekalu eye yaagachetwe as'engaki y'emiaka emerongo ene netano nomo, naye oyetenenie as'amatuko atato? 21 Korende ere igare kobora amang'ana ase hekalu y'omobere oye. 22 Nabo agachia kobokigwa as'amakweri aborokigwa baye bakainyora ng'a igatebete ring'ana eri, bakariancha riria ririko nariria ring'ana atebete Yesu. 23 Goika agachia kobao Yerusalemu ekero ki'epasaka ase rituko rinene, abanto abange bakariancha erieta riaye, kobarora ebikone arenge gokora. 24 Korende Yesu tegenete asebare, naki abamanyete bonsi, 25 naende ekiagera tarenge nokorigia as'abanto goteba amang'ana igoro ase mwanyabanto; naki ere omonyene amanyete ayare ime as'abanto.

English: 1 Now there was a Pharisee named Nicodemus, a member of the Jewish ruling council. 2 He came to Jesus at night and said, “Rabbi, we know that you are a teacher sent from God. For no one could perform the signs you are doing if God were not with him.” 3 Jesus replied, “Very truly I tell you, no one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again.” 4 “How can someone be born when they are old?” Nicodemus asked. “Surely they cannot enter a second time into their mother’s womb to be reborn?” 5 Jesus answered, “Very truly I tell you, no one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit. 6 Flesh gives birth to flesh, but the Spirit gives birth to spirit. 7 You should not be surprised that I said, ‘You must be born again.’ 8 The wind blows wherever it pleases. You hear its sound, but you cannot tell where it comes from or where it is going. So it is with everyone born of the Spirit.” 9 “How can this be?” Nicodemus asked. 10 Jesus replied, “Are you Israel’s teacher, yet you do not understand these things? 11 Very truly I tell you, we speak of what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, but you do not accept our testimony. 12 I have told you earthly things and you do not believe; how then will you believe if I tell you heavenly things? 13 No one has ever gone into heaven except the one who came down from heaven—the Son of Man. 14 Just as Moses lifted up the bronze snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, 15 that everyone who believes may have eternal life in him.” 16 For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life. 17 For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn it, but to save it. 18 Whoever believes in him is not condemned, but whoever does not believe stands condemned already because they have not believed in the name of God’s one and only Son. 19 This is the verdict: Light has come into the world, but people loved darkness instead of light because their deeds were evil. 20 Everyone who does evil hates the light, and will not come into the light for fear that their deeds will be exposed. 21 But those who live by the truth come into the light, so that it may be seen plainly that what they have done has been done in the sight of God. 22 After this, Jesus and his disciples went out into the countryside of Judea. He spent some time there with them, and baptized. 23 John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there was plenty of water there; people were coming and being baptized. 24 This happened because John had not yet been thrown into prison. 25 Now a discussion arose between John’s disciples and a Jew about purification. 26 They came to John and asked, “Rabbi, why are you baptizing here if you aren’t the Messiah?” 27 John replied, “I baptize with water, but among you stands one you do not know. 28 He is the one who comes after me, and I am not worthy to untie the sandals on his feet.” 29 The next day, John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world! 30 This is the one I meant when I said, ‘After me will come one who ranks higher than I.’ 31 The one who goes ahead of me has already gone, and I am coming after him.” 32 And John testified: “I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove and remain on him. 33 I have seen and I testify that this is the Son of God.” 34 The next day John again stood with his disciples and said, “See, the Lamb of God!” 35 The next day John was standing there again with two of his disciples. 36 When Jesus walked by, John looked at him and said, “See, the Lamb of God!” 37 The two disciples heard him say this, and they followed Jesus.
Ekegusii: 1 Narenge omonto oyomo bw'Abafarisai, erieta riaye Nikodemo, omonene bw'Abayahudi: 2 oyo agacha ase Yesu botuko, akamotebia, Rabii, twamanyire ng'a nomworokia ore, kwarure ase Nyasaye: naki omonto onde tari oranyare kobikora ebikone ebi ogokora, tatiga Nyasaye abe amo nere. 3 Yesu akairaneria, akamotebia, Ekeene, ekeene, nagotebirie, Omonto ataiboiri eria kabere, takonyara koborora obonda bwa Nyasaye. 4 Nikodemo akamotebia, Naki aranyare omonto koiborwa kare omogaka? nanyare gosoa enda ya ng'ina eria kabere aiborwe? 5 Yesu akairaneria, Ekeene, ekeene, nagotebirie, Omonto ataiboiri as'amache n'Omoika, takonyara gosoa obonda bwa Nyasaye. 6 Ekeiboire as'omobere nomobere; nekeiboire as'Omoika nomoika. 7 Tokumia ekiagera nagotebia, Nogwenerete koiborwa naende. 8 Embeo iga ekogenda as'erigetie, negeturi kiaye iga ogokeigwa, korende tomanyeti as'ekorua gose as'ekogenda: naboigo na ker'omonto oiboirwe as'Omoika. 9 Nikodemo akamoiraneria, akamotebia, Naki aranyare koba aya? 10 Yesu akairaneria akamotebia, Inee! Aye nomworokia as'Isiraeli, naya toyainyoreti? 11 Ekeene, ekeene, nagotebirie, Eritomanyete nario togokwana, neri toroche twariteba; noborori bwaito timorigwancha. 12 Kerabe nkobatebia amang'ana ense, nainwe timogwancha, naki moranche, kondabatebie amang'ana a igoro? 13 Naende omonto onde tari orinire igoro, tatiga ere oyoikire korwa igoro Omwana-o-mwanyabanto ore igoro. 14 Naende buna Musa aimogetie eng'iti eroro ime, naboigo Omwana-o-mwanyabanto agwenerete aimokererigwe: 15 erinde tasira omonto onde bwonsi oyomwanchire, korende abe nobogima bwa kare nakare. 16 Naki Nyasaye ayianchete ense, goika akarua Omwana oye omomoima, erinde 'monto onde bwonsi oyomwanchire tasira, korende anyore obogima bwa kare nakare. 17 Naki Nyasaye tamotomete as'ense Omwana oye agambie ense; korende ense ekonywe nere. 18 Oyomwanchire takogambigwa; oyotancheti otiekire kogambigwa, ekiagera atariancheti erieta ria Omwana oyomo bweka o Nyasaye. 19 Neke nakio ekina, ekiagera omobaso ochire ense, abanto bagancha omosunte kobua omobaso; naki ogokora kwabo kwarenge okobe. 20 Naki kera oyogokora amabe igagechete omobaso, gose tagocha as'omobaso, ogokora kwaye tikobaisa gokanigwa. 21 Korende oyogokora ekeene igagocha as'omobaso, ogokora kwaye kororekane ng'a iga gwakorirwe ase Nyasaye. 22 Nyuma as'aya Yesu naborokigwa baye bakagenda goika ense ya Boyahudi, akabera aroro amo nabarabwo okobatisa, 23 Yohana nere igarenge kobatisa aria Ainon, ang'e na Salim, ekiagera narenge amache amange: abanto bakomochiera bakobatiswa. 24 Naki Yohana konya tarabekwa echela. 25 Nabo, gokaoroka okoamererania as'aborokigwa ba Yohana n'Abayahudi as'amang'ana ogwesibia. 26 Bakamochiera Yohana, bakamotebia, Rabii, ere oyorenge amo naye ng'umbu ya Yorodan, oyio kwaorogetie aye, oyio nere nkobatisare, nabanto bonsi nkomochierabare. 27 Yohana akairaneria, akabora, Takonyara omonto konyora ring'ana rinde rionsi tatiga aegwe korwa igoro. 28 Inwe abanyene mwabaire kirori ng'a natebete, Inche tari Kristo, korende natomirwe gotang'ana asare. 29 Oyore nere omoriakari bw'enyangi nere omonene, korende omosani oye bw'omonene bw'enyangi iga agotenena nakomoigwa, origokera eriogi riaye omonene bw'enyangi: nabo oyo omogoko one oikeranire. 30 Ere nagwenerete amenteke, korende inche nkee. 31 Oyochire korwa igoro oyio igare igoro as'onsi: oyore bw'ense, noyo bw'ense, iga agokwana amang'ana ense: ere oyochire korwa igoro oyio igare igoro as'onsi. 32 Ayaroche nakoyaigwa, naro abereire kirori: gose onde tari oyobwanchire oborori bwaye. 33 Oyobwanchire oborori bwaye obekire ekemanyererio kiaye ng'a Nyasaye nekeene, 34 Naki ere oyotometwe na Nyasaye igakoyakwana amang'ana a Nyasaye: naki Nyasaye tari komoa Omoika as'ekerengo. 35 Tata omwanchire Omwana, omoeire bionsi as'amaboko aye. 36 Oyoramwanche Omwana nare nobogima bwa kare nakare; noyotamoigwereti Omwana takorora obogima, korende nendamwainu ya Nyasaye eramoikaransere.

English: 1 Now when the Pharisees learned that Jesus had been baptizing people and gaining more disciples than John— 2 though Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples did— 3 he left Judea and went back to Galilee. 4 As he traveled, he went through Samaria. 5 So he came to a town in Samaria called Sychar, near the plot of ground Jacob had given to his son Joseph. 6 Jacob’s well was there, and Jesus, tired from his journey, sat down beside the well. It was about noon. 7 A Samaritan woman came to draw water, so Jesus said to her, “Will you give me a drink?” 8 His disciples had gone to the town to buy food. 9 The Samaritan woman said to him, “You are a Jew, and I am a Samaritan woman. How can you ask me for a drink?” (Jews do not associate with Samaritans.) 10 Jesus answered her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is that asks you for a drink, you would have asked him for living water.” 11 “Sir,” the woman said, “you don’t have a bucket, and the well is deep. Where can you get this living water? 12 Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, as did also his sons and his livestock?” 13 Jesus answered, “Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again, 14 but whoever drinks the water I give them will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give them will become in them a spring of water welling up to eternal life.” 15 The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water so that I won’t have to come here and draw water anymore.” 16 He told her, “Go, call your husband and come back.” 17 “I have no husband,” she replied. Jesus said to her, “You are right to say you have no husband. 18 For you have had five husbands, and the man you have now is not your husband. At this you spoke the truth.” 19 The woman said, “Sir, I can see that you are a prophet. 20 Our ancestors worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews claim that the place to worship is in Jerusalem.” 21 Jesus said, “Believe me, dear woman, a time is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem. 22 You Samaritans worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, for salvation is from the Jews. 23 Yet a time is coming and has now come when the true worshipers will worship the Father in the Spirit and in truth, for they are the kind of worshipers the Father seeks. 24 God is spirit, and his worshipers must worship in the Spirit and in truth.” 25 The woman said, “I know that Messiah” (called Christ) “is coming. When he comes, he will explain everything to us.” 26 Jesus declared, “I, the one speaking to you, am he.” 27 Just then his disciples returned and were surprised to find him talking with a woman. But no one asked him, “What do you want?” or “Why are you talking with her.” 28 Then the woman left her water jar and went back to the town. “Come, see a man who told me everything I ever did,” she said to the women. “Could this be the Messiah?” 29 They came out of the town and made their way toward him. 30 Meanwhile, his disciples urged him, “Rabbi, eat something.” 31 But he said to them, “I have food you cannot comprehend.” 32 “Surely not the food someone brought him to eat?” the disciples asked each other. 33 Jesus told them, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to finish his work. 34 Don’t you have a saying, ‘Four months until harvest’? I tell you, look around and see that the fields are already ripe for harvest. 35 The reaper’s wages are substantial, and he gathers in fruit for eternal life. So that both the sower and the reaper may rejoice together. 36 For in this case, the saying holds true: ‘One sows and another reaps.’ 37 And I tell you that the person who harvests will receive a reward too, and the harvest yields an abundant crop. 38 I sent you to reap what you haven’t worked for. Others have done the hard work, and you have come to enjoy their efforts.” 39 Many of the Samaritans from that town believed in him because of the testimony of the woman who said, “He told me everything I ever did.” 40 So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them. He stayed there for two days, 41 and many more became believers because of his message. 42 They said to the woman, “We no longer believe just because of what you told us; we have heard him ourselves, and we know that he really is the Savior of the world.” 43 After the two days he left for Galilee. 44 Now Jesus himself had pointed out that a prophet has no honor in his own hometown. 45 So when he arrived in Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, having seen all that he did in Jerusalem at the Passover festival. 46 Once again he visited Cana in Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. There was a royal official whose son lay sick in Capernaum. 47 When he heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son. 48 “Sir,” he said, “come down before my child dies.” 49 Jesus replied, “Go home. Your son will live.” The man took Jesus’ word and departed. 50 While he was walking home, his servants met him with the good news that his son was recovering. 51 He asked them how much time it had taken, and they replied, “Yesterday afternoon the fever left him.” 52 Then his father realized this must have been the time when Jesus said to him, “Your son will live!” And so the whole household believed. 53 This second sign Jesus performed was in Cana of Galilee. He then went to Capernaum. 54 This was the second miracle Jesus performed, coming from Judea to Galilee.
Ekegusii: 1 Nabo Omonene agachia komanya ng'a Abafarisai baigure ng'a Yesu okorire aborokigwa abange kobua Yohana, nakobatisa, 2 (Yesu omonyene tare kobatisa, korende naborokigwa baye), 3 akarua Boyahudi akagenda Galili eria kabere. 4 Naende nagwenerete goeta gati ya Samaria. 5 Nabo agaika omochie o Samaria, okorokwa Sukar, ang'e nomogondo oria Yakobo amoete Yusufu omwana oye: 6 naende agwo yarenge ensoko ya Yakobo. Nabo Yesu, konya orosire as'orogendo rwaye, agaikaransa iga as'ensoko. Konya yabaire ang'e chinsa isano nemo. 7 Agacha omokungu o Samaria kobucha amache: Yesu akamotebia, Ing'a amache inywe. 8 Naki aborokigwa baye konya bachire omochie kogora endagera. 9 Nabo oria omokungu bw'Abasamaria akamotebia, Naki yaba aye Omoyahudi korigia amache asende, nainche nomokungu bw'Abasamaria? (naki Abayahudi tibari gosanga n'Abasamaria.) 10 Yesu akairaneria akamotebia, Onye nkwamanya ekeegwa kia Nyasaye, nere ng'o okogotebia, Ing'a amache inywe; anga nkwamosaba ere, nere anga nakoa amache are moyo. 11 Oria omokungu akamotebia, Omonene, tori negento gi'okobuchera nensoko yachire inse mono: ng'ai kwayanyorire amache aya are moyo? 12 Inee! aye nomonene kobua tata oito Yakobo, oyotoete ensoko eye, nere omonyene akanywa amache aya, nabana baye bonsi netugo yaye? 13 Yesu akairaneria, akamotebia, Ker'oyokonywa amache aya narore erang'o naende: 14 korende onde bwonsi oyoranywe amache aria ndamoe inche, takoigwa erang'o kare nakare; korende amache aria ndanyare komoa nabe ime yaye ensoko y'amache, agosoka goika obogima bwa kare nakare. 15 Omokungu oria akamotebia, Omonene, ing'a amache ayio tindora erang'o, gose timbaisa gocha aiga kobucha. 16 Yesu akamotebia, Genda, omorangerie omosacha oo oche nere aiga. 17 Omokungu oria akairaneria akamotebia, tindi nomosacha. Yesu akamotebia, gwakwanire buya, tindi nomosacha: 18 naki kwabaire nabasacha batano; nere oyore nere bono tari omosacha oo: as'ayio gwakwanire ekeene. 19 Omokungu oria akamotebia, Omonene, narorire ng'a nomobani ore. 20 Abatata baito iga barenge gosasima as'egetunwa eke; nainwe iga mogoteba ng'a Yerusalemu naase atogwenerete togosasimera. 21 Yesu akamotebia, Aye omokungu, inyancha, ensa neche, motpmosasime Tata as'egetunwa eke, nonya nase Yerusalemu. 22 Inwe iga mogosasima eki motamanyeti: intwe iga togosasima ekitemanyete: naki ogotoreka gokorua as'Abayahudi. 23 Korende ensa neche, nabono nere, abare nogosaba kw'ekeene nabamosasime Tata as'omoika nekeene: naki Tata iga akobarigia abanto buna abwo bamosasime. 24 Nyasaye n'Omoika, nabwo bakomosasima nebagwenerete komosasima as'omoika nekeene. 25 Omokungu oria akamotebia, Namanyire ng'a ngochare Masihi (okorokwa Kristo): karache ere, natoorokerie onsi. 26 Yesu akamotebia, Inche ngokwana naye, nere. 27 Erio bagacha aborokigwa baye bagakumia ekiagera arenge gokwana nomokungu; korende onde tarenge kobora, Inki okorigia? gose, Naki ogokwana nere? 28 Nabo oria omokungu akayetiga enyongo yaye, akagenda omochie ka, akabatebia abanto, 29 Inchuo, morore omonto ontebirie amang'ana onsi ayanakorire: Inee! oyio tari ere Kristo? 30 Bakaimoka korwa omochie bakamochiera. 31 Agwo nyuma aborokigwa bakamosorora bakabora, Rabii, ragera. 32 Akabatebia, Inche ninde nendagera motayemanyeti inwe. 33 Aborokigwa baye bakaborania, Inee? nomonto omoretera endagera? 34 Yesu akabatebia, Endagera yane ney'ogokora obwanchani bwaye oyontomete, nagokora emeremo yaye. 35 Timori goteba inwe, Yatigaire emetienyi ene, erio riche rigesa? Nainche nabatebirie, Ramokia amaiso aino moyerigererie emegondo, ng'a yatiekire koba emerabu ang'e ase rigesa. 36 Oyo okogesa nkonyorare eng'eria, nagosangereria amatunda as'obogima bwa kare nakare; erinde ere oyogosimeka nere oyokogesa bagoke amo. 37 Naki ring'ana riria, Oyomo osimeka, oyonde ogesa, iga rire ekeene. 38 Inche nabatomete moyagese ayamotechandereti; abande bakorire emeremo, nainwe mwasoire as'emeremo yabo. 39 Naende as'omochie oria Abasaniaria abange bagancha as'engecho y'amang'ana ay'oria omokungu, atebete ng'a, Nantebia amang'ana onsi ayanakorire. 40 Nabo ekero baria Abasamaria bachia komochiera, bakamosorora aikaranse amo nabarabwo: agaikaransa aroro amatuko abere. 41 Abanto abange kobua bagancha as'engecho ye ring'ana riaye; 42 bakamotebia omokungu oria, Bono twanchire, tari ekiagera as'amang'ana ao: naki twaigure abanyene, naende twamanyire ekeene ng'a oyo n'Omekonyi bw'ense. 43 Nyuma as'amatuko ayio abere akaimoka korwa agwo, akagenda Galili. 44 Naki Yesu omonyene atebete, ng'a omobani tari nogosikwa as'ense yaye omonyene. 45 Nabo ekero achia goika Galili bakamwancha, ekiagera baroche amang'ana onsi ayakorete Yerusalemu ekero kie rituko rinene: naki nabarabwo bagenderete rituko rinene. 46 Agaika naende Kana ya Galili, agwo akorete amache akaba edivai. Naende yarenge esagini eyemo, yarenge nomwana omorwaire Kaperinaum. 47 Oyio agachia koigwa ng'a Yesu ochire korwa Boyahudi goika Galili, akamochiera, akamosorora achiche amokonye omwana oye; ekiagera konya oisire gokwa. 48 Nabo Yesu akamotebia, Motarochi ebikone namakumigwa timogwancha nonya ng'ake. 49 Oria esagini akamotebia, Omonene, ika ritang'ani atarakwa omwana one. 50 Yesu akamotebia, Bwatia enchera yao: omwana oo moy'are. Omonto oria akariancha riria ring'ana atebetigwe na Yesu, akabwatia enchera. 51 Goika agachia koba ogoika, abasomba baye bagacha komorotota, bakamotebia, bakabora, Omwana oo moy'are. 52 Erio akababoria amang'ana ensa achagete koba buya. Bakamotebia, Igoro, chinsa isano naibere, esosera yamotigete. 53 Erio ise akainyora ng'a nensa eria eria atebetigwe na Yesu, Omwana oo moy'are: agancha ere, nenyomba yaye yonsi. 54 Neke negekone gia kabere akorete Yesu korwa ekero aruete Boyahudi kogenda Galili.

English: 1 Now there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. 2 Near the Sheep Gate there is a pool called Bethesda, which has five porticoes. 3 Here lay a great number of people who were sick—blind, lame, paralyzed—waiting for the water to be stirred. 4 An angel would come down and stir the water, and whoever went in first would be healed. 5 One man was lying there who had been ill for thirty-eight years. 6 When Jesus saw him lying there and knew he had been there a long time, he asked him, “Do you want to get well?” 7 The sick man answered, “Sir, I have no one to help me get into the pool when the water is stirred. By the time I get there, someone else goes down ahead of me.” 8 Jesus told him, “Get up! Pick up your mat and walk.” 9 At once the man was cured; he picked up his mat and began to walk. 10 It was the Sabbath day when this happened. 11 So the Jews said to the man who had been healed, “It is against our law for you to carry your mat on the Sabbath.” 12 He replied, “The man who made me well said to me, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’” 13 They asked him, “Who is this who told you to pick it up and walk?” 14 Later Jesus found him at the temple and said to him, “See, you are well again. Stop sinning or something worse may happen to you.” 15 The man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well. 16 Because of this, the Jews persecuted Jesus and tried to kill him because he did such things on the Sabbath. 17 But Jesus answered them, “My Father is still working, and I also am working.” 18 For this reason the Jews tried all the more to kill him, because not only was he breaking the Sabbath, but he was also calling God his Father, making himself equal to God. 19 Then Jesus explained, “Very truly I tell you, the Son can do nothing by himself; he can do only what he sees his Father doing. Whatever the Father does, the Son does also. 20 For the Father loves the Son and shows him all he does.
